a003733c-1e21-49e3-9c51-ea0c801e12a5.title: AI
a003733c-1e21-49e3-9c51-ea0c801e12a5.definition: Artificial Intelligence (AI) studies problems that are difficult or impractical to solve using traditional algorithmic methods.

54b5bf21-2245-45b2-a92f-64189e2f77fe.title: AI Problem Characteristics
54b5bf21-2245-45b2-a92f-64189e2f77fe.definition: The problems that AI studies are often reminiscent of those thought to require human intelligence, and AI solution strategies are often capable of generalizing across multiple classes of problems.

57fb48f0-6f70-4bb3-8edf-a17b2c2a9827.title: AI Ubiquity
57fb48f0-6f70-4bb3-8edf-a17b2c2a9827.definition: AI techniques are now widespread in computing, powering everyday applications such as email, social networks, photography, and financial markets.

f32cda36-ad03-48f2-8d46-67a88c129a38.title: Virtual Assistants
f32cda36-ad03-48f2-8d46-67a88c129a38.definition: AI systems assist users by understanding and executing requests, e.g. Siri, Alexa.

c1bf5abe-f85c-4e42-a41a-06d1603fbacc.title: Autonomous Agents
c1bf5abe-f85c-4e42-a41a-06d1603fbacc.definition: Autonomous agents are AI systems designed to perceive their environment and interact appropriately with it.

b9e2fce3-3469-415d-80f1-cd25f20fae62.title: Self-Driving Cars
b9e2fce3-3469-415d-80f1-cd25f20fae62.definition: An application of autonomous agents, where vehicles are capable of operating on their own without human intervention.

6318ed0a-343d-4388-a434-a6caf59d39c2.title: Robotics
6318ed0a-343d-4388-a434-a6caf59d39c2.definition: The field of research, design, manufacturing, operation and application of robots, including robots that operate as autonomous agents.

aff42528-5829-4295-b1ef-30e0ac9c14e0.title: Symbolic AI
aff42528-5829-4295-b1ef-30e0ac9c14e0.definition: One of the traditional approaches in AI, focuses on representing knowledge through symbols, logic and rules.

34aa8ba1-084e-4f65-abe8-d43566ae4fa5.title: Subsymbolic AI
34aa8ba1-084e-4f65-abe8-d43566ae4fa5.definition: One of the traditional approaches in AI, includes distributed processing models such as neural networks, where knowledge is not explicitly represented symbolically.

cd7f775e-7fb2-4cf0-bb0d-23e20444f33b.title: Knowledge Representation
cd7f775e-7fb2-4cf0-bb0d-23e20444f33b.definition: Methods and structures for encoding information and knowledge in a way that can be stored, accessed, and manipulated by AI systems.

c610573a-6863-47c5-969c-50c4d6b1ec73.title: Problem Solving
c610573a-6863-47c5-969c-50c4d6b1ec73.definition: The methods and strategies used by AI systems to find solutions to problems, often including search and inference.

23290a31-b39e-421f-903a-04213920944a.title: Optimization
23290a31-b39e-421f-903a-04213920944a.definition: Methods are used to find the best solution from a set of possible solutions, often to improve performance or achieve a specific goal.

5a0e4d22-b1a4-4870-8dee-66922a4ad037.title: Perception
5a0e4d22-b1a4-4870-8dee-66922a4ad037.definition: The aspect of AI that deals with the collection, processing, and interpretation of information from the environment.

f867acb9-8e1b-48de-ac38-a28013850379.title: Speech Recognition
f867acb9-8e1b-48de-ac38-a28013850379.definition: The ability of a computer to convert speech into text or other understandable formats.

af1e20b4-bf2f-4a74-bdd4-5181396396e8.title: NLU
af1e20b4-bf2f-4a74-bdd4-5181396396e8.definition: The ability of a computer to understand the meaning of text or speech in natural human language.

d8d3d528-0812-4a85-8e30-156bd1605e42.title: Computer Vision
d8d3d528-0812-4a85-8e30-156bd1605e42.definition: The field of AI enables computers to collect, process, analyze and understand images and videos from the real world.

5d244a86-610f-4916-9905-ad0e591b84b4.title: AI Search
5d244a86-610f-4916-9905-ad0e591b84b4.definition: Algorithmic techniques are used to explore the state space in search of a solution or a path from the initial state to the goal state.

36f7991d-d39a-4528-9213-a643e6c397c3.title: AI Planning
36f7991d-d39a-4528-9213-a643e6c397c3.definition: The field of AI is concerned with designing sequences of actions to achieve a specific goal or set of goals.

c1fcb644-b0c0-4fa9-be70-19135799490b.title: Generative AI
c1fcb644-b0c0-4fa9-be70-19135799490b.definition: The aspect of AI that involves generating new content, such as narratives, conversations, images, models or recommendations.

14ec33fd-b34c-4b8d-b1bc-06f2b6a4f2d2.title: AI Action
14ec33fd-b34c-4b8d-b1bc-06f2b6a4f2d2.definition: The aspect of AI that involves AI agents performing actions in their environment.

68dac5f5-f4d0-4d05-bdb2-fcadc7a6bcd2.title: Task Automation
68dac5f5-f4d0-4d05-bdb2-fcadc7a6bcd2.definition: The use of technology to perform routine or repetitive tasks without human intervention.

419f168e-ad04-4d7c-8569-09d878c57a18.title: AI Control Systems
419f168e-ad04-4d7c-8569-09d878c57a18.definition: Systems use AI techniques to manage, regulate and control the operation of devices, machines or processes.

096f684d-74d3-46ad-9877-4fbb539b2814.title: AI Architecture
096f684d-74d3-46ad-9877-4fbb539b2814.definition: The organizational structures and design of AI systems.

0bef5188-b6ba-4de7-b7ae-9a16d0454f2b.title: Single-agent System
0bef5188-b6ba-4de7-b7ae-9a16d0454f2b.definition: AI systems in which a single agent operates and interacts with its environment.

8315958d-d373-4cd1-a753-ddeb7d90bbf4.title: Multi-agent System
8315958d-d373-4cd1-a753-ddeb7d90bbf4.definition: AI systems consist of multiple agents that interact with each other and the environment to achieve common or individual goals.

5bb04979-fd2b-4d23-964e-51310fc2b74d.title: Machine Learning
5bb04979-fd2b-4d23-964e-51310fc2b74d.definition: A branch of artificial intelligence that allows systems to learn from data without being explicitly programmed, which can be used in all aspects of AI.

138a6df6-37ae-45de-a707-16daeb3a853e.title: AI Approach Suitability
138a6df6-37ae-45de-a707-16daeb3a853e.definition: The skill of determining when an AI approach is appropriate or most effective for solving a particular problem.

a2a3b69c-7347-4868-a624-615c0cdbb32c.title: AI Representation & Reasoning
a2a3b69c-7347-4868-a624-615c0cdbb32c.definition: Skill in selecting the most appropriate knowledge representation schemes and inference mechanisms for a specific AI problem.

f842e6af-0bb9-4d30-869d-863d5a8dd0eb.title: AI System Deployment
f842e6af-0bb9-4d30-869d-863d5a8dd0eb.definition: Skills to build and develop AI solutions based on selected representations and inference mechanisms.

fceeaaec-009a-4238-aed9-7557580e0c6e.title: AI Performance Evaluation
fceeaaec-009a-4238-aed9-7557580e0c6e.definition: Skills to evaluate the effectiveness and accuracy of deployed AI solutions.

c2596db5-b742-4251-9c7a-3f8a1d390890.title: AI Social Impact
c2596db5-b742-4251-9c7a-3f8a1d390890.definition: Skills to consider and evaluate the broader effects of AI systems on society, beyond technical performance.

8c82b490-3816-4570-9371-4c71312488a1.title: AI Popularity
8c82b490-3816-4570-9371-4c71312488a1.definition: Over the past decade, the term "artificial intelligence" has become popular in business circles, news articles, and everyday conversations.

55ac02a5-6fb2-4e9d-b3e3-f2ba6952c102.title: Big Data in AI
55ac02a5-6fb2-4e9d-b3e3-f2ba6952c102.definition: The widespread availability of large data sets is a key factor driving recent advances in AI, especially in machine learning.

39306386-23c6-4880-9a4a-2b3716f5e11f.title: AI Compute Power
39306386-23c6-4880-9a4a-2b3716f5e11f.definition: Increasing computing power is a key factor for the development of AI, allowing it to handle complex models and huge amounts of data.

334db5f5-9940-4a1c-a858-4ce69bc97c84.title: AI Algorithm Advances
334db5f5-9940-4a1c-a858-4ce69bc97c84.definition: Improvements in AI algorithms have contributed significantly to recent advances, making AI systems more efficient and powerful.

16d2a7fc-706b-4c29-a4f0-2dd800d00a39.title: Learned Representations
16d2a7fc-706b-4c29-a4f0-2dd800d00a39.definition: The trend in AI is a shift from knowledge representations manually designed by engineers to representations learned automatically through optimization on large data sets.

16a6dd16-14e2-4a63-98d5-c3fa11586e38.title: Neural Networks
16a6dd16-14e2-4a63-98d5-c3fa11586e38.definition: A machine learning model inspired by the structure and function of the human brain, consisting of interconnected layers of artificial neurons.

cd0b29da-053f-4823-8bab-ea23f5ef1b2e.title: Deep Learning
cd0b29da-053f-4823-8bab-ea23f5ef1b2e.definition: A branch of machine learning that uses neural networks with many hidden layers (deep neural networks) to learn complex representations of data.

a4c01b8d-d235-4ddb-8e15-62a33e0e55a1.title: AI: Tech Term vs. Marketing
a4c01b8d-d235-4ddb-8e15-62a33e0e55a1.definition: "Artificial intelligence" is now both a specialized technical term and a marketing keyword used by businesses to promote the added value of their services.

92f4b7ab-13c9-4635-8ccf-c5382e506622.title: AI Interdisciplinary Applications
92f4b7ab-13c9-4635-8ccf-c5382e506622.definition: AI techniques are increasingly widely used in many different fields such as biology, art, architecture and finance to solve specialized problems.

42db29fa-0fa8-4be2-85cf-b4f5a7a1a5cb.title: Public AI Access
42db29fa-0fa8-4be2-85cf-b4f5a7a1a5cb.definition: For the first time in history, the public has access to sophisticated AI-driven tools.

7b20faf0-48fb-46b7-b885-c9166a48fdf8.title: Generative AI Content
7b20faf0-48fb-46b7-b885-c9166a48fdf8.definition: apply AI in creating diverse types of content such as essays, poetry from suggestions, artwork from descriptions, and even fake images or videos (deepfakes) of real people.

abae52cc-7c22-4a8f-82a8-9dc3c87b64fa.title: AI Stock Trading
abae52cc-7c22-4a8f-82a8-9dc3c87b64fa.definition: Use AI technology to analyze the market, predict trends and automate stock trading transactions.

2457ee71-283f-427f-b3df-2dc25f39ec49.title: AI Content Curation
2457ee71-283f-427f-b3df-2dc25f39ec49.definition: Use AI to personalize and curate news streams and social media content for users.

c0f64019-37ef-4a10-8905-637506512055.title: AI Candidate Assessment
c0f64019-37ef-4a10-8905-637506512055.definition: apply AI to automatically analyze and evaluate job candidates' profiles and skills.

b6004687-e6fb-4d5e-9d00-4e0811c30963.definition: Use AI to support diagnosis and early detection of diseases or health conditions based on medical data.

1d58cfdd-0929-431c-b4ca-9b0bcea7648e.definition: applying AI to predict the likelihood that an individual will reoffend after being released can influence sentencing decisions.

518d2b9a-7c05-4c44-9c5e-c7ff1aadc0ba.title: AI Ethical Considerations
518d2b9a-7c05-4c44-9c5e-c7ff1aadc0ba.definition: Important ethical issues need to be understood and considered when developing and applying AI technology, given its potential for significant impact on society.

d27655f9-4405-42c8-b295-4a5b57b5ce9b.title: AI Terminology Shift
d27655f9-4405-42c8-b295-4a5b57b5ce9b.definition: Reflects common terminology changes within the AI ​​field and widespread usage outside the field.

863fca76-fbef-456a-a492-7f569c7d0d68.definition: An important issue in the social impact of AI, including in the curriculum.

576d2cd4-9d33-4787-b785-dfbfcf4e16de.definition: The clear goal is to develop critical thinking about AI in every computer science student.

d928c516-d11e-4338-9c3c-548cd7973c68.definition: New techniques became popular and were added to the curriculum.

d2ded5f3-ab44-4680-b511-5edc54de3484.definition: Unit of knowledge on types of agents and cognitive systems in AI.

bd922a39-4854-4b4a-a392-2c402c14094d.definition: Unit of knowledge on natural language processing.

591182c0-d0ad-4eeb-98ad-0a5c5e40f3fc.definition: Unit of knowledge in cognition and computer vision.

429c21a5-ac25-48c6-9e1d-c9f607c1aa20.definition: Part of the Fundamental Knowledge Representation and Reasoning unit, shared with Mathematical Foundations.

9492dc52-76c8-4567-aa36-e486b10c88b6.title: AI Problem Overview
9492dc52-76c8-4567-aa36-e486b10c88b6.definition: An overview of the types of problems AI tries to solve.

fe178d3a-561a-4aa4-a168-2514838888b7.title: Recent AI Successes
fe178d3a-561a-4aa4-a168-2514838888b7.definition: Examples of how AI has been successfully applied in practice.

9fafb03e-ae94-4183-81b5-cabb8f435709.title: AI Agent Definition
9fafb03e-ae94-4183-81b5-cabb8f435709.definition: understand different definitions of agents in AI and specific examples.

c21c4e22-989f-4972-a2c8-49c62315bfc9.title: Reactive Agents
c21c4e22-989f-4972-a2c8-49c62315bfc9.definition: A type of agent that only reacts directly to the current environment without the ability to plan or complex reasoning.

b762c814-7f05-4085-8726-04dd291edb91.title: Deliberative Agents
b762c814-7f05-4085-8726-04dd291edb91.definition: A type of agent capable of planning, reasoning, and building models of the world to make decisions.

978428f4-42d6-4b59-9831-5641ca45fdd9.title: Intelligent Behavior
978428f4-42d6-4b59-9831-5641ca45fdd9.definition: Discuss the criteria and definitions of behavior considered intelligent.

37167c9b-f39b-425b-a4a3-dd5a990d7d63.title: Turing Test
37167c9b-f39b-425b-a4a3-dd5a990d7d63.definition: A method for evaluating a machine's ability to exhibit human-equivalent intelligent behavior.

0bd1565b-29e5-4fa7-bc0d-26708f2a7239.title: Turing Test Limitations
0bd1565b-29e5-4fa7-bc0d-26708f2a7239.definition: understand the weaknesses and criticisms of the Turing test as a measure of intelligence.

0d833c6c-a08c-46ac-bc5d-5b6e95c5db82.title: Multimodal I/O
0d833c6c-a08c-46ac-bc5d-5b6e95c5db82.definition: Ability to process and produce information through a variety of media (e.g., text, images, sound).

c515eb68-770a-4942-9d12-5f0085bdd18d.title: Intelligent Behavior Simulation
c515eb68-770a-4942-9d12-5f0085bdd18d.definition: Ways in which computers can simulate aspects of intelligent behavior.

62b27394-34ec-4bc3-a155-229d06fc0246.title: Rational vs. Non-rational Reasoning
62b27394-34ec-4bc3-a155-229d06fc0246.definition: The difference between making decisions based on optimal logic and data versus other forms of reasoning.

0d506e15-a3fc-4cc7-bd61-f2633e7ff611.title: Problem Characteristics
0d506e15-a3fc-4cc7-bd61-f2633e7ff611.definition: Understanding the different characteristics of a problem can influence the AI ​​approach.

b1d2247f-94c6-4787-8340-cd50e649198d.title: Observable Problems
b1d2247f-94c6-4787-8340-cd50e649198d.definition: Distinguish between problems where the agent can observe the entire state of the environment from problems where only a part can be observed.

d2e2dba5-f78a-4b97-b699-037efa385bd2.title: Agent Problems
d2e2dba5-f78a-4b97-b699-037efa385bd2.definition: Distinguish problems with only one agent from problems with many interacting agents.

fad812c9-0433-4613-b839-0bb4f86f96b8.definition: Distinguish between problems where the outcome of an action is certain from those where there is an element of chance.

5b1d98c5-e81e-4732-91b6-45742e23f92b.definition: Distinguish between problems where the environment does not change during solution from problems where the environment changes independently of the agent.

188ea033-c350-419d-8b2c-55b79e1552f7.title: Discrete vs Continuous Problems
188ea033-c350-419d-8b2c-55b79e1552f7.definition: Distinguish between problems with a finite and countable number of states or actions from those with an infinite or continuously variable space of states or actions.

1b371a84-d55a-4caa-92e5-b69602d62c73.title: Nature of Agents
1b371a84-d55a-4caa-92e5-b69602d62c73.definition: Delve deeper into the properties, architecture, and functionality of AI agents.

3848d2f7-5a5f-4506-a563-545808591c0f.title: Agent Autonomy Types
3848d2f7-5a5f-4506-a563-545808591c0f.definition: Learn about the different levels of autonomy in AI systems, from fully automated to requiring human intervention, or a combination of both.

95350839-7d2c-4eb6-8fcf-a5a7ea093507.title: Reflex Agents
95350839-7d2c-4eb6-8fcf-a5a7ea093507.definition: Research on AI agents that operate based on simple reflex rules, responding directly to environmental signals without the need for complex planning.

f6a9eca6-7cf8-43f7-b10b-9088b6794722.title: Goal-based Agents
f6a9eca6-7cf8-43f7-b10b-9088b6794722.definition: Learn about AI agents acting to achieve one or more specific goals, often through planning and search.

4b14173c-01be-49a4-b359-a2a7b75504e5.title: Utility-based Agents
4b14173c-01be-49a4-b359-a2a7b75504e5.definition: The study of AI agents choosing actions to maximize their utility function, weighing desired and likely outcomes.

83bf48cd-823a-4566-be02-38a29c68f007.title: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
83bf48cd-823a-4566-be02-38a29c68f007.definition: Research methods and algorithms for AI agents to make optimal decisions when information about the environment or the results of actions are not completely clear.

31252783-410a-442c-89c7-de91c32daed9.title: Decision Making Incomplete Info
31252783-410a-442c-89c7-de91c32daed9.definition: Explore how AI agents process and make decisions with only partial information about the world state or available options.

2fa933df-5f9f-45d6-97ef-ddf63dfcfca0.title: Perception in AI
2fa933df-5f9f-45d6-97ef-ddf63dfcfca0.definition: analyze the role of the ability to acquire and interpret information from the environment (cognition) in the effective operation of AI agents.

7cdcaea8-362b-4902-afb5-14acbb8215d4.title: Agent-Environment Interaction
7cdcaea8-362b-4902-afb5-14acbb8215d4.definition: Learn about how AI agents interact with their environment, including influencing and responding to changes, to achieve their goals.

95080a5b-e914-4ead-982c-8b0f315538b3.title: Learning-based Agents
95080a5b-e914-4ead-982c-8b0f315538b3.definition: Research AI agents capable of improving their performance through experience, using machine learning algorithms.

47550bdb-1eee-4616-ba4c-d47fdc25fc43.title: Embodied Agents
47550bdb-1eee-4616-ba4c-d47fdc25fc43.definition: Learn about AI agents that have a physical existence in the real or simulated world, capable of physically interacting with the environment.

7406851c-b971-4140-93ed-8417b0dfaa17.title: Embodied Agent Sensors
7406851c-b971-4140-93ed-8417b0dfaa17.definition: Study the types of sensors that embodied agents use to collect information from the physical environment.

09b19e8e-a5d9-47f0-af4b-eed697bcc99c.title: Embodied Agent Dynamics
09b19e8e-a5d9-47f0-af4b-eed697bcc99c.definition: Learn about the laws of physics and motion behavior that govern embodied agents and their interactions with the environment.

99f0aec4-e943-4a98-885c-357e087f419a.title: Embodied Agent Actuators
99f0aec4-e943-4a98-885c-357e087f419a.definition: Study the parts of embodied agents that allow them to physically impact the environment (e.g., robotic arms, wheels).

7ef46844-f742-498e-9547-a3b941c23650.title: AI Applications Overview
7ef46844-f742-498e-9547-a3b941c23650.definition: Provides an overview of fields and how AI is applied in practice, from healthcare to finance to manufacturing.

00d33f3b-218e-4b88-bce5-b7c07f896562.title: AI Growth & Impact
00d33f3b-218e-4b88-bce5-b7c07f896562.definition: analyze the rapid growth of AI and its far-reaching effects on the economy, social structures, and ethical issues.

ed4f1ffd-9e0c-4aee-aedc-cebcf0e5dd59.title: Problem Characterization Practice
ed4f1ffd-9e0c-4aee-aedc-cebcf0e5dd59.definition: Practice skills in analyzing and characterizing an AI problem in specific situations, including environment, state, and goals.

05feed89-0805-43a2-93a2-1f0816cda289.title: Agent Nature (Advanced)
05feed89-0805-43a2-93a2-1f0816cda289.definition: Study in more detail the structure, types and operations of AI agents, accompanied by specific illustrative examples.

d09add7a-5454-4946-a0ac-e9f9e93aec27.title: AI Impact (Advanced)
d09add7a-5454-4946-a0ac-e9f9e93aec27.definition: A more in-depth analysis of the current and potential applications of AI, as well as its complex impacts on economic, social, ethical and security domains.

0594ecf6-c152-41c4-ac48-3be22c0eefb9.title: AI Philosophical Issues
0594ecf6-c152-41c4-ac48-3be22c0eefb9.definition: Explore deep philosophical questions related to AI, such as consciousness, intelligence, machine ethics, and the nature of intelligence.

34c0386b-1d68-48f1-8da9-9456074172d7.title: History of AI
34c0386b-1d68-48f1-8da9-9456074172d7.definition: Overview of important milestones, key figures and development of the field of artificial intelligence over time.

aeed52cd-4497-410f-b437-f0128ed997c3.title: Turing Test
aeed52cd-4497-410f-b437-f0128ed997c3.definition: understand the Turing test, a famous test proposed to evaluate the ability of a machine to exhibit intellectual behavior equivalent to or indistinguishable from humans.

a60024dd-5f56-44f2-ae1b-86e5463202d2.title: Chinese Room Experiment
a60024dd-5f56-44f2-ae1b-86e5463202d2.definition: A study of the 'Chinese Room' thought experiment and the philosophical debates it raises about the nature of understanding and consciousness in AI.

23632a32-cf47-4761-ad47-13f59bbf8206.title: Optimal Reasoning/Behavior
23632a32-cf47-4761-ad47-13f59bbf8206.definition: Distinguish and understand the behaviors or reasoning processes that achieve the best possible results based on established criteria.

2153925e-b1e2-4c8c-90ed-5d9daf2dd36a.title: Human-like Reasoning/Behavior
2153925e-b1e2-4c8c-90ed-5d9daf2dd36a.definition: Distinguish and understand behaviors or reasoning processes that simulate how humans think and act, often not necessarily optimally.

071fbf69-e2cc-466c-a036-26bfc4ee15ca.title: AI, ML, DL Distinction
071fbf69-e2cc-466c-a036-26bfc4ee15ca.definition: understand and clearly distinguish the concepts of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning and Deep Learning.

1662579f-ae33-44f7-9ce1-d785d6043ed0.title: State Space Representation
1662579f-ae33-44f7-9ce1-d785d6043ed0.definition: Learn to describe a search problem as a state space, where each state represents a configuration of the problem.

c9f112b8-9aa5-4365-86bb-2b3f0ac38101.title: States, Goals, Operators
c9f112b8-9aa5-4365-86bb-2b3f0ac38101.definition: Learn how to clearly define possible states, desired goal states, and possible actions (operators) to transition between states.

2a65a013-dddc-45d7-9a8a-13f3dd0a22fb.title: State Decomposition
2a65a013-dddc-45d7-9a8a-13f3dd0a22fb.definition: Learn to break down complex states into simpler representations or hypothesis spaces for more efficient searches.

fc5072c7-966e-4d1d-a522-35e8d9596c38.title: Graph Search Problem Solving
fc5072c7-966e-4d1d-a522-35e8d9596c38.definition: Study a problem-solving method by traversing a graph representing the state space to find the path from the initial state to the goal state.

05f7ddf4-180a-473e-b8e0-18ea02f7dff0.title: Graph as Search Space
05f7ddf4-180a-473e-b8e0-18ea02f7dff0.definition: understand how to represent the problem space as a graph, where vertices are states and edges are operators.

97c7d082-e1c3-4146-95f4-3a679340bff4.title: Tree Traversal Exploration
97c7d082-e1c3-4146-95f4-3a679340bff4.definition: Learn tree traversal techniques to explore the search space, considering it a subtree of a graph.

7614c813-1544-4146-965b-c7b2e1b19e41.title: Dynamic Graph Construction
7614c813-1544-4146-965b-c7b2e1b19e41.definition: Investigate how to build a state space graph dynamically during the search process, instead of having the entire graph from the beginning.

2b4c0d8f-6e51-4857-9dc4-78959a0c6891.title: Uninformed Graph Search
2b4c0d8f-6e51-4857-9dc4-78959a0c6891.definition: Overview of search algorithms that traverse the graph without using any additional information about the distance to the target (heuristics).

db896788-6174-49b2-88bf-a17fed97d425.title: Breadth-first Search (BFS)
db896788-6174-49b2-88bf-a17fed97d425.definition: Learn the BFS algorithm, traverse the graph by layer, ensuring to find the shortest path in the unweighted graph.

1ef8af2d-3781-49df-a46f-80c863411e02.title: Depth-first Search (DFS)
1ef8af2d-3781-49df-a46f-80c863411e02.definition: Learn the DFS algorithm, traversing the graph as deeply as possible before returning.

c8162339-9ea4-4f6f-acc0-891a3cac28e0.title: Iterative Deepening DFS (IDDFS)
c8162339-9ea4-4f6f-acc0-891a3cac28e0.definition: DFS variant research combines the benefits of BFS (optimality) with the benefits of DFS (memory efficiency).

3759e299-d1d1-4a99-b40b-51ef69cceec1.title: Uniform Cost Search (UCS)
3759e299-d1d1-4a99-b40b-51ef69cceec1.definition: Learn an optimal search algorithm for weighted graphs, always expanding the node with the smallest total path cost from the root.

e739d195-af29-45ce-958b-ad53bd2b792b.title: Heuristic Graph Search
e739d195-af29-45ce-958b-ad53bd2b792b.definition: Overview of search algorithms that use heuristic functions to estimate the distance to the target, helping to increase search efficiency.

c3129fcb-d801-467d-8c9c-c2276c652134.title: Heuristic Design & Admissibility
c3129fcb-d801-467d-8c9c-c2276c652134.definition: Learn how to design effective heuristic functions and understand the concept of heuristic feasibility to ensure algorithm optimization.

0f7a4431-73c1-467b-9a84-a49a81f8e3e4.title: Hill-climbing Algorithm
0f7a4431-73c1-467b-9a84-a49a81f8e3e4.definition: Study a simple local search algorithm that always moves to a better neighboring state, with the goal of reaching the peak (maximum).

2f07ca06-dc96-4e05-ab55-61a3b9170151.title: Local Minima & Search Landscape
2f07ca06-dc96-4e05-ab55-61a3b9170151.definition: understand the concept of local minima in search spaces and how they affect local search algorithms such as hill climbing.

34f700fe-e656-4db5-ba88-a44866bcbf78.title: Local vs Global Solutions
34f700fe-e656-4db5-ba88-a44866bcbf78.definition: Distinguish between solutions that are optimal only in a local region of the search space and solutions that are optimal over the entire space.

68a59a13-2cc9-439b-a41a-089f47e61597.title: Greedy Best-First Search
68a59a13-2cc9-439b-a41a-089f47e61597.definition: Learning search algorithms use heuristics to always expand the node believed to be closest to the target.

64fd3b12-6d4c-4b89-b7b9-7da52a7a99c4.title: A* Search
64fd3b12-6d4c-4b89-b7b9-7da52a7a99c4.definition: Research on widely used informative search algorithms, combining past path costs and heuristic estimation to find optimal paths.

91efa583-2fc0-4d44-a934-f19e1e85c272.title: Graph Search Space Complexity
91efa583-2fc0-4d44-a934-f19e1e85c272.definition: analyze the amount of memory that graph search algorithms require to operate, according to the number of vertices and edges.

1f6a1f96-e4c7-4806-8e30-24df28009419.title: Graph Search Time Complexity
1f6a1f96-e4c7-4806-8e30-24df28009419.definition: analyze the computational time required by graph search algorithms to find a solution, according to the number of vertices and edges.

6146f972-5e4d-47ae-8c1c-34d2ca1d9423.title: Bidirectional Search
6146f972-5e4d-47ae-8c1c-34d2ca1d9423.definition: Research algorithms that search simultaneously from the starting state and the goal state, hoping to meet in the middle to increase efficiency.

a0e807fe-a2ba-4eec-853e-010adfb4dfb7.title: Beam Search
a0e807fe-a2ba-4eec-853e-010adfb4dfb7.definition: Learn a variant of breadth-first search or best-first search, retaining only a limited number of nodes (beam width) at each level to reduce memory overhead.

db0e5c19-6004-4498-b1ef-69a582cb40d6.title: Two-Player Games
db0e5c19-6004-4498-b1ef-69a582cb40d6.definition: Research theories and algorithms for solving games involving two players with opposing goals.

b5456f30-5143-47f0-b16e-4ca2dcd35ff7.title: Minimax Search
b5456f30-5143-47f0-b16e-4ca2dcd35ff7.definition: Learning search algorithms are used in game theory to find the optimal move for a player assuming that the opponent also plays optimally.

ea1d502d-4376-495e-a981-f87d24176853.title: Alpha-beta Pruning
ea1d502d-4376-495e-a981-f87d24176853.definition: Research optimization techniques for the Minimax algorithm, helping to remove unnecessary branches in the search tree without affecting the final result.

64514c55-6fb3-4201-8971-76653e4fb97e.title: Ply Cutoff
64514c55-6fb3-4201-8971-76653e4fb97e.definition: understand the concept of limiting the depth of a search tree in Minimax and Alpha-beta pruning algorithms to manage computational resources.

825ecd3e-a822-48e5-afeb-f02bc2be90df.title: A* Implementation
825ecd3e-a822-48e5-afeb-f02bc2be90df.definition: Programming skills to implement the A* search algorithm in real-world problems, including the management of priority queues and related data structures.

7e85f421-71f1-4d95-93c1-d0fe61636f02.title: Constraint Satisfaction (CSP)
7e85f421-71f1-4d95-93c1-d0fe61636f02.definition: Study of constraint satisfaction problems (CSP), where the goal is to find a set of values ​​for variables such that all constraints are satisfied.

5a9a8268-71ba-40d4-a253-a5495676bf68.title: Search Space
5a9a8268-71ba-40d4-a253-a5495676bf68.definition: In-depth study of the structure and characteristics of the search space, including how it affects the effectiveness of algorithms.

e12f5329-6ca5-4aab-bbbc-434cd77d9b5c.title: Search Tree Construction
e12f5329-6ca5-4aab-bbbc-434cd77d9b5c.definition: Learn the techniques and challenges of building search trees to represent state space efficiently.

cfb274e7-eb59-493c-90af-800aa6cd60bf.title: Dynamic Search Space
cfb274e7-eb59-493c-90af-800aa6cd60bf.definition: The study of search spaces that change during problem solving, requires adaptive algorithms.

2e7878c6-d1d7-41cd-9ceb-f8a4aa03dc53.title: Combinatorial Explosion
2e7878c6-d1d7-41cd-9ceb-f8a4aa03dc53.definition: understand the problem where the size of the search space increases exponentially with the number of variables or choices, making it difficult to solve.

ccbfaf94-b952-49b9-8845-6a83d07ab38f.title: Search Space Topology
ccbfaf94-b952-49b9-8845-6a83d07ab38f.definition: Study the shape and characteristics of the search space 'landscape', including local minima, peaks, saddles, etc., and their impact on search.

99e460d6-9427-4abb-900a-e2993b235891.title: Local Search
99e460d6-9427-4abb-900a-e2993b235891.definition: Study of search algorithms that start from one solution and continuously move to better neighboring solutions, often used for optimization problems.

e8d6807d-198a-4839-8b5b-c8f36e1290ea.title: Tabu Search
e8d6807d-198a-4839-8b5b-c8f36e1290ea.definition: Learn a metaheuristic local search algorithm that uses memory (tabu lists) to avoid repeating explored solutions and escape local minima.

5d447f5e-db79-46e9-a717-4cd6b9e7111b.title: A* Variants
5d447f5e-db79-46e9-a717-4cd6b9e7111b.definition: Research advanced versions of the A* algorithm such as IDA*, SMA*, and RBFS that are designed to address memory or time constraints.

4eeeda30-6551-4ef5-9b9b-8d97c20c28e2.title: IDA* Search
4eeeda30-6551-4ef5-9b9b-8d97c20c28e2.definition: Informed Iterative Depth First Search, a variant of A* that minimizes memory requirements.

0255f02a-4b63-4bb2-93fe-c7ba424736fa.title: SMA* Search
0255f02a-4b63-4bb2-93fe-c7ba424736fa.definition: A* search simplifies memory, a variant of A* that can handle larger search spaces by eliminating the least promising nodes when memory runs out.

f9c1c476-82ee-4c32-a208-a6003a1963af.title: RBFS Search
f9c1c476-82ee-4c32-a208-a6003a1963af.definition: Recursive first-best search, a memory-friendly variant of A* uses recursion to perform a heuristic deepening search.

25ab1d61-fd83-42a3-b442-eb6a3b19fb37.title: Horizon Effect
25ab1d61-fd83-42a3-b442-eb6a3b19fb37.definition: Study the horizon effect in games, where the Minimax algorithm can ignore bad results that are outside the specified search depth.

bebce509-9bfe-46a3-bbee-c20e5558bf1b.title: Opening/Endgame Books
bebce509-9bfe-46a3-bbee-c20e5558bf1b.definition: Learn about using pre-planned strategies for the opening and late game stages of fighting games to improve AI performance.

4ff57bdc-1422-4470-9861-98e863e344be.title: Game Solved Meaning
4ff57bdc-1422-4470-9861-98e863e344be.definition: analyze what it means to find a perfect optimal strategy for a game (e.g., checkers), that guarantees never losing if the opponent makes no mistakes.

ca920580-6b68-4157-a083-b8a902bb820e.title: Minimax Implementation
ca920580-6b68-4157-a083-b8a902bb820e.definition: Programming skills to implement the Minimax search algorithm in fighting game applications.

2bd692b6-bc1b-405f-8bbc-732c1898f5e5.title: Beam Search Implementation
2bd692b6-bc1b-405f-8bbc-732c1898f5e5.definition: Programming skills to implement the Beam search algorithm in search problems that require memory efficiency.

4747b0e5-3369-4a3b-82b0-637c900684f3.title: Expectimax Search
4747b0e5-3369-4a3b-82b0-637c900684f3.definition: Research search algorithms used in games with random elements (chance nodes) or in the process of solving Markov decision making problems (MDP), combining optimization and expectations.

b05ba828-7e9c-4f01-b875-a4d3c56536fd.title: Stochastic Search
b05ba828-7e9c-4f01-b875-a4d3c56536fd.definition: Overview of search methods that use random elements to explore the solution space, especially useful for complex optimization problems.

3e8e3bcc-7d53-4a00-9ce8-dde1a05fe97f.title: Simulated Annealing
3e8e3bcc-7d53-4a00-9ce8-dde1a05fe97f.definition: Learn a metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by metallurgy, capable of escaping local minima.

72a2c75c-0335-409c-98aa-aa33d43edc13.title: Genetic Algorithms
72a2c75c-0335-409c-98aa-aa33d43edc13.definition: Study of a class of optimization algorithms inspired by natural selection and genetics, used to find approximate solutions to complex problems.

aeaf1c9d-da76-436f-ab33-d9a2982949ff.title: Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)
aeaf1c9d-da76-436f-ab33-d9a2982949ff.definition: Learn a heuristic search algorithm to make decisions in complex problems, especially in games, by randomly sampling from the search space.

8957697e-7c2b-4e84-b296-17161e4984ae.title: A*/Beam Search Design
8957697e-7c2b-4e84-b296-17161e4984ae.definition: Ability to design and implement A* search or beam search algorithms to solve a specific problem.

1752ead8-3648-4d39-8a0a-86187c61d500.title: A*/Beam vs. Other Searches
1752ead8-3648-4d39-8a0a-86187c61d500.definition: Compare the performance of the A* or beam search algorithm with other search algorithms based on solution cost, number of nodes expanded, and other criteria.

2bb570ac-25d0-415f-9ff5-a9f3bda6c9db.title: Minimax Search
2bb570ac-25d0-415f-9ff5-a9f3bda6c9db.definition: understand and apply the Minimax search algorithm to solve two-player fighting games.

3a66c0e3-e75a-42ef-98ad-703fe1d887b1.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning
3a66c0e3-e75a-42ef-98ad-703fe1d887b1.definition: apply alpha-beta pruning to reduce the search space in two-player fighting games (e.g., Connect Four).

9c83a883-7c21-4eaf-861a-1a329e3a4cf5.title: Genetic Algorithms
9c83a883-7c21-4eaf-861a-1a329e3a4cf5.definition: understand the concept and working mechanism of genetic algorithms.

061918c5-8e0b-4b86-bb00-9a7e30b95c76.title: GA vs. Other Optimizers
061918c5-8e0b-4b86-bb00-9a7e30b95c76.definition: Compare and contrast genetic algorithms with classical search techniques, explaining when to use genetic algorithms to learn a model versus other forms of optimization (e.g., gradient descent).

a5c244fe-41cc-445d-9a94-78e6489b0d1d.title: Heuristic Search Types
a5c244fe-41cc-445d-9a94-78e6489b0d1d.definition: understand and differentiate between different heuristic search techniques.

483ac21f-9486-459a-871e-882f7f1ef679.title: Heuristic Search Applicability
483ac21f-9486-459a-871e-882f7f1ef679.definition: Compare and contrast the applicability of different heuristic search techniques to a specific problem.

74f4f9b0-1845-4aa7-bbc2-11d03884e4ba.title: CSP Modeling
74f4f9b0-1845-4aa7-bbc2-11d03884e4ba.definition: Ability to model logic or Sudoku problems into a constraint satisfaction problem.

4aa9a26e-1c45-44d6-88f2-061fe9cca954.title: Backtrack Search for CSP
4aa9a26e-1c45-44d6-88f2-061fe9cca954.definition: apply backtracking search to solve constraint satisfaction problems.

77b4f095-789e-46b9-afad-666e3afb4a3e.title: Arc Consistency
77b4f095-789e-46b9-afad-666e3afb4a3e.definition: Determine the extent to which arc consistency can reduce the search space in the constraint satisfaction problem.

2880787c-d8e6-43f0-b082-ceb65e72ea3c.title: Knowledge Representation Types
2880787c-d8e6-43f0-b082-ceb65e72ea3c.definition: understand different types of knowledge representation in AI.

c34b82fc-ddd2-4dba-8dc9-76c1f28a9a13.title: Symbolic/Logic KR
c34b82fc-ddd2-4dba-8dc9-76c1f28a9a13.definition: Master the concept of symbolic and logical knowledge representation.

a8e5e610-c260-4185-a42b-aff2cf46e8a0.title: NLP to KR
a8e5e610-c260-4185-a42b-aff2cf46e8a0.definition: The ability to create a symbolic or logical representation from a problem statement in natural language.

13f3e84f-88f3-4f90-b04a-cbc5536f61e0.title: Graphical Models
13f3e84f-88f3-4f90-b04a-cbc5536f61e0.definition: Introduction to graphical models such as Naive Bayes and Bayesian networks for knowledge representation and inference.

91be289b-507e-43f1-9390-65b325710216.title: Probabilistic Inference Overview
91be289b-507e-43f1-9390-65b325710216.definition: Overview of the fundamentals of probabilistic inference.

b7076b81-68bf-426a-8a87-304360c8fd3e.title: Bayes' Theorem
b7076b81-68bf-426a-8a87-304360c8fd3e.definition: Master Bayes' Theorem and its significance in probabilistic inference.

8fa45e95-1b53-42eb-84ff-b735ba34f915.title: Bayesian Inference
8fa45e95-1b53-42eb-84ff-b735ba34f915.definition: understand the fundamentals of Bayesian inference and how it works.

a12c5e05-3241-493a-867f-22f896bc56db.title: Random Variables & Distributions
a12c5e05-3241-493a-867f-22f896bc56db.definition: understand random variables and types of probability distributions.

3fb50223-eb09-437e-8fc1-525857876494.title: Axioms of Probability
3fb50223-eb09-437e-8fc1-525857876494.definition: Master the basic axioms of probability.

8a202853-d782-4ac5-994a-ad4e3e2d4399.title: Probabilistic Inference
8a202853-d782-4ac5-994a-ad4e3e2d4399.definition: Ability to perform probabilistic inference to draw conclusions based on data and models.

4062f2df-494a-4e31-989f-4e965ab2e3b2.definition: apply Bayesian inference to more complex examples and problems.

7421152e-2f7b-4030-98d2-28eac8eb76b7.title: Probabilistic Independence
7421152e-2f7b-4030-98d2-28eac8eb76b7.definition: understand the concept of independence of random variables in probability.

4287eb6c-6628-4f43-8b0d-323f5c6fca26.title: Conditional Independence
4287eb6c-6628-4f43-8b0d-323f5c6fca26.definition: understand the concept of conditional independence of random variables.

05fdc832-c113-4888-b0bf-bbbd049b4edc.definition: Introduction to Markov chains and their basic properties.

b1623ff0-f044-427d-b7e0-96aa82cfa16e.definition: An introduction to Markov models, including basic applications.

ad0165ca-febe-4dc2-bdf7-3b98405f3596.definition: understand the concept of value and how to make decisions under conditions of uncertainty.

c552edf1-17a0-4371-a0b6-d3755bb7dbe6.definition: understand definitions and diverse examples of machine learning tasks.

c5f264aa-3899-40f7-8726-986d0e4cbec1.title: Supervised Learning
c5f264aa-3899-40f7-8726-986d0e4cbec1.definition: Master the concept of supervised learning.

1feb1da5-ec5c-4bf6-8514-7d45ee31cf74.title: Classification
1feb1da5-ec5c-4bf6-8514-7d45ee31cf74.definition: Understanding the classification problem in supervised learning.

24834b13-b800-41b8-a0e0-0407671285c8.definition: Understanding the regression problem in supervised learning.

ac7ea336-8d1a-4a36-8728-ae36a5729e6e.title: Reinforcement Learning
ac7ea336-8d1a-4a36-8728-ae36a5729e6e.definition: Master the concept of reinforcement learning.

fd454382-0744-4c2c-b7c8-dd543d21bc3b.title: Unsupervised Learning
fd454382-0744-4c2c-b7c8-dd543d21bc3b.definition: Master the concept of unsupervised learning.

be076f69-5df4-464b-ac28-e3a87c095b1c.title: Clustering
be076f69-5df4-464b-ac28-e3a87c095b1c.definition: Understanding the clustering problem in unsupervised learning.

0e470897-8689-40b8-a232-c079176886ac.title: No Free Lunch Theorem
0e470897-8689-40b8-a232-c079176886ac.definition: understand the 'There is no free lunch' theorem and its implications in machine learning.

687a7da4-1cc6-4b7c-b0f6-a0b8386ae98a.title: ML Error Sources
687a7da4-1cc6-4b7c-b0f6-a0b8386ae98a.definition: understand sources of error and undecidability limits in machine learning systems.

a853baa8-1e47-49e3-9fca-caa970334232.title: Simple Statistical Supervised Learning
a853baa8-1e47-49e3-9fca-caa970334232.definition: Understanding how statistical supervised learning models work is simple enough to properly use existing implementations.

c6ea1ebb-8b1f-40c8-b840-c35b603f6d24.title: Linear Regression
c6ea1ebb-8b1f-40c8-b840-c35b603f6d24.definition: Master the fundamentals of linear regression as an example of supervised learning.

bb9924bb-87fa-4908-b4e2-819547c716c0.title: Decision Trees
bb9924bb-87fa-4908-b4e2-819547c716c0.definition: Master the fundamentals of decision trees as an example of supervised learning.

48e2486c-8fc4-4b97-ad4f-10722891e0b6.title: Overfitting
48e2486c-8fc4-4b97-ad4f-10722891e0b6.definition: Understanding the overfitting problem in machine learning.

de90d306-5c09-402c-a7e5-d5abf6804dfc.title: Controlling Model Complexity
de90d306-5c09-402c-a7e5-d5abf6804dfc.definition: Intuitively understand methods for controlling solution complexity such as regularization and pruning.

d439e653-f6a3-49cc-865c-d6158debf1c3.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
d439e653-f6a3-49cc-865c-d6158debf1c3.definition: understand the trade-off between bias (underfitting) and variance (overfitting) in machine learning.

96020a99-5330-4017-bcb4-a2274e1bf41e.title: Data Preprocessing
96020a99-5330-4017-bcb4-a2274e1bf41e.definition: understand the importance and pitfalls of data preprocessing choices.

cbb41a54-0fe9-42d5-a902-52f27ce072f1.title: Missing Value Handling
cbb41a54-0fe9-42d5-a902-52f27ce072f1.definition: Missing value handling techniques such as imputing or marking as missing, along with their consequences.

eb53cd55-0356-4926-8898-fb35d9042e33.title: Feature Encoding
eb53cd55-0356-4926-8898-fb35d9042e33.definition: Methods for encoding categorical variables and real-valued data for machine learning models.

d80394ab-fd93-48d8-a1d5-86f901d110f0.title: Data Normalization/Standardization
d80394ab-fd93-48d8-a1d5-86f901d110f0.definition: understand data normalization and standardization techniques.

091b1205-457b-43d2-af61-07f5ac27304f.title: Real-world Data ML
091b1205-457b-43d2-af61-07f5ac27304f.definition: The importance of using real data instead of textbook examples in machine learning.

9399ceb0-3262-4c68-ba78-e032ea218edc.title: Hypothesis Space & Complexity
9399ceb0-3262-4c68-ba78-e032ea218edc.definition: Understanding hypothesis spaces and their complexity in machine learning.

652d1239-f0d4-4294-a7c8-575363787eef.title: Simple Feature Expansion
652d1239-f0d4-4294-a7c8-575363787eef.definition: Basic feature expansion techniques are simple, such as squaring univariate features.

60f8246a-25e7-4d34-8577-47cfd59c4b38.title: Learned Feature Representations
60f8246a-25e7-4d34-8577-47cfd59c4b38.definition: Understanding feature representations learned through machine learning models.

94a000db-8a3b-4a27-a064-9dccc8bd59c7.title: ML Model Evaluation
94a000db-8a3b-4a27-a064-9dccc8bd59c7.definition: understand the fundamentals of machine learning model evaluation.

3f140527-c538-42eb-b6c5-82b9964bfd98.title: Train-Validation-Test Split
3f140527-c538-42eb-b6c5-82b9964bfd98.definition: understand the importance of dividing data into training, validation, and test sets.

f60a277a-5525-403e-aee6-211291c21882.title: Classification Metrics
f60a277a-5525-403e-aee6-211291c21882.definition: Common performance metrics for evaluating classification models (e.g. accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score).

42e19b4e-96be-49ed-873b-66b7c6b95279.title: Held-out Data Performance
42e19b4e-96be-49ed-873b-66b7c6b95279.definition: Method for estimating model performance on held-out data.

1a7f5927-deeb-4010-b5e9-4f3b516efac1.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
1a7f5927-deeb-4010-b5e9-4f3b516efac1.definition: Use a test set to fine-tune the parameters of a machine learning model.

149acdd3-460f-4276-a709-7f3e1aa316d6.title: Model Understanding & Limitations
149acdd3-460f-4276-a709-7f3e1aa316d6.definition: Master how a model works, its limitations and pitfalls, and the implications of the decisions the model makes.

6885ecca-1202-4d35-982d-9460ceb4f897.title: Basic Neural Networks
6885ecca-1202-4d35-982d-9460ceb4f897.definition: The fundamentals of how neural networks work and their training, without going into computational detail.

4f0731b6-6832-499f-9e9a-3b5ac2a0d859.title: Basic Generative Neural Networks
4f0731b6-6832-499f-9e9a-3b5ac2a0d859.definition: A basic introduction to generative neural networks, including large language models (LLMs).

ec04bacb-a030-45f5-bd65-00dd13e74dec.title: ML Ethics
ec04bacb-a030-45f5-bd65-00dd13e74dec.definition: Ethical issues related to machine learning, focusing on real data, real scenarios, and case studies.

776eff14-6e9b-42c4-8faf-e853a8186c05.title: Bias & Unintended Consequences
776eff14-6e9b-42c4-8faf-e853a8186c05.definition: understand bias in data sets, algorithms, evaluations, and their unintended consequences in machine learning.

6551eb83-096c-4b3a-9d50-b53a3f633b6d.title: ML as Optimization
6551eb83-096c-4b3a-9d50-b53a3f633b6d.definition: Describe how basic machine learning problems, such as linear regression or logistic regression, are defined and solved in terms of optimizing an objective function.

9c7af2df-de9d-4043-8b1e-c042412a3e23.title: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS)
9c7af2df-de9d-4043-8b1e-c042412a3e23.definition: A linear regression method optimizes by minimizing the sum of squares of residuals between predicted and actual values.

7b1ea492-6b05-4eb9-884f-11d103ad5a39.title: Logistic Regression
7b1ea492-6b05-4eb9-884f-11d103ad5a39.definition: A classification algorithm uses the sigmoid function to model the probability of a class, often used for binary classification problems.

f62da636-dedf-474c-802b-d3514f0cc71e.title: Objective Function
f62da636-dedf-474c-802b-d3514f0cc71e.definition: Function that an optimization algorithm seeks to minimize (cost/loss function) or maximize (profit function) to achieve the machine learning goal.

e300ad19-8fd3-4e19-b09c-3e963a378113.title: Gradient Descent
e300ad19-8fd3-4e19-b09c-3e963a378113.definition: An iterative optimization algorithm that finds the local minimum (or maximum) of a function by moving against the function's gradient.

aa471d1e-5039-4c33-8215-cd5cd3e3de36.title: Regularization for Overfitting
aa471d1e-5039-4c33-8215-cd5cd3e3de36.definition: Techniques that add constraints or penalties to the model to reduce complexity, help the model generalize better on new data, and avoid overfitting to the training data.

676f196f-ef66-4ee4-9568-3f9d0db3409f.title: Regularization Formulas
676f196f-ef66-4ee4-9568-3f9d0db3409f.definition: The mathematical representation of the normalization terms (e.g., L1, L2) is added to the objective function to control the complexity of the model.

5d4b2c94-1637-46fc-90b2-ef5ca393cd0d.title: Ensemble Learning
5d4b2c94-1637-46fc-90b2-ef5ca393cd0d.definition: The technique combines multiple machine learning models to create a more powerful model, often delivering better overall performance than a single model.

bce2e0db-a547-458a-a71c-40bcac11457e.title: Weighted Majority Vote Ensemble
bce2e0db-a547-458a-a71c-40bcac11457e.definition: A method of combining output from component models in an ensemble by assigning weights to each model and taking a weighted majority decision.

457a1271-3363-4f5f-a78e-ef4b578035e1.title: Deep Learning
457a1271-3363-4f5f-a78e-ef4b578035e1.definition: A branch of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with many layers (deep networks) to learn representations of data at different levels of abstraction.

450733a7-fd02-4b2e-9a03-4a3fdbca6338.title: Deep Feedforward Networks (Intuitive)
450733a7-fd02-4b2e-9a03-4a3fdbca6338.definition: understand the structure and basic operation of multi-layer feedforward neural networks, in which information only moves in one direction from the input layer to the output layer, without going into deep mathematical formulas.

9c4ad7e2-a2af-40f1-a0bf-fb31ab3b5dc0.title: CNN Intuition
9c4ad7e2-a2af-40f1-a0bf-fb31ab3b5dc0.definition: Understanding the basic structure and operation of CNNs, especially in image processing, which uses convolutional layers to automatically learn spatial features, without going into deep mathematical formulas.

51e6c0bf-876b-42f0-bd0d-af38d35b02bf.title: Feature Visualization
51e6c0bf-876b-42f0-bd0d-af38d35b02bf.definition: Techniques to visualize and understand what the layers of a deep neural network are learning or detecting in the input data, helping to explain the model.

f0c4fcef-f5b9-42ca-a573-1792d0c22c89.title: Deep Architectures
f0c4fcef-f5b9-42ca-a573-1792d0c22c89.definition: Overview of other types of neural network architectures beyond feedforward and convolutional networks, designed for specific types of data and tasks.

49fa7f7d-daa2-423e-b76b-a24550eb6832.title: Generative Neural Networks
49fa7f7d-daa2-423e-b76b-a24550eb6832.definition: A type of neural network that is capable of generating new data (e.g., images, text) that is similar to the training data it learned from.

4d8f419e-2a7e-427b-865e-ece702cd2e6d.title: Recurrent Neural Networks
4d8f419e-2a7e-427b-865e-ece702cd2e6d.definition: Neural networks are specifically designed to process sequential data (e.g. time series, text), capable of maintaining an internal 'memory' state.

12c14ba8-5e9f-4cf8-a3e0-37415387359c.title: Transformer Model
12c14ba8-5e9f-4cf8-a3e0-37415387359c.definition: A groundbreaking neural network architecture that uses attention mechanisms, which are especially effective in natural language processing and other sequential tasks.

8c8aec20-82a6-423e-944c-598305a592a0.title: Model Evaluation
8c8aec20-82a6-423e-944c-598305a592a0.definition: Methods and metrics are used to measure how well a machine learning model performs its task on unseen data.

6374411d-f436-4285-ab60-b089c824142a.title: Classification Metrics
6374411d-f436-4285-ab60-b089c824142a.definition: Metrics used to evaluate the performance of classification models, including error rate, accuracy, coverage, F1-score, etc.

40cab761-0bdd-4c94-9443-48a4796f6cbf.title: Error Rate
40cab761-0bdd-4c94-9443-48a4796f6cbf.definition: The proportion of false predictions (including false positives and false negatives) in the total number of predictions of a classification problem.

669276fa-0268-4450-934a-bd701c3c8822.title: Precision
669276fa-0268-4450-934a-bd701c3c8822.definition: The proportion of true positives among all cases predicted to be positive.

b73c0195-6f61-4773-bfff-210a0dbd668e.title: Recall
b73c0195-6f61-4773-bfff-210a0dbd668e.definition: Proportion of true positives among all true positives.

2be73da2-de76-4ecf-ab3c-c36a83f1e22f.title: Regression Metrics
2be73da2-de76-4ecf-ab3c-c36a83f1e22f.definition: Metrics used to evaluate the performance of regression models, such as mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), R-squared, etc.

4bb7925d-2d58-4819-b540-55996b780e23.title: Confusion Matrix
4bb7925d-2d58-4819-b540-55996b780e23.definition: A table summarizing the performance of a classification algorithm, showing the number of correct and incorrect predictions for each class.

17111def-4471-4c92-8be1-dd13a9f48009.title: Cross-validation
17111def-4471-4c92-8be1-dd13a9f48009.definition: A technique to more reliably evaluate model performance and minimize overfitting by dividing the data into multiple subsets for iterative training and testing.

94d67e20-6a29-4cc7-a8f1-cbad2ce097fa.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
94d67e20-6a29-4cc7-a8f1-cbad2ce097fa.definition: The process of finding optimal values ​​for the hyperparameters of a machine learning model to achieve the best performance.

00b88b0c-8cba-4965-91ac-178ff960057a.title: Grid Search
00b88b0c-8cba-4965-91ac-178ff960057a.definition: A method of fine-tuning hyper-parameters by trying all possible combinations of parameter values ​​in a predetermined grid.

e39ffd05-deb2-4b5b-b7f8-a633872db30b.title: Random Search
e39ffd05-deb2-4b5b-b7f8-a633872db30b.definition: A method for fine-tuning hyper-parameters by randomly sampling parameter combinations from a defined space.

33d12147-46a8-47df-a318-5e926ed6db19.title: Reinforcement Learning
33d12147-46a8-47df-a318-5e926ed6db19.definition: Introduces the basic principles and algorithms of reinforcement learning, where an agent learns to perform actions in an environment to maximize cumulative rewards.

14b4eb28-fd14-4438-b402-d432fedae874.title: ML Applications
14b4eb28-fd14-4438-b402-d432fedae874.definition: Practical domains and problems that machine learning algorithms can be applied to solve.

5e9e8f37-6800-4241-b1a5-67c8fcd96ca2.title: ML in Healthcare
5e9e8f37-6800-4241-b1a5-67c8fcd96ca2.definition: Examples include the use of machine learning for disease diagnosis, drug development, medical image analysis, and treatment personalization.

74d017da-7401-4833-8ff1-7618772a0c57.title: ML in Economics
74d017da-7401-4833-8ff1-7618772a0c57.definition: Examples of using machine learning are for market forecasting, consumer behavior analysis, and financial optimization.

2bb807aa-d671-4c9d-9c0b-ab3f92433bb6.title: ML in Computer Vision
2bb807aa-d671-4c9d-9c0b-ab3f92433bb6.definition: Examples of the use of machine learning in computer vision, such as object recognition, face detection, and image analysis.

98f6203d-0c9b-4bf0-bbfd-08a5748617f3.title: ML in NLP
98f6203d-0c9b-4bf0-bbfd-08a5748617f3.definition: Examples of the use of machine learning in natural language processing (NLP), such as machine translation, sentiment analysis, and text generation.

7d1cc08e-5ec5-44d2-94d2-d549903c68a2.title: ML in Robotics
7d1cc08e-5ec5-44d2-94d2-d549903c68a2.definition: Examples of using machine learning are for robot control, environmental perception, and motion planning.

cd30ed37-a6b6-4440-9884-7ef68162a5fb.title: ML in Gaming
cd30ed37-a6b6-4440-9884-7ef68162a5fb.definition: Examples of using machine learning are to develop gaming AI, create intelligent opponents, and optimize playing strategies.

1f16a617-a900-4af6-ad53-7714f0a13d95.title: ML Ethics
1f16a617-a900-4af6-ad53-7714f0a13d95.definition: Ethical issues related to the design, implementation, and use of machine learning systems, including privacy, fairness, accountability, and transparency.

df2fff58-e5ba-4923-875d-9098281f4307.title: ML Ethics: Real Scenarios
df2fff58-e5ba-4923-875d-9098281f4307.definition: Emphasizes the importance of considering the ethical implications of machine learning in real-life situations and with real data.

15e96ed7-f750-443a-ab89-a9b9a4cc3525.title: ML Ethics Case Studies
15e96ed7-f750-443a-ab89-a9b9a4cc3525.definition: analyze specific cases where ethical issues in machine learning have arisen and how they were or could be resolved.

417cd8f8-e0b6-4661-9e18-abd6ade19412.title: ML Privacy
417cd8f8-e0b6-4661-9e18-abd6ade19412.definition: Challenges and solutions related to protecting personal information when using data to train and deploy machine learning models.

5762f636-8dbd-4c1d-8d73-83b40bd9ad3b.title: ML Fairness
5762f636-8dbd-4c1d-8d73-83b40bd9ad3b.definition: Ensure that machine learning models do not create or perpetuate biased results that discriminate against specific groups of people.

f4a8f97f-b663-42c8-9fc2-8f0d0273545a.title: ML Intellectual Property
f4a8f97f-b663-42c8-9fc2-8f0d0273545a.definition: Legal and ethical issues related to ownership of data, models, algorithms, and other intellectual products in the field of machine learning.

4764eb63-8aa3-4c01-ae92-782519ba7135.title: Explainable AI (XAI)
4764eb63-8aa3-4c01-ae92-782519ba7135.definition: The ability to understand how a machine learning model makes decisions, or predictions, is especially important for 'black box' systems.

e3a97c1b-6575-42ff-afbf-c78088adb9eb.title: Statistical Learning
e3a97c1b-6575-42ff-afbf-c78088adb9eb.definition: Machine learning methods are grounded in statistical theory, using statistical models and principles to analyze data and make predictions.

275c9dea-11c3-47b5-9ef3-ae879448f7e5.title: Parameter Estimation
275c9dea-11c3-47b5-9ef3-ae879448f7e5.definition: The process of using sample data to estimate the unknown parameters of a probability distribution or statistical model.

b269b5f5-9144-4b6e-96f1-b22d63480958.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
b269b5f5-9144-4b6e-96f1-b22d63480958.definition: A method of parameter estimation by finding parameter values ​​that maximize the probability of observing the given data.

9cc60205-fec4-43f9-b67d-cb2f1f2fddf7.title: Supervised Learning
9cc60205-fec4-43f9-b67d-cb2f1f2fddf7.definition: A type of machine learning in which an algorithm is trained on a labeled data set, learning to map inputs to desired outputs.

0bb7bc2b-9cc1-4519-83a3-964495547ca0.title: Decision Tree
0bb7bc2b-9cc1-4519-83a3-964495547ca0.definition: A nonparametric prediction model uses a decision tree structure in which each internal node represents an attribute, each branch represents an attribute value, and each leaf node represents a class or value.

29b98e7b-6ec7-4812-b106-22ce839ee35a.title: Nearest Neighbor Classification
29b98e7b-6ec7-4812-b106-22ce839ee35a.definition: A non-parametric classification algorithm assigns a new data point to the class of the closest data point(s) in the training set.

2ab858d3-2d1d-4ff7-991e-effefc346b54.title: Nearest Neighbor Regression
2ab858d3-2d1d-4ff7-991e-effefc346b54.definition: A non-parametric regression algorithm uses the values ​​of the closest data points in the training set to predict the value for a new data point.

73021ab4-9aab-4ca4-9c5c-372f9fbfc099.title: Simple Neural Networks
73021ab4-9aab-4ca4-9c5c-372f9fbfc099.definition: Neural network models, with few layers and basic structure, are often used as an introductory step before learning more complex architectures.

12440083-baf0-4e69-8714-e5fcb4715dcc.title: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
12440083-baf0-4e69-8714-e5fcb4715dcc.definition: A type of feedforward neural network consisting of at least three layers of nodes (input layer, one or more hidden layers, and output layer), capable of learning nonlinear relationships.

33319503-7a36-47c7-b6be-7ca5b1cca49a.title: Linear Regression
33319503-7a36-47c7-b6be-7ca5b1cca49a.definition: A linear model predicts a continuous target variable from one or more independent variables by finding the best linear relationship.

6d4851c6-6e53-46bf-9b9c-277308fcf022.title: Logistic Regression
6d4851c6-6e53-46bf-9b9c-277308fcf022.definition: A statistical model is used to model the probability of a binary target variable (2-class classification) using a logistic function.

cdee7aca-3a3e-4d0d-b0d8-9d4033f3ccd8.title: Support Vector Machines (SVM)
cdee7aca-3a3e-4d0d-b0d8-9d4033f3ccd8.definition: A supervised learning algorithm is used for both classification and regression, which works by finding the best dividing hyperplane between data classes.

b2090ec8-6d33-4cb8-879a-aa243b8ec31a.title: Kernel Functions (SVM)
b2090ec8-6d33-4cb8-879a-aa243b8ec31a.definition: Functions are used in SVM to transform data into a higher dimensional space, allowing the search for nonlinear separating hyperplanes.

c600822b-b200-4091-b598-a33b03d5de57.title: Gaussian Processes
c600822b-b200-4091-b598-a33b03d5de57.definition: A non-parametric machine learning method based on multivariate Gaussian distribution, used for regression and classification problems.

06246620-9b31-45a0-9667-396185534787.title: Overfitting
06246620-9b31-45a0-9667-396185534787.definition: The phenomenon of a model overlearning the training data, including noise, leads to poor performance when faced with new, never-before-seen data.

7b92cbce-f9f9-49d0-ba75-d2148863444c.title: Curse of Dimensionality
7b92cbce-f9f9-49d0-ba75-d2148863444c.definition: Problems arise when analyzing and organizing data in high-dimensional space, as data becomes more sparse and algorithms become less efficient.

10fc581a-37a5-4c02-b590-d5ca65b0e06d.title: Regularization (Math)
10fc581a-37a5-4c02-b590-d5ca65b0e06d.definition: Deep dive into the mathematical formulas and calculations of normalization techniques, including L1 and L2, to control model complexity.

7d54dd1d-f37c-468a-b718-957e616f6112.title: L2 Regularization
7d54dd1d-f37c-468a-b718-957e616f6112.definition: A form of normalization that adds the square of the weight magnitude to the objective function (also called Ridge Regression or weight decay), which helps reduce large weights and avoid overfitting.

b9bedc24-26ab-4348-8dc4-2384e9c0a9c6.title: L1 Normalization
b9bedc24-26ab-4348-8dc4-2384e9c0a9c6.definition: A form of normalization that adds the absolute value of the weights to the objective function (also called Lasso Regression), which tends to bring some weights to zero, helping with feature selection.

dda56f74-4f03-483b-b956-bacb3ad1a62c.title: Experiment Design
dda56f74-4f03-483b-b956-bacb3ad1a62c.definition: create a systematic plan for performing machine learning experiments, including how to collect, prepare data, and evaluate models to ensure reliable results.

f1c19337-6f64-4189-9db4-e0539804e9d2.title: Data Preparation
f1c19337-6f64-4189-9db4-e0539804e9d2.definition: Steps to process raw data to make it suitable and efficient for a machine learning model, including cleaning, transforming, and encoding the data.

5bc431eb-53eb-48d2-9973-b7f30f349848.title: Data Standardization
5bc431eb-53eb-48d2-9973-b7f30f349848.definition: Adjusting data values ​​so they have a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1, helps machine learning algorithms work more effectively.

88dbe56b-6845-4f7f-bbf2-1af78f77b08d.title: Data Representation
88dbe56b-6845-4f7f-bbf2-1af78f77b08d.definition: How the data is encoded or structured so that it can be used effectively by machine learning algorithms, e.g., feature vector format.

d7098882-683a-42b2-b454-e9ba36cb8c6e.title: One-hot Encoding
d7098882-683a-42b2-b454-e9ba36cb8c6e.definition: The technique converts categorical variables into a numeric format (binary vector) that can be used by a machine learning model, avoiding erroneous ordering of categories.

134627aa-4df4-46d3-b1e8-fe09fcdee5a9.title: Hypothesis Space
134627aa-4df4-46d3-b1e8-fe09fcdee5a9.definition: The set of all functions or models that a machine learning algorithm can choose from to solve a particular problem.

5f9c82de-85b0-4182-a514-c17d29d09cee.title: Bias (ML)
5f9c82de-85b0-4182-a514-c17d29d09cee.definition: Systematic errors or biases in data, algorithms, or machine learning decision-making processes, can lead to inaccurate or unfair results.

4d98e011-a7ee-44aa-bbca-037e39b1f23b.title: Algorithmic Bias
4d98e011-a7ee-44aa-bbca-037e39b1f23b.definition: Systematic bias in an algorithm, often due to biased training data or algorithm design, leads to unfair or inaccurate results for specific groups.

39c9fcb4-7131-4a1c-a4ac-fe084fde9aa4.title: Search Bias
39c9fcb4-7131-4a1c-a4ac-fe084fde9aa4.definition: Bias in the way an algorithm searches or explores the solution space, can cause optimal solutions or important regions of the space to be overlooked.

a2e110e1-18dd-40c3-9e58-c30281dcec4f.title: Data Splitting
a2e110e1-18dd-40c3-9e58-c30281dcec4f.definition: The process of dividing the overall data set into different subsets (training, validation, testing) to effectively train and evaluate the model.

6225efda-db8b-43e1-bc0d-d9cda0ec108b.title: Stratified Splitting
6225efda-db8b-43e1-bc0d-d9cda0ec108b.definition: Data partitioning technique to ensure that the scale distribution of important classes or attributes is preserved in all data subsets (training, validation, testing).

ac71eed7-d84e-4aba-89a7-3c7986d938c8.title: Training Set
ac71eed7-d84e-4aba-89a7-3c7986d938c8.definition: The data portion is used to train the machine learning model, where the model learns patterns and relationships from the data.

7d5fd966-2104-4f77-9953-a02027c1e241.title: Validation Set
7d5fd966-2104-4f77-9953-a02027c1e241.definition: The independent data section is used to fine-tune the model's hyper-parameters and to select the best model, avoiding overfitting during training.

ad7dd32b-911e-4f20-a36a-fc7974cbaff3.title: Test Set
ad7dd32b-911e-4f20-a36a-fc7974cbaff3.definition: A completely independent portion of the data is used to evaluate the final performance of the trained model, providing an unbiased estimate of generalization ability.

9cad7c51-b65f-42e8-885a-cd1b243d97d1.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
9cad7c51-b65f-42e8-885a-cd1b243d97d1.definition: The process of finding optimal values ​​for the hyperparameters of a machine learning model to achieve the best performance, usually through grid search or random search combined with cross-validation.

a6ab71a6-60ae-4b99-899d-da1b1f97668d.title: Grid Search
a6ab71a6-60ae-4b99-899d-da1b1f97668d.definition: A systematic method for fine-tuning hyper-parameters by trying all possible combinations of parameter values ​​within a predetermined grid, often combined with cross-validation.

0376714e-9bf7-4738-9a35-b35df0d961f9.title: Random Search
0376714e-9bf7-4738-9a35-b35df0d961f9.definition: An effective method for fine-tuning hyperparameters is by randomly sampling parameter combinations from a defined space, often combined with cross-validation.

a6241e1d-3772-4adb-a974-fc63e1610a41.title: Performance Evaluation
a6241e1d-3772-4adb-a974-fc63e1610a41.definition: Advanced methods and metrics are used to measure and compare the performance of machine learning models, including ROC and AUC curves.

82a76057-ee7d-42fe-b075-1c421cb9502d.title: Cross-Validation
82a76057-ee7d-42fe-b075-1c421cb9502d.definition: More advanced cross-validation techniques, including different variations (e.g., K-fold, leave-one-out) to evaluate model performance and robustly tune parameters.

2feaf03c-fa08-46a0-b620-013750f6f0a2.title: Error Rate
2feaf03c-fa08-46a0-b620-013750f6f0a2.definition: The basic evaluation metric for classification, measuring the misprediction rate, is considered in an advanced context along with other metrics.

37e13ef7-88f5-40ba-bb42-c48627262474.title: Precision
37e13ef7-88f5-40ba-bb42-c48627262474.definition: Index that evaluates the accuracy of positive predictions, used in advanced classification performance analytics.

2e6924cd-f424-4a4e-a22a-131ac1577644.title: Recall
2e6924cd-f424-4a4e-a22a-131ac1577644.definition: The metric evaluates the model's ability to find all actual positives, used in advanced classification performance analyses.

8f72b0c8-0e22-4688-a682-f9d1a95b8094.title: Confusion Matrix
8f72b0c8-0e22-4688-a682-f9d1a95b8094.definition: A detailed tool to analyze classifier performance, providing insight into the types of errors made, especially useful in complex classification scenarios.

a7ce5d10-c628-44fa-acd4-c14f70e581c1.title: ROC Curve
a7ce5d10-c628-44fa-acd4-c14f70e581c1.definition: A graph showing the model's classification performance at all possible classification thresholds, commonly used to evaluate binary classification models.

9800f88b-6d57-4f2c-815c-79f043e23c8b.title: AUC
9800f88b-6d57-4f2c-815c-79f043e23c8b.definition: An index that summarizes the overall performance of a classifier across all thresholds, with higher values ​​indicating a better classification model.

bffb1b5f-8a04-4a11-81f1-6f095c3c1589.title: Bayesian Learning
bffb1b5f-8a04-4a11-81f1-6f095c3c1589.definition: A machine learning approach based on Bayes' theorem, which combines prior knowledge with observational data to create posterior inference.

af41b449-09dc-431e-bb83-c2c1575acb20.title: Naive Bayes
af41b449-09dc-431e-bb83-c2c1575acb20.definition: A classification algorithm based on Bayes' theorem with the assumption of strong independence between features, commonly used in text classification.

21a15365-ff05-4242-b55e-ea264f3d6334.title: Naive Bayes & Linear Models
21a15365-ff05-4242-b55e-ea264f3d6334.definition: Study how Naive Bayes, although based on probability, can be understood and related to linear classification models.

635fff0c-d718-449c-b185-d911494b1b99.title: Bayesian Networks
635fff0c-d718-449c-b185-d911494b1b99.definition: Graphical models represent a set of variables and the conditional probability dependencies between them.

2554953d-4c0c-4dee-ba8b-fdc9468b5e8c.title: Prior Probability
2554953d-4c0c-4dee-ba8b-fdc9468b5e8c.definition: The initial belief about the probability of an event or parameter before any new data is observed.

da17ef13-2b63-4fac-897d-989c765db9f4.title: Posterior Probability
da17ef13-2b63-4fac-897d-989c765db9f4.definition: The probability of an event or parameter, after considering new data, is calculated by combining the prior probability and the data through Bayes' theorem.

a5f76cd8-e7cc-4932-9845-3f6fff3b7c37.title: Generative Models (Bayes)
a5f76cd8-e7cc-4932-9845-3f6fff3b7c37.definition: The models learn the joint probability distribution of data and labels, allowing the generation of new data samples and the estimation of label probabilities for a given input.

c16ee952-64fc-485c-9434-6191c4613806.title: Deep Learning
c16ee952-64fc-485c-9434-6191c4613806.definition: In-depth study of the theories, architecture, and applications of deep learning, including mathematical and technical aspects.

bb0b7078-9f58-48f5-becd-3a9870fdcdc3.title: Deep Feedforward Networks
bb0b7078-9f58-48f5-becd-3a9870fdcdc3.definition: A detailed study of the structure, operation, and mathematical aspects of deep feedforward neural networks (also known as MLPs), including activation functions, backpropagation, and optimization.

49c03528-cf6f-4f8f-b0fd-ef74674ca3b8.title: Neural Tangent Kernel
49c03528-cf6f-4f8f-b0fd-ef74674ca3b8.definition: A theoretical concept that helps understand the behavior of large neural networks (with an infinite number of neurons) during training, linking them to kernel models.

204839ce-c3c5-42d1-94bb-371cd854c434.title: Neural Net Training
204839ce-c3c5-42d1-94bb-371cd854c434.definition: Study the fundamentals and challenges of training neural networks, including weight initialization, optimization, learning rates, and normalization techniques.

114a8e44-000c-4242-a54a-4a61c303cf2d.title: Convolutional Neural Networks
114a8e44-000c-4242-a54a-4a61c303cf2d.definition: A detailed study of the structure, layers (convolution, pooling, fully connected) and operation of CNNs, including mathematical aspects and extensive applications in computer vision.

400492db-bb95-49fc-9c48-fa7b8d8ab4b6.title: Autoencoders
400492db-bb95-49fc-9c48-fa7b8d8ab4b6.definition: The neural network is trained to encode the input data into a lower-dimensional representation (encoding) and then decode that representation to reconstruct the original input.

520b8f39-96d1-46fc-bf37-fcabaacbe7a3.title: Recurrent Neural Networks
520b8f39-96d1-46fc-bf37-fcabaacbe7a3.definition: Deeper research on types of recurrent networks (e.g., RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs) and their ability to process sequential data, remember information over time, and applications in NLP and time series.

2c52f487-b40f-4615-b173-c73b57070718.title: Deep Learning Representation
2c52f487-b40f-4615-b173-c73b57070718.definition: How data is encoded or transformed by deep networks to create meaningful features, helping the model learn more complex patterns.

9efb3cc6-51e2-453e-bd1a-1936eb5d287c.title: Transfer Learning
9efb3cc6-51e2-453e-bd1a-1936eb5d287c.definition: Technique of using a model that has been trained on a large task or data set (e.g., pre-trained models) to improve performance on a new task or smaller data set.

101f5494-f4c1-42bb-af0c-4a8b0825f8ba.title: Adversarial Training
101f5494-f4c1-42bb-af0c-4a8b0825f8ba.definition: A technique for training models to become more robust against adversarial disturbances (adversarial examples), helping to improve model robustness and safety.

6a688773-d196-4f8c-a2d9-cc4bd7047ac6.title: GANs
6a688773-d196-4f8c-a2d9-cc4bd7047ac6.definition: A class of machine learning algorithms in which two neural networks (a generator and a discriminator) compete with each other to generate realistic new data and differentiate real/fake data.

6f52683c-ff8d-41dd-aef6-d0b480883e54.title: Attention Mechanism
6f52683c-ff8d-41dd-aef6-d0b480883e54.definition: A technique that allows a neural network to focus on the most important parts of the input data when processing information, especially useful in NLP and vision.

63fcbde6-4a44-451d-aa6e-b8b9df1956df.title: Representation (General)
63fcbde6-4a44-451d-aa6e-b8b9df1956df.definition: The study of how data is structured, encoded, or transformed into suitable formats so that machine learning algorithms can process and learn effectively.

59888a24-f068-4781-88f3-b21bc5ef329d.title: Handcrafted Features
59888a24-f068-4781-88f3-b21bc5ef329d.definition: Data features are designed by humans based on domain knowledge and experience, which often requires a high level of expertise and can be time-consuming.

5e3072b3-b51e-42fe-945f-9877435e51bd.title: Basis Expansion
5e3072b3-b51e-42fe-945f-9877435e51bd.definition: Technique that transforms data into a higher dimensional space by using basis functions (e.g., polynomial functions, spline functions) to model nonlinear relationships.

9ccf32f5-e7a6-4419-87e5-3e4e91e7a933.title: Learned Representation
9ccf32f5-e7a6-4419-87e5-3e4e91e7a933.definition: Data features are automatically discovered and extracted from raw data by the model (e.g., by a deep neural network), which is often more efficient and flexible than manual representation.

1f3e9e69-92e6-4c22-b794-1145cfd0a51c.title: Deep Nets (Learned Rep.)
1f3e9e69-92e6-4c22-b794-1145cfd0a51c.definition: Use deep neural networks as a powerful tool to automatically learn and extract meaningful, hierarchical representations from input data.

2816e5ee-1a6d-452f-b16e-3c3cb7d684e2.title: Unsupervised Learning
2816e5ee-1a6d-452f-b16e-3c3cb7d684e2.definition: A type of machine learning in which the algorithm looks for patterns, hidden structures, or relationships in unlabeled data, without a predetermined desired output.

d5e472da-9569-4f56-9d6b-fdc599c6ecf0.title: Clustering
d5e472da-9569-4f56-9d6b-fdc599c6ecf0.definition: The technique of grouping similar data points into clusters, or groups, based on some similarity measure, is a core task of unsupervised learning.

46d3ee08-a3ef-4baf-a8c8-95b0e4f5c7d1.title: K-means Clustering
46d3ee08-a3ef-4baf-a8c8-95b0e4f5c7d1.definition: An iterative clustering algorithm divides the data into k clusters, where each data point belongs to the cluster with the closest center.

23d6c65d-c574-43f1-9cba-6fbe9377cef3.title: Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)
23d6c65d-c574-43f1-9cba-6fbe9377cef3.definition: A statistical model that represents data points as originating from a finite mixture of Gaussian (usually Gaussian) distributions, used for clustering and density estimation.

9dfc64ea-16dc-45a2-bbba-af4a58bde175.title: Expectation-Maximization (EM)
9dfc64ea-16dc-45a2-bbba-af4a58bde175.definition: An iterative algorithm for finding maximum likelihood estimates or maximum posterior estimates of parameters in statistical models with unobservable latent variables.

7aab85f6-2000-4803-8e17-01c296bbdd01.title: Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs)
7aab85f6-2000-4803-8e17-01c296bbdd01.definition: A type of artificial neural network belonging to the family of self-organizing neural networks, used to reduce data dimensionality and visualize complex relationships in data.

4d45da21-5cbe-44b4-81f1-479dc5fcb80b.title: Graph Analysis
4d45da21-5cbe-44b4-81f1-479dc5fcb80b.definition: Study the structure, properties, and relationships between nodes and edges in data represented as graphs, to discover patterns and useful information.

c9a97caa-b2a8-462d-b42c-cb4516a93bff.title: PageRank Algorithm
c9a97caa-b2a8-462d-b42c-cb4516a93bff.definition: An algorithm used by Google to rank web pages in search results, measuring the relative importance of a node (page) in a graph based on link structure.

7e3e960f-f615-41ba-baf6-73ea2671e49c.title: Semi-Supervised Learning
7e3e960f-f615-41ba-baf6-73ea2671e49c.definition: A type of machine learning that uses both labeled and unlabeled data to train a model, especially useful when labeling the data is expensive.

c7d70290-8bc3-43a4-91b2-00f955b98b0c.title: Graphical Models
c7d70290-8bc3-43a4-91b2-00f955b98b0c.definition: Mathematical structures represent conditional dependencies between variables through a graph, helping with probabilistic analysis and inference.

1b3b1d40-60ef-4fb4-92bf-def809837bc7.title: Ensemble Learning
1b3b1d40-60ef-4fb4-92bf-def809837bc7.definition: Research advanced model ensemble methods, including boosting, bagging, and random forest, to improve model performance and robustness.

01555869-962d-4cb2-824b-72bc0a7e1722.title: Weighted Majority Vote
01555869-962d-4cb2-824b-72bc0a7e1722.definition: The method combines output from component models by assigning weights to each model, especially useful in model ensembles.

21d77912-aadd-4137-a9b1-07c63bde0108.title: Boosting
21d77912-aadd-4137-a9b1-07c63bde0108.definition: A model ensemble technique that builds a strong classifier by combining multiple weak classifiers, training sequentially to focus on misclassified data samples.

544ebde3-ebd2-4802-9c19-bf2d7b0dad66.title: Bagging
544ebde3-ebd2-4802-9c19-bf2d7b0dad66.definition: A model ensemble technique that creates multiple versions of a model by resampling the training data (with replacement) and then combining the predictions.

4b9528e2-42b3-4bee-a860-2ec0d44a28d8.title: Random Forest
4b9528e2-42b3-4bee-a860-2ec0d44a28d8.definition: An ensemble learning algorithm uses multiple decision trees, each trained on a randomly sampled subset of data and a random feature subset, and then the predictions are aggregated.

87a10c46-5a22-4358-af44-3adb624db6e5.title: Gated Ensembles
87a10c46-5a22-4358-af44-3adb624db6e5.definition: A model ensemble architecture in which a 'gating' network learns to dynamically combine the output of component models based on the characteristics of the input.

8e495dec-2661-457e-b8b6-93fc36bcf14b.title: Learning Theory
8e495dec-2661-457e-b8b6-93fc36bcf14b.definition: An overview of the mathematical research on machine learning, focusing on understanding why machine learning algorithms work and their generalizability.

02b091bd-ae76-496e-9600-4feec681f27a.title: Learning Theory Overview
02b091bd-ae76-496e-9600-4feec681f27a.definition: Explain the fundamentals behind the ability of machine learning algorithms to learn and generalize from limited data, including the concepts of training error and generalization error.

e73aa01b-191d-4354-a1ec-55dafe8998d7.title: VC Dimension
e73aa01b-191d-4354-a1ec-55dafe8998d7.definition: A measure of the capacity or complexity of a class of functions (e.g. a machine learning model), indicating the maximum number of data points that the model can 'sort' in every possible way.

39de3d75-4094-4b16-9f09-df41a452c435.title: Generalization Bounds
