39de3d75-4094-4b16-9f09-df41a452c435.definition: Mathematical bounds dictate how well a model can generalize on new, never-before-seen data, based on its performance on training data and the complexity of the model.

451b611e-5c95-4ea8-a56d-eb9fc7e1e692.title: Reinforcement Learning
451b611e-5c95-4ea8-a56d-eb9fc7e1e692.definition: A branch of machine learning that focuses on how intelligent agents should perform actions in an environment to maximize the concept of cumulative rewards over time.

1c95733c-984d-4605-96c6-fa149c3f9461.title: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off
1c95733c-984d-4605-96c6-fa149c3f9461.definition: The balance between trying new actions to explore the potential for greater rewards (exploration) and leveraging existing knowledge to maximize immediate rewards (exploitation) in reinforcement learning problems.

aabecffc-fe4a-466f-8c06-f72945f87a33.title: Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)
aabecffc-fe4a-466f-8c06-f72945f87a33.definition: A mathematical framework for modeling decision making in situations where outcomes are partly random and partly under the control of the decision maker. This is the basis of many reinforcement learning algorithms.

25b0480f-3254-4397-bf02-9dd4c65dfc57.title: Value & Policy Iteration
25b0480f-3254-4397-bf02-9dd4c65dfc57.definition: Two basic algorithms in reinforcement learning to find optimal policies in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). Value iteration finds the optimal value function, while policy iteration finds the optimal policy directly.

1886afad-6b4f-4b33-aa52-1142c3ca9eca.title: Policy Gradient Methods
1886afad-6b4f-4b33-aa52-1142c3ca9eca.definition: A class of reinforcement learning algorithms optimizes parametric policies directly by estimating the gradient of the objective function (usually the total reward) over the policy parameters.

4683c1cb-7153-4438-aa73-e7ec4d582e29.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)
4683c1cb-7153-4438-aa73-e7ec4d582e29.definition: The combination of reinforcement learning and deep learning, using deep neural networks to represent value or policy functions, allows learning from complex, high-dimensional input data.

060e94d8-1e8e-47c8-8a62-3ab4b5260d51.title: Learning from Demonstration (LfD)
060e94d8-1e8e-47c8-8a62-3ab4b5260d51.definition: A method in machine learning that allows a system to learn a behavior by observing examples of that behavior performed by an agent (usually a human).

e798facf-0d68-492c-8508-b703e908a245.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL)
e798facf-0d68-492c-8508-b703e908a245.definition: A technique for inferring the hidden reward function that an agent is trying to optimize, based on observations of that agent's behavior.

e71b7f63-81d6-45c9-86d6-d569ab3f0541.title: Explainable AI (XAI)
e71b7f63-81d6-45c9-86d6-d569ab3f0541.definition: The field of research in machine learning aims to create models that are more understandable to humans, providing transparency into how decisions are made and the reasoning behind predictions.

a38daeaa-2209-48e9-a781-0ae49f290821.title: Feature Importance
a38daeaa-2209-48e9-a781-0ae49f290821.definition: The ability to determine how much each input feature contributes to the prediction or decision of a machine learning model, helps to better understand the model's behavior.

f5eebb2f-a7fb-4da2-8fef-590611b50995.title: LIME
f5eebb2f-a7fb-4da2-8fef-590611b50995.definition: An agnostic model explanation technique provides local explanations for the predictions of any classifier or regressor, by approximating the model's behavior around a particular example.

3731406c-f77f-4cff-9a01-28ac7a9d9784.title: Shapley Values
3731406c-f77f-4cff-9a01-28ac7a9d9784.definition: A method from game theory to allocate 'value' or equitable contribution to each feature in making predictions of a machine learning model.

e4ebb837-a8d7-47bd-8214-da58b94d0d57.title: Interpretable Models
e4ebb837-a8d7-47bd-8214-da58b94d0d57.definition: Machine learning models are designed to make it easier to understand how they operate or make decisions, with ways of representing data or knowledge that enhance interpretation.

db1c04b3-4597-4eb8-a7ad-76405ec87dcf.title: Recommendation Systems
db1c04b3-4597-4eb8-a7ad-76405ec87dcf.definition: Software systems that provide recommendations of items (products, movies, articles, etc.) to users, based on their interests, past behavior, and/or the behavior of similar users.

3365b75a-ddf6-4d5e-8c55-69888e64d4f9.title: ML Hardware
3365b75a-ddf6-4d5e-8c55-69888e64d4f9.definition: The physical components of computers and systems are designed or optimized to accelerate the complex and resource-intensive calculations of machine learning algorithms.

8b8a7616-ce75-4cf5-885a-71cf1d47adae.title: GPU
8b8a7616-ce75-4cf5-885a-71cf1d47adae.definition: Specialized processors were originally designed for graphics rendering, but with their powerful parallel architecture, they have become extremely effective for training deep learning models.

a8815fb3-7fe2-4950-b40e-282f40c6dc07.title: TPU
a8815fb3-7fe2-4950-b40e-282f40c6dc07.definition: Application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) were specifically developed by Google to accelerate neural network calculations, especially tensor operations in deep learning.

d77f3532-c590-4876-a62d-b3a6c66b3f38.title: ML in Healthcare
d77f3532-c590-4876-a62d-b3a6c66b3f38.definition: The use of machine learning algorithms to solve problems in the medical field, including disease diagnosis, drug development, medical image analysis, treatment personalization, and patient outcome prediction.

9fce655a-65a2-42e0-8210-6687197237b4.title: ML in Economics
9fce655a-65a2-42e0-8210-6687197237b4.definition: The application of machine learning techniques to analyze economic data, predict market trends, model consumer behavior, optimize economic policy, and detect financial fraud.

a8f0371b-4e61-4254-8e93-375b1a659e2d.title: ML in Education
a8f0371b-4e61-4254-8e93-375b1a659e2d.definition: The use of machine learning to improve the teaching and learning process, including intelligent tutoring systems, personalizing learning pathways, predicting student performance and analyzing educational data.

0cd73d0f-1106-4704-ae81-594ca46a7ece.title: ML in Computer Vision
0cd73d0f-1106-4704-ae81-594ca46a7ece.definition: The application of machine learning to enable computers to 'understand' and process images and videos, including object recognition, face detection, image segmentation and image description.

0f9b7fcd-e606-4923-a1a1-429c26bd8c1d.title: ML in NLP
0f9b7fcd-e606-4923-a1a1-429c26bd8c1d.definition: The use of machine learning to process and understand human language, including machine translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization, speech recognition, and text generation.

128e514e-f128-4035-8fc5-a770dbc9d7d7.title: ML in Robotics
128e514e-f128-4035-8fc5-a770dbc9d7d7.definition: Integrating machine learning into robots allows them to learn from experience, adapt to new environments, improve control, and perform complex tasks automatically.

bc0f8898-abbd-47a5-bc73-b768a8b97d38.title: ML in Gaming
bc0f8898-abbd-47a5-bc73-b768a8b97d38.definition: The use of machine learning to develop game agents (adversarial AI), generate game content, adjust difficulty, and analyze player behavior.

ac8fd1ed-a516-41de-bcb5-67ea352f9a88.title: ML in Data Mining
ac8fd1ed-a516-41de-bcb5-67ea352f9a88.definition: applying machine learning techniques to discover valuable patterns, trends, and insights from large data sets. (Refer also to DM/Data Analytics).

30563d93-1d95-4206-8fdb-4dacf6d70935.title: ML Ethics
30563d93-1d95-4206-8fdb-4dacf6d70935.definition: The study of ethical, social, and legal issues arising from the development and deployment of machine learning systems, including issues of bias, fairness, privacy, and accountability.

c68d24f6-e3a0-4aff-bc0b-98bbf93ef3dd.title: Real-world ML Ethics
c68d24f6-e3a0-4aff-bc0b-98bbf93ef3dd.definition: Focuses on analyzing real-life situations and concrete examples to better understand the ethical implications of real-world machine learning systems and methods to address them. (Refer to SEP-Context).

35af8731-6106-4d08-9cba-50dec216a6fa.title: Dataset Bias
35af8731-6106-4d08-9cba-50dec216a6fa.definition: The presence of bias or unrepresentation in the data used to train a machine learning model, resulting in the model making unfair or inaccurate predictions or decisions for certain groups.

e4ebc996-933e-4470-823e-23be8c084cc0.title: Algorithmic Bias
e4ebc996-933e-4470-823e-23be8c084cc0.definition: Systematic or unfair bias in the results of a machine learning algorithm, which may be due to the algorithm design, the training data set, or both.

6d59e126-2ab5-43ef-8c89-ce6bd2685e54.title: Evaluation Bias
6d59e126-2ab5-43ef-8c89-ce6bd2685e54.definition: The presence of bias in the process of evaluating the performance of a machine learning model, can lead to an incorrect assessment of the model's ability to generalize or be fair.

a87a23db-6c48-4b49-9db3-0f910449ff7a.title: ML Data Privacy
a87a23db-6c48-4b49-9db3-0f910449ff7a.definition: Issues related to protecting personal and sensitive information used in training and deploying machine learning models, ensuring compliance with regulations and individual rights. (Refer also to SEP-Privacy).

9c37fcb7-5d28-420a-ac10-81b5e3b2ded8.title: ML Fairness
9c37fcb7-5d28-420a-ac10-81b5e3b2ded8.definition: Ensure that machine learning systems make decisions or predictions that do not discriminate or disadvantage specific individuals or groups, regardless of their sensitive attributes.

7cc4517b-e2a4-48b5-8a24-574e5ff2cedf.title: ML Trust
7cc4517b-e2a4-48b5-8a24-574e5ff2cedf.definition: The level of confidence a user or stakeholder has in a machine learning system's ability to operate reliably, securely, and fairly, especially in mission-critical applications.

bca7a1be-8a34-4a94-9515-8af25c2014dc.title: Ethical ML Explainability
bca7a1be-8a34-4a94-9515-8af25c2014dc.definition: The ethical aspect of ensuring that machine learning model decisions and operations can be understood and explained by humans contributes to building trust and accountability. (Related to AI-009 but focusing on ethical aspects).

c525b020-647a-4329-828a-22f9036c0d53.title: Supervised Learning
c525b020-647a-4329-828a-22f9036c0d53.definition: A type of machine learning algorithm that learns a mapping from input to output based on pre-labeled input-output example pairs.

f45e4dae-a0e3-4bce-9164-421d7ec10462.title: Unsupervised Learning
f45e4dae-a0e3-4bce-9164-421d7ec10462.definition: A type of machine learning algorithm that looks for hidden patterns and structures in unlabeled data, such as clustering or dimensionality reduction.

ce7790e1-fa70-478b-8351-6b3c312b3eab.title: Compare ML Paradigms
ce7790e1-fa70-478b-8351-6b3c312b3eab.definition: Ability to distinguish and compare the characteristics, operating principles, and appropriate applications of supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.

bbb0cc4c-ed5c-4423-802f-3e6716267570.title: ML Paradigm Selection
bbb0cc4c-ed5c-4423-802f-3e6716267570.definition: The ability to determine which machine learning style (supervised, reinforcement, unsupervised) is most appropriate to solve a specific problem based on the nature of the data and the goal.

950f750a-682e-4e3d-86b3-2a9ec1fa1f0d.title: AI
950f750a-682e-4e3d-86b3-2a9ec1fa1f0d.definition: The field of computer science specializes in creating intelligent machines that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.

3c3aae26-57c5-463e-8e72-c1e7f34e2f68.title: ML
3c3aae26-57c5-463e-8e72-c1e7f34e2f68.definition: A subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn from data, identify patterns, and make decisions with minimal human intervention.

3f27202d-4882-4d84-a012-301a759e8096.title: DL
3f27202d-4882-4d84-a012-301a759e8096.definition: A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers (deep neural networks) to learn representations of data with multiple levels of abstraction.

2dd15034-5095-401e-847f-06f1f484573d.title: AI ML DL Distinction
2dd15034-5095-401e-847f-06f1f484573d.definition: Ability to clearly differentiate the concepts of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning, understanding the hierarchical relationship and core differences between them.

a4ea7ea6-60f4-4dd6-b7ad-ecefc82a2880.title: Classification Problem Formulation
a4ea7ea6-60f4-4dd6-b7ad-ecefc82a2880.definition: The ability to structure a real-world problem so that it can be solved using classification techniques, including determining the input and output characteristics to be predicted.

2481dd0b-a9fa-4ac9-97cb-3e119bee5113.title: ML Input Features
2481dd0b-a9fa-4ac9-97cb-3e119bee5113.definition: Attributes or independent variables of data are used as input to a machine learning model to make predictions or decisions.

5e71dae3-3584-4ff1-89a5-6b32e900e9da.title: ML Output Prediction
5e71dae3-3584-4ff1-89a5-6b32e900e9da.definition: The value or label that a machine learning model is trained to produce based on input features.

e528e5ca-e4c7-416b-b566-22c4f150086c.title: Classification Problem
e528e5ca-e4c7-416b-b566-22c4f150086c.definition: A type of supervised learning problem in which the goal is to predict a discrete label or category for an input data point.

2d4d62c7-ac89-4fb8-9367-4626f16702e3.title: Simple Statistical Learning
2d4d62c7-ac89-4fb8-9367-4626f16702e3.definition: Basic machine learning algorithms are based on statistical principles, used to solve classification or regression problems, such as logistic regression, k-NN, or simple decision trees.

f3f801db-dbf7-4a8a-a2ff-3a545c9a7de3.title: Classifier Accuracy
f3f801db-dbf7-4a8a-a2ff-3a545c9a7de3.definition: Technique that quantifies the performance of a classifier by calculating the proportion of correct predictions it makes on a test data set.

274619b4-1599-428b-bc19-2d0bae980452.title: Overfitting
274619b4-1599-428b-bc19-2d0bae980452.definition: A situation in machine learning where a model overlearns details and noise from training data to the point that it performs poorly on new, unseen data.

979be2da-fe2b-40a8-95cb-a5783e1826f9.title: Learning Curve
979be2da-fe2b-40a8-95cb-a5783e1826f9.definition: Histograms show model performance (e.g., accuracy, error) as a function of the amount of training data or number of training iterations, used to diagnose overfitting or underfitting.

3a194c0f-87e1-4294-862e-e18c0cc96e8d.title: Overfitting Solutions
3a194c0f-87e1-4294-862e-e18c0cc96e8d.definition: Techniques used to minimize overfitting include regularization, data augmentation, choosing a simpler model, or using early stopping techniques.

aa696540-b412-4b39-ba1b-119cd0c420d5.title: ML as Optimization
aa696540-b412-4b39-ba1b-119cd0c420d5.definition: understand that training a machine learning model often involves minimizing a loss function or maximizing an objective function by adjusting model parameters through optimization algorithms.

3158cdcf-f891-4474-a4d9-a0dbde0df15c.title: ML as Search
3158cdcf-f891-4474-a4d9-a0dbde0df15c.definition: The concept of machine learning involves searching the space of models or parameters to find the model that best fits the given data and goals.

f2271469-d811-47f7-8a68-ed5a8167d094.title: Implement Statistical Learning
f2271469-d811-47f7-8a68-ed5a8167d094.definition: Ability to code and configure statistical learning algorithms to build models from data, often using specialized libraries and frameworks.

b67e11a9-92a2-4c6c-9b58-d00c464f74db.title: Classifier Training
b67e11a9-92a2-4c6c-9b58-d00c464f74db.definition: The process of tuning the parameters of a classification model by feeding it labeled training data so that it can learn to map inputs to output classes.

e6fc86c2-68ef-4ff4-b394-0f764b2ef581.title: Predict New Data
e6fc86c2-68ef-4ff4-b394-0f764b2ef581.definition: Use a trained machine learning model to create predictions or classifications on never-before-seen data points.

9c81900e-3d0e-4a3c-b2f3-6cf960967df4.title: NN Training Process
9c81900e-3d0e-4a3c-b2f3-6cf960967df4.definition: The steps and techniques involved in adjusting the weights and biases of the neural network to minimize prediction error on the training data, often through backpropagation algorithms and gradient optimization methods.

cde84901-d374-46bd-87d0-da31a66dbd39.title: NN Learned Representations
cde84901-d374-46bd-87d0-da31a66dbd39.definition: The abstract data features and structures that a neural network automatically learns from input data through its hidden layers, help the model understand and process information effectively.

f933b136-48f8-4fd7-bd0e-4ca328a03679.title: ML Performance Evaluation
f933b136-48f8-4fd7-bd0e-4ca328a03679.definition: Explain proper evaluation procedures in Machine Learning, including the difference between performance on training and test sets, as well as problems that can occur during evaluation that lead to inaccurate performance reporting.

24421ff1-8100-4f86-a19e-341010466cdd.title: Compare ML Algos & Metrics
24421ff1-8100-4f86-a19e-341010466cdd.definition: Compare two Machine Learning algorithms on a data set, implementing your own data preprocessing steps and evaluation methods (e.g., metrics and how to handle the train/test set split).

cf00dcff-b710-44f7-8575-368baca3e7f9.title: Visualize NN Training
cf00dcff-b710-44f7-8575-368baca3e7f9.definition: Visualize the training progress of a neural network through learning curves in a popular tool (e.g., TensorBoard) and visualize the features the network has learned.

6dcec437-ae8f-40af-b586-c247a023e7bd.title: Compare ML Techniques
6dcec437-ae8f-40af-b586-c247a023e7bd.definition: Compare and contrast several machine learning techniques (e.g., decision trees, logistic regression, Naive Bayes, neural networks, and belief networks), providing examples of where each strategy is superior.

b2ffdfbf-14ab-4311-bb3a-f6ea2ab4c000.title: evaluate Simple ML System
b2ffdfbf-14ab-4311-bb3a-f6ea2ab4c000.definition: Evaluating the performance of a simple machine learning system on a real-world dataset.

14399a37-f95c-4d49-bdee-b3d5c8b2e3bf.title: Current ML Theory
14399a37-f95c-4d49-bdee-b3d5c8b2e3bf.definition: Describes the current state of machine learning theory, including its achievements and limitations.

c5b96fc5-61eb-41e7-877b-7b35dd7a5512.title: Overfitting
c5b96fc5-61eb-41e7-877b-7b35dd7a5512.definition: Overfitting is explained, along with techniques for detecting and managing it.

71dbbdb4-ce0d-4424-a8dc-8c9c39b83c8f.title: Triple Tradeoff
71dbbdb4-ce0d-4424-a8dc-8c9c39b83c8f.definition: Explain the three-factor trade-off between hypothesis space size, training set size, and performance accuracy.

e8f153c3-e8db-4d87-a38c-08c9b297a8a3.title: ML Ethical Issues
e8f153c3-e8db-4d87-a38c-08c9b297a8a3.definition: Describe ethical issues related to data selection, preprocessing steps, algorithm selection, and visualization/presentation of results in a practical Machine Learning application.

3c905ae7-5cb0-436b-af6b-7289b0d80099.title: Specific AI Applications
3c905ae7-5cb0-436b-af6b-7289b0d80099.definition: At least one application of AI to a specific problem and domain (e.g. medicine, health, sustainability, social networks, economics, education, robotics).

277328ac-471c-4851-8c99-a396dc9f3795.title: AI Problem Formulation
277328ac-471c-4851-8c99-a396dc9f3795.definition: How to express and evaluate a specific application as an AI problem.

bddf1f21-347f-4ccd-a413-4043fe9c5f9c.title: Handle Ill-posed Problems
bddf1f21-347f-4ccd-a413-4043fe9c5f9c.definition: The way to solve problems is not clearly defined or is misplaced.

e3d45817-0381-487b-9e5d-166f75cae7b7.title: Data Availability & Quality
e3d45817-0381-487b-9e5d-166f75cae7b7.definition: Issues of data availability, scarcity and purity.

12376361-7afe-4b02-be85-7d2e1a12cea0.title: Basic Data Preprocessing
12376361-7afe-4b02-be85-7d2e1a12cea0.definition: Basic techniques for data cleaning and preprocessing.

5be6ae3b-3fad-4bfa-b2be-8e250bdeb68a.title: Dataset Bias
5be6ae3b-3fad-4bfa-b2be-8e250bdeb68a.definition: Types of bias possible in the dataset.

6d67b7f1-ea46-4879-a94b-69e3d9f8ed6d.title: Algorithmic Bias
6d67b7f1-ea46-4879-a94b-69e3d9f8ed6d.definition: Different types of bias can appear in AI algorithms.

db736320-7b91-4a01-8ac3-ae401e8fe413.title: Evaluation Bias
db736320-7b91-4a01-8ac3-ae401e8fe413.definition: Types of bias can affect the evaluation of AI systems.

536e6634-ba63-4fa4-876e-6294b4622222.title: evaluate AI Social Impact
536e6634-ba63-4fa4-876e-6294b4622222.definition: Assess the social impacts of implementing AI applications.

33fecafe-e297-4aec-9c77-1e0a0f072cf6.title: Deep Image Generative Models
33fecafe-e297-4aec-9c77-1e0a0f072cf6.definition: High-level overview of deep image generation models (e.g., DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion), their uses, and limitations/difficulties.

081e9a57-1553-4090-9d12-01a587077b60.title: LLMs
081e9a57-1553-4090-9d12-01a587077b60.definition: High-level overview of major language models (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard), their uses, and limitations/difficulties.

c7ed2529-54cd-4e9f-9a9f-f1657d7d0601.title: AI Social Impact
c7ed2529-54cd-4e9f-9a9f-f1657d7d0601.definition: Overview of the social impact of Artificial Intelligence.

2aab92dc-8478-42d3-9502-fef5f204e4b4.title: Diverse AI Applications
2aab92dc-8478-42d3-9502-fef5f204e4b4.definition: Research and apply artificial intelligence in many different fields such as medicine, health, sustainability, social media, economics, education, and robotics.

1a6149dd-2a9c-4e52-b95b-df30aa96414d.title: AI Problem Formulation
1a6149dd-2a9c-4e52-b95b-df30aa96414d.definition: Skills to identify and build a real-life problem into one that can be solved using artificial intelligence.

00225d15-3e0e-4f77-b0d5-2ade18f443f4.title: AI Problem Evaluation
00225d15-3e0e-4f77-b0d5-2ade18f443f4.definition: Skills to evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of an AI solution for a specific problem.

184baa98-f2f4-467c-a7b9-e98b6445f848.title: Ill-defined Problems
184baa98-f2f4-467c-a7b9-e98b6445f848.definition: Approach and solve problems where requirements or constraints are not clearly defined.

3f107055-0259-4895-b411-d647ca0976ed.title: Ambiguous Problems
3f107055-0259-4895-b411-d647ca0976ed.definition: Methods of approaching and solving problems that do not have a unique solution, discontinuous solutions that depend on input data, or that do not exist.

4ab56b40-c756-4af8-a987-b58eec33b251.title: Data Availability & Scarcity
4ab56b40-c756-4af8-a987-b58eec33b251.definition: Issues related to data availability to train AI models, including cases where data is abundant or scarce.

16445a24-ffc9-41ad-8f8e-5d04b6b08e75.title: Data Quality
16445a24-ffc9-41ad-8f8e-5d04b6b08e75.definition: Importance and techniques to ensure high quality data, free of errors or noise, for AI applications.

8eba177e-2669-4346-af85-92d4aa0ed33a.title: Basic Data Cleaning
8eba177e-2669-4346-af85-92d4aa0ed33a.definition: Basic techniques for handling missing data, duplicate data, and other data errors.

78518fec-e628-41e2-986d-30dfc9af0dde.title: Data Preprocessing
78518fec-e628-41e2-986d-30dfc9af0dde.definition: Steps to prepare raw data for use in machine learning models, including normalization, normalization, and data transformation.

afc65f68-fba4-47a0-b6b2-41b042eba3e9.title: Dataset Bias
afc65f68-fba4-47a0-b6b2-41b042eba3e9.definition: The existence of biases or unfair representation in the training data set, leading to potentially biased AI models.

4bbff4ed-5dc5-49b9-9603-3ce9dd8e41f0.title: Algorithmic Bias
4bbff4ed-5dc5-49b9-9603-3ce9dd8e41f0.definition: Bias in the results or decisions of an AI algorithm due to algorithm design, training data, or implementation.

a61e1ec4-862e-456e-84f6-e99a500c154e.title: Evaluation Bias
a61e1ec4-862e-456e-84f6-e99a500c154e.definition: Bias occurs during the evaluation of AI models, possibly due to the wrong choice of metrics, unrepresentative test data sets, or other factors.

6647fec5-32aa-40cf-bcab-9d4fa0e65c93.title: AI Social Impact Assessment
6647fec5-32aa-40cf-bcab-9d4fa0e65c93.definition: analyze and evaluate the broad impacts of AI applications on society, including ethical, equity, privacy, and sustainability aspects.

83c77ff1-d65b-4af9-ad39-cfd1128de978.title: Deployed Deep Generative Models
83c77ff1-d65b-4af9-ad39-cfd1128de978.definition: An in-depth introduction to deep learning-based generative AI models deployed in practice.

d8167dcb-e685-4d15-a78a-1deaf5f2546f.title: Deep Image Generative Models
d8167dcb-e685-4d15-a78a-1deaf5f2546f.definition: The operating mechanism of deep learning models capable of creating new images, including structure and principles.

ad203629-734e-43cd-a0cd-6a84763c68a5.title: DALL-E
ad203629-734e-43cd-a0cd-6a84763c68a5.definition: An example of an outstanding deep image generation model, capable of generating images from text descriptions.

66b2cb01-2c06-4a1f-8807-eb0c91b01153.title: Midjourney
66b2cb01-2c06-4a1f-8807-eb0c91b01153.definition: Example of another deep image generation model, known for its ability to generate high-quality artistic images.

ec7334af-d654-406f-b924-372174492f43.title: Stable Diffusion
ec7334af-d654-406f-b924-372174492f43.definition: An example of an open source deep image generation model that allows the generation of images from text or other images.

51fe126f-63e3-4827-b563-2dcf874b7b19.title: Attention (Image Generative Models)
51fe126f-63e3-4827-b563-2dcf874b7b19.definition: The role and how the attention mechanism works in deep image generation models to focus on important parts of the data.

48bc0b24-56ff-404a-8666-5d42223e40a5.title: How LLMs Work
48bc0b24-56ff-404a-8666-5d42223e40a5.definition: The underlying mechanism and architecture of large language models capable of understanding and generating natural text.

f8ced102-02d5-45e9-8338-1272217a8852.title: ChatGPT
f8ced102-02d5-45e9-8338-1272217a8852.definition: Example of a large language model, designed for dialogue and the generation of contextually relevant text.

2bed4741-2f7f-4525-ae7c-6f06fb6be46d.title: Bard
2bed4741-2f7f-4525-ae7c-6f06fb6be46d.definition: An example of another large language model, developed by Google, is capable of performing many language-related tasks.

962ce381-5265-458c-a413-66ab4b976513.title: Attention (LLMs)
962ce381-5265-458c-a413-66ab4b976513.definition: The role and how attention mechanisms work in large language models to process and produce coherent text.

40f6b824-b29a-48d7-8af2-3ee13866848c.title: Foundational Models
40f6b824-b29a-48d7-8af2-3ee13866848c.definition: The concept of large models is trained on vast data and can be adapted for a variety of tasks.

48f7ae05-be2f-4b32-9614-34c52501feb5.title: Using Foundational Models
48f7ae05-be2f-4b32-9614-34c52501feb5.definition: Methods and techniques for applying and customizing platform models for specific applications.

672a1b4e-4337-4be0-815d-42c49a35dcf3.title: Benefits of Large Data Pre-training
672a1b4e-4337-4be0-815d-42c49a35dcf3.definition: The advantages of using large amounts of data to train underlying models include generalization and high performance.

39bc51b7-1f57-463d-96f6-ed51457ad32a.title: Challenges of Large Data Pre-training
39bc51b7-1f57-463d-96f6-ed51457ad32a.definition: Challenges and difficulties encountered when training underlying models on big data, such as cost, bias, and privacy issues.

8711a6fd-355e-460a-ae55-c5380953eb45.title: AI Social Impact Analysis
8711a6fd-355e-460a-ae55-c5380953eb45.definition: Extensive research on the impact of artificial intelligence on various aspects of society.

b38158c8-9a0e-47e8-836a-363b33f1c3c6.title: AI Ethics
b38158c8-9a0e-47e8-836a-363b33f1c3c6.definition: Ethical principles and ethical issues arise from the development and deployment of AI.

de358e78-20db-4abe-80ba-b2d571c3e2c0.title: AI Fairness
de358e78-20db-4abe-80ba-b2d571c3e2c0.definition: Ensure that AI systems do not create or exacerbate inequality or discrimination.

5883265b-9a39-47ab-a2e7-fa07ff035571.title: AI Trustworthiness
5883265b-9a39-47ab-a2e7-fa07ff035571.definition: Build user trust in AI systems through reliability, safety, and performance.

137a58f8-953f-4179-b47f-26f8a411516f.title: Explainable AI (XAI)
137a58f8-953f-4179-b47f-26f8a411516f.definition: The ability of AI systems to explain the reasoning behind their decisions or predictions in an easy-to-understand manner.

74727c7a-ee21-42a2-a59b-017e8a01d255.title: AI Data Privacy
74727c7a-ee21-42a2-a59b-017e8a01d255.definition: Issues related to protecting personal information and how data is used in AI training.

039043fe-7f13-4bd6-810e-262a179cbd3a.title: Human Autonomy in AI
039043fe-7f13-4bd6-810e-262a179cbd3a.definition: The relationship between AI systems and human decision-making and control capabilities.

26fd12e2-674d-44ec-bd03-6567beba04b9.title: AI Regulation
26fd12e2-674d-44ec-bd03-6567beba04b9.definition: The legal and regulatory frameworks needed to govern the development and deployment of AI.

81b41a5d-e47a-494a-80a5-a2e80dabeb00.title: AI Sustainability
81b41a5d-e47a-494a-80a5-a2e80dabeb00.definition: The environmental and social impacts of AI, and how to develop AI responsibly and sustainably.

1c82f540-9c11-43df-a151-a7ff9d26c109.title: Propositional Logic
1c82f540-9c11-43df-a151-a7ff9d26c109.definition: Review basic concepts of propositional logic, including syntax, semantics, and logical operations.

5da560c3-2e0f-4c3e-b368-f2948d8ff107.title: Predicate Logic
5da560c3-2e0f-4c3e-b368-f2948d8ff107.definition: Review the basic concepts of predicate logic, including predicates, variables, quantifiers, and inference rules.

58aef31e-b0e8-4adb-a215-50db825bceb3.title: Propositional Resolution
58aef31e-b0e8-4adb-a215-50db825bceb3.definition: Deductive technique for proving the unsatisfactoriness of a set of propositions in propositional logic.

d66eb3ff-de5c-4c50-b022-52988aac9152.title: Propositional Theorem Proving
d66eb3ff-de5c-4c50-b022-52988aac9152.definition: Use deductive methods, such as solution, to prove the correctness of a theorem in propositional logic.

6b794b8b-ec56-4735-a02c-241cd5c6ae39.title: Forward Chaining
6b794b8b-ec56-4735-a02c-241cd5c6ae39.definition: An inference strategy starts from known facts and applies rules to infer new facts until the goal is achieved.

08e1c6dc-9395-468e-9dd7-08693ca70063.title: Backward Chaining
08e1c6dc-9395-468e-9dd7-08693ca70063.definition: An inference strategy starts from a goal and looks for rules that can lead to that goal, tracing back to the necessary conditions.

9253c8c0-a5f0-4d3f-9a78-6285b9841c62.title: Knowledge Representation Issues
9253c8c0-a5f0-4d3f-9a78-6285b9841c62.definition: Discuss the challenges and difficulties in representing knowledge effectively so that computers can process and reason.

a5a9af58-a013-41fb-a63c-8144c7ad6288.title: Description Logics (DLs)
a5a9af58-a013-41fb-a63c-8144c7ad6288.definition: A family of knowledge representation languages ​​used to model concepts and the relationships between them.

13bc6488-9120-43de-b351-1b5808a67005.title: Ontology Engineering
13bc6488-9120-43de-b351-1b5808a67005.definition: The process of building and developing ontologies, i.e. models that formalize concepts and relationships in a knowledge domain.

947d8cda-9e8f-4bdf-8d1c-16f8bc4efd0d.title: Semantic Web
947d8cda-9e8f-4bdf-8d1c-16f8bc4efd0d.definition: An extension of the World Wide Web where data is given semantic meaning, allowing computers to understand and process information more effectively.

0c3cca0c-c202-49d5-9984-5e5e465a37ac.title: Non-monotonic Reasoning
0c3cca0c-c202-49d5-9984-5e5e465a37ac.definition: Type of inference in which conclusions can be revoked when new information is added.

be920a79-5b6e-458d-b2f9-d32150d730a1.title: Non-classical Logics
be920a79-5b6e-458d-b2f9-d32150d730a1.definition: Logic systems extend or modify the principles of classical logic to handle problems such as inconsistency, uncertainty, or nonmonotonicity.

01ca8217-a99e-46e8-9ff3-ea4252861e65.title: Default Reasoning
01ca8217-a99e-46e8-9ff3-ea4252861e65.definition: A form of nonmonotonic inference where conclusions are drawn based on default assumptions in the absence of conflicting information.

f1685c62-7a7b-4432-b60f-b933575c3dae.title: Argumentation
f1685c62-7a7b-4432-b60f-b933575c3dae.definition: The study of how to construct, analyze and evaluate logical arguments, especially in multi-agent systems.

139043a3-f108-4d43-bea4-61627e2b9fe9.title: Action & Change Reasoning
139043a3-f108-4d43-bea4-61627e2b9fe9.definition: Techniques and models for representing and reasoning about how actions change the state of the world.

7bb7447f-2c5b-4bf3-b7e2-cae131785250.title: Situation Calculus
7bb7447f-2c5b-4bf3-b7e2-cae131785250.definition: A first-order predicate logic language is used to represent knowledge about actions and their effects.

69c7ed65-0e5a-47e3-9284-05826c1b64f3.title: Event Calculus
69c7ed65-0e5a-47e3-9284-05826c1b64f3.definition: A logic-based knowledge representation method used to reason about time and occurrences.

6fd538de-c1bc-452a-8de0-af92275f8ec1.title: Temporal Reasoning
6fd538de-c1bc-452a-8de0-af92275f8ec1.definition: Reason about temporal relationships between events and states, including concepts such as before, after, and concurrent.

8fcaac3d-9d96-4def-9e1b-42bce8c6f710.title: Spatial Reasoning
8fcaac3d-9d96-4def-9e1b-42bce8c6f710.definition: Infer spatial relationships between objects, including location, shape, and orientation.

025ee188-cab0-4811-9061-3c17c793557f.title: Logic Programming
025ee188-cab0-4811-9061-3c17c793557f.definition: A style of programming based on formal logic, in which programs are written as logical statements and execution is a process of proving theorems.

0fb85e91-1610-48e9-9cf5-47b0ad24b58b.title: Prolog
0fb85e91-1610-48e9-9cf5-47b0ad24b58b.definition: A popular logic programming language, commonly used in AI applications involving knowledge representation and inference.

71df73bc-c1b8-4d77-95c3-2693640c3655.title: Answer Set Programming (ASP)
71df73bc-c1b8-4d77-95c3-2693640c3655.definition: A form of non-monotonic logic programming, used to solve search and optimization problems by finding 'solution sets'.

df07cf88-35e3-47f4-b4df-4a683a7da20e.title: Rule-based Expert Systems
df07cf88-35e3-47f4-b4df-4a683a7da20e.definition: AI systems simulate human decision-making using a set of 'IF-THEN' rules.

a04096aa-fc4d-4b24-a62a-662d7f7224a6.title: Semantic Networks
a04096aa-fc4d-4b24-a62a-662d7f7224a6.definition: A method of representing knowledge as a graph, where nodes represent concepts and edges represent relationships between them.

0ba0231e-1664-48f4-92c0-f5d368c48ca4.title: Model-based Reasoning
0ba0231e-1664-48f4-92c0-f5d368c48ca4.definition: An inference method uses a qualitative or quantitative model of a system to predict or explain its behavior.

bad15cfd-bffa-491d-80ca-c46bfc121490.title: Case-based Reasoning
bad15cfd-bffa-491d-80ca-c46bfc121490.definition: A method of inference that solves new problems by adapting solutions used in similar cases before.

7d0ba2d0-c014-441f-878c-4bc03bd8df62.title: Clausal Form
7d0ba2d0-c014-441f-878c-4bc03bd8df62.definition: A standard form of logic formulas, commonly used in theorem solutions and proofs, consisting of clauses containing only selection operators.

a68811c7-dca7-454a-a1b5-a043e1a5b420.title: Planning Systems
a68811c7-dca7-454a-a1b5-a043e1a5b420.definition: AI systems are capable of generating a sequence of actions to achieve a specific goal from an initial state.

a179f5fd-618f-4477-80ba-c637afdd261e.title: Planning as Search
a179f5fd-618f-4477-80ba-c637afdd261e.definition: View planning as a search problem in state space or plan space.

12d2f387-4a11-45f4-934e-a32debc68144.title: Operator-based Planning
12d2f387-4a11-45f4-934e-a32debc68144.definition: The planning method uses operator (action) definitions to transition world states.

43c2f026-645b-4e06-8aca-e1bc48cf61af.title: Propositional Planning
43c2f026-645b-4e06-8aca-e1bc48cf61af.definition: A type of planning that uses propositional logic to represent states and goals, often involving conversion to a Boolean satisfaction problem.

424153ba-841c-4247-a5e0-102ea43af249.title: Monotonic Inference
424153ba-841c-4247-a5e0-102ea43af249.definition: A type of inference in which conclusions drawn are never revoked when new information becomes available.

248d7081-8f9d-4713-ad98-a4c70378a6dd.title: Non-monotonic Inference
248d7081-8f9d-4713-ad98-a4c70378a6dd.definition: A type of inference in which conclusions may change or be revoked as new information is added, as opposed to monotonic inference.

0134f59a-8a47-4b24-be66-34c0a8e656d8.title: Conditional Independence
0134f59a-8a47-4b24-be66-34c0a8e656d8.definition: Review the concept of two variables being conditionally independent of each other when the value of a third variable is known.

3e7c0996-f12d-4867-aa13-05309ee38ab7.title: Probabilistic Knowledge Representation
3e7c0996-f12d-4867-aa13-05309ee38ab7.definition: Methods for representing knowledge in probabilistic models, including how to represent uncertainty and stochastic relationships.

9e31a7ed-b7b4-445d-97c1-243a6eee4ad3.title: Bayesian Networks
9e31a7ed-b7b4-445d-97c1-243a6eee4ad3.definition: The probabilistic graphical model represents a set of variables and the conditionally independent relationships between them.

950ff792-8afc-49c7-aad4-e556f0563a2d.title: Exact Bayesian Inference
950ff792-8afc-49c7-aad4-e556f0563a2d.definition: Algorithms to calculate exact probability distributions of variables in a Bayesian Network given observational information.

0a2dace9-85c0-4837-9a5a-606db03fb65b.title: Bayesian Inference Complexity
0a2dace9-85c0-4837-9a5a-606db03fb65b.definition: An analysis of the computational cost and factors affecting the complexity of exact inference algorithms in Bayesian Networks.

017707fe-cb34-43c4-ae97-0a391ccbad34.title: Markov Blankets
017707fe-cb34-43c4-ae97-0a391ccbad34.definition: The set of nodes in a Bayesian Network such that, knowing their value, a node becomes independent of all other nodes in the network.

340bbc1a-aeb4-458c-92f1-ea10cfbae04b.title: d-separation
340bbc1a-aeb4-458c-92f1-ea10cfbae04b.definition: A graphical criterion for determining conditional independence between sets of variables in Bayesian Networks.

36cbd6f9-5baf-4119-af23-8e4dee5b53d7.title: Monte Carlo Sampling
36cbd6f9-5baf-4119-af23-8e4dee5b53d7.definition: Simulation techniques rely on random sampling to estimate quantities in complex probability models.

f099ae98-c024-4c76-b562-94e95f092758.title: Gibbs Sampling
f099ae98-c024-4c76-b562-94e95f092758.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling algorithm is used to sample from a multivariate probability distribution that is difficult to sample directly.

a03a3c60-0884-423b-bb65-47e9cdc13006.title: Markov Networks
a03a3c60-0884-423b-bb65-47e9cdc13006.definition: The undirected probability graph model represents dependency relationships between variables through potential functions on subgroups of variables.

81d6105e-d255-4785-8744-3999d0f7fc9a.title: Relational Probabilistic Models
81d6105e-d255-4785-8744-3999d0f7fc9a.definition: Probabilistic models extend probabilistic graph theory to represent relationships between entities, allowing inference and learning in complex domains.

f5c297b5-29fe-413e-bd25-e8942c0266ca.title: Hidden Markov Models (HMM)
f5c297b5-29fe-413e-bd25-e8942c0266ca.definition: A statistical model in which the system being modeled is assumed to be a Markov process with hidden states that are not directly observable, but can only be inferred from available observations.

f18bb9ab-79a6-4329-9554-bc54c10b3fe0.title: Decision Theory
f18bb9ab-79a6-4329-9554-bc54c10b3fe0.definition: The study of the decisions of agents when the consequences of their choices are not known with certainty, including probabilistic and utility inference methods.

d6c52145-42a8-47df-b7fd-f948086df7fd.title: Preferences and Utility Functions
d6c52145-42a8-47df-b7fd-f948086df7fd.definition: Concepts in decision theory for quantifying the degree of desirability or value that an agent assigns to various outcomes or states.

1f09487f-60f2-4ea7-ae9b-187f12b1b2a7.title: Expected Utility Maximization
1f09487f-60f2-4ea7-ae9b-187f12b1b2a7.definition: A principle in decision theory according to which a rational agent should choose the action that maximizes the total expected value (utility) of all possible outcomes.

0068ecc8-101a-4b51-85ba-5962ef7c7f3b.title: Game Theory
0068ecc8-101a-4b51-85ba-5962ef7c7f3b.definition: Study mathematical models of conflict and cooperation between intelligent and rational decision-making agents.

6fbbf083-7595-4725-a293-4e8525bede2e.title: Propositional & First-Order Logic
6fbbf083-7595-4725-a293-4e8525bede2e.definition: Review the fundamentals of propositional and first-order logic, used as the foundation for knowledge representation and reasoning in AI.

05279423-09c3-4d53-a4b5-dc4c46c2e34d.title: Planning Operators & State Representation
05279423-09c3-4d53-a4b5-dc4c46c2e34d.definition: How to identify possible actions (operators) and how to describe states of the world in AI planning problems.

5e0a14bf-9125-4b55-b801-1f9eea1fe85c.title: Total Order Planning
5e0a14bf-9125-4b55-b801-1f9eea1fe85c.definition: A planning method in which all actions in the plan are arranged in a specific linear order.

48626b8f-70f2-4102-a801-c6430cd19452.title: Partial Order Planning
48626b8f-70f2-4102-a801-c6430cd19452.definition: A planning method in which only the necessary ordering constraints between actions are specified, allowing unrelated actions to be performed in parallel or in any order.

430c8514-ea51-422c-80d0-68860799da92.title: Plan Graphs & GraphPlan
430c8514-ea51-422c-80d0-68860799da92.definition: Techniques for representing planning problems in graph form to find effective solutions, such as the GraphPlan algorithm.

668fe32b-e954-447c-9aa9-fcb4bab03d7f.title: Hierarchical Planning
668fe32b-e954-447c-9aa9-fcb4bab03d7f.definition: A planning method that divides a large problem into smaller, more abstract sub-problems and solves them in a hierarchical structure.

caf38934-057b-4f62-b9fe-95fbc631b3dd.title: Planning Languages & Representation
caf38934-057b-4f62-b9fe-95fbc631b3dd.definition: Standard languages ​​and methods for describing planning problems, including states, goals, and operators.

4692d0b8-5377-4212-a424-ba2f6005a399.title: PDDL
4692d0b8-5377-4212-a424-ba2f6005a399.definition: A standardized language used to describe planning domains and problems in AI, allowing different planners to work on the same problem definition.

88dd1846-256c-4774-a784-db1715301a30.title: Multi-agent Planning
88dd1846-256c-4774-a784-db1715301a30.definition: Plan for systems that include multiple interacting agents, where each agent may have its own goals and need to coordinate actions.

b8bb94ff-fae5-4957-b3cb-c3af4b071c76.title: MDP-based Planning
b8bb94ff-fae5-4957-b3cb-c3af4b071c76.definition: Planning in uncertain environments using a Markov Decision Process framework to find optimal action policies.

f5dfd9ee-ac5b-4a8a-a2a5-dc0b859a9fa6.title: Planning, Execution & Replanning
f5dfd9ee-ac5b-4a8a-a2a5-dc0b859a9fa6.definition: The study of how plans are created, implemented, and continuously adjusted in changing or uncertain environments.

23016a27-e208-4a86-9ef7-b32e49a9b1ff.title: Conditional Planning
23016a27-e208-4a86-9ef7-b32e49a9b1ff.definition: A type of planning that creates plans with ramifications, allowing the agent to react to uncertain outcomes of actions.

9b08ff60-91db-47cb-a9b3-dde384650652.title: Continuous Planning
9b08ff60-91db-47cb-a9b3-dde384650652.definition: Plan in environments where time and actions can occur continuously rather than discretely.

c582ff5b-8aa1-45c9-83f9-dd6f0e01b705.title: Probabilistic Planning
c582ff5b-8aa1-45c9-83f9-dd6f0e01b705.definition: Planning in environments where the outcomes of actions are uncertain and described by probability distributions.

1064fa74-fc00-4866-9de5-8d71ec8f6306.title: Agent Architectures
1064fa74-fc00-4866-9de5-8d71ec8f6306.definition: Frameworks, or structural designs for building intelligent agents, dictate how they process information, make decisions, and perform actions.

a59588db-148e-4c09-ab7e-dfca41b91170.title: Reactive Agent Architectures
a59588db-148e-4c09-ab7e-dfca41b91170.definition: Simple agent architectures respond directly to environmental stimuli without the need to plan or maintain internal models.

0302ae5f-4e13-43c9-a52c-c30fda47c488.title: Layered Agent
0302ae5f-4e13-43c9-a52c-c30fda47c488.definition: Agent architectures include multiple layers to handle behaviors at different levels of abstraction, combining reaction and planning.

cc7b72e0-2482-465d-ba61-f6925cbd0788.title: Cognitive Agent
cc7b72e0-2482-465d-ba61-f6925cbd0788.definition: Agent architectures simulate human cognitive abilities such as reasoning, learning, planning, and knowledge maintenance.

86b06074-26e8-4980-a7df-33e1b6fe97cc.title: Agent Theory
86b06074-26e8-4980-a7df-33e1b6fe97cc.definition: Theoretical study of intelligent agents, including mathematical formulas to describe their behavior, goals, and interactions.

a3b414c7-9749-4333-a9bb-1bf28784cd2f.title: Agent Rationality
a3b414c7-9749-4333-a9bb-1bf28784cd2f.definition: The concept of rational agent behavior, where the agent acts to achieve its goals in the most efficient manner, based on available information.

f568bbd5-4c31-47d6-86b4-c237e2c1d464.title: Game Theory
f568bbd5-4c31-47d6-86b4-c237e2c1d464.definition: The study of strategies and interactions of intelligent and rational agents in competitive or cooperative situations, especially in the context of multi-agent systems.

8a2df9f1-e46f-4db4-aa40-f41045e2ec4c.title: Decision-Theoretic Agent
8a2df9f1-e46f-4db4-aa40-f41045e2ec4c.definition: Agents make decisions based on the principles of decision theory, considering the utility and probability of different outcomes.

3db43cd2-afe0-4fe3-aeee-6f46fd243138.title: Agent MDP
3db43cd2-afe0-4fe3-aeee-6f46fd243138.definition: Use Markov Decision Processes to model and solve agent decision-making problems in dynamic and uncertain environments.

c160bdab-e11d-44e2-b078-a1f7d0aeb835.title: Bandit Algorithms
c160bdab-e11d-44e2-b078-a1f7d0aeb835.definition: Algorithms are used for explore-exploit problems, where an agent must make repeated choices from a set of options (arm) to maximize the reward.

f76bf2a8-cbbb-414c-886c-381a89c62684.title: Software Agent
f76bf2a8-cbbb-414c-886c-381a89c62684.definition: Computer programs perform autonomous tasks on behalf of users or other programs in a digital environment.

69821394-4dc9-4cae-aa51-4d748c3d4f9a.title: Personal AI Assistant
69821394-4dc9-4cae-aa51-4d748c3d4f9a.definition: Software agents are designed to assist users in daily tasks, providing information and automating activities.

cc02c88a-200b-47f4-a8ab-a62812b635fa.title: Info Retrieval Agent
cc02c88a-200b-47f4-a8ab-a62812b635fa.definition: Agents specialize in searching, retrieving, and filtering information from different sources for users.

4363df54-be55-47a3-bc74-f7f14918fa53.title: Collaborative Agent
4363df54-be55-47a3-bc74-f7f14918fa53.definition: Agents work together to achieve a common goal or share information to improve each other's performance, applicable in both software agents and multi-agent systems.

f590e320-30fa-48fe-8931-ec973e59f713.title: Information Gathering Agent
f590e320-30fa-48fe-8931-ec973e59f713.definition: Agents are designed to automatically collect and synthesize information from their environment.

2da758cf-c3fc-45c9-a3d5-7049f2fbe543.title: Trustworthy Agent
2da758cf-c3fc-45c9-a3d5-7049f2fbe543.definition: Agents are designed to exhibit human-like characteristics or emotions to enhance user trust and engagement.

b2feaa3f-77ae-41ca-8dca-76a11f0af8dc.title: Agent Emotion Modeling
b2feaa3f-77ae-41ca-8dca-76a11f0af8dc.definition: Techniques and methods for AI agents to recognize, express, and react to emotions, to create more natural interactions.

902e60e2-b80b-418a-8b95-96e228646363.title: Learning Agent
902e60e2-b80b-418a-8b95-96e228646363.definition: Agents have the ability to improve their performance over time by learning from experience or data.

95c8104d-b5c7-4d37-ae86-98c256437aa9.title: Cognitive Systems
95c8104d-b5c7-4d37-ae86-98c256437aa9.definition: AI systems are designed to simulate and replicate human cognitive abilities such as learning, reasoning, memory, problem solving, and decision making.

23b0acb3-f3f7-4aac-9296-acb687ca9597.title: Cognitive Architectures
23b0acb3-f3f7-4aac-9296-acb687ca9597.definition: Frameworks or theories about the overall structure of a cognitive system, integrating different information processing capabilities.

7c0110a0-1400-4663-a737-146ecded2d3b.title: ACT-R Architecture
7c0110a0-1400-4663-a737-146ecded2d3b.definition: A cognitive architecture developed at Carnegie Mellon University, focused on modeling human cognition and learning, including memory components and modules.

6859d016-868e-44d6-9ae1-c3f7a33f5ad8.title: SOAR Architecture
6859d016-868e-44d6-9ae1-c3f7a33f5ad8.definition: An artificial intelligence synthesis and cognitive architecture designed to solve problems by searching the state space and using 'chunking' to learn.

a0b6cbdc-c412-4f21-bc9e-6bfa48b62347.title: ICARUS Architecture
a0b6cbdc-c412-4f21-bc9e-6bfa48b62347.definition: A cognitive architecture focuses on high-level cognitive modeling, conceptual learning, and goal-based planning.

ccf601e9-8148-4973-b56b-50d9f275da8b.title: FORR Architecture
ccf601e9-8148-4973-b56b-50d9f275da8b.definition: A cognitive architecture designed to model decision making and learning, especially in strategically demanding tasks.

b5296d08-4638-4ca4-b634-b19d6d9bdebb.title: Cognitive Perception
b5296d08-4638-4ca4-b634-b19d6d9bdebb.definition: The ability of a cognitive system to collect, interpret, and process information from the environment through sensors or input data.

a0b1bee1-bf4f-449e-bf1b-6d82bf172c86.title: Cognitive Decision Making
a0b1bee1-bf4f-449e-bf1b-6d82bf172c86.definition: The process by which the cognitive system chooses between different actions or outcomes, often based on goals, knowledge, and available information.

c8a82575-a44f-4120-843e-639fe92baef9.title: Cognitive Prediction
c8a82575-a44f-4120-843e-639fe92baef9.definition: The ability of a cognitive system to estimate future events or states based on current and past information.

6f4dcb0a-3090-49f8-9782-37c1203fe23b.title: Cognitive Knowledge Maintenance
6f4dcb0a-3090-49f8-9782-37c1203fe23b.definition: Processes and techniques for updating, modifying, and managing the knowledge base of a cognitive system over time.

04309cdd-cada-4330-b1de-53aa088a8c51.title: Cognitive Knowledge Representation
04309cdd-cada-4330-b1de-53aa088a8c51.definition: How knowledge is encoded and stored so that cognitive systems can use it to reason and make decisions.

c58bcf9d-f60e-4b5e-97e2-cf8e8085617a.title: Cognitive Knowledge Organization
c58bcf9d-f60e-4b5e-97e2-cf8e8085617a.definition: Methods for structuring and organizing knowledge to optimize retrieval and use in cognitive systems.

598db06c-31e9-42e6-be8e-a578ddc9b2cd.title: Cognitive Knowledge Utilization
598db06c-31e9-42e6-be8e-a578ddc9b2cd.definition: How the cognitive system applies existing knowledge to solve problems, make decisions, or perform tasks.

06f2c88d-6f36-468d-83b4-0c6311f23b08.title: Cognitive Knowledge Acquisition
06f2c88d-6f36-468d-83b4-0c6311f23b08.definition: Methods and processes for capturing new knowledge from the environment, data, or people and integrating it into cognitive systems.

372108ae-a1b9-4ef9-af60-208d59c406aa.title: Cognitive Knowledge Refinement
372108ae-a1b9-4ef9-af60-208d59c406aa.definition: The process of improving the accuracy, completeness, and efficiency of knowledge in a cognitive system through learning or feedback.

ab3e8e31-40f8-4b60-aae0-ac993e957f6c.title: Cognitive System Evaluation
ab3e8e31-40f8-4b60-aae0-ac993e957f6c.definition: Practical use cases of cognitive systems and methods to evaluate their performance, efficiency, and rationality.

2a3f3d92-952c-44be-b274-03ee973a86be.title: Multi-Agent Systems
2a3f3d92-952c-44be-b274-03ee973a86be.definition: Systems consist of multiple agents that interact with each other and with the environment to achieve their own goals or common goals.

88018362-ab81-4c09-8e39-084641b0fb06.title: Agent Teams
88018362-ab81-4c09-8e39-084641b0fb06.definition: A collection of collaborating actors with assigned roles and responsibilities to perform more complex tasks.

8631f25f-6263-4e54-b85c-38edb0038bee.title: Competitive Agents
8631f25f-6263-4e54-b85c-38edb0038bee.definition: Agents in a multi-agent system have conflicting goals and compete with each other to maximize their own utility or reward.

7b742e14-bd52-43c2-95f4-3d34a2686b3a.title: MAS Auctions
7b742e14-bd52-43c2-95f4-3d34a2686b3a.definition: Application of auction mechanisms to allocate resources or tasks among competing agents in a multi-agent system.

7c57c6ed-53bb-4ca6-b4bc-c8ec34759e2c.title: MAS Voting
7c57c6ed-53bb-4ca6-b4bc-c8ec34759e2c.definition: Voting methods and algorithms for aggregating the preferences or decisions of multiple agents into a common choice.

d9a0072c-916c-488b-ac11-84a3fb0a4572.title: Swarm Intelligence
d9a0072c-916c-488b-ac11-84a3fb0a4572.definition: Multi-agent systems simulate the collective behavior of populations of organisms (such as ants, birds) to solve problems.

7282c0bb-de67-4df9-8642-d9ecb4b24e04.title: MAS Learning
7282c0bb-de67-4df9-8642-d9ecb4b24e04.definition: The field that studies how agents in a multiagent system learn and adapt in their interacting environments.

c25ad772-d3a6-4bbc-aa27-0a7cadb1e7d5.title: Human-Agent Interaction
c25ad772-d3a6-4bbc-aa27-0a7cadb1e7d5.definition: The study of how humans and AI agents interact, including interface design, communication, and trust.

e3f2284a-11a7-435d-b9a4-c7d77ceb37c4.title: HAI Communication Methods
e3f2284a-11a7-435d-b9a4-c7d77ceb37c4.definition: The ways in which humans and AI agents exchange information, including both verbal and nonverbal communication.

88420bfc-c027-4c0a-8f25-e1b1e10d7ba8.title: HAI Verbal Communication
88420bfc-c027-4c0a-8f25-e1b1e10d7ba8.definition: The techniques and challenges of using spoken or written language for AI agents to interact with humans.

53e5ed02-564a-4777-b6ff-5159872123bd.title: HAI Nonverbal Communication
53e5ed02-564a-4777-b6ff-5159872123bd.definition: Research on how AI agents can use or interpret non-verbal signals such as gestures, facial expressions, and tone of voice to interact with humans.

dbda9fc7-bdce-47c6-94d8-93616d98fb89.title: HAI Practical Issues
dbda9fc7-bdce-47c6-94d8-93616d98fb89.definition: Practical challenges and considerations in designing, implementing, and maintaining AI human-agent interaction systems.

19e21f81-b586-40fd-b78c-c7ec733ca9c9.title: Transactional Agents
19e21f81-b586-40fd-b78c-c7ec733ca9c9.definition: AI agents are designed to carry out buying, selling, auctioning or negotiating activities in financial markets or e-commerce.

2f7e39e0-0375-48d9-b86d-78bd0d8be8d4.title: Agent-based Supply Chain
2f7e39e0-0375-48d9-b86d-78bd0d8be8d4.definition: apply AI agents to automate, optimize and manage supply chain processes.

b3faf053-7c89-4c46-aada-12f911bc9d9c.title: Ethical AI Interaction
b3faf053-7c89-4c46-aada-12f911bc9d9c.definition: Ethical concerns arise from AI systems' interactions with humans, including privacy, responsibility, bias, and fairness.

c4aa6977-2263-4ecd-b14c-da591b53c3d7.title: AI Interaction Regulations
c4aa6977-2263-4ecd-b14c-da591b53c3d7.definition: Legal and regulatory frameworks govern the design, deployment, and use of human-interactive AI systems to ensure safety, security, and fairness.

e1fa0bb0-b6d3-4b57-b6ad-921851f44035.title: NLP
e1fa0bb0-b6d3-4b57-b6ad-921851f44035.definition: The field of AI focuses on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate natural human language.

44aaafb8-11cd-4515-a1da-9dce08f82d61.title: Deterministic & Stochastic Grammar
44aaafb8-11cd-4515-a1da-9dce08f82d61.definition: understand and distinguish between deterministic grammars (which always produce the same result for the same input) and stochastic grammars (which use probability to choose between options).

8932fd94-7071-4450-a870-fb67a151f29c.title: Parsing Algorithms
8932fd94-7071-4450-a870-fb67a151f29c.definition: Research methods and algorithms to analyze the syntactic structure of a sentence in natural language.

4eb2f672-0001-4eff-93b6-edc154a722a3.title: CFG & CYK Parser
4eb2f672-0001-4eff-93b6-edc154a722a3.definition: Learn about Context-Free Grammar (CFG) and graph parsing algorithms like CYK, which are used to determine whether a string belongs to a specific grammar.

2d045a21-6beb-4d10-bc5e-d0535bcf8c5c.title: PCFG & Weighted CYK
2d045a21-6beb-4d10-bc5e-d0535bcf8c5c.definition: Research on Probabilistic Context-Free Grammar (PCFG) and how the CYK algorithm can be extended to handle probabilities in grammars.

50452273-84e8-4126-aaf2-cc8983135fed.title: Semantic Representation
50452273-84e8-4126-aaf2-cc8983135fed.definition: Explore methods for representing the semantic meaning of natural language, a core task in Natural Language Processing.

04520e56-75dd-45ab-9761-09815e37b303.title: Logic Knowledge Representation
04520e56-75dd-45ab-9761-09815e37b303.definition: Learn how to use formal logic to represent and reason on knowledge from natural language.

f09dbfb0-a390-42a1-be57-6eb9c3c9f3eb.title: Semantic Roles
f09dbfb0-a390-42a1-be57-6eb9c3c9f3eb.definition: Study how entities in a sentence play different roles (e.g., agent, object, tool) in an event or action.

33d52f82-508e-42b2-9fc3-140dcea9552e.title: Temporal Representation
33d52f82-508e-42b2-9fc3-140dcea9552e.definition: Explore methods for representing and reasoning about temporal information extracted from text.

8a9395a3-67a2-4799-97d9-a605ddeae90d.title: BDI Model
8a9395a3-67a2-4799-97d9-a605ddeae90d.definition: The study of cognitive models for representing the beliefs, desires, and intentions of agents, especially in the context of language processing and social reasoning.

5dd507ce-9a5e-4002-94ec-b37fac2e9a1a.title: Corpus-based Methods
5dd507ce-9a5e-4002-94ec-b37fac2e9a1a.definition: Learn about using large data sets (corpora) to analyze, model, and develop NLP applications.

5fcc4ce1-9418-4100-a732-dbcba561895d.title: N-gram & HMM
5fcc4ce1-9418-4100-a732-dbcba561895d.definition: Study statistical models such as N-grams (sequences of words) and Hidden Markov Models (HMM) to predict and analyze sequences in natural language.

523647a1-74ca-4607-a4cb-7ab7de07dc99.title: Smoothing & Backoff
523647a1-74ca-4607-a4cb-7ab7de07dc99.definition: Learn smoothing and redundancy techniques for handling invisible events (sparse data) in statistical language models.

040637ba-f2a9-4ed7-9614-90cacd862750.title: POS Tagging & Morphology
040637ba-f2a9-4ed7-9614-90cacd862750.definition: Study practical applications of NLP such as word-class tagging (assigning word-class labels to each word) and morphology (studying word structure).

1162ebe7-da4a-4631-99a3-443ed64a1bfd.title: Information Retrieval
1162ebe7-da4a-4631-99a3-443ed64a1bfd.definition: Learn about methods and systems for searching and retrieving relevant information from a document collection.

e316d358-635b-4f03-9762-06a3078bbdda.title: Vector Space Model
e316d358-635b-4f03-9762-06a3078bbdda.definition: Study the vector space model, where documents and queries are represented as vectors to calculate similarity.

3ef04196-47af-41ea-b62d-5a71d9ea357a.title: TF-IDF
3ef04196-47af-41ea-b62d-5a71d9ea357a.definition: Learn about the TF (Term Frequency) and IDF (Inverse Document Frequency) statistics used to evaluate the importance of a word in a document and in a collection of documents.

80057504-aba2-4680-b279-26eb880b54cc.title: Precision & Recall
80057504-aba2-4680-b279-26eb880b54cc.definition: Study important performance metrics such as precision and recall in information retrieval and classification tasks.

adb629d8-296a-442f-a5e3-e6f03c6283d3.title: Information Extraction
adb629d8-296a-442f-a5e3-e6f03c6283d3.definition: Learn about techniques for automatically extracting structured information from unstructured text.

9573f88a-a377-406f-adda-ec70dd6813a7.title: Machine Translation
9573f88a-a377-406f-adda-ec70dd6813a7.definition: Research methods and models to automatically translate text from one language to another.

327b5f42-891b-42f1-a3d2-eacc1bffb344.title: Text Classification & Clustering
327b5f42-891b-42f1-a3d2-eacc1bffb344.definition: Learn about methods for assigning predefined labels or categories to text.

507e153f-ce7a-4dcf-9a39-2565641ee22a.title: Bag-of-Words Model
507e153f-ce7a-4dcf-9a39-2565641ee22a.definition: Study the bag of words model, a simple representation in NLP and information retrieval, where word order is ignored and only word frequency is considered.

c409383c-b0fc-45b6-8c0e-c475f9e5934f.title: Deep Learning for NLP
c409383c-b0fc-45b6-8c0e-c475f9e5934f.definition: Learn advanced deep learning techniques applied in the field of Natural Language Processing.

a1ded43c-2253-4c23-8e6c-c14157177a56.title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)
a1ded43c-2253-4c23-8e6c-c14157177a56.definition: Research Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), a type of neural network suitable for processing sequence data such as text.

e88b2914-1e20-48df-9586-96b0d36f9121.title: Transformer Model
e88b2914-1e20-48df-9586-96b0d36f9121.definition: Learn about the Transformer architecture, an advanced model based on self-attention, revolutionizing NLP tasks.

34a5ee98-6b72-4810-85a2-9485f8982b68.title: Multimodal Embeddings
34a5ee98-6b72-4810-85a2-9485f8982b68.definition: Study how to represent data from multiple modalities (e.g., text, images) into a common vector space to understand multimodal context.

ec93d487-dcf1-4f06-b93e-145792245f1c.title: Generative Language Models
ec93d487-dcf1-4f06-b93e-145792245f1c.definition: Learn about language models that produce new, coherent, and meaningful text.

592a5f0c-c516-49ff-897b-419616d3d31e.title: Robotics Overview
592a5f0c-c516-49ff-897b-419616d3d31e.definition: Overview of current challenges, unsolved problems, and significant advances in the field of robotics.

d2a387b8-c52a-4582-a8e0-1a9ad6f375f2.title: Modern Robotic Systems & Sensors
d2a387b8-c52a-4582-a8e0-1a9ad6f375f2.definition: Explore the most advanced robotic systems, the types of sensors they use, and how sensor data is processed for decision making.

5af0e715-0174-421c-9ac6-6229939c33df.title: Robot Control Architectures
5af0e715-0174-421c-9ac6-6229939c33df.definition: Study different ways to design robot control systems, including proactive (planning) and reactive (sensor-based) architectures, along with the Braitenberg vehicle concept.

0ae644b5-7908-4a57-9185-ee4c15dfc20c.title: Robotics World Models
0ae644b5-7908-4a57-9185-ee4c15dfc20c.definition: Learn how robots build and maintain internal representations of their surroundings (world models) to plan and navigate.

305a4db4-a77e-4ae2-9b15-a6024a8e6aa1.title: Robotics Uncertainty
305a4db4-a77e-4ae2-9b15-a6024a8e6aa1.definition: Explores the nature of uncertainties in sensor data and in the implementation of robot control actions, as well as methods for managing them.

1783fc6d-dcaa-4b2a-920e-1cde153fc749.title: Robotics Sensors & Actuators
1783fc6d-dcaa-4b2a-920e-1cde153fc749.definition: Learn about the input devices (sensors) and output devices (actuators) that robots use to interact with the physical world.

e428d1a5-83e2-4fef-a4f2-b6b15ecf115c.title: Robotics Sensors
e428d1a5-83e2-4fef-a4f2-b6b15ecf115c.definition: Study specific types of sensors used in robotics, including LIDAR, sonar, vision systems, depth sensors, stereoscopic, event cameras, microphones, and tactile sensors.

15c26f70-1686-408d-a1ce-5408ac3a7fed.title: Robotics Actuators
15c26f70-1686-408d-a1ce-5408ac3a7fed.definition: Learn about the types of actuators that robots use to move, manipulate, or physically interact, such as wheels, robotic arms, and grippers.

2eca49e5-0463-438c-9cab-8b1373695dc8.title: Robotics Coordinate Systems
2eca49e5-0463-438c-9cab-8b1373695dc8.definition: Study how to represent the position and orientation of a robot and its components using coordinate systems, translations and rotations in 2D and 3D space.

bc18f05d-8194-4640-910e-ad4d0d49e184.title: Configuration Space & Maps
bc18f05d-8194-4640-910e-ad4d0d49e184.definition: Learn about the configuration space (the set of all possible positions and orientations of the robot) and the types of environment maps used to plan the robot's movements.

7b2d32c9-7acd-4f5a-b903-d9f2d49ee463.title: Uncertain Sensor Data Interpretation
7b2d32c9-7acd-4f5a-b903-d9f2d49ee463.definition: Study methods and algorithms for processing and interpreting data from robotic sensors, which often contain uncertainty and noise.

88238159-221b-49c0-97ed-6819c324ea22.title: SLAM in Robotics
88238159-221b-49c0-97ed-6819c324ea22.definition: Learn about the Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) problem, where a robot builds a map of its environment while simultaneously tracking its own position within that map.

68eda592-79da-4bfa-82ed-e65f698bf8d1.title: Robotics Navigation & Control
68eda592-79da-4bfa-82ed-e65f698bf8d1.definition: Study of algorithms and strategies that allow robots to move through their environment autonomously and perform the necessary control actions.

696babf5-d658-4df1-970f-efc2e1617d3e.title: Forward & Inverse Kinematics
696babf5-d658-4df1-970f-efc2e1617d3e.definition: Learn about forward kinematics (determining the final position based on joint angles) and inverse kinematics (determining joint angles to achieve the desired final position) of a robot arm.

2c93a519-0136-4158-a7fe-e6b01ad6d453.title: Motion Planning & Trajectory Opt.
2c93a519-0136-4158-a7fe-e6b01ad6d453.definition: Research algorithms to find safe and effective paths for robots to move in environments with obstacles, as well as optimize trajectories according to criteria such as time or energy.

df1473bb-4e6c-4e14-bbbf-229e418a4345.title: Robotics Manipulation & Grasping
df1473bb-4e6c-4e14-bbbf-229e418a4345.definition: Learn about techniques and strategies for robots to manipulate and grasp various objects in physical environments.

87e50cee-b117-425d-bf38-6c92a6e8f338.title: Joint Control & Dynamics
87e50cee-b117-425d-bf38-6c92a6e8f338.definition: Study how to control each individual joint of the robot and understand how the dynamics (force, torque) affect the robot's movements.

61ad8853-0139-4f77-9a6e-f5bcbbcbd429.title: Vision-based Robot Control
61ad8853-0139-4f77-9a6e-f5bcbbcbd429.definition: Learn about robot control systems that use data from visual sensors (cameras) to guide movement and interaction.

1e51ab08-a879-4173-a5a5-3aa03e088cc2.title: Multi-Robot Coordination
1e51ab08-a879-4173-a5a5-3aa03e088cc2.definition: Research methods for multiple robots to work together effectively to complete a common task, including task assignment and communication.

77483937-11f3-42e7-90dd-15cc2d619034.title: Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
77483937-11f3-42e7-90dd-15cc2d619034.definition: Explore the research field of how humans and robots can interact naturally and effectively.

106f692a-865d-4c99-a2b3-3c5df20ee555.title: Shared Workspace HRI
106f692a-865d-4c99-a2b3-3c5df20ee555.definition: Learn about scenarios and designs where humans and robots share a physical space to perform tasks.

6239a492-3abe-4f63-ac41-886928a7adab.title: Human-Robot Teaming & Physical HRI
6239a492-3abe-4f63-ac41-886928a7adab.definition: Research on how humans and robots can form teams to complete tasks, including direct physical interaction between the two.

3bc1e004-8172-455f-b043-082d5692eb6a.title: Socially Assistive Robots
3bc1e004-8172-455f-b043-082d5692eb6a.definition: Learn about robots designed to assist humans in social, educational or healthcare activities.

581eb00a-d76a-4d27-8b29-984c0ffeed7c.title: HRI Intent Prediction
581eb00a-d76a-4d27-8b29-984c0ffeed7c.definition: Research methods for robots to predict human actions, tasks or goals to improve coordination in HRI.

c5e09607-202b-4eb5-bda8-a00df7092644.title: HRI Collaboration & Communication
c5e09607-202b-4eb5-bda8-a00df7092644.definition: Learn diverse forms of human-robot communication and cooperation, from explicit commands to nonverbal signals, to achieve common goals.

6eceab6b-751d-46c6-9952-09acf88345e6.title: Robot-Human Trust
6eceab6b-751d-46c6-9952-09acf88345e6.definition: Research the importance of trust and factors that influence the building, maintenance or loss of trust between humans and robots.

c0f8d2fc-9118-45d1-90fb-5530e86e4793.title: Robotics Impact
c0f8d2fc-9118-45d1-90fb-5530e86e4793.definition: Explore the diverse applications of robotics and analyze the social, economic, and ethical impacts associated with their deployment.

e581c21a-01ff-4711-92f4-01261ff07007.title: Robot Labor Impact
e581c21a-01ff-4711-92f4-01261ff07007.definition: Research the broader impacts of robotics on society, the economy and the labor market, including right-to-work issues.

39c5f7ca-961d-4d3e-a4b9-47d9a0ded37b.title: Robot Privacy Ethics
39c5f7ca-961d-4d3e-a4b9-47d9a0ded37b.definition: analyze ethical and privacy issues arising from the use of robots, especially robots capable of collecting sensitive data or interacting with humans.

3579493e-5697-49dd-8e33-18a67194ad56.title: Autonomous Robot Liability
3579493e-5697-49dd-8e33-18a67194ad56.definition: Research legal frameworks and challenges in determining liability when autonomous robots cause damage or accidents.

75166c2d-f114-48de-8094-d209bc9d30f5.title: Autonomous Weapons Ethics
75166c2d-f114-48de-8094-d209bc9d30f5.definition: Discusses the ethical and social issues involved in the development and use of fully autonomous weapons systems capable of making killing decisions without human intervention.

c0a4ac71-aea8-4ae2-9341-2512c6309d94.title: Human Supervision Robotics
c0a4ac71-aea8-4ae2-9341-2512c6309d94.definition: Research the importance and methods to ensure humans can still effectively monitor and control autonomous robotic systems.

553caab3-144a-4fec-988f-d3fbe10adf0e.title: Robot Navigation Strategies
553caab3-144a-4fec-988f-d3fbe10adf0e.definition: Study different methods and algorithms for robots to move in environments with complete or incomplete information, including path planning, obstacle avoidance, and positioning.

fa219529-cfee-41b5-ac13-205b67a6930a.title: Robot Navigation Analysis
fa219529-cfee-41b5-ac13-205b67a6930a.definition: evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of different robot navigation strategies, considering their effectiveness, reliability, and applicability in specific situations.

08edf0bb-494b-4bdb-99d8-963593846e2f.title: Multi-Robot Coordination
08edf0bb-494b-4bdb-99d8-963593846e2f.definition: Methods and algorithms for synchronizing and managing the actions of a group of robots to complete a common task.

3ce6bde1-c4ad-415d-aa95-990fef4e4f74.title: Multi-Robot Sensor Fusion
3ce6bde1-c4ad-415d-aa95-990fef4e4f74.definition: Methods for robots to share and integrate sensor data from multiple sources to gain a more comprehensive view of the environment and support common missions.

928ed787-b09c-42bf-85a6-d26e9441d4dd.title: Multi-Robot vs. HRI
928ed787-b09c-42bf-85a6-d26e9441d4dd.definition: analyze the differences in goals, methods, and challenges between collaborative autonomous robotic systems and robotic systems that work alongside humans.

3c60a6c2-dae5-4592-8130-9f39b717ca45.title: Multi-Robot vs. HRI Contexts
3c60a6c2-dae5-4592-8130-9f39b717ca45.definition: Study how requirements, constraints, and characteristics of the task environment shape different approaches to multi-robot coordination and human-robot collaboration.

d8a87ef0-9785-45fe-8b94-a7737fa98f68.title: Robot Social Impact
d8a87ef0-9785-45fe-8b94-a7737fa98f68.definition: analyzes the impacts of robotics on society, including employment, social interaction, and cultural change.

1dfdb263-1a1d-494c-9bbb-56c63092b603.title: Robot Economic Impact
1dfdb263-1a1d-494c-9bbb-56c63092b603.definition: analyze the economic impacts of robotics, including productivity, production costs, and resource distribution.

157a8425-bf96-476d-98d9-175d6c72bec2.title: Robot Ethics
157a8425-bf96-476d-98d9-175d6c72bec2.definition: analyze ethical issues related to robot design, deployment, and use, such as privacy, responsibility, and fairness.

11b3d663-fd30-4c9b-9af7-d15abed3dec7.title: Computer Vision
11b3d663-fd30-4c9b-9af7-d15abed3dec7.definition: The field that studies how computers can 'understand' and process images and videos from the real world, including methods of image acquisition, representation and analysis.

fc560e3d-f037-469a-bd5c-3b12f836b53e.title: Image Acquisition
fc560e3d-f037-469a-bd5c-3b12f836b53e.definition: Methods and technologies for collecting image data from sensor devices such as cameras.

8a3e385f-f6b3-4c71-b892-9b7bb1f7ae87.title: Image Representation
8a3e385f-f6b3-4c71-b892-9b7bb1f7ae87.definition: Ways to store and structure image data for computer processing, such as pixel matrices, histograms, or feature-based descriptions.

c1e53c40-eef5-4620-84b8-3993156aed75.title: Image Processing
c1e53c40-eef5-4620-84b8-3993156aed75.definition: Techniques for transforming, enhancing, or extracting information from digital images, including filtering, transforming, and restoring images.

e1cefdee-cf4c-44e9-948b-56840ee0b1c6.title: Image Properties
e1cefdee-cf4c-44e9-948b-56840ee0b1c6.definition: Image characteristics and properties such as brightness, contrast, color, texture, and shape.

c420fe61-a3ec-4812-9c45-de48d8ef1447.title: Shape Representation
c420fe61-a3ec-4812-9c45-de48d8ef1447.definition: Methods for describing and encoding the shape of an object in an image, such as by contour, region, or geometric feature.

08edb7cb-fe9b-4319-9d4a-b8b011122d19.title: Object Recognition
08edb7cb-fe9b-4319-9d4a-b8b011122d19.definition: The process of identifying and classifying specific objects in an image or video.

94fc63a4-1530-4d8c-bb0d-8b205c7aaa3a.title: Image Segmentation
94fc63a4-1530-4d8c-bb0d-8b205c7aaa3a.definition: Technique of dividing a digital image into segments (sets of pixels) to simplify or change the image representation, making analysis easier.

90f17a33-d78a-46e8-9822-a380649bdac3.title: Motion Analysis (CV)
90f17a33-d78a-46e8-9822-a380649bdac3.definition: Techniques for detecting, tracking, and estimating object or camera motion in an image or video sequence.

2ae2c133-7a27-473c-9dc2-bf2aafc9d6f3.title: Generative Models (CV)
2ae2c133-7a27-473c-9dc2-bf2aafc9d6f3.definition: Machine learning models are capable of generating new image data similar to training data, which is used in image synthesis, quality enhancement, and style transformation.

ed91c741-fc35-420e-b5c2-0b4c105fa44c.title: Audio Recognition
ed91c741-fc35-420e-b5c2-0b4c105fa44c.definition: The computer process of identifying and classifying different types of sounds (e.g., environmental noise, animal sounds, music).

67329a2e-4f43-4df3-a989-452eea63cb97.title: Speech Recognition
67329a2e-4f43-4df3-a989-452eea63cb97.definition: Technology that converts spoken language into text, allowing computers to understand and respond to human speech.

af18e920-0a11-4508-817e-121ec064bcb3.title: Tactile Sensing
af18e920-0a11-4508-817e-121ec064bcb3.definition: Research on how AI systems process and interpret information from tactile sensors to physically interact with the environment.

073ddc73-dbdc-4235-9ece-d3ff1302bb19.title: Proprioception
073ddc73-dbdc-4235-9ece-d3ff1302bb19.definition: The ability of a robot or AI system to sense the position, orientation, and movement of its own body parts.

e24fb35c-37ba-4b34-85bf-a6107d23ddc5.title: AI Olfaction & Others
e24fb35c-37ba-4b34-85bf-a6107d23ddc5.definition: Explore other non-visual or auditory sensory modalities that AI can use, such as sensing smell (olfactory).

898ed24b-a607-4474-b3d5-4a70873d26f6.title: Modular Recognition
898ed24b-a607-4474-b3d5-4a70873d26f6.definition: Design identity systems into independent, exchangeable or reusable components, to improve flexibility and maintainability.

cadcf2c7-5d98-4bb6-b539-e9949195c70f.title: Pattern Recognition Methods
cadcf2c7-5d98-4bb6-b539-e9949195c70f.definition: Techniques and algorithms for finding and identifying patterns in data, often used for classification or clustering.

3e77ac0a-ee59-4d1f-acdd-c7f70b76e7ae.title: Classification Algorithms
3e77ac0a-ee59-4d1f-acdd-c7f70b76e7ae.definition: Machine learning algorithms are used to assign category labels to data points based on features learned from the training data set.

57aeec63-3a30-4de8-8def-106946873c63.title: Classification Metrics
57aeec63-3a30-4de8-8def-106946873c63.definition: Metrics and statistics used to evaluate the performance of a classification algorithm, such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score.

5097a971-1780-4349-974d-5d4cdfc95f0a.title: Statistical Pattern Recognition
5097a971-1780-4349-974d-5d4cdfc95f0a.definition: apply statistical methods such as Bayesian analysis and support vector machines (SVM) to build pattern recognition models.

762e470f-93a5-4417-a73d-8836b08aacbf.title: Deep Learning (PR)
762e470f-93a5-4417-a73d-8836b08aacbf.definition: Use deep neural networks, such as convolutional networks (CNN) and recurrent networks (RNN), to automatically learn features and perform high-performance pattern recognition.

f42df36e-baf4-4c88-9b3c-45851d2e35c1.title: Thresholding Segmentation
f42df36e-baf4-4c88-9b3c-45851d2e35c1.definition: A simple image segmentation method based on choosing a threshold value to separate pixels into two or more groups (e.g., foreground and background).

ad2706ae-d7be-41e0-8f24-15b4950ca78b.title: Edge-based Segmentation
ad2706ae-d7be-41e0-8f24-15b4950ca78b.definition: Image segmentation techniques are based on detecting boundaries and edges in images, where pixel intensities change suddenly.

eeedf4c3-f59f-4884-aeb8-74b977ae9361.title: Region-based Segmentation
eeedf4c3-f59f-4884-aeb8-74b977ae9361.definition: Image segmentation methods group neighboring pixels with similar properties (e.g., color, texture) into larger regions.

b2b3ba71-aa1c-495e-8fe8-0e0c30900349.title: Contour Shape Representation
b2b3ba71-aa1c-495e-8fe8-0e0c30900349.definition: A way to represent the shape of an object by describing its outer boundary (contour).

92d6975a-c62b-48e1-b736-ee6189cc19a6.title: Region Shape Representation
92d6975a-c62b-48e1-b736-ee6189cc19a6.definition: A way of representing the shape of an object by describing the properties of the region it occupies (e.g. area, center, moment).

b649b537-8a2f-4d53-9fc1-8322be49d790.title: Speaker Recognition
b649b537-8a2f-4d53-9fc1-8322be49d790.definition: The technology determines a speaker's identity from their voice, as opposed to recognizing speech content.

90ac641c-25e7-4277-af56-0b9753753a3b.title: Cross-Modal Data Conversion
90ac641c-25e7-4277-af56-0b9753753a3b.definition: Technique that transforms data from one type of sensor (e.g., tactile) into a format that can be processed by another sensory domain (e.g., visual).

9a869e61-f178-49f9-b713-af6f43c336b8.title: Feature Extraction Algorithms
