9a869e61-f178-49f9-b713-af6f43c336b8.definition: Algorithms are used to extract salient and meaningful features from raw data (e.g., images, sounds) to reduce data dimensionality and improve machine learning performance.

151e4b3e-82d3-4de5-97ae-9722394d7aad.title: Edge Detection
151e4b3e-82d3-4de5-97ae-9722394d7aad.definition: An image processing technique for identifying points in an image that have abrupt changes in pixel intensity, often representing the boundaries of objects.

21958e5a-e1d3-4f1e-996c-e3cdf7cf8bc0.title: Corner Detection
21958e5a-e1d3-4f1e-996c-e3cdf7cf8bc0.definition: An image processing technique for finding special points in an image where two edges intersect, often used as feature points for tracking or image registration.

31d90bec-0cca-49c8-bfbe-8759de3fc113.title: Audio Fourier Coefficients
31d90bec-0cca-49c8-bfbe-8759de3fc113.definition: apply Fourier transform to analyze the frequency spectrum of audio signals, extracting coefficients representing the frequency components of the signal.

f9254c1b-53a9-4b3d-b8ad-3ad4bf8bfeda.title: High-Level Perception Fusion
f9254c1b-53a9-4b3d-b8ad-3ad4bf8bfeda.definition: The process of synthesizing low-level features (e.g., edges, corners) into more complex perceptual concepts (e.g., contours, objects, phonemes).

5ed8d604-a981-480d-b6e8-5a4863f09457.title: Contour/Polygon Construction
5ed8d604-a981-480d-b6e8-5a4863f09457.definition: Algorithms combine basic visual features (such as line segments or points) to form more complex geometric structures such as contours or polygons of objects.

f3acab2a-7abf-4bcb-b347-02875efabf7c.title: Phoneme Hypothesis
f3acab2a-7abf-4bcb-b347-02875efabf7c.definition: The process of analyzing audio signals to make predictions about the phonemes (the smallest meaningful units of sound) present in speech.

83af7130-6f82-445e-b886-cd2f67f16e66.title: AI Fundamentals
83af7130-6f82-445e-b886-cd2f67f16e66.definition: Overview of the fundamental areas of Artificial Intelligence and the ability to understand, develop, and apply techniques in each area.

9a311438-d819-44ec-ac3d-c1b6f6b40d24.title: AI Search
9a311438-d819-44ec-ac3d-c1b6f6b40d24.definition: Ability to solve problems using search techniques in Artificial Intelligence.

f1eada2f-7496-4e96-8cd0-f510bc07f990.title: KRR
f1eada2f-7496-4e96-8cd0-f510bc07f990.definition: Knowledge of knowledge representation methods and inference techniques in Artificial Intelligence.

4e037d25-0e0c-4afc-945a-ead7dde793ac.title: ML Fundamentals
4e037d25-0e0c-4afc-945a-ead7dde793ac.definition: understand and apply simple machine learning methods to solve problems in Artificial Intelligence.

6c59c84e-7684-441b-af1d-9f4a766ce0d2.title: Bayesian Reasoning
6c59c84e-7684-441b-af1d-9f4a766ce0d2.definition: Knowledge of probability and ability to apply basic Bayesian reasoning to solve problems in AI.

abc542ea-6488-4672-a67f-7727c965a973.title: AI Ethics
abc542ea-6488-4672-a67f-7727c965a973.definition: Understanding of various applications of AI and related ethical and social impacts. This topic is integrated throughout the AI ​​course.

110ff028-5d2f-4769-820c-a102b947d5d4.title: ML Learning Types
110ff028-5d2f-4769-820c-a102b947d5d4.definition: Ability to understand, develop, and apply mechanisms for supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.

9e6733b1-bbab-49b4-903e-aa5661a0763b.title: ML KRR
9e6733b1-bbab-49b4-903e-aa5661a0763b.definition: Knowledge of knowledge representation and inference methods in the context of Machine Learning applications.

0958f53b-eae9-4bf0-b190-a648dab3237e.title: Selected NLP Topics
0958f53b-eae9-4bf0-b190-a648dab3237e.definition: Selected topics in Natural Language Processing, including TF-IDF, bag of words, and text classification.

1f039587-eda4-43a0-84fa-4b618d86f0e8.title: TF-IDF
1f039587-eda4-43a0-84fa-4b618d86f0e8.definition: TF-IDF technique to evaluate the importance of a word in a document compared to the entire document set.

6ee839d4-4a46-4e2c-9939-d6a3a66077ac.title: Bag of Words
6ee839d4-4a46-4e2c-9939-d6a3a66077ac.definition: Bag of Words model to represent text as a vector of word frequency counts, ignoring grammar and word order.

2b07729d-e8b9-4263-9ca6-7a594a8ee432.title: Text Classification
2b07729d-e8b9-4263-9ca6-7a594a8ee432.definition: Techniques for classifying text into defined categories.

e3332793-f51c-49ed-a53d-d9f92dea3a91.title: ML Ethics
e3332793-f51c-49ed-a53d-d9f92dea3a91.definition: Ability to explain the ethical and social implications of applying machine learning to real-world problems. This topic is integrated throughout the course.

1c843dac-596b-49d6-bda8-f0c548977f66.title: ML Algorithm Selection
1c843dac-596b-49d6-bda8-f0c548977f66.definition: Ability to select the most suitable machine learning algorithm for a specific problem.

4af5a8db-a5f5-4335-8d37-4670f9facdb3.title: ML Data Preprocessing
4af5a8db-a5f5-4335-8d37-4670f9facdb3.definition: Ability to appropriately preprocess data to prepare it for machine learning algorithms.

df4c1ba2-9a79-43c4-acab-9f4b2c990495.title: ML Evaluation Techniques
df4c1ba2-9a79-43c4-acab-9f4b2c990495.definition: Ability to apply appropriate evaluation techniques to measure machine learning model performance.

02cbec59-c7e2-463f-a8cb-bde6258d96c7.title: ML Model Interpretability
02cbec59-c7e2-463f-a8cb-bde6258d96c7.definition: Ability to explain trained machine learning models, including understanding their strengths and limitations.

88aae7d5-867d-4f25-a25a-214030d582eb.title: Detecting Data Bias & Errors
88aae7d5-867d-4f25-a25a-214030d582eb.definition: Ability to identify biased data sets and other sources of error that can affect machine learning results.

c804057e-b8ac-4851-9100-45ecbd534ecb.title: Data Bias Mitigation
c804057e-b8ac-4851-9100-45ecbd534ecb.definition: Ability to apply methods to compensate for biased data sets and minimize their impact.

648ce0d8-ffbe-48bc-9d5b-84536376fbd6.title: Supervised Learning
648ce0d8-ffbe-48bc-9d5b-84536376fbd6.definition: understand and apply the basic mechanisms and principles of supervised learning.

d16b5e57-4c8f-475c-9fe7-4263d087a286.title: Unsupervised Learning
d16b5e57-4c8f-475c-9fe7-4263d087a286.definition: understand and apply the basic mechanisms and principles of unsupervised learning.

efd1cb62-702e-4fbe-9a6e-a2196ab7c51f.title: Reinforcement Learning
efd1cb62-702e-4fbe-9a6e-a2196ab7c51f.definition: understand and apply the basic mechanisms and principles of reinforcement learning.

b6a7851b-b862-4212-8362-5ec3dbb584ce.title: Robotics Fundamentals
b6a7851b-b862-4212-8362-5ec3dbb584ce.definition: Ability to understand and use robotics techniques to perceive the world using sensors, position the robot, plan paths, and navigate in simple robotics applications.

9c4997cd-8462-419b-8814-a1ceaf80c50f.title: Robotics Hardware
9c4997cd-8462-419b-8814-a1ceaf80c50f.definition: Knowledge focuses on the robot's hardware, including components and structures.

19ff2d09-b250-48e1-b9f3-ab03b30263d9.title: Robotics Constraints
19ff2d09-b250-48e1-b9f3-ab03b30263d9.definition: Knowledge of important constraints and considerations in robot design, operation and programming.

bc5a705c-e492-464f-bcfc-141ffaacde96.title: Robotics Software Architecture
bc5a705c-e492-464f-bcfc-141ffaacde96.definition: Knowledge of software architectures used to develop and control robots.

6c919917-751d-41ab-92c6-6f5f1de2bfa1.title: Robotics Search Techniques
6c919917-751d-41ab-92c6-6f5f1de2bfa1.definition: Selected search topics are well integrated with robotics, e.g. A* algorithm and path search.

15c6dac4-1763-4aad-b680-564681f8f814.title: A* Search Algorithm
15c6dac4-1763-4aad-b680-564681f8f814.definition: understand and apply the A* search algorithm to plan optimal paths for robots.

7ee4733c-a4ea-4521-b2ea-a855e66df96a.title: Robotics Pathfinding
7ee4733c-a4ea-4521-b2ea-a855e66df96a.definition: Ability to plan paths and navigate robots in simple environments.

536b84e8-86f3-4f0c-bf88-c9b7fee3361c.title: Machine Learning in Robotics
536b84e8-86f3-4f0c-bf88-c9b7fee3361c.definition: Selected machine learning topics are well integrated with robotics, e.g. neural networks for object recognition.

b103daf2-fc4f-4034-9901-f1542108dfde.title: Object Recognition NNs
b103daf2-fc4f-4034-9901-f1542108dfde.definition: applying neural networks to object recognition tasks in robotics applications.

a1b518c9-de3b-4d71-80b9-e8aee71fb90a.title: Robotics Ethics
a1b518c9-de3b-4d71-80b9-e8aee71fb90a.definition: Focus on social impact and specific, integrated robotics applications throughout the robotics course.

769b447f-8872-4bed-8278-4b06b29089c5.title: Robot Sensor Perception
769b447f-8872-4bed-8278-4b06b29089c5.definition: Ability to use robotic techniques to collect and process information from sensors to perceive the environment.

73223b06-8af5-4aa7-8de8-40653d8065cf.title: Robot Localization
73223b06-8af5-4aa7-8de8-40653d8065cf.definition: The ability to locate the robot in the environment based on features and maps.

bc2a9cb0-79c1-48de-b8e9-f1702c602508.title: Robotics Computer Vision Basics
bc2a9cb0-79c1-48de-b8e9-f1702c602508.definition: Ability to understand and apply simple computer vision techniques in robotics applications.

8e803026-e557-4fbe-9de2-34e9f4933ed3.title: Robotics Motion Planning
8e803026-e557-4fbe-9de2-34e9f4933ed3.definition: Ability to understand and apply motion planning techniques for robots.

32645371-43a8-4594-a06e-7be0f2165f50.title: Forward Kinematics
32645371-43a8-4594-a06e-7be0f2165f50.definition: Ability to understand and apply forward kinematics techniques to determine the position and orientation of robot joints based on joint angles.

104fdc24-c5e1-42f9-bfb6-732f86d58b6e.title: Inverse Kinematics
104fdc24-c5e1-42f9-bfb6-732f86d58b6e.definition: Ability to understand and apply inverse kinematics techniques to determine the joint angle required for a desired end position and orientation.

f9984469-1d90-484b-b217-64eaaf899057.title: Data Visualization Types
f9984469-1d90-484b-b217-64eaaf899057.definition: Understanding of different types of charts and graphs for data visualization.

d056048f-3616-4dc0-b9cb-082fa5d2509c.title: Data Visualization Libraries
d056048f-3616-4dc0-b9cb-082fa5d2509c.definition: Knowledge of popular software libraries used to create data visualizations.

59ecd54f-c618-4fc7-a41b-537b30f85d26.title: Data Visualization Fundamentals
59ecd54f-c618-4fc7-a41b-537b30f85d26.definition: The fundamentals and theoretical foundations behind designing and creating effective data visualizations.

5b3dd6d0-d640-4680-8d40-dce99c165b6c.title: Ethical Data Visualization
5b3dd6d0-d640-4680-8d40-dce99c165b6c.definition: Understanding of ethical issues related to the presentation and interpretation of data through visualization.

66f30c22-edd4-478d-ab0f-f936eb09d7cb.title: Parallel Data Processing
66f30c22-edd4-478d-ab0f-f936eb09d7cb.definition: Concepts and techniques for parallel data processing in data management systems.

c4a7eb16-240c-48d3-bd76-38f0b20eb799.title: Distributed Data Processing
c4a7eb16-240c-48d3-bd76-38f0b20eb799.definition: Distributed data processing concepts and techniques, including frameworks such as MapReduce and cloud frameworks.

2b834684-5569-4780-8f83-0fb195a147a4.title: MapReduce
2b834684-5569-4780-8f83-0fb195a147a4.definition: MapReduce programming model and framework for processing and generating large data sets with distributed algorithms.

3bb5348b-820a-4dab-bc33-3a061a031be2.title: Cloud Data Processing Frameworks
3bb5348b-820a-4dab-bc33-3a061a031be2.definition: Cloud-based frameworks and platforms are used for large-scale data processing and analysis.

28cbacbe-2834-4df0-96c5-9ce461186fe2.title: Graph Data Modeling
28cbacbe-2834-4df0-96c5-9ce461186fe2.definition: Knowledge of how to represent data in graph form and applications in data modeling.

eaea64e1-7535-4bf0-9922-cc1f0e96b5fa.title: Entity Resolution
eaea64e1-7535-4bf0-9922-cc1f0e96b5fa.definition: Techniques for identifying and merging records referencing the same entity in different data sources.

f221acff-3af7-4ac7-94a7-d8a10aa704eb.title: SQL
f221acff-3af7-4ac7-94a7-d8a10aa704eb.definition: Ability to use SQL to query, manage, and manipulate data in relational databases.

d1381452-65fc-497c-95c9-01fa3e390c23.title: Query Building
d1381452-65fc-497c-95c9-01fa3e390c23.definition: Skills in building effective and accurate queries to extract desired information from data.

7dfbe288-9ac2-4b88-bacf-a89e091dd644.title: Graph Database (NoSQL)
7dfbe288-9ac2-4b88-bacf-a89e091dd644.definition: Knowledge of graph databases and how they are used in NoSQL systems.

72485793-dcc7-4690-9670-607f0f6fb6ad.title: Data Lakes
72485793-dcc7-4690-9670-607f0f6fb6ad.definition: Concepts and applications of data lakes for storing large amounts of raw, unstructured or semi-structured data.

62e2939e-3dce-449c-abde-e8e2ca2f792f.title: NoSQL Data Consistency
62e2939e-3dce-449c-abde-e8e2ca2f792f.definition: Issues and solutions related to data consistency in NoSQL database environments.

00f00252-4511-4695-ad5b-2ca044f694b2.title: Data Privacy
00f00252-4511-4695-ad5b-2ca044f694b2.definition: Knowledge of principles, regulations and techniques to protect the privacy of personal data.

da7854a9-bb3b-4428-b708-075196c5ae25.title: PII
da7854a9-bb3b-4428-b708-075196c5ae25.definition: Understanding Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and the importance of protecting it.

bc8a8851-d53f-4727-b4c1-41aa15669b20.title: PII Protection
bc8a8851-d53f-4727-b4c1-41aa15669b20.definition: Techniques and measures to protect Personally Identifiable Information from unauthorized access or misuse.

6ab9df0e-dff8-4a81-b2ec-104d03a6c86b.title: Data Discovery Techniques
6ab9df0e-dff8-4a81-b2ec-104d03a6c86b.definition: Techniques and methods for exploring, analyzing, and summarizing key characteristics of data sets.

c951b8f7-b736-4051-a62f-2876ca5b54b5.title: Data Science Lifecycle
c951b8f7-b736-4051-a62f-2876ca5b54b5.definition: Understanding of the different stages in the lifecycle of a data science project, from collection to deployment.

636eba5d-d1b6-475b-b023-3051a8ea2e4f.title: Data Provenance
636eba5d-d1b6-475b-b023-3051a8ea2e4f.definition: Understanding the origin, history and transformation of data.

aa9972f0-4ee0-4404-95b7-7bd99ca34b88.title: Machine Learning for Data Science
aa9972f0-4ee0-4404-95b7-7bd99ca34b88.definition: Machine learning techniques are applied in data science, including data preprocessing, missing data filling, supervised/semi-supervised/unsupervised learning, text analysis, graph analysis, PageRank, empirical methodology, evaluation, and ethics.

d36461f3-a2ca-45ef-ab03-e21570f72103.title: ML Data Preprocessing
d36461f3-a2ca-45ef-ab03-e21570f72103.definition: Specific data preprocessing techniques are needed to prepare data for machine learning models in data science.

b3d52cb8-ab70-424c-b9a1-a203a615cb0e.title: Missing Data Imputation
b3d52cb8-ab70-424c-b9a1-a203a615cb0e.definition: Methods and techniques for handling and filling in missing data values ​​in a data set.

83b8e831-11e5-4f89-82e1-c68493ffc5c9.title: Supervised Learning
83b8e831-11e5-4f89-82e1-c68493ffc5c9.definition: apply supervised learning methods to solve problems in data science, such as classification and regression.

2275ba7e-956c-4a41-875b-102597fd7b45.title: Semi-Supervised Learning
2275ba7e-956c-4a41-875b-102597fd7b45.definition: Learning methods use both labeled and unlabeled data to train the model.

6521c86f-fe20-4dbe-9e47-82d80a211911.title: Unsupervised Learning
6521c86f-fe20-4dbe-9e47-82d80a211911.definition: apply unsupervised learning methods to discover hidden structure in unlabeled data.

d6c65719-1772-408e-b411-33033d91f994.title: Text Analysis
d6c65719-1772-408e-b411-33033d91f994.definition: Techniques for analyzing and extracting meaningful information from text data in data science.

1dc9e658-5cd0-42c1-a2a3-4a3fb23aa2aa.title: Graph Analysis
1dc9e658-5cd0-42c1-a2a3-4a3fb23aa2aa.definition: Methods and tools for analyzing data represented as graphs in data science.

4e2d3def-a877-4bfe-8e63-1a64f4794141.title: PageRank Algorithm
4e2d3def-a877-4bfe-8e63-1a64f4794141.definition: understand and apply the PageRank algorithm to rank nodes in a graph, especially web pages.

6f2ab554-18be-44f2-894c-6226de1892ed.title: Experimental Methodology (ML/DS)
6f2ab554-18be-44f2-894c-6226de1892ed.definition: Methods and processes for designing, performing, and analyzing experiments in machine learning and data science.

da25f425-a9d9-48ba-ba25-c5721cbfdeb8.title: ML Model Evaluation
da25f425-a9d9-48ba-ba25-c5721cbfdeb8.definition: Techniques and criteria for evaluating machine learning model performance in data science projects.

c45a4aff-8048-4a06-8862-aa73cdad9926.title: ML/DS Ethics
c45a4aff-8048-4a06-8862-aa73cdad9926.definition: Ethical issues related to the development, deployment, and use of machine learning and data science systems.

650625bb-8363-4d20-98fa-8a1a42271c52.title: DS Societal & Ethical Responsibility (SEP)
650625bb-8363-4d20-98fa-8a1a42271c52.definition: Specific ethical and social impacts of data science applications, integrated throughout the course.

d0c5e9c7-11f3-4487-8298-983b2ebcbace.title: Statistical Analysis
d0c5e9c7-11f3-4487-8298-983b2ebcbace.definition: Statistical analysis techniques to understand data, draw conclusions, and support decisions.

8c7c2e79-33ea-457a-a4b5-9064465e5caf.title: Hypothesis Testing
8c7c2e79-33ea-457a-a4b5-9064465e5caf.definition: Statistical hypothesis testing methods for evaluating claims about a data set or population.

f16fbf57-d4f1-404c-beeb-385da73e5c3b.title: Statistical Experimental Design
f16fbf57-d4f1-404c-beeb-385da73e5c3b.definition: Principles and methods for designing experiments to collect statistically significant data and control extraneous variables.

e243cbd2-87cf-4b7a-8254-fdea4e4fb1b9.title: Formulating Data Analysis Problems
e243cbd2-87cf-4b7a-8254-fdea4e4fb1b9.definition: Ability to convert business or research questions into solvable problems using data analysis.

c4910dcf-727a-4579-b505-29f324da4c00.title: Data Storage Techniques
c4910dcf-727a-4579-b505-29f324da4c00.definition: Ability to understand and use data management techniques to store data effectively in current systems.

7831fc3e-b379-4005-9ad9-9671719994f3.title: Algorithm Foundations
7831fc3e-b379-4005-9ad9-9671719994f3.definition: Area of ​​knowledge that focuses on the nature of computation, including the concepts and skills needed to design and analyze algorithms to solve real-world computational problems.

4d512080-b209-48f1-8879-195c2b03024e.title: Algorithm
4d512080-b209-48f1-8879-195c2b03024e.definition: Structured computational processes that operate on data elements are the foundation of all theoretical calculations and applied programs.

167247de-6556-4717-8949-68728123e634.title: Data Structures
167247de-6556-4717-8949-68728123e634.definition: Ways of organizing data to allow efficient storage and access, are the foundation of all theoretical calculations and applied programs.

93971e3d-cab7-4b72-85fd-ed08f7672a77.title: Theory of Computation
93971e3d-cab7-4b72-85fd-ed08f7672a77.definition: The study of mathematical models of computation and problems that can be solved using algorithms.

42a2a65d-dc39-4010-9bc1-d1dc11914264.title: Algorithm Capabilities & Limits
42a2a65d-dc39-4010-9bc1-d1dc11914264.definition: Understanding of what algorithms can and cannot achieve, as well as the factors that influence their performance and applicability.

97c927c2-1bb9-4c88-a079-85f4e8126ef6.title: Algorithm Societal & Environmental Impact
97c927c2-1bb9-4c88-a079-85f4e8126ef6.definition: evaluate the ethical, social, and environmental consequences of algorithm development and implementation in real-world applications.

65d069da-e476-45b5-8524-f45dc94184c5.title: Nature of Computation
65d069da-e476-45b5-8524-f45dc94184c5.definition: understand the fundamentals and underlying theories that govern how computing works, independent of language or hardware.

3a168e93-2f0d-431f-9a7c-7236a31eee9f.title: Computational Problems
3a168e93-2f0d-431f-9a7c-7236a31eee9f.definition: Problems can be solved using computer algorithms, often defined in terms of inputs and desired outputs.

2359c622-a06f-4086-8ae2-3551027ce8c2.title: Computational Problem Solving
2359c622-a06f-4086-8ae2-3551027ce8c2.definition: Techniques and approaches for designing and implementing algorithmic solutions to real-world computational problems.

38446c98-7757-4db9-b843-1e34f2536e8b.title: Algorithm Design
38446c98-7757-4db9-b843-1e34f2536e8b.definition: The process of creating new algorithms or adapting existing algorithms to solve specific problems, taking into account efficiency and correctness.

8f17d5c6-8e92-4cf9-875f-611064af807a.title: Algorithm Analysis
8f17d5c6-8e92-4cf9-875f-611064af807a.definition: The process of estimating the resources (time, memory) required for an algorithm and evaluating its correctness under different circumstances.

a834ad2b-701d-49f8-b006-8674c0130a21.title: Computational Complexity
a834ad2b-701d-49f8-b006-8674c0130a21.definition: Research on the amount of resources (time, space) needed to solve computational problems, providing a theoretical basis for evaluating algorithm performance.

87c9df9a-3818-4a1a-8268-bf0abc085ede.title: Computability
87c9df9a-3818-4a1a-8268-bf0abc085ede.definition: The study of which problems can be solved by an algorithm, and which problems cannot, through formal computational models.

b21965c3-9603-49a1-9738-435adaec42ec.title: Foundational Data Structures & Algorithms
b21965c3-9603-49a1-9738-435adaec42ec.definition: The unit focuses on fundamental data structures and algorithms, providing an essential foundation for every computer science student. (Total hours CS Core: 11, KA Core: 6)

1d325d66-b353-43fe-b857-51deab9dacf3.title: Algorithm Strategies
1d325d66-b353-43fe-b857-51deab9dacf3.definition: The unit focuses on general methods and techniques for algorithm design, such as divide and conquer, dynamic programming, and more. (Total KA Core hours: 6)

e4021a48-9014-497d-b6f2-5c09549df50b.title: Complexity Analysis
e4021a48-9014-497d-b6f2-5c09549df50b.definition: The unit focuses on methods for quantifying the efficiency of algorithms in time and space. (Total hours CS Core: 6, KA Core: 3)

858a951c-0280-4201-b760-31eae8063383.title: Computational Models & Formal Languages
858a951c-0280-4201-b760-31eae8063383.definition: The unit focuses on theoretical models of computation and the formal languages ​​used to describe them. (Total hours CS Core: 9, KA Core: 23)

77ecc9b3-a919-4031-ac71-db3253554162.title: AL Societal, Ethical & Professional (SEP)
77ecc9b3-a919-4031-ac71-db3253554162.definition: The unit of knowledge ensures that the social, ethical and professional implications of computing are addressed throughout the AL area topics.

0349b402-7096-4552-ae7e-c8640dc2b61b.title: Linear Search
0349b402-7096-4552-ae7e-c8640dc2b61b.definition: A simple search algorithm that examines each element in a list or array in turn until the target is found or the list is exhausted.

78572b65-26da-4926-8959-61ebcd5d7a3f.title: Big O Notation
78572b65-26da-4926-8959-61ebcd5d7a3f.definition: A mathematical notation used to describe the worst-case behavior of a function when the argument goes to infinity, often used to classify the performance of an algorithm.

88e74852-0526-496c-9d0f-a5ec1d0766a9.title: O(n) Complexity
88e74852-0526-496c-9d0f-a5ec1d0766a9.definition: Linear time or space complexity, which means the time or space required to execute the algorithm increases linearly with the input size (n).

51a4188b-7134-4390-a228-b16fd60b7cea.title: Brute-Force Strategy
51a4188b-7134-4390-a228-b16fd60b7cea.definition: A simple problem-solving strategy by systematically trying out all possible possibilities or solutions until a solution is found.

d1a6ea00-823f-499b-808a-7f3095d6ebfb.title: Abstract Data Type (ADT)
d1a6ea00-823f-499b-808a-7f3095d6ebfb.definition: A mathematical model for a data structure that defines the operations allowed on the data without specifying how the data is stored internally.

4206db02-b8e5-493b-a60a-3c4354d713db.title: ADT Operations
4206db02-b8e5-493b-a60a-3c4354d713db.definition: Functions or methods are defined as part of an Abstract Data Type's interface, allowing interaction with the data it represents (e.g. add, delete, search).

6a8f22cc-f229-428d-9a4a-e9c6125be99b.title: Dictionary/Map
6a8f22cc-f229-428d-9a4a-e9c6125be99b.definition: A data structure that stores key-value pairs, allowing the value to be retrieved by its unique key.

0913677e-0127-45c3-ab7c-5067f247580f.title: Dictionary Add
0913677e-0127-45c3-ab7c-5067f247580f.definition: The operation adds a new key-value pair to the dictionary data structure.

0f96d05b-abc9-4e7a-860e-c8fba2454880.title: Dictionary Remove
0f96d05b-abc9-4e7a-860e-c8fba2454880.definition: The operation removes a key-value pair from a dictionary data structure based on its key.

4dac19f1-c4e7-4ecc-895f-b62727a7bf1f.title: Dictionary Search
4dac19f1-c4e7-4ecc-895f-b62727a7bf1f.definition: The operation retrieves the value associated with a specific key in a dictionary data structure.

234616fe-a74c-40d8-9e93-3c42e24d4980.title: Arrays
234616fe-a74c-40d8-9e93-3c42e24d4980.definition: A set of data elements of the same type stored in contiguous memory locations, accessible by an index.

53b32c1d-7533-4008-881c-e48ca338d04c.title: Numeric Array
53b32c1d-7533-4008-881c-e48ca338d04c.definition: Arrays contain data elements with numeric values ​​(e.g. integers, floats).

0aef7b16-2ef7-4c87-b5b3-ae24f0735cd6.title: Non-Numeric Array
0aef7b16-2ef7-4c87-b5b3-ae24f0735cd6.definition: Arrays contain data elements with non-numeric values ​​(for example, characters, strings, objects).

6eadcf5b-8b09-46bc-8b3a-9916ea529596.title: String as Array
6eadcf5b-8b09-46bc-8b3a-9916ea529596.definition: A sequence of characters is represented as an array, where each character occupies a position in the array and is accessed by index.

aa1f9df3-9d9d-494e-9363-232badc92918.title: 1D Array (Vector)
aa1f9df3-9d9d-494e-9363-232badc92918.definition: An array whose elements are arranged in a single dimension, often called a vector.

00806d60-235d-4ee6-aa06-e5f18c20a0e6.title: Multi-dimensional Array (Matrix)
00806d60-235d-4ee6-aa06-e5f18c20a0e6.definition: An array whose elements are arranged in multiple dimensions, often used to represent matrices or grids.

4ac544dc-1225-43fd-b356-77fe90fc4eaa.title: Record/Struct/Tuple
4ac544dc-1225-43fd-b356-77fe90fc4eaa.definition: Aggregate data structures allow fields or attributes of different data types to be grouped into a single unit.

7dc5bb04-5290-45a1-a277-cdd2ba0a9f16.title: Object (Data Structure)
7dc5bb04-5290-45a1-a277-cdd2ba0a9f16.definition: In object-oriented programming, an instance of a class, including both data (properties) and methods (behavior) that operate on that data.

3123ab40-8caf-4e68-9609-8cf69759f7ca.title: Linked Lists
3123ab40-8caf-4e68-9609-8cf69759f7ca.definition: A linear data structure where elements are not stored in contiguous memory locations but are linked by pointers or references.

650f7432-03e3-449a-b191-7173cb334d5e.title: Singly Linked List
650f7432-03e3-449a-b191-7173cb334d5e.definition: A linked list in which each node points to the next node in the chain, but there is no link back.

adcae34b-ac81-430d-838f-e36c488567f4.title: Doubly Linked List
adcae34b-ac81-430d-838f-e36c488567f4.definition: A linked list in which each node points to both the next and previous node in the chain, allowing two-way traversal.

d8fe7bd0-78b8-4444-8d4e-5a68d78be027.title: Linear Linked List
d8fe7bd0-78b8-4444-8d4e-5a68d78be027.definition: A linked list has a clear start (head) and end (tail) point, where the nodes are arranged in a linear sequence.

c8189f8f-f2c5-425f-994c-ad072fe9ea05.title: Circular Linked List
c8189f8f-f2c5-425f-994c-ad072fe9ea05.definition: A linked list in which the last node points back to the first node (or another node), forming a continuous loop.

92036f78-9711-498b-8056-ea79398c8030.title: Stacks
92036f78-9711-498b-8056-ea79398c8030.definition: An abstract data structure that operates on the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle, with the main operations being push and pop.

8ac45b10-3551-473c-a8c3-6bb8996f6629.title: Queues
8ac45b10-3551-473c-a8c3-6bb8996f6629.definition: An abstract data structure that operates on the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle, with the main operations being insert (enqueue) and remove (dequeue).

cc5588fa-198b-40d8-859a-79351c98848d.title: Deques
cc5588fa-198b-40d8-859a-79351c98848d.definition: A double-ended queue allows elements to be added and removed from both ends of the queue efficiently.

d459c9d8-14be-4b60-826d-1f4a04bb4779.title: Heap Priority Queue
d459c9d8-14be-4b60-826d-1f4a04bb4779.definition: A priority queue is implemented using a heap data structure, where elements are retrieved based on their priority instead of order of arrival.

9fcf92ea-4206-4328-a1c8-c5be369a2c71.title: Hash Table/Map
9fcf92ea-4206-4328-a1c8-c5be369a2c71.definition: A data structure that maps keys to values ​​using a hash function to calculate an index or 'hash' into an array of buckets or slots.

66fa7e3a-67db-4ab3-9fc8-8750c8a274a9.title: Hash Collision Resolution
66fa7e3a-67db-4ab3-9fc8-8750c8a274a9.definition: Techniques used to handle the situation when two different keys hash to the same index in the hash table, such as probing or chaining.

7a5abff1-3264-44e1-a8c4-73a81ce98fc2.title: Hash Collision Complexity
7a5abff1-3264-44e1-a8c4-73a81ce98fc2.definition: analyze the performance of hash collision resolution methods, typically with respect to the time required to find, add, or delete elements when there is a collision.

fd6f2bc5-b57c-4ebc-9b1b-d2888bf24c02.title: Linear Probing
fd6f2bc5-b57c-4ebc-9b1b-d2888bf24c02.definition: A hash collision resolution method in which alternative locations are searched sequentially or according to a specific pattern (e.g., squared) in a hash table.

73eee2c9-aad2-4110-b273-edb597470c7b.title: Chaining
73eee2c9-aad2-4110-b273-edb597470c7b.definition: A method of hash collision resolution in which each location in a hash table contains a linked list or other data structure for all elements hashed to that location.

5f0b6574-1a59-4cf6-96fe-1f7d125d04e5.title: Rehashing
5f0b6574-1a59-4cf6-96fe-1f7d125d04e5.definition: A technique used to resolve hash collisions or when the load factor becomes too high, in which the hash table is rebuilt with a larger size and a new hash function.

48c50581-e8bf-4cb7-ae41-8a1ff75fade7.title: Graphs
48c50581-e8bf-4cb7-ae41-8a1ff75fade7.definition: A non-linear data structure consisting of nodes/vertices and edges connecting them, used to model complex relationships.

b26ff280-982d-4ac7-aab1-83fc2da0a523.title: Undirected Graph
b26ff280-982d-4ac7-aab1-83fc2da0a523.definition: A graph in which edges are undirected, meaning the connection between two vertices is symmetric (if A goes to B, then B goes to A).

d9c1a6ef-f511-4dcc-83bf-64173b3d15e6.title: Directed Graph
d9c1a6ef-f511-4dcc-83bf-64173b3d15e6.definition: A graph in which edges are directed, meaning the connection from one vertex to another is not necessarily symmetric.

0db826bb-171f-4e0d-8b6b-ea54515fa89a.title: Acyclic Graph
0db826bb-171f-4e0d-8b6b-ea54515fa89a.definition: A graph does not contain any cycles (a path that starts and ends at the same vertex) like a Tree.

88d03d1d-dd26-4af8-b008-7d12d8750d07.title: Cyclic Graph
88d03d1d-dd26-4af8-b008-7d12d8750d07.definition: A graph contains at least one cycle (a path that starts and ends at the same vertex).

33490d25-d201-4166-b75e-019a1d5898a1.title: Disconnected Graph
33490d25-d201-4166-b75e-019a1d5898a1.definition: A graph in which at least one pair of vertices has no path between them, i.e. it is made up of many connected components.

4484d37c-e2b9-4c5b-baf1-52928e04a91f.title: Connected Graph
4484d37c-e2b9-4c5b-baf1-52928e04a91f.definition: A graph in which there is a path between every pair of vertices, i.e. all vertices are connected.

c160192a-a27c-4f4d-80f9-6b32a13494ac.title: Unweighted Graph
c160192a-a27c-4f4d-80f9-6b32a13494ac.definition: A graph in which edges have no value (weight) associated with them, representing only the existence of a connection.

00d5514f-ed71-475c-89ec-0156ce793a00.title: Weighted Graph
00d5514f-ed71-475c-89ec-0156ce793a00.definition: A graph in which each edge has a numerical value (weight) associated with it, typically representing cost, distance, or strength of the relationship.

79bc6617-5b74-4026-8019-0421c49aa06d.title: Graph Representation
79bc6617-5b74-4026-8019-0421c49aa06d.definition: Different ways of storing graph structures in computer memory, such as adjacency lists or adjacency matrices, affect the efficiency of graph operations.

46f0f197-0204-486e-b797-793e7c80a04d.title: Adjacency List
46f0f197-0204-486e-b797-793e7c80a04d.definition: A method of representing a graph in which each vertex has a list (usually a linked list or array) of its neighbors.

317146d0-2d25-4387-8c5d-4fa96f3d2c27.title: Adjacency Matrix
317146d0-2d25-4387-8c5d-4fa96f3d2c27.definition: A method of representing a graph using a square matrix, whose elements indicate whether there are any edges between two vertices (usually 0 or 1, or an edge weight).

ba194fe3-9a44-4980-8fbb-2df7d708ba9d.title: Trees
ba194fe3-9a44-4980-8fbb-2df7d708ba9d.definition: A non-linear, hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes and edges without cycles, with a single root node.

53b0a70e-1dab-4bf6-93b6-d0b6aff6ed3c.title: Binary Tree
53b0a70e-1dab-4bf6-93b6-d0b6aff6ed3c.definition: A type of tree in which each node has at most two children, often called left children and right children.

e4f5384f-46a3-4bfb-b29a-e01c5340443d.title: N-ary Tree
e4f5384f-46a3-4bfb-b29a-e01c5340443d.definition: A type of tree in which each node can have at most N children, extended from the concept of a binary tree.

ddfea37d-0f23-4fc7-a221-eff07daab42e.title: Search Tree
ddfea37d-0f23-4fc7-a221-eff07daab42e.definition: A type of tree in which values ​​are stored in a particular order (e.g., smaller keys are in the left subtree, larger keys in the right subtree) to allow efficient searches, insertions, and deletions.

492d87dc-993c-48ad-95ca-ec830d2cd620.title: Balanced Tree
492d87dc-993c-48ad-95ca-ec830d2cd620.definition: A binary search tree is structured so that the height of the tree is kept to a minimum or approximately balanced, ensuring best performance for search, insert, and delete operations.

96f0a5e9-c981-4a6b-a164-ee9d758c48eb.title: AVL Tree
96f0a5e9-c981-4a6b-a164-ee9d758c48eb.definition: A self-balancing binary search tree, where the difference in height between the left and right subtrees of any node is at most 1.

f4a17cf1-16d6-4f58-87f9-5435b1f1e0e4.title: Red-Black Tree
f4a17cf1-16d6-4f58-87f9-5435b1f1e0e4.definition: A self-balancing binary search tree, uses a 'color' attribute (red or black) for each node along with strict rules to maintain balance after modification operations.

d33c5711-69d4-4a83-8b04-928a3f1f45f7.title: Heap (Data Structure)
d33c5711-69d4-4a83-8b04-928a3f1f45f7.definition: A complete binary tree organized to satisfy the heap property (e.g. max-heap: largest element at the root; min-heap: smallest element at the root), commonly used to implement priority queues.

5251d93d-c157-4d71-8ff9-c9df2bb1c856.title: Sets
5251d93d-c157-4d71-8ff9-c9df2bb1c856.definition: A data structure that stores unique, unordered elements and supports operations such as union, intersection, and difference.

1d2047c1-16fd-46f1-a5aa-70f0aef11eb7.title: Search Algorithms
1d2047c1-16fd-46f1-a5aa-70f0aef11eb7.definition: Methods used to locate a specific item or set of items in a data structure.

62337fe3-ee9c-4933-abf8-6333834dccee.title: O(n) Complexity
62337fe3-ee9c-4933-abf8-6333834dccee.definition: Linear time complexity representation, which states that the execution time of the algorithm increases proportionally to the input size (n).

9df2fd91-8274-47d0-85be-e858c3b940da.title: Linear Search
9df2fd91-8274-47d0-85be-e858c3b940da.definition: The simplest search algorithm, examines each element in the list in order until the target is found or the list is exhausted. Has O(n) complexity.

34b7d2a1-4c0c-4ea0-8485-8e94e9dd2848.title: O(log n) Complexity
34b7d2a1-4c0c-4ea0-8485-8e94e9dd2848.definition: A representation of logarithmic time complexity, which indicates that an algorithm's execution time increases significantly more slowly than the input size, typically involves bisecting the search space.

7c0aaa72-1f3e-4306-8d46-24038f987faf.title: Binary Search
7c0aaa72-1f3e-4306-8d46-24038f987faf.definition: An efficient search algorithm for sorted data works by repeatedly bisecting the search space. Has O(log n) complexity.

a042b779-faac-4535-810b-2e53ba18adfb.title: O(log_b n) Complexity
a042b779-faac-4535-810b-2e53ba18adfb.definition: Logarithmic time complexity with base b, typically applied to search algorithms on tree or hierarchical data structures (e.g., binary trees, B-trees).

7d7a54c5-3998-43d6-9d5a-1c864662a6aa.title: Depth-First Search
7d7a54c5-3998-43d6-9d5a-1c864662a6aa.definition: The algorithm searches the tree or graph, exploring as deeply as possible along each branch before backtracking and exploring another branch. It is a form of non-informational search.

b6ded3d7-bade-40f4-841a-6c2df551505f.title: Breadth-First Search
b6ded3d7-bade-40f4-841a-6c2df551505f.definition: The algorithm searches a tree or graph, exploring all nodes at the same level before moving on to the next level. It is a form of non-informational search.

dd6a818d-aaca-472c-9f1d-ad720a55855e.title: Sorting Algorithms
dd6a818d-aaca-472c-9f1d-ad720a55855e.definition: Systematic methods are used to arrange a set of items in a specific order (e.g., numbers, letters).

c112042c-126c-4f7b-987e-ba1008be082d.title: Stable Sort
c112042c-126c-4f7b-987e-ba1008be082d.definition: A property of a sorting algorithm that ensures that the relative order of elements with equal keys is maintained in the sorted output.

d9384b28-9f64-44db-9a63-dc06ff4a1a9b.title: Unstable Sort
d9384b28-9f64-44db-9a63-dc06ff4a1a9b.definition: A property of sorting algorithms, which does not guarantee that the relative order of elements with equal keys is maintained in the sorted output.

5cabb1ba-7a75-419f-8498-72e671526df3.title: O(n^2) Complexity
5cabb1ba-7a75-419f-8498-72e671526df3.definition: Represents the squared time complexity, which indicates that the execution time of the algorithm increases with the square of the input size (n).

cc6533ea-fffb-42cb-a4c8-f09c43f6f264.title: Insertion Sort
cc6533ea-fffb-42cb-a4c8-f09c43f6f264.definition: A simple sorting algorithm constructs the final sorted array or list element by element by inserting each unsorted element into its correct position. Has O(n^2) complexity.

06305459-c16d-43fd-bf65-d1a4273bca3d.title: Selection Sort
06305459-c16d-43fd-bf65-d1a4273bca3d.definition: The sorting algorithm is simple, iteratively finding the smallest (or largest) element from the unsorted section and placing it at the beginning of the sorted section. Has O(n^2) complexity.

02fc2e76-d9f9-4b46-983f-04906e393bf2.title: O(n log n) Complexity
02fc2e76-d9f9-4b46-983f-04906e393bf2.definition: The time complexity is common for efficient sorting algorithms, representing a trade-off between linear and logarithmic performance.

00615f13-f1d1-4531-a1df-94cd86e17262.title: Quicksort
00615f13-f1d1-4531-a1df-94cd86e17262.definition: The sorting algorithm is based on the divide and conquer method, selecting a pivot element and partitioning the array around it. Has average complexity O(n log n).

7b4d7dab-03c7-4246-a4e2-c5b9e74b88f8.title: Mergesort
7b4d7dab-03c7-4246-a4e2-c5b9e74b88f8.definition: The sorting algorithm is based on the divide-and-conquer method, which divides the list into smaller sublists, sorts them recursively, and then merges them. Has complexity O(n log n).

0cd059d7-3d0f-4292-89b9-628a62ef92e4.title: Timsort
0cd059d7-3d0f-4292-89b9-628a62ef92e4.definition: The hybrid sort algorithm, which combines insertion sort and merge sort, is designed to work efficiently on many types of real-world data and is the default sorting algorithm in Python and Java.

32b2a5e2-6ca2-4698-8863-96215f0ce6d7.title: Graph Algorithms
32b2a5e2-6ca2-4698-8863-96215f0ce6d7.definition: Algorithms are designed to solve problems related to graph structure, such as path finding, spanning tree finding, connectivity analysis, etc.

a146868b-fa00-4ec2-9214-f07215e3dd13.title: Shortest Path Algorithms
a146868b-fa00-4ec2-9214-f07215e3dd13.definition: A set of algorithms used to find the path with the least weighted sum between two vertices or between a vertex and all other vertices in the graph.

b54b7aa7-62c1-464c-a2e2-f9f3ffad50d1.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
b54b7aa7-62c1-464c-a2e2-f9f3ffad50d1.definition: The algorithm finds the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices in a graph with non-negative edge weights.

91d2e0ad-9fd9-46ca-b987-e229e02d0f66.title: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
91d2e0ad-9fd9-46ca-b987-e229e02d0f66.definition: The algorithm finds the shortest path between all pairs of vertices in a graph with weight (can be negative, but has no negative cycles). apply dynamic planning.

d7c8f9e2-4232-416b-b659-9dd153e74ddd.title: Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithms
d7c8f9e2-4232-416b-b659-9dd153e74ddd.definition: Set of algorithms used to find a subtree of a weighted undirected graph, including all vertices, with the smallest possible total edge weights.

111fc7fa-76fb-4960-b5e4-9b5e36911220.title: Prim's Algorithm
111fc7fa-76fb-4960-b5e4-9b5e36911220.definition: Greedy algorithm to find the minimum spanning tree for a weighted undirected graph, starting from a vertex and expanding the tree by adding the least weighted edge connecting the new vertex to the existing tree.

bddf61bc-7c31-4a75-8b35-1ea315305039.title: Kruskal's Algorithm
bddf61bc-7c31-4a75-8b35-1ea315305039.definition: Greedy algorithm to find the minimum spanning tree for a weighted undirected graph, by continuously adding edges with the least weight without forming cycles.

4a1d6cb9-3bc6-4d9c-8929-aecaafe00bff.title: Heapsort
4a1d6cb9-3bc6-4d9c-8929-aecaafe00bff.definition: The sorting algorithm is based on the binary heap data structure. It sorts by building a max-heap and continuously extracting the largest element. Has complexity O(n log n).

9bababa4-37fa-4d03-9b9d-5bd847335e84.title: Pseudo-linear O(n) Complexity
9bababa4-37fa-4d03-9b9d-5bd847335e84.definition: Algorithms that have nearly linear complexity O(n) under some specific conditions (e.g., limited range of input values), typically do not rely on comparison.

a8272795-a8ac-43ed-8345-96fc72a8c102.title: Bucket Sort
a8272795-a8ac-43ed-8345-96fc72a8c102.definition: The non-comparison sorting algorithm works by distributing elements into a finite number of 'bins', then sorting each bin individually. Effective when data is evenly distributed.

79db0bf4-6421-404b-97b3-5cf3929f2a8f.title: Counting Sort
79db0bf4-6421-404b-97b3-5cf3929f2a8f.definition: The comparison-free sorting algorithm works by counting the number of occurrences of each key value in the array. Suitable for integers in a small range.

9c76b63e-6ecc-4835-8eeb-dfd4c7f78e0c.title: Radix Sort
9c76b63e-6ecc-4835-8eeb-dfd4c7f78e0c.definition: The non-comparison sorting algorithm sorts numbers by processing individual digits (or bits) from least significant position to most significant position.

a1a44724-e07e-41ee-ab78-eed1f2841630.title: Transitive Closure
a1a44724-e07e-41ee-ab78-eed1f2841630.definition: In graph theory, transitive closure of a directed graph is a new graph that contains an edge from vertex u to vertex v if there is a path from u to v in the original graph.

fd6e75e8-dc81-44c0-a02a-4524a8a7831b.title: Warshall's Algorithm
fd6e75e8-dc81-44c0-a02a-4524a8a7831b.definition: Algorithm to find transitive closure of a directed graph. It uses dynamic programming to identify all pairs of vertices that have a path between them.

e672e74a-726b-43eb-89cd-3c2ef4889d96.title: Topological Sort
e672e74a-726b-43eb-89cd-3c2ef4889d96.definition: The algorithm arranges the vertices of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) in a linear order such that for each edge directed from u to v, vertex u appears before vertex v in the order.

820b6f73-1166-4c86-ac76-ddbd50f6ef2c.title: Pattern Matching
820b6f73-1166-4c86-ac76-ddbd50f6ef2c.definition: Techniques and algorithms for finding similar patterns, subsequences, or structures in data, commonly used in text processing and biology.

c0537230-7749-476a-b84c-7859291ce19c.title: Efficient String Matching
c0537230-7749-476a-b84c-7859291ce19c.definition: Algorithms are designed to quickly find occurrences of one or more patterns in a large text string.

3cba46f3-e33a-4907-ba35-5a5174b10604.title: Boyer-Moore Algorithm
3cba46f3-e33a-4907-ba35-5a5174b10604.definition: Efficient string matching algorithm, often one of the fastest string matching algorithms in practice. It works by skipping parts of the text based on 'bad character' and 'good suffix' rules.

192efd3e-80a3-4764-ab19-7e9af038295d.title: KMP Algorithm
192efd3e-80a3-4764-ab19-7e9af038295d.definition: Efficient string matching algorithm, avoids rechecking characters in the text by using information about the prefixes and suffixes of the pattern. Has linear complexity.

790c51f6-5b49-4ca0-83e8-dd9243375fb9.title: Longest Common Subsequence
790c51f6-5b49-4ca0-83e8-dd9243375fb9.definition: The problem is to find the longest subsequence of both input strings. Usually solved by dynamic programming.

42cf8a72-ab3a-41ab-a481-d8c4ea62506f.title: Regex Matching
42cf8a72-ab3a-41ab-a481-d8c4ea62506f.definition: The process of searching and matching strings according to patterns defined by regular expressions, widely used in text processing.

59dd023b-a0bc-4020-a122-309d00c4a2eb.title: Cryptographic Algorithms
59dd023b-a0bc-4020-a122-309d00c4a2eb.definition: Algorithms and techniques used to secure information and communication, including encryption, hashing, digital signatures, and more.

bb585e05-9aaf-461a-a09f-b3f8d8c85d61.title: SHA-256
bb585e05-9aaf-461a-a09f-b3f8d8c85d61.definition: Cryptographic hash functions belong to the SHA-2 family, which produces a unique 256-bit (32-byte) hash value from input data. Widely used in information security and blockchain.

fd0a0c23-77ec-4e1a-ad6e-53f3cfc72417.title: Parallel Algorithms
fd0a0c23-77ec-4e1a-ad6e-53f3cfc72417.definition: Algorithms are designed to perform calculations simultaneously on multiple processors or threads, to speed up execution of large problems.

f5c0b6dd-1ef7-4868-bd66-8bdf12694d54.title: Consensus Algorithms
f5c0b6dd-1ef7-4868-bd66-8bdf12694d54.definition: Algorithms enable a distributed group of agents to reach agreement on a single data value or system state, even in the presence of errors or malicious behavior.

43ab11b9-1094-47c2-99dc-e2a08317b56c.title: Blockchain
43ab11b9-1094-47c2-99dc-e2a08317b56c.definition: A distributed ledger technology that records transactions in a secure and immutable way through the use of cryptographically linked blocks. Usually based on a consensus algorithm.

7e7c89ad-c3a3-4505-bbef-310f7122982e.title: Proof of Work (PoW)
7e7c89ad-c3a3-4505-bbef-310f7122982e.definition: A consensus mechanism used in distributed systems (e.g., Bitcoin) to prevent service abuse and validate transactions, requires a certain amount of computational work.

7dce137f-52b5-4a48-b14b-dd8248caabd3.title: Proof of Stake (PoS)
7dce137f-52b5-4a48-b14b-dd8248caabd3.definition: A consensus mechanism in distributed systems where validators are chosen based on the amount of cryptocurrency they own and 'stake', to secure the network.

76fd1a47-5bf1-467d-b2c6-2de53fc6d7cc.title: Quantum Algorithms
76fd1a47-5bf1-467d-b2c6-2de53fc6d7cc.definition: The algorithms are designed to run on quantum computers, exploiting quantum mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement to solve complex problems.

126e64cf-21aa-4412-8cb6-c28091e15f6c.title: Oracle-based Quantum Algorithms
126e64cf-21aa-4412-8cb6-c28091e15f6c.definition: Quantum algorithms use an 'oracle' (black box) to evaluate a function, often with significantly fewer queries than classical computers.

a169f974-b3c9-4825-a78e-8bb575bb8571.title: Deutsch-Jozsa Algorithm
a169f974-b3c9-4825-a78e-8bb575bb8571.definition: One of the earliest quantum algorithms, demonstrating that quantum computers can solve some problems faster than classical computers under certain circumstances.

d14d4a33-424e-4609-a14a-788275412d5f.title: Bernstein-Vazirani Algorithm
d14d4a33-424e-4609-a14a-788275412d5f.definition: Quantum algorithms can find a hidden binary string (or linear binary function) with just one oracle query, while classical algorithms need many more queries.

cad57aaf-e205-4ae8-887a-1dee9490dd21.title: Simon's Algorithm
cad57aaf-e205-4ae8-887a-1dee9490dd21.definition: The quantum algorithm searches for a hidden 'cycle' of a function, demonstrating a superpolynomial speed-up compared to the best classical algorithm.

0b1046c2-f2c0-4a0f-bc10-79b89d90284f.title: QFT Superpolynomial Speedup
0b1046c2-f2c0-4a0f-bc10-79b89d90284f.definition: The concept of using quantum Fourier transform to achieve a significant (better than polynomial) speedup in algorithm runtime compared to classical algorithms.

30fb77d1-cb92-446d-9b28-97c3b4230649.title: Shor's Algorithm
30fb77d1-cb92-446d-9b28-97c3b4230649.definition: The famous quantum algorithm for factoring large integers and calculating discrete logarithms, has the potential to break many existing public cryptosystems.

0ad26d36-2cf7-4906-afe3-f9ebc89d865e.title: Amplitude Amplification
0ad26d36-2cf7-4906-afe3-f9ebc89d865e.definition: The concept of using amplitude amplification techniques in quantum computing to achieve polynomial (e.g., square root) speedups over classical algorithms, often in search problems.

03b079cd-3022-4964-96da-71d768fd4d98.title: Grover's Algorithm
03b079cd-3022-4964-96da-71d768fd4d98.definition: Quantum algorithm for searching in unstructured or unsorted databases, providing quadratic speed-up compared to classical search.

19a4f734-af73-4c44-8f75-11585b9834e1.title: Fast Fourier Transform
19a4f734-af73-4c44-8f75-11585b9834e1.definition: Efficient algorithm for computing the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and inverse Fourier transform of a series, which has wide applications in signal and image processing.

9f4e3be0-7b82-4b25-bd32-8113d082e78b.title: Differential Evolution
9f4e3be0-7b82-4b25-bd32-8113d082e78b.definition: A metaheuristic optimization algorithm belongs to the family of evolutionary algorithms, used to solve continuous optimization problems using mutation, hybridization, and selection operators.

45ef7e8a-ac61-486d-b81f-0f3a0913c9e0.title: Algorithm Paradigms
45ef7e8a-ac61-486d-b81f-0f3a0913c9e0.definition: Generic design methods for building efficient algorithms provide a framework for solving different types of problems.

b552ca2f-6e56-4906-b8c7-df253b5f5764.title: Brute-Force
b552ca2f-6e56-4906-b8c7-df253b5f5764.definition: A simple algorithm design model that examines all possible possibilities directly to find a solution to a problem.

bdcee147-b708-493f-8fb8-30edf275cd0e.title: Traveling Salesperson Problem
bdcee147-b708-493f-8fb8-30edf275cd0e.definition: The famous optimization problem, finding the shortest path through a list of cities and back to the starting point, each city is visited only once. Is an example of an NP-hard problem.

0e95521e-8373-455b-9252-65022d5f7928.title: Knapsack Problem
0e95521e-8373-455b-9252-65022d5f7928.definition: Optimization problem, choose a set of items with different weights and values ​​to maximize the total value without exceeding the weight limit of a bag. Can be solved by exhaustive, greedy or dynamic programming.

aa3c55da-0536-49da-a2ee-3c6a951c4c7a.title: Decrease-and-Conquer
aa3c55da-0536-49da-a2ee-3c6a951c4c7a.definition: The algorithm design model solves a problem by transforming it into a smaller version of itself, solving the smaller version, and then expanding the solution.

d83bd8bd-a71b-4211-9175-afc02c6b335f.title: Decrease-by-Constant
d83bd8bd-a71b-4211-9175-afc02c6b335f.definition: A variation of the Reduce and Conquer model, where the size of the problem decreases by a constant (usually 1) at each step, for example in insertion sort.

cfad1d6f-fda8-43f8-9a8a-06579ec8fda7.title: Decrease-by-Constant Factor
cfad1d6f-fda8-43f8-9a8a-06579ec8fda7.definition: A variation of the Reduce and Conquer model, where the size of the problem decreases by a constant factor (e.g., bisection) at each step, for example in binary search.

aa2edeb1-563e-4ef8-baf0-51b3bb18ccd1.title: Decrease-by-Variable Size
aa2edeb1-563e-4ef8-baf0-51b3bb18ccd1.definition: A variation of the Reduce and Conquer model, where the size of the problem is reduced by a variable amount at each step, depending on the input data.

de765f4b-11fe-4e6c-9c18-7916eae6f41d.title: Euclidean Algorithm
de765f4b-11fe-4e6c-9c18-7916eae6f41d.definition: An efficient algorithm for calculating the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers, which is an example of a variable dimensionality reduce-and-conquer model.

5bba6d16-3304-444a-ae72-af5cbd7b8979.title: Divide-and-Conquer
5bba6d16-3304-444a-ae72-af5cbd7b8979.definition: The algorithm design model solves a problem by dividing it into smaller, independent sub-problems of the same type, solving them recursively, and then combining the solutions.

e9a6bd6b-aa9a-4793-9804-37cccf122cb2.title: Strassen Algorithm
e9a6bd6b-aa9a-4793-9804-37cccf122cb2.definition: The matrix multiplication algorithm is faster than the standard algorithm, using a divide-and-conquer method to reduce the number of multiplications. Has complexity O(n^log2 7).

69c4686e-f4b8-4e09-88cc-87c03148f850.title: Greedy Algorithm
69c4686e-f4b8-4e09-88cc-87c03148f850.definition: The algorithm design model makes a locally optimal choice at each step in the hope that this sequence of choices will lead to a globally optimal solution.

37529f3a-8b3a-415e-905b-f4adcd772ee7.title: Transform-and-Conquer
37529f3a-8b3a-415e-905b-f4adcd772ee7.definition: The algorithm design model solves a problem by transforming it into another instance whose solution is known, then solving for the new instance and transforming the result back.

e9af0c13-a014-46e1-ba9d-e9fb24b78f47.title: Instance Simplification
e9af0c13-a014-46e1-ba9d-e9fb24b78f47.definition: Techniques in the transform and conquer paradigm that transform a complex representation of a problem into a simpler representation that is easier to solve, often by preprocessing the data.

cdf2d4e9-33c2-4b3e-b3eb-665c7f8826df.title: Duplicate Detection by Sorting
cdf2d4e9-33c2-4b3e-b3eb-665c7f8826df.definition: Technique for finding duplicate elements in a list by first sorting the list, then traversing adjacent elements to detect similar values.

f612433d-880b-4a06-b0c1-def18086c1ce.title: Change of Representation
f612433d-880b-4a06-b0c1-def18086c1ce.definition: Techniques in the transform and conquer paradigm that change the representation of data or a problem so that solving becomes easier or more efficient (e.g., using heap for heapsort).

20bf05e2-37d0-4294-951c-78bae2fd2fbd.title: Problem Reduction
20bf05e2-37d0-4294-951c-78bae2fd2fbd.definition: Engineering in the transform and conquer model transforms a problem into another problem that already has an algorithm to solve, then applies that algorithm.

d97240e4-92bf-4df0-987b-c4d8a532bcc4.title: Least Common Multiple
d97240e4-92bf-4df0-987b-c4d8a532bcc4.definition: Mathematical concept, the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both (or more) given integers. Usually calculated by reducing to the greatest common divisor.

d3034af1-4441-4ca7-8723-fb98380982d7.title: Linear Programming
d3034af1-4441-4ca7-8723-fb98380982d7.definition: Mathematical technique for optimizing (maximizing or minimizing) a linear objective function, subject to linear constraints. There are many applications in resource optimization.

d98ac940-c2fb-4823-8272-2b69e648c53f.title: Dynamic Programming
d98ac940-c2fb-4823-8272-2b69e648c53f.definition: The algorithm design model solves complex problems by dividing them into overlapping subproblems and storing the results of the subproblems to avoid recomputation.

7c491fd6-7a64-4c1b-86e3-e621cada652b.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
7c491fd6-7a64-4c1b-86e3-e621cada652b.definition: The algorithm finds the shortest path from a source to all other vertices in a graph with (possibly negative) edge weights and is capable of detecting negative cycles.

b84917ce-d2ac-4b2f-ab97-df91edca2a64.title: Space-Time Tradeoff
b84917ce-d2ac-4b2f-ab97-df91edca2a64.definition: Concept in algorithm design where an algorithm can be designed to use less time but more storage space, or vice versa, to achieve desired performance.

300ac15e-13b8-4a28-aad9-b27cf2e105ca.title: Hashing
300ac15e-13b8-4a28-aad9-b27cf2e105ca.definition: Technique of mapping input data of arbitrary size to a fixed-sized value (hash value), commonly used for fast searches, data integrity checking, and in hash tables for storage.

312d36cc-de0f-4899-ac04-9b336f593882.title: Exponential Growth Handling
312d36cc-de0f-4899-ac04-9b336f593882.definition: Techniques and algorithms are used to solve problems whose search space or complexity increases exponentially, often by pruning or estimation.

1ec89dab-1c08-457e-9757-d9620ef52f81.title: A* Algorithm
1ec89dab-1c08-457e-9757-d9620ef52f81.definition: The algorithm searches for the optimal path in the graph, using a heuristic function to estimate the cost from the current node to the goal, combined with the actual cost from the starting point, to find an efficient path.

1568f3be-9892-40eb-91d4-8933ba138291.title: Branch-and-Bound
1568f3be-9892-40eb-91d4-8933ba138291.definition: General algorithm design method for finding optimal solutions to discrete and combinatorial optimization problems, by dividing the search space into branches and eliminating non-potential (near) branches.

dad582f4-9551-442f-bad6-c809e6d9368b.title: Backtracking
dad582f4-9551-442f-bad6-c809e6d9368b.definition: Algorithmic techniques recursively solve problems by attempting to construct a solution step by step, eliminating options that do not lead to a valid solution, and backtracking to try other options.

cf837470-b6c5-4e87-a9e1-fb0f6f252cef.title: Iteration and Recursion
cf837470-b6c5-4e87-a9e1-fb0f6f252cef.definition: Two basic methods for repeating a block of code or a process. Iteration uses loops (for, while), while recursion uses functions that call themselves.

e7c8d233-d4f5-4128-9268-f1e40a5c9f07.title: Factorial
e7c8d233-d4f5-4128-9268-f1e40a5c9f07.definition: Mathematical function that calculates the product of all positive integers less than or equal to a given positive integer. Often used as an example to illustrate the concepts of iteration and recursion.

a34c2a58-6451-4dee-aec9-44723cc31751.title: Tree Search
a34c2a58-6451-4dee-aec9-44723cc31751.definition: General concept of algorithms that explore nodes and branches of a tree data structure to search for a specific node or gather information.

a50f1a5d-6ae1-4362-a5e4-d893b0dc4619.title: Approximation Algorithms
a50f1a5d-6ae1-4362-a5e4-d893b0dc4619.definition: The algorithms are designed to find an approximate solution to NP-hard optimization problems in polynomial time, when finding an optimal solution is not feasible.

bbf77808-d301-4590-ba4e-80dd9ae35ead.title: Iterative Improvement
bbf77808-d301-4590-ba4e-80dd9ae35ead.definition: Algorithms start with a feasible solution and then continuously improve it by taking small steps until a stopping criterion is reached (e.g., no further improvement is possible).

ae62674c-cef6-41f7-b1c0-61a6db1af2ab.title: Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm
ae62674c-cef6-41f7-b1c0-61a6db1af2ab.definition: Algorithm to calculate maximum flow in flow network. It works by finding paths that increase the flow from the source to the destination until there are no more paths that can be increased.

cc08fcec-b7a2-4004-acbf-4b1b7be9563c.title: Simplex Algorithm
cc08fcec-b7a2-4004-acbf-4b1b7be9563c.definition: A popular algorithm for solving linear programming problems, finding the optimal solution by moving between vertices of a polyhedral feasible region.

6eada02e-9ceb-4be6-ac82-c9a108a044e5.title: Randomized Algorithms
6eada02e-9ceb-4be6-ac82-c9a108a044e5.definition: Algorithms use randomness as part of their logic, often to find efficient solutions to problems that the algorithm determines are difficult to solve, or to achieve good average performance.

361e11ab-706d-4f5a-a69b-75a3f65b0d61.title: Max-Cut Problem
361e11ab-706d-4f5a-a69b-75a3f65b0d61.definition: Optimization problem on graph: find a partition of vertices into two sets such that the number of edges going between the two sets is maximum. It is an NP-hard problem.

0a83a003-372f-490f-b356-285932faaaeb.title: Balls and Bins Problem
0a83a003-372f-490f-b356-285932faaaeb.definition: A classic probability problem, often used to analyze the performance of random algorithms and data structures such as hash tables and load distribution.

30ba2f44-9d0a-4edc-afc5-a3fdaa2b6a8d.title: Quantum Computing
30ba2f44-9d0a-4edc-afc5-a3fdaa2b6a8d.definition: Field of research that uses quantum mechanical phenomena to perform calculations, with the potential to solve some problems faster than classical computers.

ae02ca16-8ced-42ad-b31e-cc3d4a605afc.title: Algorithm Paradigm Characteristics
ae02ca16-8ced-42ad-b31e-cc3d4a605afc.definition: Ability to explain the defining characteristics of various algorithmic models and illustrate them with concrete examples, showing how those examples satisfy the model's characteristics.

d175d28f-b5d3-484e-961f-8d8d5d0286d3.title: Algorithm Paradigm Evaluation
d175d28f-b5d3-484e-961f-8d8d5d0286d3.definition: Ability to evaluate and select appropriate algorithm models for practical problems, and analyze the advantages, disadvantages and trade-offs between selected models and algorithms.

6c62aaf3-508e-49b0-afdf-71d232c704fb.title: Iterative Algorithms
6c62aaf3-508e-49b0-afdf-71d232c704fb.definition: Concepts and examples of algorithms that use iterative structures to solve problems.

5984cf1d-6cd2-42c8-87a9-61db5b1b85d5.title: Recursive Algorithms
5984cf1d-6cd2-42c8-87a9-61db5b1b85d5.definition: Concepts and examples of algorithms that use recursive (calling itself) structures to solve problems.

60b92cad-3391-4de7-a54c-569186200086.title: Iteration vs. Recursion
60b92cad-3391-4de7-a54c-569186200086.definition: analyze the advantages, disadvantages and appropriate use cases of iterative and recursive algorithms.

4c431d7a-13e2-4223-a6bc-267bc2304cce.title: Greedy Method
4c431d7a-13e2-4223-a6bc-267bc2304cce.definition: Concept of the greedy method in algorithm design, including how it works and the conditions to ensure an optimal solution.

23817022-4850-4914-b692-8dad87a3b0fd.title: Greedy Optimality
23817022-4850-4914-b692-8dad87a3b0fd.definition: evaluate when a greedy algorithm can provide an optimal solution to a problem and when it cannot.

c33ec1ad-0bca-4650-9f5c-dcfa67d44be0.title: Exponential Complexity Handling
c33ec1ad-0bca-4650-9f5c-dcfa67d44be0.definition: Techniques and strategies for solving or approximating problems of exponential algorithmic complexity, in search of more feasible solutions.

41b40d99-f88f-42ab-9852-123f55e2eca2.title: Complexity Analysis Framework
41b40d99-f88f-42ab-9852-123f55e2eca2.definition: Conceptual framework used to evaluate algorithm performance, including basic factors and methods.

6d23665e-c25d-45ed-80ce-49babe1f30c9.title: Algorithm Performance Cases
6d23665e-c25d-45ed-80ce-49babe1f30c9.definition: Methods for evaluating the performance of an algorithm based on different input scenarios: best, average, and worst.

7b0c08be-ecdc-4085-97fb-61254fa3ba64.title: Empirical & Asymptotic Measurement
7b0c08be-ecdc-4085-97fb-61254fa3ba64.definition: Methods for measuring algorithm performance, including actual measurement and evaluation based on the growth rate of the complexity function.

0151d263-469a-4150-8bac-31ab9682792b.title: Input Size & Basic Operations
0151d263-469a-4150-8bac-31ab9682792b.definition: Basic factors to analyze algorithm complexity: input data size and number of primitive operations performed.

c521de71-3e7a-457f-ab06-8dc307b03362.title: Time-Space Efficiency
c521de71-3e7a-457f-ab06-8dc307b03362.definition: There are two main aspects of algorithm performance: the amount of time and the amount of memory space the algorithm requires.

784aa08c-0250-4bef-8d35-580676d3f368.title: Asymptotic Complexity Analysis
784aa08c-0250-4bef-8d35-580676d3f368.definition: Method for analyzing algorithm performance as input size approaches infinity, focusing on upper and lower bounds for the average and worst case.

c56d6262-ed22-4380-9f2d-eb4ae827b792.title: Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta
c56d6262-ed22-4380-9f2d-eb4ae827b792.definition: Formal mathematical notation used to describe the upper bound (Big-O), lower bound (Big-Omega), and strict bound (Big-Theta) of algorithmic complexity.

06591175-82ea-4a05-b1e2-012c00f8b596.title: Basic Complexity Classes
06591175-82ea-4a05-b1e2-012c00f8b596.definition: Groups classify algorithms based on the growth rate of the time or space complexity function.

25f57f01-3878-43fc-aad5-201e235dea27.title: O(1) Complexity
25f57f01-3878-43fc-aad5-201e235dea27.definition: Complexity class whose execution time is constant, independent of input size (e.g. array access).

9bab04f2-4f4b-4d02-bd24-0b29888da30c.title: O(log n) Complexity
9bab04f2-4f4b-4d02-bd24-0b29888da30c.definition: A class of complexity whose execution time increases as a logarithm of the input size (e.g., binary search).

45d1fd84-54d5-423d-b10e-09036e5fb9c4.title: O(n) Complexity
45d1fd84-54d5-423d-b10e-09036e5fb9c4.definition: Complexity class where execution time increases linearly with input size (e.g. linear search).

936484a8-06fd-439f-bcac-cefc189d05ec.title: O(n log n) Complexity
936484a8-06fd-439f-bcac-cefc189d05ec.definition: Complexity class whose execution time increases as n multiplied by the logarithm of n (e.g., mergesort).

d558b94a-cd2a-4487-9b18-c58e8a56343e.title: O(n^2) Complexity
d558b94a-cd2a-4487-9b18-c58e8a56343e.definition: A class of complexity whose execution time increases as the square of the input size (e.g. selection sort).

ff11efa8-a681-429c-8ce8-2ee20cb464f1.title: O(n^c) Complexity
ff11efa8-a681-429c-8ce8-2ee20cb464f1.definition: Complexity class where execution time increases as a power of the input size (e.g. O(n^3) Gauss elimination).

1b6ac486-f0cc-4bbd-9f00-103facb705ff.title: O(2^n) Complexity
1b6ac486-f0cc-4bbd-9f00-103facb705ff.definition: The class of complexity whose execution time increases exponentially with the input size, typically hard problems (e.g. Knapsack, SAT, TSP).

4e28ce42-d17a-4eaf-8025-0737c40d9a6d.title: O(n!) Complexity
4e28ce42-d17a-4eaf-8025-0737c40d9a6d.definition: A class of complexity whose execution time increases with the factorial of the input size, commonly encountered in problems that list all permutations (e.g., Hamiltonian Cycles, all permutations).

1f10fcb7-a60b-4923-b72f-4ca012425684.title: Empirical Performance Measurement
1f10fcb7-a60b-4923-b72f-4ca012425684.definition: The technique measures the actual performance of an algorithm by running it with different input data sets.

8a02dc4f-818a-4a57-96b0-9b44efa496de.title: Feasibility & Intractability
8a02dc4f-818a-4a57-96b0-9b44efa496de.definition: Classify problems into those that can be solved in polynomial time (feasible) and those that cannot (or are very difficult) to solve in polynomial time (impossible).

ea4f1714-3654-4187-8ff6-937007afeacf.title: P, NP, NP-Complete Classes
ea4f1714-3654-4187-8ff6-937007afeacf.definition: Important problem classes in computational complexity theory: P (solvable in polynomial time), NP (verifiable in polynomial time) and NP-Complete (is NP and the most difficult of NP).

f248598a-c650-45fd-a2f9-42de5a599825.title: NP-Complete Problems
f248598a-c650-45fd-a2f9-42de5a599825.definition: Problems in the NP-Complete class, have the characteristic that if a polynomial time algorithm is found for one problem, all other problems in the NP class can be solved in polynomial time (e.g. SAT, Knapsack, TSP).

0b02c169-39b0-4e5e-b381-1b826710c8e0.title: Reduction
0b02c169-39b0-4e5e-b381-1b826710c8e0.definition: The technique of converting one problem into another problem, often used to prove the NP-hardness or NP-completeness of a problem.

15ca7cba-8b37-4e3a-af69-a3d5ddbb7da5.title: Time-Space Trade-off
15ca7cba-8b37-4e3a-af69-a3d5ddbb7da5.definition: Algorithm design principle where reducing time requirements can increase space requirements and vice versa.

5f1bf839-cd53-458d-a863-878ca887bfd9.title: Little-o, Little-Omega, Little-Theta
5f1bf839-cd53-458d-a863-878ca887bfd9.definition: Additional mathematical notations to more strictly describe the asymptotic bounds of the complexity function (e.g., Little-o for a non-tight upper bound).

7b08958a-4f2b-43ff-bee1-c6f5e1074c4f.title: Formal Recurrence Analysis
7b08958a-4f2b-43ff-bee1-c6f5e1074c4f.definition: Techniques for analyzing the complexity of recursive algorithms using formal mathematical tools such as recursive equations.

7fdbd6f8-ecb9-4566-bbfc-1585a7bc5741.title: Amortized Analysis
7fdbd6f8-ecb9-4566-bbfc-1585a7bc5741.definition: Technique that analyzes the performance of a sequence of operations, where the high cost of some operations is offset by the low cost of other operations, yielding a low average cost per operation.

e2620ad4-86f0-42e0-b454-9bd800cb50f9.title: Turing Machine Complexity Models
e2620ad4-86f0-42e0-b454-9bd800cb50f9.definition: Theoretical models for defining and analyzing computational complexity are based on the concept of Turing machines.

2894421a-755b-4d36-a41b-bd97a9e00dcb.title: Turing Time Complexity
2894421a-755b-4d36-a41b-bd97a9e00dcb.definition: Define time complexity in the context of the Turing machine model.

8439db2d-b3fa-417d-af94-a28f133e8737.title: P, NP, NP-C, EXP (Turing)
8439db2d-b3fa-417d-af94-a28f133e8737.definition: The complexity classes P, NP, NP-Complete and EXP are defined based on the execution time of a Turing machine.

b9d3cf8d-799c-4c4a-94e3-a86fef062440.title: Cook-Levin Theorem
b9d3cf8d-799c-4c4a-94e3-a86fef062440.definition: The fundamental theorem in complexity theory proves that the SAT problem is NP-Complete.

d5ef54a2-dc29-421b-bad9-173b04a4c6af.title: Turing Space Complexity
d5ef54a2-dc29-421b-bad9-173b04a4c6af.definition: Define space complexity in the context of the Turing machine model.

382743c9-bbcc-4cb7-a65a-c384b59dad13.title: NSpace & PSpace Classes
382743c9-bbcc-4cb7-a65a-c384b59dad13.definition: Space complexity classes are defined by Turing machines: NSpace (non-deterministic polynomial space) and PSpace (deterministic polynomial space).

d627f000-53c5-4ddf-b097-472a3d6d141f.title: Savitch's Theorem
d627f000-53c5-4ddf-b097-472a3d6d141f.definition: The theorem proves that any language that can be recognized by a non-deterministic Turing machine with space S(n) can also be recognized by a deterministic Turing machine with space S(n)^2.

4a6bd1b8-0042-47a7-9570-3df12382382b.title: BST Balance Impact
4a6bd1b8-0042-47a7-9570-3df12382382b.definition: Explain how the balanced structure of a binary search tree affects the time complexity of operations such as search, insertion, deletion.

2009f358-1dca-4e22-a654-b4ea98fe70ed.title: NP-Hard, NP, NP-Complete Relation
2009f358-1dca-4e22-a654-b4ea98fe70ed.definition: Explain the relationship between the complexity classes NP, NP-Hard, and NP-Complete, where NP-Hard is the set of problems at least as difficult as the NP-Complete problem, and NP is the set of problems that are verifiable in polynomial time.

8d65b16f-5708-43cc-9367-2af817314948.title: Recurrence Relations for Time Complexity
8d65b16f-5708-43cc-9367-2af817314948.definition: The technique uses recursive equations to model and solve the time complexity of recursively defined algorithms.

eb330bb0-9547-4b73-9456-56c7025b6949.title: Master Theorem
eb330bb0-9547-4b73-9456-56c7025b6949.definition: Theorems used to solve recursive equations have a certain form, often appearing when analyzing the complexity of divide-and-conquer algorithms.

e5fe78f5-5810-4a01-b1b5-b32c923bfd1a.title: P and NP Complexity Classes
e5fe78f5-5810-4a01-b1b5-b32c923bfd1a.definition: Explain the definition and meaning of the P (polynomial time) and NP (nondeterministic polynomial time) complexity classes, including the relationship between them and their significance in computational theory.

8a32ca67-cbe1-4f5a-b4df-8ce679ed7fad.title: NP-Complete & Reduction Proofs
8a32ca67-cbe1-4f5a-b4df-8ce679ed7fad.definition: Prove that a problem is NP-Complete by attributing a known canonical NP-Complete problem (e.g., 3SAT and Clique) to it.

94b0da38-4fa0-4e09-806f-52558a7b079f.title: P-space & EXP Relation
94b0da38-4fa0-4e09-806f-52558a7b079f.definition: Explain the P-space (polynomial space) complexity class and its relationship to the EXP (exponential time) class.

6f4528cb-207a-45b3-af59-45f53ea154a3.title: Formal Automata Models
6f4528cb-207a-45b3-af59-45f53ea154a3.definition: An overview of formal automaton models used to describe language recognition and computation processes.

adb3a867-1114-4960-8b6b-90f277c8d0dc.title: Finite State Automaton (FSA)
adb3a867-1114-4960-8b6b-90f277c8d0dc.definition: Concepts, operations, and applications of finite-state automatons, including deterministic and non-deterministic variants.

ca60703a-a670-4955-955e-1515a9a148a3.title: Pushdown Automaton (PDA)
ca60703a-a670-4955-955e-1515a9a148a3.definition: Concept, operation and applications of stack automaton, a computational model more powerful than FSA, capable of processing context-free language.

49245e6e-2810-4c1b-97c2-6bddb7e3a8be.title: Linear Bounded Automaton (LBA)
49245e6e-2810-4c1b-97c2-6bddb7e3a8be.definition: Concepts, operations and applications of linear edge automatons, computational models involving context-sensitive languages.

7f931d2d-eef7-49af-91f6-1bc7321fa031.title: Turing Machine
7f931d2d-eef7-49af-91f6-1bc7321fa031.definition: Basic concept, structure, and operation of a Turing Machine, a universal computational model that represents any algorithm.

5e0e9c69-8250-49fc-9438-f87be1a01f71.title: Formal Language, Grammar, Chomsky Hierarchy
5e0e9c69-8250-49fc-9438-f87be1a01f71.definition: An overview of formal languages, the grammar used to describe them, and the Chomsky hierarchy that classifies language types based on the expressive power of the grammar.

db2a7d8f-3abe-4cc6-83d0-7fead1998a8c.title: Regular Language (Type-3)
db2a7d8f-3abe-4cc6-83d0-7fead1998a8c.definition: Definition, properties and representations of formal languages, corresponding to finite state automatons.

3fdb774a-d266-4bab-87ec-a051bf47aa1c.title: Regular Expression (Regex)
3fdb774a-d266-4bab-87ec-a051bf47aa1c.definition: Syntax, semantics, and applications of regular expressions for describing and matching patterns in regular languages.

6fcbd19c-0be2-4a65-a56b-bff6b02af457.title: Context-Free Language (Type-2)
6fcbd19c-0be2-4a65-a56b-bff6b02af457.definition: Definition, properties, and representations of context-free languages, corresponding to stack automatons.

a200e98f-a07a-49dd-b8cd-c95424c94ccb.title: Context-Sensitive Language (Type-1)
a200e98f-a07a-49dd-b8cd-c95424c94ccb.definition: Definition, properties, and representations of context-sensitive languages, corresponding to linear boundary automatons.

1dc1eb93-91c9-4a9d-895f-a4d92ef66dcf.title: Recursively Enumerable Language (Type-0)
1dc1eb93-91c9-4a9d-895f-a4d92ef66dcf.definition: Definition, properties, and representations of recursive enumeration languages, corresponding to Turing Machines.

1c0800ed-e775-4a3c-adb1-230246c79680.title: Chomsky Hierarchy Relations
1c0800ed-e775-4a3c-adb1-230246c79680.definition: analyze the correspondence relationship between automaton types (FSA, PDA, LBA, Turing Machine), language types (regular, context-free, context-sensitive, recursively enumerable) and grammar types in the Chomsky hierarchy.

e65be407-3e28-479d-931e-53581018fd32.title: Decidability, Computability, Halting Problem
e65be407-3e28-479d-931e-53581018fd32.definition: The concepts of problem determinism, function computability, and Halting Problem along with their meaning in computational theory.

b06f6b89-6035-4423-ae1d-3a8b74a3cafd.title: Church-Turing Thesis
b06f6b89-6035-4423-ae1d-3a8b74a3cafd.definition: Explain the Church-Turing Thesis, which asserts that a Turing Machine can compute any function that an algorithm can compute, and what it means for computer science.

bc134d37-491b-4db0-9a5a-5ebd01738436.title: Algorithm Correctness
bc134d37-491b-4db0-9a5a-5ebd01738436.definition: Methods and techniques for proving the correctness of an algorithm, ensuring the algorithm behaves as expected for all valid inputs.

f46e2aba-d255-4532-a8fc-9c63159f962c.title: Invariants (Loop, Recursion)
f46e2aba-d255-4532-a8fc-9c63159f962c.definition: Use invariants (e.g. loop invariants) to prove the correctness of algorithms in iterative, recursive, or tree search structures.

ec72807c-5466-48c3-be1a-1f321e9d3ce2.title: DFA vs NFA
ec72807c-5466-48c3-be1a-1f321e9d3ce2.definition: Compare and contrast the capabilities of deterministic and non-deterministic automatons in models such as FSA and PDA, including parity in computational power.

4ff81385-eb81-4ca6-be98-c1ed8bad3f90.title: Pumping Lemma Proofs
4ff81385-eb81-4ca6-be98-c1ed8bad3f90.definition: apply Pumping Lemma to prove that a language does not belong to a certain class of formal languages.

8dda8427-96ba-4a41-a367-314a328ef016.title: Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages
8dda8427-96ba-4a41-a367-314a328ef016.definition: Use Pumping Lemma to prove the limits of finite-state automatons and regular languages, i.e. prove that a language is not regular.

53b0ce9a-c15a-4dac-992c-fd5bd570397c.title: Pumping Lemma for CFL
53b0ce9a-c15a-4dac-992c-fd5bd570397c.definition: Use Pumping Lemma to demonstrate the limits of stack automaton and context-free languages, i.e. prove a language is not context-free.

a166d665-9643-4bad-b72a-9fc6d2090ca6.title: Advanced Decidability (Arithmetization, Diagonalization)
a166d665-9643-4bad-b72a-9fc6d2090ca6.definition: Advanced techniques for decidability analysis, including arithmetic and diagonalization, to prove undecidable problems, such as the Stationarity Problem.

b00d4370-9132-4a17-8884-ccd873ab2969.title: Arithmetization & Diagonalization for Halting Problem
b00d4370-9132-4a17-8884-ccd873ab2969.definition: apply arithmetic and diagonalization techniques to prove that the Stopping Problem for Turing Machines is undecidable.

329fe50f-5809-4e0e-9dcb-cefa273110ae.title: Reducibility
329fe50f-5809-4e0e-9dcb-cefa273110ae.definition: The concept of reducibility between problems and different types of reducibility is used to classify the difficulty of problems.

4567f8c9-8474-4430-9b82-a67e5f7295c6.title: Time Complexity (Turing Machine)
4567f8c9-8474-4430-9b82-a67e5f7295c6.definition: Algorithm time complexity analysis based on the Turing Machine model, including asymptotic notations and classification of time complexity classes.

feaf7b3e-cc93-4fa5-9cc7-4331ba8afecf.title: Space Complexity (Pspace, Savitch's Theorem)
