feaf7b3e-cc93-4fa5-9cc7-4331ba8afecf.definition: Concept of space complexity (amount of memory required), space complexity classes such as Pspace and Savitch's Theorem.

626507f6-886f-4b42-85b0-bb88ba3f540b.title: Equivalent Computation Models
626507f6-886f-4b42-85b0-bb88ba3f540b.definition: Study of different computational models with power equivalent to Turing Machines, demonstrating that they can simulate each other.

b4c522a7-b51f-4234-839e-c282c29f261e.title: Turing Machine Variants
b4c522a7-b51f-4234-839e-c282c29f261e.definition: Study the standard Turing Machine and its variants such as the multiband Turing Machine, the Deterministic Turing Machine, and demonstrate their equivalence in computational power.

5fa92847-2fb3-4b9b-bdf4-1e70a4c82fc3.title: Lambda Calculus
5fa92847-2fb3-4b9b-bdf4-1e70a4c82fc3.definition: Introduction to Lambda Calculus as a formal computational model, especially important in functional programming.

50d08560-fdfc-4ad6-bc10-a7262de5c8c3.title: Mu-Recursive Functions
50d08560-fdfc-4ad6-bc10-a7262de5c8c3.definition: Introduction to Recursive Functions Mu as another formal computational model, equivalent to a Turing Machine.

a57c7b10-ed81-43f4-ba8e-3a1d4a634cf4.title: Quantum Computing
a57c7b10-ed81-43f4-ba8e-3a1d4a634cf4.definition: An overview of the field of quantum computing, its basic principles and potential.

43768421-323a-4a34-b725-87bf4fee30e7.title: Quantum Mechanics Postulates
43768421-323a-4a34-b725-87bf4fee30e7.definition: Study the basic postulates of quantum mechanics that underlie quantum computing.

21215402-4e43-41dd-95c0-6e00b2d882a2.title: Quantum State Space
21215402-4e43-41dd-95c0-6e00b2d882a2.definition: The concept of the state space that qubits can exist in in quantum computing.

34f736fd-488f-4f90-a1e8-6d8709f77526.title: Quantum State Evolution
34f736fd-488f-4f90-a1e8-6d8709f77526.definition: Rules and how quantum states change over time or due to the effects of quantum operations.

63dc5fca-ccd8-42fb-896f-5da7afa11d3c.title: Quantum State Composition
63dc5fca-ccd8-42fb-896f-5da7afa11d3c.definition: How the states of multiple qubits combine to form the states of a larger quantum system.

5674176d-6d7f-4db7-a7a0-bcc07db6d6a5.title: Quantum State Measurement
5674176d-6d7f-4db7-a7a0-bcc07db6d6a5.definition: The process of measuring quantum states and the associated wave function collapse.

7a1d2b24-9918-444f-8e1e-1b8b96b373c8.title: Qubit Column Vector Representation
7a1d2b24-9918-444f-8e1e-1b8b96b373c8.definition: How to represent the state of qubits (quantum bits) using column vectors in linear algebra.

3e022e9f-8693-47a0-be9f-484cbcf66d53.title: Quantum Operation Matrix Representation
3e022e9f-8693-47a0-be9f-484cbcf66d53.definition: The way to represent quantum operations (quantum gates) uses matrices to influence the qubit state.

26720c22-5ea7-4936-9f00-a717ff9df27d.title: Basic Quantum Gates (XNOT, CNOT)
26720c22-5ea7-4936-9f00-a717ff9df27d.definition: Introduce and explain basic quantum gates such as XNOT gate (Pauli-X) and CNOT gate (Controlled-NOT).

8e925654-e881-4ee1-8347-1283fe45634e.title: Universal Turing Machine
8e925654-e881-4ee1-8347-1283fe45634e.definition: Explain the concept of a Universal Turing Machine, its ability to simulate any other Turing Machine, and its operation as a model of a programmable computer.

4e6763e2-f554-4025-8a60-8edc1f2ec762.title: Regex vs Type-3 Regular Expressions
4e6763e2-f554-4025-8a60-8edc1f2ec762.definition: Explain the difference between regular expressions used in programming languages ​​(which often have extended features beyond Type-3 regular languages) and formal regular expressions that correspond to Type-3 acceptors.

be8c0de1-fbef-43af-933c-498427a7da39.title: Rice's Theorem
be8c0de1-fbef-43af-933c-498427a7da39.definition: Explain Rice's Theorem, an important result in the theory of computation about the undecidability of non-trivial properties of computable functions.

047ae408-c7a9-4157-84c4-02e583ecfecf.title: Proof of Uncomputability by Reduction
047ae408-c7a9-4157-84c4-02e583ecfecf.definition: Explain an example of proving a problem to be non-computable by reducing it to a known non-computable problem.

f308d456-d25b-4491-b66f-18c015270176.title: Primitive Recursive Functions
f308d456-d25b-4491-b66f-18c015270176.definition: Explain primitive recursive functions, their meaning, and their implementation on a Turing Machine.

11450427-ae44-4ddd-bfb4-f1829ff4c9af.title: General Recursive Functions
11450427-ae44-4ddd-bfb4-f1829ff4c9af.definition: Explain general recursive functions, their meaning, and their implementation on a Turing Machine.

81798694-d6b6-4521-a653-8b1ea4779514.title: Recursive Function Components
81798694-d6b6-4521-a653-8b1ea4779514.definition: Explain the basic components that make up recursive functions: zero function, successor, selection, primitive recursion, composition, and the Mu operator.

43980652-e534-47af-9f8b-25a3fd2794f4.title: Recursive Functions on Turing Machine
43980652-e534-47af-9f8b-25a3fd2794f4.definition: Explain how primitive and general recursive functions can be implemented or simulated on a Turing Machine model.

ea5acc98-e3d7-4e4b-8bb3-116369db8dc1.title: Lambda Calculus Computation
ea5acc98-e3d7-4e4b-8bb3-116369db8dc1.definition: Explains how calculations are performed in Lambda Calculus, including concepts such as Alpha transformation and Beta reduction.

c2a9fcf3-f486-4847-9ca1-5da62e33905f.title: Alpha Conversion (Lambda Calculus)
c2a9fcf3-f486-4847-9ca1-5da62e33905f.definition: Explain the process of renaming bound variables in Lambda Calculus without changing the meaning of the expression.

331646d0-76c1-4f2a-bcfe-d2106b0501d0.title: Beta Reduction (Lambda Calculus)
331646d0-76c1-4f2a-bcfe-d2106b0501d0.definition: Explain the function application process in Lambda Calculus, replacing parameters with arguments.

f4ef06f2-6420-4b29-b0ad-c1d9423e025e.title: Quantum State Space
f4ef06f2-6420-4b29-b0ad-c1d9423e025e.definition: Explain the state space of a quantum system, represented as a unit vector in Hilbert space.

f6413b45-4c9a-4d4a-9e04-d01cdc0b5900.title: Quantum State Evolution (Unitary Operators)
f6413b45-4c9a-4d4a-9e04-d01cdc0b5900.definition: Explain the state evolution of a quantum system through the use of unitary operators.

41954476-58d8-44bd-8dcd-59fe933f5f20.title: Quantum State Composition (Tensor Product)
41954476-58d8-44bd-8dcd-59fe933f5f20.definition: Explain how to combine the states of multiple quantum systems through the use of tensor products.

a092f55e-920d-445c-ab01-f04fb349bb66.title: Quantum Measurement (Probabilistic Outcome)
a092f55e-920d-445c-ab01-f04fb349bb66.definition: Explain the probabilistic measurement results of a quantum state.

79ce8b85-61e3-4427-b127-71f70e389d30.title: Pauli-X Gate
79ce8b85-61e3-4427-b127-71f70e389d30.definition: Explain the operation of a quantum XNOT gate (also called Pauli-X) on a quantum bit represented by a matrix and column vector.

d570d697-58a6-4c84-8a73-827573a8f0fe.title: CNOT Gate
d570d697-58a6-4c84-8a73-827573a8f0fe.definition: Explain the operation of a CNOT (Controlled-NOT) quantum gate on a quantum bit represented by a matrix and column vector.

f2c56840-a496-4a40-ab99-8a6dc3a10a44.title: Qubit Representation (Matrix/Vector)
f2c56840-a496-4a40-ab99-8a6dc3a10a44.definition: Explain how a quantum bit is represented as a matrix and column vector in quantum computing.

329a1787-fc49-4ee3-b704-258cf8e0675c.title: Ethical & Safe Algorithms
329a1787-fc49-4ee3-b704-258cf8e0675c.definition: understand and evaluate algorithms from a social, ethical, and security perspective.

1c455de5-2095-430d-bdd5-60837af003bd.title: Algorithmic Fairness
1c455de5-2095-430d-bdd5-60837af003bd.definition: understand the concept and importance of fairness in algorithm design and implementation.

e14f15fb-b61b-45f8-ac01-464c6707e909.title: Anonymity
e14f15fb-b61b-45f8-ac01-464c6707e909.definition: understand concepts and techniques that ensure anonymity in data processing and algorithms.

376f026e-c8a1-4077-a76a-4172c92f8d99.title: Differential Privacy
376f026e-c8a1-4077-a76a-4172c92f8d99.definition: Explain how differential privacy protects personal information in a data set.

209e8001-05c8-463a-9e28-75d0ce17ede2.title: Algorithmic Accountability
209e8001-05c8-463a-9e28-75d0ce17ede2.definition: understand accountability regarding algorithmic decisions and outcomes.

3b0ec617-278e-4b20-a21b-c5a249c9836a.title: Algorithmic Transparency
3b0ec617-278e-4b20-a21b-c5a249c9836a.definition: understand the need for transparency in algorithmic operations and decisions.

f29c8726-ab3b-4430-b3f2-2cabd66694c6.title: Responsible Algorithms
f29c8726-ab3b-4430-b3f2-2cabd66694c6.definition: understand the principles of designing and implementing algorithms responsibly, considering social and ethical impact.

a504ab1c-66d9-4cdc-b28b-3cb280ffa179.title: Inefficient Algorithm Impact
a504ab1c-66d9-4cdc-b28b-3cb280ffa179.definition: analyze the economic and other impacts of using ineffective algorithms.

c962aed0-4a11-4cda-be26-061faac11c84.title: Algorithmic Sustainability
c962aed0-4a11-4cda-be26-061faac11c84.definition: evaluate algorithms for sustainability aspects, including long-term environmental and social impacts.

f01b92db-816f-41fc-b49b-c0dfb86bfa16.title: Context-Aware Computing
f01b92db-816f-41fc-b49b-c0dfb86bfa16.definition: understand systems and algorithms that collect and use contextual information to provide appropriate services or decisions.

d78c14e2-66cf-46b1-81db-67dd8e553643.title: Algorithmic Social Solutions
d78c14e2-66cf-46b1-81db-67dd8e553643.definition: Develop algorithmic solutions to solve real-world social problems, for example routing ambulances to hospitals.

704afbbc-0e84-4235-8b23-1144a7e973e2.title: Algorithm Environmental Impact
704afbbc-0e84-4235-8b23-1144a7e973e2.definition: Explain the impact an algorithm can have on the environment when used to solve a real-world problem.

72c83b18-6c37-44cb-85f9-e00fef74f872.title: Algorithm Social Impact
72c83b18-6c37-44cb-85f9-e00fef74f872.definition: Explain how an algorithm can affect different social groups in different ways when used in real-world problems.

b08a891f-bfaf-4c70-9f12-73c9ddc1bf20.title: Data Structure & Algorithm Selection
b08a891f-bfaf-4c70-9f12-73c9ddc1bf20.definition: Prepare a presentation to justify the choice of the appropriate data structure and/or algorithm to solve a given practical problem.

ec131a43-331c-46e7-b151-908c896f3b02.title: Algorithm Design Choices
ec131a43-331c-46e7-b151-908c896f3b02.definition: Explain the effects of design choices related to algorithm design.

087c3098-5af2-4001-89bc-470fd6c07434.title: Proof-of-Work Algorithm
087c3098-5af2-4001-89bc-470fd6c07434.definition: Explain Proof-of-Work algorithms, especially the trade-offs associated with them.

99f1bd7d-7b78-40b7-9123-11067d47577f.title: Proof-of-Stake Algorithm
99f1bd7d-7b78-40b7-9123-11067d47577f.definition: Explain Proof-of-Stake algorithms, especially the trade-offs associated with them.

4a525aa1-d887-4822-ae0e-a33ac078cfb5.title: PoW vs PoS Trade-offs
4a525aa1-d887-4822-ae0e-a33ac078cfb5.definition: Explain the trade-offs involved when comparing Proof-of-Work and Proof-of-Stake algorithms.

8dc28c0b-a527-43f0-948a-15d8d68a29d6.title: Big-O Complexity Analysis
8dc28c0b-a527-43f0-948a-15d8d68a29d6.definition: Introducing the method of analyzing algorithm complexity using Big-O notation.

4641d31a-62ad-4182-9800-a80631969193.title: Graph Algorithms
4641d31a-62ad-4182-9800-a80631969193.definition: Learn about algorithms that work on graph data structures, such as finding the shortest path or traversing a graph.

42016d34-2695-461e-8864-0bd38e9299ab.title: Backtracking Algorithm
42016d34-2695-461e-8864-0bd38e9299ab.definition: Learn about the backtracking algorithm, a technique for solving problems by systematically trying each solution.

e4005ae0-d4ec-4e7c-95a1-93c93b161ba9.title: Array
e4005ae0-d4ec-4e7c-95a1-93c93b161ba9.definition: Array data structure and basic operations with arrays.

ab96e5a0-cbc5-4a7d-a63e-c0502ee506b1.title: String
ab96e5a0-cbc5-4a7d-a63e-c0502ee506b1.definition: Character string data structure and basic operations with strings.

46db4db2-c399-4053-8a3e-22b8602ea4a7.title: Search Algorithms
46db4db2-c399-4053-8a3e-22b8602ea4a7.definition: Introducing algorithms used to search for an element in a data set.

71deaa70-7690-4f9b-bd3f-d80bacf2090a.title: Linear Search O(n)
71deaa70-7690-4f9b-bd3f-d80bacf2090a.definition: Linear search algorithm with O(n) time complexity.

74b9ca9e-381d-4a2f-82a5-2f8e14757ba8.title: Algorithmic SEP Basic
74b9ca9e-381d-4a2f-82a5-2f8e14757ba8.definition: Social, ethical, and professional issues related to algorithmic platforms, are presented at a basic level during SEP hours.

440ad6a0-95d4-4211-8488-2dd2823ce10a.title: Brute Force Strategy Basic
440ad6a0-95d4-4211-8488-2dd2823ce10a.definition: A strategy that solves a problem by trying every possible possibility directly, for example in linear search. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: under 1 hour)

068fbeba-1728-4974-ba8e-a132cf21f4ff.title: Linear Search Algorithm
068fbeba-1728-4974-ba8e-a132cf21f4ff.definition: A search algorithm iterates through each element in a list sequentially until the desired element is found or the list is exhausted. (Example for exhaust and repeat)

9a2af92d-5733-4b24-bb78-63ac5737739a.title: Iteration Strategy Basic
9a2af92d-5733-4b24-bb78-63ac5737739a.definition: Technique that solves a problem by repeating a set of instructions until a certain condition is achieved, a typical example is linear search. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: under 1 hour)

8389995c-ed0f-442d-ae84-9c1ec00f0243.title: Basic Complexity Classes
8389995c-ed0f-442d-ae84-9c1ec00f0243.definition: The basic classifications of algorithm complexity are based on the computational resources (time or space) they consume. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: under 1 hour)

6bcdc3fc-2784-4bda-9b7f-49598da1b2f0.title: O(1) Constant Time
6bcdc3fc-2784-4bda-9b7f-49598da1b2f0.definition: The runtime complexity of the algorithm does not vary with input size. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: under 1 hour)

705269f9-da8c-45e4-9115-01c90865d5af.title: O(n) Linear Time
705269f9-da8c-45e4-9115-01c90865d5af.definition: The runtime complexity of the algorithm increases proportionally to the input size. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: under 1 hour)

8af693c6-5c44-4cdb-a6d5-66f113ac7013.title: Abstract Data Types (ADTs)
8af693c6-5c44-4cdb-a6d5-66f113ac7013.definition: The concept of a data type is defined by behavior from the user's perspective, not the internal implementation. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

672c7225-17c4-4f5f-a73a-f8004d31cf82.title: Binary Search
672c7225-17c4-4f5f-a73a-f8004d31cf82.definition: An efficient search algorithm for finding an item in a sorted list by repeatedly bisecting the search space. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

729b2875-cf3c-4424-ac94-ef4d4d41de37.title: Multidimensional Arrays
729b2875-cf3c-4424-ac94-ef4d4d41de37.definition: Array data structures have more than one index to access elements, such as matrices. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

2c4c1fd5-fa2f-4c08-8f54-7363bbbf9f92.title: Linked List
2c4c1fd5-fa2f-4c08-8f54-7363bbbf9f92.definition: A linear data structure consists of a sequence of 'nodes', where each node contains data and a pointer to the next node. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

59bbc09f-5049-4506-b024-9159a6526443.title: Hash Map & Collision Strategies
59bbc09f-5049-4506-b024-9159a6526443.definition: A data structure that maps keys to values ​​using a hash function, including methods for dealing with two keys hashing into the same location. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

aa2f5da9-eeb9-4373-a5ec-2c542fd2b2b8.title: Records, Structs, Tuples
aa2f5da9-eeb9-4373-a5ec-2c542fd2b2b8.definition: Composite data types allow data items of different types to be grouped under a single name. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

b9772bc6-4665-4182-938c-16fb2601d18c.title: Object
b9772bc6-4665-4182-938c-16fb2601d18c.definition: An entity in object-oriented programming that combines data and methods that operate on that data. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

d909221c-e52e-4310-8f26-7e3529e3694f.title: Set
d909221c-e52e-4310-8f26-7e3529e3694f.definition: A data structure that stores a unique set of values, in no particular order. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

f61cfcb5-a5a5-4344-b14c-ccb2ac459b25.title: Stack
f61cfcb5-a5a5-4344-b14c-ccb2ac459b25.definition: The data structure follows the LIFO principle (Last-In, First-Out). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

9467f92e-83a1-4b0f-bea2-805d7958e212.title: Queue
9467f92e-83a1-4b0f-bea2-805d7958e212.definition: The data structure follows the FIFO principle (First-In, First-Out). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

c663912c-f998-4b9d-89be-15cf346e3fcf.title: Deque
c663912c-f998-4b9d-89be-15cf346e3fcf.definition: Double-ended queue, allowing elements to be added and removed from both ends. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

63362a38-62ab-4948-97ea-66bea9c1079b.title: Binary Tree
63362a38-62ab-4948-97ea-66bea9c1079b.definition: Tree data structure in which each node has at most two child nodes. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

a7c2233c-9913-42d0-b9d7-c4ad94eb642a.title: Ordered Tree
a7c2233c-9913-42d0-b9d7-c4ad94eb642a.definition: A tree data structure whose child nodes are arranged in a certain order (e.g., binary search tree). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

bef6e54b-9e89-4811-888e-d7937bdae216.title: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
bef6e54b-9e89-4811-888e-d7937bdae216.definition: The tree or graph traversal algorithm starts from the root node and explores all neighboring nodes at the current level before moving on to deeper levels. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

7ce666bf-de32-4a18-b31b-a99c8c742a34.title: Depth-First Search (DFS)
7ce666bf-de32-4a18-b31b-a99c8c742a34.definition: The tree or graph traversal algorithm starts at the root node and explores as far each branch as possible before backtracking. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

55943a93-a073-429b-ae3c-6c8ff4abd2af.title: Search Algorithms
55943a93-a073-429b-ae3c-6c8ff4abd2af.definition: Algorithms are designed to search for an item or a set of items with specific properties in a data structure. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

02a25de8-948b-4d96-8b0f-05ef09966e90.title: Selection Sort O(n²)
02a25de8-948b-4d96-8b0f-05ef09966e90.definition: An in-place sorting algorithm compares the elements in the list to find the smallest (or largest) element and swaps it with the element in the first unsorted position. Runtime complexity is O(n²). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

f3bf0774-be6e-4ab4-aeba-fafd1f82b093.title: Binary Search O(log n)
f3bf0774-be6e-4ab4-aeba-fafd1f82b093.definition: Efficient search algorithm in sorted list, has logarithmic running time complexity O(log₂ n). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

53f095a9-c96e-41ff-addd-ec4bed76a9e3.title: Sorting Algorithms Intermediate
53f095a9-c96e-41ff-addd-ec4bed76a9e3.definition: Algorithms are designed to arrange the elements of a list in a certain order. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

74b2c374-f32e-4cbf-8048-b4172f0cb3a3.title: Merge Sort O(n log n)
74b2c374-f32e-4cbf-8048-b4172f0cb3a3.definition: A sorting algorithm based on the divide-and-conquer principle, with running time complexity O(n log n). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

a32bff74-6c8d-4931-b4b0-fcfc5aa68ea9.title: Tree Search O(log b n)
a32bff74-6c8d-4931-b4b0-fcfc5aa68ea9.definition: A search algorithm on a tree data structure with logarithmic runtime complexity, often used for balanced trees or search trees. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 12 hours)

cf01d2ca-df97-465f-8e8b-931917e51445.title: Brute Force
cf01d2ca-df97-465f-8e8b-931917e51445.definition: A strategy that solves a problem by trying every possible possibility directly, such as a selection sort algorithm. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

5f885258-299d-4da4-97ed-6653263bdad6.title: Decrease-and-Conquer
5f885258-299d-4da4-97ed-6653263bdad6.definition: An algorithmic strategy that solves a problem by transforming it into a smaller version of the same problem, for example searching a tree by depth or breadth. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

3e43875a-30bf-421d-922f-9d8518d03dd0.title: Divide-and-Conquer
3e43875a-30bf-421d-922f-9d8518d03dd0.definition: An algorithmic strategy divides the problem into smaller subproblems, solves the subproblems independently, and then combines the solutions. For example: merge sort, quick sort. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

2889a180-0b0f-486c-bcc2-1c6279669142.title: Quicksort
2889a180-0b0f-486c-bcc2-1c6279669142.definition: A sorting algorithm based on the divide and conquer principle, which usually has good performance in practice. (An example for Divide-and-Conquer)

6e327c87-73ca-46c2-852f-1e42c984942c.title: Iteration vs Recursion
6e327c87-73ca-46c2-852f-1e42c984942c.definition: Compare and differentiate between two basic programming techniques for solving problems, including for example factorials or tree searches. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

362edc16-771a-461b-bdf1-3d3eda043872.title: Space-Time Tradeoff
362edc16-771a-461b-bdf1-3d3eda043872.definition: Concept in algorithm design where memory resources are used to reduce execution time, or vice versa, a typical example is hashing. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

b6594c3d-8bf4-454f-89a6-fc5ea0e19983.title: Complexity Analysis Framework
b6594c3d-8bf4-454f-89a6-fc5ea0e19983.definition: Systematic structure for evaluating algorithm performance in time and space. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

22434eb0-7e04-4fce-8c9c-7cb83bdba69c.title: Intermediate Complexity Classes
22434eb0-7e04-4fce-8c9c-7cb83bdba69c.definition: Basic classifications of algorithm complexity, advanced above the foundation level, include logarithmic, linear logarithmic, and quadratic classes. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

3a30f941-0fad-4b24-bed7-d71e49542eda.title: Logarithmic Time O(log n)
3a30f941-0fad-4b24-bed7-d71e49542eda.definition: The runtime complexity of an algorithm increases with the logarithm of the input size, for example binary search. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

14d547ef-f373-4f2f-93a1-adeb7f56b662.title: Linearithmic Time O(n log n)
14d547ef-f373-4f2f-93a1-adeb7f56b662.definition: The runtime complexity of the algorithm increases as n multiplied by the logarithm of n, for example merge sort. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

1343a27a-61f9-4c60-9dec-37ea56389309.title: Quadratic Time O(n²)
1343a27a-61f9-4c60-9dec-37ea56389309.definition: The runtime complexity of an algorithm increases with the square of the input size, for example in select sort. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

81c631f5-9830-42e8-a5e4-13dc3cc56b02.title: Time-Space Tradeoff
81c631f5-9830-42e8-a5e4-13dc3cc56b02.definition: Algorithm design considerations regarding optimization between execution time and amount of memory space required. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

d007c1d5-fb4a-4c1b-a7b6-04427b31739b.title: Algorithmic SEP
d007c1d5-fb4a-4c1b-a7b6-04427b31739b.definition: Enhance and refine understanding of the impact of algorithm design and use on society, presented at an intermediate level during SEP hours.

4e70fe91-1949-4e1e-b1ef-eb41c942b319.title: Graph
4e70fe91-1949-4e1e-b1ef-eb41c942b319.definition: A nonlinear data structure consists of a set of vertices (nodes) and edges (links) connecting those vertices. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

cf5e6819-1504-4f79-91e2-0002ff666427.title: Graph Algorithms (Advanced)
cf5e6819-1504-4f79-91e2-0002ff666427.definition: Algorithms are designed to solve problems on graph data structures, such as finding the shortest path or traversing the graph. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

d5556e4b-80a1-4473-9d2a-f1bc0398ac0a.title: Asymptotic Complexity Analysis
d5556e4b-80a1-4473-9d2a-f1bc0398ac0a.definition: Method for analyzing the performance of an algorithm when the input size approaches infinity, using the notation Big O, Big Omega, Big Theta. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

4555be29-3ec7-4181-85c4-f811b8230617.title: Advanced Complexity Classes
4555be29-3ec7-4181-85c4-f811b8230617.definition: The basic classifications of algorithmic complexity, considered at a more advanced level, include higher complexity classes such as exponential and factorial. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

9cd9a729-4066-4be6-9650-63e8310a7ec0.title: Exponential Time O(2^n)
9cd9a729-4066-4be6-9650-63e8310a7ec0.definition: The runtime complexity of an algorithm increases exponentially with the input size, often indicating intractable problems. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

a724b344-46bd-40b3-9ad7-e7292cdf8d15.title: Factorial Time O(n!)
a724b344-46bd-40b3-9ad7-e7292cdf8d15.definition: The runtime complexity of an algorithm increases with the factorial of the input size, which often occurs in permutation or all-instance problems. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

7ac22295-38f0-4ac8-b5cc-0a488be6ce50.title: Empirical Performance Measurement
7ac22295-38f0-4ac8-b5cc-0a488be6ce50.definition: The methods realistically measure the runtime and memory consumption of algorithms by running them against specific data sets. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

41a3f5c7-24aa-4c09-a161-6259f699f74e.title: Tractability
41a3f5c7-24aa-4c09-a161-6259f699f74e.definition: The likelihood that a problem can be solved by an algorithm in a reasonable amount of time (usually polynomial time). (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

da50ff65-9313-4d1d-8d05-82535ca36db0.title: Intractability
da50ff65-9313-4d1d-8d05-82535ca36db0.definition: The concept of problems for which there are no known polynomial time algorithms to solve them, often requiring exponential or factorial time. (As part of the AL-Complexity unit: 3 hours)

883ffc97-d41b-4c50-a963-ebda3220280b.title: Brute Force (Advanced)
883ffc97-d41b-4c50-a963-ebda3220280b.definition: The strategy of solving problems by trying every possible possibility directly, is often applied to difficult problems such as the delivery man problem or the bag problem. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

0ca65ddb-7e39-47f4-b5d4-75b223ca27c7.title: Traveling Salesperson Problem
0ca65ddb-7e39-47f4-b5d4-75b223ca27c7.definition: An optimization problem in which a salesperson must visit a set of cities and return to the starting point, finding the shortest possible route that passes through each city exactly once. (An example of Brute Force)

67af373f-dc9b-4a1c-be61-19c0af8d78f3.title: Knapsack Problem
67af373f-dc9b-4a1c-be61-19c0af8d78f3.definition: An optimization problem in which a set of items, each with a weight and value, must be placed into a bag of limited capacity such that the total value is maximized. (An example of Brute Force)

cdcd200e-4ff3-4263-8227-d817d6b41374.title: Decrease-and-Conquer (Advanced)
cdcd200e-4ff3-4263-8227-d817d6b41374.definition: An algorithmic strategy that solves a problem by transforming it into a smaller version of the same problem, for example topological sorting. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

62e7aa28-1730-4525-966e-2bb4ee58fbee.title: Topological Sort
62e7aa28-1730-4525-966e-2bb4ee58fbee.definition: Linearize the vertices of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) such that for every directed edge u -> v, vertex u comes before vertex v in the sort order. (An example for Decrease-and-Conquer)

02e7a3a0-68bd-4931-998d-59543e526753.title: Divide-and-Conquer (Advanced)
02e7a3a0-68bd-4931-998d-59543e526753.definition: An algorithmic strategy divides the problem into smaller subproblems, solves the subproblems independently, and then combines the solutions. For example, Strassen's algorithm for matrix multiplication. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

b9e430c4-9c1a-44d1-9f40-9e7426b96de4.title: Strassen's Algorithm
b9e430c4-9c1a-44d1-9f40-9e7426b96de4.definition: An algorithm for multiplying two n x n matrices that is faster than the standard matrix multiplication algorithm, using the principle of divide and conquer. (An example for Divide-and-Conquer)

f4b8a46b-48f6-49d4-9c86-d4244de75a3b.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm (Greedy)
f4b8a46b-48f6-49d4-9c86-d4244de75a3b.definition: An algorithmic strategy makes a locally optimal choice at each step in the hope of finding a globally optimal solution, such as Dijkstra's algorithm for finding the shortest path. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

916ad93f-b7a2-499e-88d3-640a9fa94805.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
916ad93f-b7a2-499e-88d3-640a9fa94805.definition: Algorithm to find the shortest path between nodes in a graph with positive edge weights. (An example for Greedy)

9c3c3ce4-cab8-4447-9efa-61f2f321c583.title: Kruskal's Algorithm (Greedy)
9c3c3ce4-cab8-4447-9efa-61f2f321c583.definition: An algorithmic strategy makes a locally optimal choice at each step in the hope of finding a globally optimal solution, for example the Kruskal algorithm for finding a minimum spanning tree. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

6d61448b-f405-49e1-9467-582bea5bed2d.title: Kruskal's Algorithm
6d61448b-f405-49e1-9467-582bea5bed2d.definition: Algorithm to find the minimum spanning tree for a weighted undirected graph. (An example for Greedy)

6ffc6bd3-2e54-4ccf-a60b-a8958c9359c0.title: Transform-and-Conquer: Heapsort
6ffc6bd3-2e54-4ccf-a60b-a8958c9359c0.definition: An algorithmic strategy solves a problem by transforming it into a version that a known algorithm can solve, such as heap sorting. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

9714546f-a6bf-4d92-ae94-0fd3eb00b45b.title: 2-3 Tree
9714546f-a6bf-4d92-ae94-0fd3eb00b45b.definition: A type of balanced search tree, where each node can have 2 or 3 child nodes, ensuring a logarithmic tree height. (An example for Transform-and-Conquer/Reduction)

d00751d5-613b-4dd5-b517-c34b2b98b21d.title: AVL Tree
d00751d5-613b-4dd5-b517-c34b2b98b21d.definition: A type of self-balancing binary search tree that maintains height balance of two subtrees to ensure logarithmic search, insertion, and deletion performance. (An example for Transform-and-Conquer/Reduction)

281d2fd1-0667-4997-810a-972caa7a6492.title: Red-Black Tree
281d2fd1-0667-4997-810a-972caa7a6492.definition: A type of self-balancing binary search tree that uses color attributes (red/black) to ensure logarithmic tree height and efficient operations. (An example for Transform-and-Conquer/Reduction)

e0ca1160-6180-42c3-892a-c821ccd03850.title: Warshall's Algorithm (DP)
e0ca1160-6180-42c3-892a-c821ccd03850.definition: An algorithmic technique that solves problems by dividing them into overlapping subproblems and optimization subproblems, storing the results to avoid recalculation. For example, Warshall's algorithm for finding transitive closure. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

e2d765cb-8e40-415f-8643-2433e172c8a1.title: Floyd's Algorithm (DP)
e2d765cb-8e40-415f-8643-2433e172c8a1.definition: An algorithmic technique that solves problems by dividing them into overlapping subproblems and optimization subproblems, storing the results to avoid recalculation. For example, Floyd's algorithm to find all shortest paths. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

ba7793ec-698f-47d0-890a-5961c29416eb.title: Floyd's Algorithm
ba7793ec-698f-47d0-890a-5961c29416eb.definition: The algorithm finds the shortest path between all pairs of vertices in a directed, weighted graph, which can handle negative weights. (An example for Dynamic Programming)

c2d05a69-293c-42ef-a611-63c7c05e63c1.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm (DP)
c2d05a69-293c-42ef-a611-63c7c05e63c1.definition: An algorithmic technique that solves problems by dividing them into overlapping subproblems and optimization subproblems, storing the results to avoid recalculation. For example, the Bellman-Ford algorithm for finding the shortest path from a source in a graph has negative edge weights. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

9beb434b-3979-4401-9764-08ac16eb7813.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
9beb434b-3979-4401-9764-08ac16eb7813.definition: The algorithm finds the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices in a directed graph with negative edge weights, detecting negative cycles. (An example for Dynamic Programming)

f9028785-696e-49ba-bb90-ed861e2e5f1c.title: A* Algorithm
f9028785-696e-49ba-bb90-ed861e2e5f1c.definition: Techniques used to solve problems of exponential complexity using approximation or intelligent search methods, such as the A* search algorithm. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

46173b70-c382-466b-8b64-f14e56192ce7.title: A* Algorithm
46173b70-c382-466b-8b64-f14e56192ce7.definition: A best path finding algorithm prioritizes finding a path from a source vertex to a destination vertex in a graph, using a heuristic function to estimate the lowest cost from the current vertex to the destination. (An example for Handling Exponential Growth)

c7de74ad-b35d-484b-8a37-b30e39aa8092.title: Branch-and-Bound
c7de74ad-b35d-484b-8a37-b30e39aa8092.definition: Techniques used to solve problems of exponential complexity using approximation or intelligent search methods, such as the branch-and-bound method. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

0a1c39e0-4772-4266-93f9-d10c5a3687da.title: Backtracking
0a1c39e0-4772-4266-93f9-d10c5a3687da.definition: Techniques used to solve problems of exponential complexity using approximation or intelligent search methods, such as backtracking algorithms. (As part of the AL-Strategies unit: 3 hours)

9fd8ffbb-a457-465b-aecf-de9dfe660d5f.title: Formal Models of Computation
9fd8ffbb-a457-465b-aecf-de9dfe660d5f.definition: Abstract mathematical models are used to study computation, including theoretical constructs such as Turing machines, grammars, and languages. (As part of AL-Models unit: 9 hours)

ded9443f-51a2-49c0-ae60-290a4c2b91ec.title: Formal Grammars
ded9443f-51a2-49c0-ae60-290a4c2b91ec.definition: System of rules for creating or analyzing strings in a formal language, often used in formal language theory. (As part of AL-Models unit: 9 hours)

9cc97bae-5159-43a2-a4cf-76c1696f1eb5.title: Formal Languages
9cc97bae-5159-43a2-a4cf-76c1696f1eb5.definition: A finite set of strings constructed from a set of symbols (alphabet), defined by a formal grammar. (As part of AL-Models unit: 9 hours)

5b51574b-514e-4726-ab68-cdaec2223874.title: Turing Machine
5b51574b-514e-4726-ab68-cdaec2223874.definition: An abstract mathematical model of a computer, used to define algorithms and study the limits of computation. (As part of AL-Models unit: 9 hours)

85288886-e4a6-4188-89bb-7ee25009bd47.title: Halting Problem Undecidability
85288886-e4a6-4188-89bb-7ee25009bd47.definition: The theorem proves that no algorithm can determine in general terms whether an arbitrary computer program stops (terminates) or runs forever. (As part of AL-Models unit: 9 hours)

bf3ca64a-b7cf-4d13-afc0-4e798faebb71.title: AL-SEP: Ethics & Society
bf3ca64a-b7cf-4d13-afc0-4e798faebb71.definition: Improve your understanding and ability to analyze the far-reaching impact of algorithm design and use on society, presented at an advanced level in SEP hours.

1a7c8788-50f3-430c-aed7-ba66acd548cf.title: Graph Algorithms (Advanced)
1a7c8788-50f3-430c-aed7-ba66acd548cf.definition: In-depth study of graph data structures and the complex algorithms used to process them, within the context of a 4-course framework. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

4a8b6a02-dcf8-4909-b10d-e1ed48afb248.title: Sorting Algorithms (Advanced)
4a8b6a02-dcf8-4909-b10d-e1ed48afb248.definition: Algorithms designed to sort the elements of a list in a certain order, including more efficient algorithms and algorithms with pseudo-linear complexity. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

5c4b7202-f30b-4d50-be1d-597bee477a07.title: Heap Sort O(n log n)
5c4b7202-f30b-4d50-be1d-597bee477a07.definition: The sorting algorithm is based on a heap data structure, which has a runtime complexity of O(n log n). (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

71c76ed0-a4d0-4436-b5e4-95e9504d83f8.title: Pseudo-Linear Complexity O(n)
71c76ed0-a4d0-4436-b5e4-95e9504d83f8.definition: Sorting algorithms have near-linear complexity O(n) under some specific conditions, such as bin sorting. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

1ffb9bdc-83be-4d28-806a-f5c36d94d50a.title: Bucket Sort
1ffb9bdc-83be-4d28-806a-f5c36d94d50a.definition: The sorting algorithm divides elements into a finite number of 'buckets', then sorts each bucket separately. Effective with evenly distributed data. (An example for Pseudo O(n) complexity)

a77f1f6b-7194-4662-b0dc-961576343f57.title: Pseudo-Linear Complexity O(n)
a77f1f6b-7194-4662-b0dc-961576343f57.definition: Sorting algorithms have near-linear complexity O(n) under some specific conditions, such as counting sort. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

578f74d6-0010-4182-801a-5acdd7872635.title: Counting Sort
578f74d6-0010-4182-801a-5acdd7872635.definition: The sorting algorithm uses the frequency of occurrence of elements to place them in their correct position. Effective when the value range is small. (An example for Pseudo O(n) complexity)

8dd5760c-cfd7-4749-a6e9-1a0659c03b9f.title: Pseudo-Linear Complexity O(n)
8dd5760c-cfd7-4749-a6e9-1a0659c03b9f.definition: Sorting algorithms have near-linear complexity O(n) under some specific conditions, such as radix sorting. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

43706de7-7b70-42b0-af8b-31f71b855d88.title: Radix Sort
43706de7-7b70-42b0-af8b-31f71b855d88.definition: The sorting algorithm is not based on comparison, sorting elements by grouping them by individual digits or characters. (An example for Pseudo O(n) complexity)

1cebb59f-714b-4a5b-af60-8a8d5e1c9f62.title: Transitive Closure (Warshall)
1cebb59f-714b-4a5b-af60-8a8d5e1c9f62.definition: An algorithm that calculates all pairs of vertices (u,v) such that there is a path from u to v in a directed graph, such as Warshall's algorithm. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

112dd890-bd8a-4c92-9d59-524256c3fef9.title: Graph Matching
112dd890-bd8a-4c92-9d59-524256c3fef9.definition: In graph theory, a set of edges with no vertices in common, often used in pairwise assignment or search problems. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

6b830602-1225-4412-9d32-b98f629421d6.title: Efficient String Matching
6b830602-1225-4412-9d32-b98f629421d6.definition: Efficient search algorithms for finding the occurrence of a pattern (substring) in a text (mainstring), for example the Boyer-Moore algorithm. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

2e111152-81b0-474d-8889-56382ca429b9.title: Boyer-Moore Algorithm
2e111152-81b0-474d-8889-56382ca429b9.definition: An efficient string search algorithm, often the fastest standard string search algorithm, by ignoring parts of the text that are unlikely to contain a pattern. (An example for Efficient String Matching)

3d786e5e-1eea-4a81-85c1-15b369390787.title: Efficient String Matching
3d786e5e-1eea-4a81-85c1-15b369390787.definition: Efficient search algorithms for finding the occurrence of a pattern (substring) in a text (mainstring), for example the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm. (As part of an AL-Foundational unit: 3 hours)

dac7888a-10db-47d0-a1bb-261bb5f78739.title: KMP Algorithm
dac7888a-10db-47d0-a1bb-261bb5f78739.definition: An efficient string search algorithm that avoids rechecking previously checked text characters. (An example for Efficient String Matching)

363660ba-e814-44eb-a166-4bc19a4b07b8.title: Longest Common Subsequence
363660ba-e814-44eb-a166-4bc19a4b07b8.definition: The ability to find the longest common substring between two or more given strings, a fundamental problem in dynamic programming and computational biology.

fb4e9fd9-0c54-4f7e-af54-91c728f12188.title: Regular Expression Matching
fb4e9fd9-0c54-4f7e-af54-91c728f12188.definition: Ability to use and understand regular expressions to search, match, and manipulate text based on specific patterns.

ddf7d616-1a06-4296-a373-6466950d052b.title: Algorithm Complexity
ddf7d616-1a06-4296-a373-6466950d052b.definition: Study of the computational resources (time, space) an algorithm requires to complete a task. Includes asymptotic analysis and basic complexity classes.

d09c71b1-37bd-4fe5-8767-76ed24204011.title: Asymptotic Complexity Analysis
d09c71b1-37bd-4fe5-8767-76ed24204011.definition: Mathematical method for describing the bounded behavior of an algorithm as input size increases, using Big O, Big Omega, and Big Theta notation.

1c1968f6-bf9c-4530-9fc3-949e56851d1b.title: Fundamental Complexity Classes
1c1968f6-bf9c-4530-9fc3-949e56851d1b.definition: Standard categories for classifying computational problems based on the resources required to solve them, such as O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2).

8b69685e-9cc8-4599-897b-6d8ebc51a9de.title: Exponential Complexity O(2^n)
8b69685e-9cc8-4599-897b-6d8ebc51a9de.definition: The complexity class represents an exponential growth of computational time or space with input size, often appearing in NP-hard problems with no known polynomial algorithm.

fd252d4d-f6f1-47ec-b73e-bb963c05cfc9.title: Factorial Complexity O(n!)
fd252d4d-f6f1-47ec-b73e-bb963c05cfc9.definition: The complexity class represents very rapid growth of computational time or space, typical for algorithms that iterate over all permutations, as in some brute-force methods.

044d1e06-4759-40fb-99a3-1fdaf942a6d3.title: Empirical Performance Measurement
044d1e06-4759-40fb-99a3-1fdaf942a6d3.definition: Practical techniques for evaluating the performance of algorithms by running them on real data and measuring runtime, memory usage, and other metrics.

4c417d99-d0d3-4443-946e-20805696fe92.title: Feasibility & Intractability
4c417d99-d0d3-4443-946e-20805696fe92.definition: Distinguish between problems that can be solved efficiently (in polynomial time) and problems that cannot be solved efficiently (in superpolynomial runtime), often involving the P and NP classes.

fcbd2e54-7eda-4600-bb0e-0472789bcdd9.title: Algorithm Strategies
fcbd2e54-7eda-4600-bb0e-0472789bcdd9.definition: Algorithm design and development methods to solve different types of computational problems, including exhaustion, divide and conquer, greed, etc.

43edfa02-8bfa-4310-af63-6ff5cf9c0ccb.title: Brute Force Strategy
43edfa02-8bfa-4310-af63-6ff5cf9c0ccb.definition: A method of solving problems by systematically trying every possible possibility until the right solution is found, often the simplest but ineffective method.

c9797bb9-3b2b-41d0-aaa3-2d1e1fa96954.title: Traveling Salesperson Problem
c9797bb9-3b2b-41d0-aaa3-2d1e1fa96954.definition: An optimization problem in which the goal is to find the shortest path through a set of cities and back to the starting point, a classic example of an NP-hard problem often illustrated by exhaustion.

8b32278a-9376-4373-80c4-3857ee18e763.title: Knapsack Problem
8b32278a-9376-4373-80c4-3857ee18e763.definition: An optimization problem in which the goal is to select items with different weights and values ​​to maximize the total value while not exceeding the bag's weight limit, another example of a problem that can be solved by brute force or dynamic programming.

47e9137f-1e9f-4604-9ded-cdcb4e0ef48a.title: Decrease-and-Conquer
47e9137f-1e9f-4604-9ded-cdcb4e0ef48a.definition: A strategy for designing an algorithm by reducing the size of a problem instance to a smaller instance, solving the smaller problem, and then expanding the solution to the solution of the original problem.

7ebb1c48-bc5d-4dbf-bb12-f8bb5651bf46.title: Topological Sort
7ebb1c48-bc5d-4dbf-bb12-f8bb5651bf46.definition: The algorithm sorts the vertices of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) in a linear order such that for every directed edge from u to v, u comes before v in the sort order.

de51d264-dbc4-428d-a51f-588ac0516107.title: Divide-and-Conquer Strategy
de51d264-dbc4-428d-a51f-588ac0516107.definition: A robust algorithmic strategy consists of three steps: dividing the larger problem into smaller subproblems, recursively solving the subproblems, and combining the subsolutions to form the solution of the original problem.

a02d3783-fd20-42d7-86d1-d16ff5719709.title: Strassen Algorithm
a02d3783-fd20-42d7-86d1-d16ff5719709.definition: A more efficient matrix multiplication algorithm than the standard algorithm, using a divide-and-conquer strategy to reduce the number of multiplications needed, especially useful for large matrices.

3ae0178b-3795-4fe8-be49-22efab0c5704.title: Greedy Strategy
3ae0178b-3795-4fe8-be49-22efab0c5704.definition: An algorithm design method in which a locally optimal choice is made at each step in the hope that it will lead to a globally optimal solution.

04b07f32-e8c5-49f2-a111-dc0a52522b47.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
04b07f32-e8c5-49f2-a111-dc0a52522b47.definition: An algorithm for finding the shortest path between nodes in a graph with positively weighted edges, commonly used in network routing.

dfd53dd7-31b4-41e0-b849-fd1c766b8f7a.title: Kruskal's Algorithm
dfd53dd7-31b4-41e0-b849-fd1c766b8f7a.definition: An algorithm to find the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) for a weighted undirected graph, by adding the edges with the least weight without forming a cycle.

4f9fc552-da01-443f-bc27-944554578c9b.title: Transform-and-Conquer
4f9fc552-da01-443f-bc27-944554578c9b.definition: An algorithmic strategy involves transforming a given problem into another (usually simpler or already solved) instance, solving the transformed instance, and then transforming the solution back.

fbde3aa6-d016-4af5-90bc-e46aa1768680.title: Heapsort Algorithm
fbde3aa6-d016-4af5-90bc-e46aa1768680.definition: A sorting algorithm based on the heap data structure, where the sorting problem is transformed into building and maintaining a heap.

70e81c1a-66f1-42ce-9b78-2da9cbe60fa6.title: 2-3 Tree
70e81c1a-66f1-42ce-9b78-2da9cbe60fa6.definition: A type of balanced search tree (B-tree) can contain 2 or 3 keys in each node and have all leaves at the same level, used to maintain efficient insertion, deletion, and search operations.

8bc356a6-ee0e-4486-afa6-92ea0d7a79db.title: AVL Tree
8bc356a6-ee0e-4486-afa6-92ea0d7a79db.definition: A type of self-balancing binary search tree, where the difference in height of the left and right subtrees of any node cannot be greater than 1.

75941853-b4af-4c0f-bd7b-596de2b18edb.title: Red-Black Tree
75941853-b4af-4c0f-bd7b-596de2b18edb.definition: Another type of self-balancing binary search tree, ensuring search, insertion, and deletion operations have O(log n) time complexity.

0aadf867-12ce-4144-aa1a-3a988d689d9a.title: Dynamic Programming
0aadf867-12ce-4144-aa1a-3a988d689d9a.definition: A mathematical optimization technique and algorithm design method that solves complex problems by dividing them into simpler subproblems and storing their results to avoid recalculation.

c3009a9c-e36f-4d7e-82fd-644e1299e432.title: Warshall's Algorithm
c3009a9c-e36f-4d7e-82fd-644e1299e432.definition: Algorithm to find transitive closure of a directed graph, indicating which pairs of vertices have a path between them.

b6be97ae-17d1-4b48-94cf-9e471fb3e04e.title: Floyd's Algorithm
b6be97ae-17d1-4b48-94cf-9e471fb3e04e.definition: An algorithm to find the shortest path between all pairs of vertices in a weighted graph, which can handle negative edge weights (but no negative cycles).

ba326b4d-ebb7-4b22-8bd7-211adf98aca6.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
ba326b4d-ebb7-4b22-8bd7-211adf98aca6.definition: An algorithm to find the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph, which can handle negative edge weights and detect negative cycles.

2ad7aadb-1296-47b9-94a7-8aaff6cce65a.title: Handling Exponential Growth
2ad7aadb-1296-47b9-94a7-8aaff6cce65a.definition: Techniques and approaches for managing and solving problems of exponentially growing time complexity, often by finding approximate solutions or using heuristics.

4566d7c1-66be-40fd-a1aa-1f143983d902.title: A* Heuristic
4566d7c1-66be-40fd-a1aa-1f143983d902.definition: A best path search algorithm prioritizes the expansion of nodes by estimating the lowest cost from the current node to the destination, commonly used in artificial intelligence and pathfinding.

f2f7bfbc-31e7-493c-a02c-deedc7db79bd.title: Branch-and-Bound
f2f7bfbc-31e7-493c-a02c-deedc7db79bd.definition: An algorithmic strategy for finding optimal solutions to complex optimization problems, by dividing the search space into branches and eliminating unpromising branches using upper/lower bounds.

c127e88c-95d2-477f-992b-86ab044b8d04.title: Backtracking
c127e88c-95d2-477f-992b-86ab044b8d04.definition: A problem-solving technique by trying to construct a solution step by step; When a potential solution is no longer valid or does not lead to a solution, the algorithm backtracks and tries another option.

36f38fc2-6010-464b-aec8-ce248398838c.title: P, NP, NP-Complete
36f38fc2-6010-464b-aec8-ce248398838c.definition: Computational complexity theory models use Turing Machines to define and classify the P, NP, and NP-Complete problem classes, which are central to the Theory of Computation.

8eb8d6f1-da59-4f37-b7b8-ce8070e56869.title: Class P
8eb8d6f1-da59-4f37-b7b8-ce8070e56869.definition: The set of decision problems that can be solved by a deterministic polynomial Turing machine.

3449574c-e1c8-485a-b31b-acfb463fe162.title: Class NP
3449574c-e1c8-485a-b31b-acfb463fe162.definition: The set of decision problems whose solutions can be verified by a non-deterministic polynomial Turing machine.

b9ff28b6-da2c-473d-ac23-565b442c30cc.title: Class NP-Complete
b9ff28b6-da2c-473d-ac23-565b442c30cc.definition: The set of problems in NP, to which every other problem in NP can be reduced in polynomial time, represents the hardest problems in NP.

70bd3a0e-278a-4172-b3d1-c3d624b38835.title: Space Complexity
70bd3a0e-278a-4172-b3d1-c3d624b38835.definition: The study of the amount of memory or storage space an algorithm requires to run, often expressed in asymptotic notation.

97fc15b7-7e85-4d50-8022-0089f785c321.title: Class NSpace
97fc15b7-7e85-4d50-8022-0089f785c321.definition: The set of problems that can be solved by a Turing machine is unknown in a limited amount of space.

1c7f1d2e-0442-4ecf-ab63-06721afd9f57.title: Class PSpace
1c7f1d2e-0442-4ecf-ab63-06721afd9f57.definition: The set of problems that can be solved by a Turing machine is defined in a polynomial amount of space.

d0852492-0784-49ec-aef7-65e9cba1ac3e.title: Savitch's Theorem
d0852492-0784-49ec-aef7-65e9cba1ac3e.definition: An important theorem in space complexity theory, which states that any problem that can be solved by a non-deterministic Turing machine in space S(n) can also be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in space S(n)^2.

99704af0-4d44-40cd-94d7-4c1083cf40f4.title: AL-Models
99704af0-4d44-40cd-94d7-4c1083cf40f4.definition: Study of fundamental and theoretical computational models, covering all core topics of CS and KA in the advanced context of computational theory.

fc38a808-1a45-4402-b318-ffe812b8ef0a.title: Generative AI Architecture
fc38a808-1a45-4402-b318-ffe812b8ef0a.definition: Research into the necessary evolution in computer architecture aims to better support generative AI technologies, a potential and important area of ​​future research.

3f5867ab-40f3-4fd4-af0a-e3468d1cda2f.title: Generative AI Hardware Design
3f5867ab-40f3-4fd4-af0a-e3468d1cda2f.definition: Research on the impact and application of generative AI technology in the hardware design process.

124b197f-1030-4bd4-9c42-def143700eb9.title: Relational Database
124b197f-1030-4bd4-9c42-def143700eb9.definition: The study of database systems based on the relational model, which is the foundation of traditional data management.

dfdc924e-3267-4012-8f57-01aa044e6900.title: Data Modeling
dfdc924e-3267-4012-8f57-01aa044e6900.definition: The process of creating a blueprint or abstract representation of data, its structure, and relationships.

c32dbaf0-8dcc-42a3-8c00-013c5f7837d2.title: Database Design
c32dbaf0-8dcc-42a3-8c00-013c5f7837d2.definition: The process of determining the structure of a database to store and manage data effectively.

fe0ad6a3-6f4e-48d9-9768-3b40d4a13f74.title: E-R Data Model
fe0ad6a3-6f4e-48d9-9768-3b40d4a13f74.definition: An abstract model is used to describe the structure of a database through entities, attributes, and relationships.

3df2dbc9-9a08-43ea-b6c0-2aa190630736.title: Relational Model
3df2dbc9-9a08-43ea-b6c0-2aa190630736.definition: A data model organizes data into tables (relations) with rows and columns, based on predicate logic.

d47ea7a7-1446-45c8-b4ea-f60f27e77ad5.title: Normalization Theory
d47ea7a7-1446-45c8-b4ea-f60f27e77ad5.definition: A set of rules for designing database table structures to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity.

8fee4c2b-ad23-46ac-a41e-8364ab3ec13c.title: Query Construction
8fee4c2b-ad23-46ac-a41e-8364ab3ec13c.definition: The process of creating statements or expressions to retrieve, modify, or manipulate data in a database.

e89daeec-d5a6-467f-9354-a6d19d25fa21.title: Relational Algebra
e89daeec-d5a6-467f-9354-a6d19d25fa21.definition: A procedural query language used to manipulate data in the relational model.

0a1cee77-4c16-4505-8812-655ba146a5d4.title: SQL
0a1cee77-4c16-4505-8812-655ba146a5d4.definition: Standard language for managing and manipulating data in relational database systems.

80712244-97c8-4dc1-b93f-e855c6b39774.title: Query Processing
80712244-97c8-4dc1-b93f-e855c6b39774.definition: The process of executing a query on a database, including parsing, optimization, and execution steps.

12959836-ca99-4583-b692-ba6b6717d585.title: Indices
12959836-ca99-4583-b692-ba6b6717d585.definition: Data structures are used to improve the speed of retrieving data from the database.

cd63a70f-d01e-458c-a7a5-5faee489b686.title: B+ Tree
cd63a70f-d01e-458c-a7a5-5faee489b686.definition: A type of tree structure commonly used to create indexes in databases.

7ccbf8ea-091f-4f6c-a86f-2a803e07b5ac.title: Hash Indices
7ccbf8ea-091f-4f6c-a86f-2a803e07b5ac.definition: A type of index that uses hash functions to map data keys to their storage locations.

f427e964-90f8-4a36-9f9b-3caedc5750f6.title: External Sorting
f427e964-90f8-4a36-9f9b-3caedc5750f6.definition: Algorithms that sort data that cannot fit completely into main memory are commonly used in query processing.

7eb28836-5a2c-49fc-9a00-4f8dac9c3360.title: Select Algorithm
7eb28836-5a2c-49fc-9a00-4f8dac9c3360.definition: The algorithm is used to select rows (tuples) from a table that satisfy a certain condition.

ce8d1ce8-4eaf-42e1-923d-f72ed0d534eb.title: Project Algorithm
ce8d1ce8-4eaf-42e1-923d-f72ed0d534eb.definition: Algorithm used to select columns (attributes) from a table, removing duplicate columns.

7fe652d1-0756-4fea-bb5c-0106b379d1d3.title: Join Algorithm
7fe652d1-0756-4fea-bb5c-0106b379d1d3.definition: Algorithm used to combine rows from two or more tables based on a common column or related condition.

93b6739b-afaf-4492-bfbf-e5b03535b676.title: Query Optimization
93b6739b-afaf-4492-bfbf-e5b03535b676.definition: The process of finding the most efficient execution plan for a query to reduce time and resources.

a5306cfd-100e-4579-99d4-7721309a40d7.title: Query Transformations
a5306cfd-100e-4579-99d4-7721309a40d7.definition: Techniques that change the structure of a query without changing its semantics, in search of a more efficient execution plan.

13ab318d-13d1-4353-8d25-4584b53ffdf0.title: Index Selection
13ab318d-13d1-4353-8d25-4584b53ffdf0.definition: The process of choosing the most suitable index to use for a particular query to optimize performance.

2ca1dbc5-1dbe-408d-9519-2febd132e9ae.title: DBMS Internals
2ca1dbc5-1dbe-408d-9519-2febd132e9ae.definition: Research on the components and internal mechanisms of database management systems.

bcde977f-be9a-4e0d-a8d6-6e221b1334e5.title: Concurrency Control
bcde977f-be9a-4e0d-a8d6-6e221b1334e5.definition: Techniques that ensure data consistency when multiple users or applications access and modify the same data simultaneously.

606f4d81-3dc7-43e0-b1dc-a52863022a8c.title: Locking
606f4d81-3dc7-43e0-b1dc-a52863022a8c.definition: A concurrency control technique in a DBMS that prevents conflicting transactions from accessing the same data by placing locks.

9debe20f-57d9-4235-b023-e7465e9cc6e0.title: Transaction Management
9debe20f-57d9-4235-b023-e7465e9cc6e0.definition: The system ensures transactions are executed in an atomic, consistent, isolated, and persistent (ACID) manner.

4bd73b83-1fc0-48cc-92fe-c0f10db74731.title: Buffer Management
4bd73b83-1fc0-48cc-92fe-c0f10db74731.definition: Manage data movement between main memory and secondary memory (drive) to optimize data access performance.

2ccc6a74-85d3-4eff-9fa5-13a31cb52caa.title: DBMS User Skills
2ccc6a74-85d3-4eff-9fa5-13a31cb52caa.definition: Skills needed to use a database management system to organize, access, and update data.

b1741402-713a-48dc-a111-e3d4f3489307.title: Unstructured Data in DBMS
b1741402-713a-48dc-a111-e3d4f3489307.definition: Ability to take an unorganized set of data, apply data modeling principles to organize it using a DBMS.

e0545588-9245-4cd7-9c75-2d9c477b67a5.title: Data Querying
e0545588-9245-4cd7-9c75-2d9c477b67a5.definition: Skills in using query languages ​​(e.g., SQL) to retrieve information from databases.

e7ac897f-9ad5-4fed-9584-a64bbbfa96e9.title: Data Update Query
e7ac897f-9ad5-4fed-9584-a64bbbfa96e9.definition: Skill in using query languages ​​(e.g., SQL) to modify information that already exists in a database.

027205e2-b1de-41d0-b64f-5a7339256757.title: Data in Organization
027205e2-b1de-41d0-b64f-5a7339256757.definition: Understanding of the strategic and operational importance of data to an organization's operations, decisions and goals.

ad8f6b6c-bf75-4cf1-9b80-12dc37cb4730.title: Data Life Cycle
ad8f6b6c-bf75-4cf1-9b80-12dc37cb4730.definition: The different stages that data goes through from creation to destruction.

4f27fd55-8cff-471d-ba91-708533e7eea2.title: Data Creation
4f27fd55-8cff-471d-ba91-708533e7eea2.definition: The first phase of the data lifecycle, which involves collecting and entering new data into the system.

33d819fd-aa19-4716-b15b-08e82c5ef91b.title: Data Processing
33d819fd-aa19-4716-b15b-08e82c5ef91b.definition: The stage in the data lifecycle that involves transforming, organizing, and storing data for effective use.

e8a1f966-b933-4f29-bb27-21106ba8f8d3.title: Data Review & Reporting
e8a1f966-b933-4f29-bb27-21106ba8f8d3.definition: The stage in the data lifecycle where data is analyzed, evaluated, and presented in reports or visualizations.

b06f617a-15ec-4d44-90ae-23e92afe2588.title: Data Retention & Retrieval
b06f617a-15ec-4d44-90ae-23e92afe2588.definition: The stage in the data lifecycle that involves storing data for a certain period of time and the ability to retrieve it when needed.

c95d2443-1fd5-4b53-85c1-4d09cd60a6e9.title: Data Destruction
c95d2443-1fd5-4b53-85c1-4d09cd60a6e9.definition: The final stage of the data lifecycle where data is securely and permanently deleted from all storage systems.

4ec0e7bd-4491-452a-aaf5-70110bcdd77e.title: Social Data Collection
4ec0e7bd-4491-452a-aaf5-70110bcdd77e.definition: Understanding the impact of data collection on individuals and society, including issues of ethics and public acceptance.

60de4e6d-43e3-4767-80c5-d320fc7ffe5e.title: Legal Data Collection
60de4e6d-43e3-4767-80c5-d320fc7ffe5e.definition: understand regulations, laws and policies related to data collection, storage and use.

47c01c24-17d2-46cb-82fd-e40a9f80c71f.title: Data Collection Scale
47c01c24-17d2-46cb-82fd-e40a9f80c71f.definition: Consider the scale and volume of data collected, along with its challenges and social/legal implications.

4ce9f5c7-9eb1-4817-9ace-62b1dd1240e3.title: Data Privacy
4ce9f5c7-9eb1-4817-9ace-62b1dd1240e3.definition: The concept of individuals' rights over their personal data and how that data is collected, stored, used and shared.

acf10401-7cc5-4324-9c80-1079bfca283d.title: Privacy by Design
acf10401-7cc5-4324-9c80-1079bfca283d.definition: Approach integrating privacy into the design and operation of database systems from an early stage.

c3b2c0b1-4f0d-4f45-af2b-b48e8f7aa377.title: De-identification
c3b2c0b1-4f0d-4f45-af2b-b48e8f7aa377.definition: The process of removing or modifying personally identifiable information from data to protect privacy.

07ca2185-7bfd-44be-ae54-8182ef613a88.title: Data Ownership
07ca2185-7bfd-44be-ae54-8182ef613a88.definition: Legal rights and control over a particular set of data, including the rights of access, modification, and distribution.

f65ccddf-ada1-46af-9b7d-51094da51c7f.title: Data Reliability
f65ccddf-ada1-46af-9b7d-51094da51c7f.definition: The degree to which data is considered accurate, consistent, and reliable for its intended use.

256e3b94-3e4b-4483-91c5-7e95f53f8201.title: Database Security
256e3b94-3e4b-4483-91c5-7e95f53f8201.definition: Measures to protect databases from threats, unauthorized access and data loss.

9d73b516-0aa0-4ca8-b645-64e589ca13f2.title: Intended Data Use
9d73b516-0aa0-4ca8-b645-64e589ca13f2.definition: understand the intended and intended uses of collected data.

3749c71f-f3fd-4bac-b21c-8a4f6ac7bbef.title: Unintended Data Use
3749c71f-f3fd-4bac-b21c-8a4f6ac7bbef.definition: Be aware of uses of data that may arise beyond the original purpose, which may raise ethical or legal issues.

60710d63-71f2-45bc-9e76-eca08f17ca8c.title: Emerging Data Tech
60710d63-71f2-45bc-9e76-eca08f17ca8c.definition: Research into new and advanced data technologies that are supplementing or replacing traditional relational systems.

a7274894-37ef-4e9e-ae3d-e8db58a1cd94.title: Big Data Analytics
a7274894-37ef-4e9e-ae3d-e8db58a1cd94.definition: understand the technologies and methods used to store, process, and analyze extremely large and complex data sets.

4a4e77a0-b0dc-45a8-b1a9-ee5342713033.title: NoSQL Databases
4a4e77a0-b0dc-45a8-b1a9-ee5342713033.definition: Non-relational database systems provide more flexible data storage and retrieval mechanisms, designed for the specific use cases of big data.

4d0d6289-9825-4b26-8a8b-a0650ea7c70d.title: JSON (NoSQL)
4d0d6289-9825-4b26-8a8b-a0650ea7c70d.definition: Open, lightweight, easy-to-read text data format widely used in NoSQL databases to store structured data.

e025f417-c9f7-440c-82d6-e515b907d092.title: XML (NoSQL)
e025f417-c9f7-440c-82d6-e515b907d092.definition: A markup language used to encode documents in a human-readable and machine-readable format, sometimes used in NoSQL databases.

535404a5-4b1a-4047-9d13-1bbbd35c40ee.title: Key-Value Store
535404a5-4b1a-4047-9d13-1bbbd35c40ee.definition: A type of NoSQL database that stores data as key-value pairs, providing quick access by key.

7d1b5afe-0f02-4823-b02c-b7a432a7e212.title: Cloud Databases
7d1b5afe-0f02-4823-b02c-b7a432a7e212.definition: Databases are built, deployed, and delivered as a service through a cloud computing platform.

c53bade9-9f38-4f04-bdab-bad6e40696d2.title: MapReduce
c53bade9-9f38-4f04-bdab-bad6e40696d2.definition: A parallel programming and execution model for processing large data sets across computer clusters.

3766515e-7c98-4b38-adfc-cc04f218400b.title: Dataframes
3766515e-7c98-4b38-adfc-cc04f218400b.definition: A table data structure with columns of different types, widely used in data analysis and data science.

fe1b01e3-1055-46b5-8063-43ebe447d364.title: Traditional Data Roles
fe1b01e3-1055-46b5-8063-43ebe447d364.definition: Understanding of traditional job positions in the data management field.

246b4924-69d9-4303-979a-8d5ce10bd573.title: Emerging Data Roles
246b4924-69d9-4303-979a-8d5ce10bd573.definition: Understanding of new and evolving job positions in the data management field, reflecting technological change.

fd11203d-380d-40be-b477-ffa9222a2421.title: Product Feature Engineer
fd11203d-380d-40be-b477-ffa9222a2421.definition: A role that uses both SQL and NoSQL operational databases to build and improve product features.

a4913004-ee1c-4daa-9913-53f20b16a1fe.title: Operational Databases
a4913004-ee1c-4daa-9913-53f20b16a1fe.definition: Types of databases used for daily business operations, including both relational and non-relational systems.

4f30a73f-99e4-402b-b0e3-8561164b11e3.title: Data Engineer
4f30a73f-99e4-402b-b0e3-8561164b11e3.definition: The role writes analytical SQL, Python and Scala code to build data assets for business teams.

17819381-3e67-48ac-9bd0-9be2f0cf045a.title: Analytical SQL
17819381-3e67-48ac-9bd0-9be2f0cf045a.definition: Use SQL to perform complex queries, analyze data, and create reports for business purposes.

8567a2de-5d08-404c-bfb7-4315fb4177d1.title: Python for Data Assets
8567a2de-5d08-404c-bfb7-4315fb4177d1.definition: Use the Python programming language to develop, manage, and process data, creating data assets for analysis.

84b707a3-c903-47ab-aeed-99ce92d5b21c.title: Scala for Data Assets
84b707a3-c903-47ab-aeed-99ce92d5b21c.definition: Use Scala programming language to develop large-scale data solutions, especially in Big Data environments.

100bc000-6196-42eb-9c2e-2078778f2981.title: Building Data Assets
100bc000-6196-42eb-9c2e-2078778f2981.definition: Skill in creating cleaned, transformed, and structured data sets to support business analysis and decision making.

0cfb2ed3-66a8-4d3c-b4ca-8d7b286f3c1b.title: Business Analyst
0cfb2ed3-66a8-4d3c-b4ca-8d7b286f3c1b.definition: The role builds and manages data, regularly using Excel spreadsheets, to support business analysis and reporting.

a9ed7de3-2d48-49f2-a15e-d6a907b82910.title: Excel Data Management
a9ed7de3-2d48-49f2-a15e-d6a907b82910.definition: Skills in using spreadsheet software such as Excel to organize, analyze and present data.

cdb9a0e4-1992-4003-9786-da880556b22d.title: Data Infrastructure Engineer
cdb9a0e4-1992-4003-9786-da880556b22d.definition: The role implements data management systems in various data applications (e.g. OLTP).

d4e90f3a-9e63-47be-b95c-9ecf6d54f21a.title: Data System Deployment
d4e90f3a-9e63-47be-b95c-9ecf6d54f21a.definition: Skills to install, configure and deploy data management systems and solutions.

dfef46e8-1e19-4c1b-9701-346c78b0af5c.title: OLTP Applications
dfef46e8-1e19-4c1b-9701-346c78b0af5c.definition: Database systems are designed to handle large numbers of small, rapid, frequent, and concurrent transactions.

fa7c7633-0799-4042-ae41-c3d4d38f19af.title: Data Societal Issues
fa7c7633-0799-4042-ae41-c3d4d38f19af.definition: Understanding the broad impacts of data on society, including privacy, bias and equality.

99e0bd1f-3d70-450c-9a63-5c5afd6f4a4d.title: Data Ethical Issues
99e0bd1f-3d70-450c-9a63-5c5afd6f4a4d.definition: Awareness of the ethical principles that govern the collection, use, storage and sharing of data.

d7389dfd-bbc7-4e87-b94f-2dd789c53abf.title: Data Professional Issues
d7389dfd-bbc7-4e87-b94f-2dd789c53abf.definition: Understanding of responsibilities and professional standards when working with data in various roles.

91d17490-3e5d-4eda-b0be-4d0a00773672.title: Data Custodian
91d17490-3e5d-4eda-b0be-4d0a00773672.definition: A role responsible for the secure and ethical storage and use of institutional data.

749c6560-cd94-400c-9a58-c8ce033e5dfc.title: Data as Resource
749c6560-cd94-400c-9a58-c8ce033e5dfc.definition: View data as a valuable asset that needs to be managed, similar to other enterprise resources.

068e0675-4055-42c5-a3e1-a11f76dd875f.title: Information Systems Mgmt
068e0675-4055-42c5-a3e1-a11f76dd875f.definition: The field of managing information systems to support organizational operations and decision making.

fcf98a8d-2902-4e70-a059-5f90ff8428d6.title: Customer Data Ownership
fcf98a8d-2902-4e70-a059-5f90ff8428d6.definition: understand the concept that data about customers belongs to (or is owned by) those customers.

f9cc1f02-0e0a-492f-b4d0-e5f36100168e.title: Secure Ethical Data Storage
f9cc1f02-0e0a-492f-b4d0-e5f36100168e.definition: Responsibility for ensuring the organization's data is stored securely and in accordance with ethical principles.

0f34fc53-ffbb-4964-8e07-512f9bb50743.title: Secure Ethical Data Use
0f34fc53-ffbb-4964-8e07-512f9bb50743.definition: Responsibility for ensuring the organization's data is used securely and in accordance with ethical principles.

396aa846-abd6-4443-9c56-40cac23a12e1.title: Responsible Data Custodian
396aa846-abd6-4443-9c56-40cac23a12e1.definition: Concepts and responsibilities of those who play a role in protecting and managing data in a safe, ethical and legal manner.

4479fadf-f055-4278-a2f7-058adf7398b9.title: Role of Data
4479fadf-f055-4278-a2f7-058adf7398b9.definition: Study of the importance, value, and fundamental applications of data in information systems and the broader context of computer science and society.

8d026c91-7dc7-4740-b9de-a45f9a7e5be1.title: Data Lifecycle
8d026c91-7dc7-4740-b9de-a45f9a7e5be1.definition: The study of the different stages data goes through, from creation to destruction, including Creation, Processing, Evaluation/Reporting, Retention/Retrieval and Destruction.

dcd5fc07-bfc8-41c8-b911-3cf36fde2ef1.title: Data Creation Phase
dcd5fc07-bfc8-41c8-b911-3cf36fde2ef1.definition: The first phase of the data lifecycle, focuses on collecting, ingesting or creating new data from different sources.

992d2492-f41b-4fe1-a89d-c6e47b6002c7.title: Data Processing Phase
992d2492-f41b-4fe1-a89d-c6e47b6002c7.definition: The transformation phase, which organizes, cleans, and prepares data for use, includes activities such as normalization, integration, and transformation.

a5b71e6d-985c-4794-b75e-3512a3763227.title: Data Evaluation Phase
a5b71e6d-985c-4794-b75e-3512a3763227.definition: The phase of analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data in reports, charts, or other forms to support decision making and understanding.

0b151b91-1df3-4585-a032-f67db9046b36.title: Data Retention Phase
0b151b91-1df3-4585-a032-f67db9046b36.definition: Stages secure and organized data storage, as well as the ability to access and retrieve data as needed according to policies and regulations.

8890c64f-b519-4ecd-86ac-cb2ca5857880.title: Data Disposal Phase
8890c64f-b519-4ecd-86ac-cb2ca5857880.definition: The final stage in the data lifecycle, involves securely and permanently deleting or discarding data when it is no longer needed, in compliance with legal and ethical requirements.

c963214b-c7bc-4bfb-ba1d-029a22bf004c.title: Database Core Concepts
c963214b-c7bc-4bfb-ba1d-029a22bf004c.definition: Introduces the basic concepts of database systems, including their rationale, advantages, and key components, providing a foundation for deeper understanding.

819dd49a-afa1-4a51-8777-ce145453c189.title: Database Systems Purpose
819dd49a-afa1-4a51-8777-ce145453c189.definition: understand the primary functions and goals that a database system is designed to serve, such as efficiently managing large amounts of data and ensuring consistency and integrity.

ea9230c8-69b8-49a7-a7ae-ac5c36b3de28.title: Database Systems Advantages
ea9230c8-69b8-49a7-a7ae-ac5c36b3de28.definition: understand the key benefits of using a database system over traditional data storage methods, such as reduced duplication, improved data sharing, security, and data integrity.

63b1ade2-4c11-40b6-b599-affafea876eb.title: Database Systems Components
63b1ade2-4c11-40b6-b599-affafea876eb.definition: Identify and describe the elements that make up a complete database system, including users, applications, database management system (DBMS), and data.

60c845ca-7082-44a4-9725-faad1fdbd76a.title: Database Systems Core Concepts (KA Core)
60c845ca-7082-44a4-9725-faad1fdbd76a.definition: A more in-depth study of the core concepts of database systems, delving into their technical and theoretical aspects.

53e17f34-9808-4255-9126-d1e337802e11.title: Data Modeling (CS Core)
53e17f34-9808-4255-9126-d1e337802e11.definition: Introduces the basic principles and techniques for designing data structures, including the concepts of entities, attributes, and relationships.

950c34fc-65d1-40a6-b560-c92a4abd809b.title: Data Modeling (KA Core)
950c34fc-65d1-40a6-b560-c92a4abd809b.definition: In-depth study of various data models (e.g., relational model, entity-relationship model), normalization, and advanced database design principles.

b8c875e5-b610-4172-97eb-0d66081660cc.title: Relational Database (CS Core)
b8c875e5-b610-4172-97eb-0d66081660cc.definition: Introduces the basic concepts of relational databases, including tables, rows, columns, primary keys, and foreign keys, as the foundation for querying and data management.

c051d572-11f9-4002-af5a-6e58936d6099.title: Relational Database (KA Core)
c051d572-11f9-4002-af5a-6e58936d6099.definition: In-depth study of relational database theory, relational algebra, relational analysis, and data normalization principles to design efficient and non-redundant databases.

1da2c20e-a625-4002-b242-8c9935cd79e0.title: Query Building (CS Core)
1da2c20e-a625-4002-b242-8c9935cd79e0.definition: Learn to write basic queries in a standard query language (e.g., SQL) to retrieve, insert, update, and delete data in a database.

93b49383-117d-409b-987e-06f5e0ba825f.title: Query Building (KA Core)
93b49383-117d-409b-987e-06f5e0ba825f.definition: In-depth study of building complex queries, optimizing query performance, using advanced functions, triggers, stored procedures and other complex data query techniques.

7b8a8137-5142-4bf3-863a-9d5af1cd8929.title: Query Processing
7b8a8137-5142-4bf3-863a-9d5af1cd8929.definition: The study of how database management systems analyze, optimize, and execute queries, including steps such as parsing, semantic checking, plan optimization, and query execution.

b4652da0-aed6-4cc6-8f9b-498ac4fe747c.title: DBMS Internal Structure
b4652da0-aed6-4cc6-8f9b-498ac4fe747c.definition: Detailed study of the internal architecture and operating mechanisms of a Database Management System (DBMS), including memory management, data storage, indexing, transaction management, and error recovery.

5d57ef11-14c7-4b2f-a5e9-b76c5537639a.title: NoSQL Approaches (CS Core)
5d57ef11-14c7-4b2f-a5e9-b76c5537639a.definition: An introduction to the different approaches and types of non-relational (NoSQL) databases (e.g. Key-Value, Document, Column-Family, Graph), as well as their appropriate use cases.

94b0e308-4cb8-44df-bc64-e3891827a3dc.title: NoSQL Systems (KA Core)
94b0e308-4cb8-44df-bc64-e3891827a3dc.definition: In-depth study of specific NoSQL database systems, architectures, data models, query languages, and implementation techniques for applications requiring high scalability and flexibility.

bd36bb74-abb3-410f-b7e2-2445c0806353.title: MapReduce (CS Core)
bd36bb74-abb3-410f-b7e2-2445c0806353.definition: Introduction to the MapReduce programming model for processing and analyzing large data sets in a distributed and parallel manner, commonly used in Big Data systems.

5496fe77-559e-445d-87b6-dfda74ab7e1a.title: Data Security & Privacy (CS Core)
5496fe77-559e-445d-87b6-dfda74ab7e1a.definition: Basic concepts of data security, including threats, vulnerabilities, access controls, and principles for protecting user privacy and sensitive data.

6cbc06fd-f3f3-471f-802c-e21044059f65.title: Data Security & Privacy (KA Core)
6cbc06fd-f3f3-471f-802c-e21044059f65.definition: In-depth study of data security techniques, policies and standards, encryption, intrusion detection and prevention, privacy management, and compliance with relevant laws.

40be277e-df2e-4f73-bb0c-708e0ff8391a.title: Data Analysis
40be277e-df2e-4f73-bb0c-708e0ff8391a.definition: Introduces basic concepts and techniques in data analysis, including collecting, cleaning, transforming, exploring, and modeling data to extract useful information and support decision making.

674ed255-dd94-411b-a7ca-44d356ec3854.title: Distributed/Cloud Databases
674ed255-dd94-411b-a7ca-44d356ec3854.definition: Study the architecture, challenges, and techniques of distributed databases and how they are deployed and managed in cloud computing environments to achieve scalability, high availability, and fault tolerance.

643317d5-e296-401d-be7a-8700b94c7f11.title: Semi-structured/Unstructured Databases
643317d5-e296-401d-be7a-8700b94c7f11.definition: Study how to store, manage, and query data types that do not fit neatly into the traditional relational model, including XML, JSON, free text, and multimedia objects.

878a5706-aef0-4828-8399-2dd110115964.title: Data Management Ethics & Society
878a5706-aef0-4828-8399-2dd110115964.definition: Consider the social, ethical and professional aspects related to data management, including issues of privacy, security, responsibility, social impact of data use and industry ethical standards.

0c484ddb-a7f9-4f7c-9236-ad47193dfab4.title: Functional Dependency Theory
0c484ddb-a7f9-4f7c-9236-ad47193dfab4.definition: In-depth study of functional dependencies between attributes in a relation, a fundamental concept in relational database design and normalization theory.

1d602c31-3ac4-471a-8cad-43b8b84b0679.title: Armstrong's Axioms Completeness
1d602c31-3ac4-471a-8cad-43b8b84b0679.definition: Work on proving the completeness of Armstrong's Axioms, a set of inference rules for functional dependencies, ensuring that all functional dependencies can be derived from a given set.

418e929b-df85-4ac5-8d39-57803a5b0b9b.title: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
418e929b-df85-4ac5-8d39-57803a5b0b9b.definition: One of the higher standards in relational database design, aimed at eliminating update anomalies and ensuring data integrity by eliminating non-trivial functional dependencies in keys.

f89ef071-1975-4986-b6f4-7bc84388fc6c.title: SQL Queries
f89ef071-1975-4986-b6f4-7bc84388fc6c.definition: Skills in writing and executing Structured Query Language (SQL) statements to manipulate and retrieve data from relational databases.

bd054422-96aa-412b-9138-7c8849e20d0c.title: Indexes for Query Performance
bd054422-96aa-412b-9138-7c8849e20d0c.definition: Understanding how indexes are used to speed up data retrieval and improve the performance of queries, especially in large and complex database systems.

fdea6fc1-d6b5-4dd8-b66d-1325de63066f.title: Efficient Data Storage
fdea6fc1-d6b5-4dd8-b66d-1325de63066f.definition: Techniques and methods to optimize storage space utilization and access performance for data in a database system, especially important in OLTP applications.

4bd8dfd7-e9e1-40d7-8545-f9a6a9913947.title: Efficient Data Access
4bd8dfd7-e9e1-40d7-8545-f9a6a9913947.definition: Techniques and strategies to ensure data can be quickly, securely, and efficiently retrieved from the database system, minimizing latency and enhancing throughput.

bb9e17ce-23d3-40ab-8034-2bbaf9bdb4e1.title: Programmatic DB Access
bb9e17ce-23d3-40ab-8034-2bbaf9bdb4e1.definition: Skills and knowledge to connect and interact with existing databases through programming code, using APIs, drivers (JDBC, ODBC) or ORM.

97456386-a206-409c-a5ab-5881c1f5674d.title: Persistent Data Store Design
