97456386-a206-409c-a5ab-5881c1f5674d.definition: Principles and methods for designing data storage systems capable of persisting data across sessions and application restarts, taking into account legal and ethical aspects.

ec1f928a-8e2f-4022-8697-0ea8ccf42ca8.title: Data Storage Legal Aspects
ec1f928a-8e2f-4022-8697-0ea8ccf42ca8.definition: Understanding of legal regulations related to data collection, storage, use and sharing, including data protection laws, privacy and industry standards.

efcacc58-967c-4152-b43c-9e5caa2f8274.title: Data Storage Ethical Aspects
efcacc58-967c-4152-b43c-9e5caa2f8274.definition: Consider ethical issues arising from data storage and use, including responsibility for personal data, fairness, transparency and avoidance of bias.

4f26a6bf-3369-401a-964d-4f93d63b7e87.title: Data Storage Privacy Concerns
4f26a6bf-3369-401a-964d-4f93d63b7e87.definition: Identify and understand issues related to protecting personal information and sensitive data stored in systems, ensuring compliance with privacy principles.

6ca64ea5-e6ad-4128-95df-4f74c3674840.title: Data Protection
6ca64ea5-e6ad-4128-95df-4f74c3674840.definition: Measures and strategies to ensure the security, integrity and accessibility of data, including methods to protect against loss, corruption, unauthorized access and other threats.

d9726654-0421-4a71-b2dd-5e5eaf1561c4.title: OLTP Implementation
d9726654-0421-4a71-b2dd-5e5eaf1561c4.definition: Techniques and challenges in designing and implementing online transaction processing systems, placing a high priority on transaction performance, data consistency, and concurrency.

cd7c964b-6fe6-4916-88ad-f4e27427cb0a.title: Early Programmatic DB Access
cd7c964b-6fe6-4916-88ad-f4e27427cb0a.definition: Encourage learning and practice of database access through programming early in the curriculum, reflecting industry needs and realities.

1639652c-bf60-4d39-8153-f85b179174d1.title: SEP in Data Management
1639652c-bf60-4d39-8153-f85b179174d1.definition: Emphasis on consideration of Social, Ethical, and Professional aspects when studying and practicing Data Management, including in both CS and KA core courses, to develop responsible professionals.

57ae64f2-20e9-44fb-b6a0-99c6f34cac75.title: Security in Data Management
57ae64f2-20e9-44fb-b6a0-99c6f34cac75.definition: Emphasis is placed on considering Security aspects when studying and practicing Data Management, including in both CS and KA core courses, to ensure data systems are securely protected.

a183d134-9b33-4473-887c-f151bd6ea652.title: DBMS Core Function Design
a183d134-9b33-4473-887c-f151bd6ea652.definition: Research and design the basic functions of a database management system, including query mechanisms, transaction management, cache management, and data access methods.

a2f37afb-c8a9-4be9-877c-38feaae8f954.title: Query Mechanisms
a2f37afb-c8a9-4be9-877c-38feaae8f954.definition: Methods and techniques used to process and execute data queries in a database management system.

1fa35c48-c144-41dc-97a3-9ae277abe5c0.title: Buffer Management
1fa35c48-c144-41dc-97a3-9ae277abe5c0.definition: Strategies and algorithms for managing data transfer between main memory and secondary memory in a database management system.

59ff1df1-ab4e-4691-84ac-acdd2f36ede8.title: Data Access Methods
59ff1df1-ab4e-4691-84ac-acdd2f36ede8.definition: Techniques used to efficiently access and retrieve data from storage structures in a database management system.

f9eb6b76-f4d5-47c5-84e5-320290e4797c.title: Database Architecture
f9eb6b76-f4d5-47c5-84e5-320290e4797c.definition: The overall structure of a database system, including its components and how they interact with each other.

39e1d2bc-ce4b-4a94-9689-b61424884248.title: Data Independence
39e1d2bc-ce4b-4a94-9689-b61424884248.definition: Ability to change the schema at one level without affecting the schema at higher levels (physical and logical data independence).

14f106ae-8742-4e74-a14b-c394d2789a0d.title: Data Abstraction
14f106ae-8742-4e74-a14b-c394d2789a0d.definition: Ability to display data at different levels of detail, hiding underlying setting details from the user.

5b6df0b0-de88-486e-9803-07b82dd1b7c0.title: Transaction Management
5b6df0b0-de88-486e-9803-07b82dd1b7c0.definition: Techniques and principles to ensure consistency, isolation, atomicity, and persistence (ACID properties) of database transactions.

6e372be5-dd3b-45d8-b5d4-c05db835a710.title: Data Normalization
6e372be5-dd3b-45d8-b5d4-c05db835a710.definition: The process of organizing the columns and tables of a relational database to reduce data duplication and improve data integrity.

bb00191c-f70f-4614-a7d5-871fad1e9168.title: Big Data Management Methods
bb00191c-f70f-4614-a7d5-871fad1e9168.definition: Techniques and systems used to efficiently store, process, and analyze large data sets.

8c27f0bc-a1ee-4b35-ba84-0562081ad485.title: NoSQL Database Systems
8c27f0bc-a1ee-4b35-ba84-0562081ad485.definition: Non-relational database systems, designed to handle unstructured and semi-structured data, are commonly used in large-scale web applications and big data.

ae1adf9a-7ae3-40e9-ace7-d1f45c4c1bb5.title: MapReduce Usage
ae1adf9a-7ae3-40e9-ace7-d1f45c4c1bb5.definition: A programming model for processing large data sets with a parallel and distributed algorithm on a computer cluster.

e4728cbc-5062-47fa-9453-6c15e6debb90.title: CRUD Applications
e4728cbc-5062-47fa-9453-6c15e6debb90.definition: The methods and architecture for designing and implementing database systems focus on basic create, Read, Update, and Delete operations.

153a4b6e-0e05-4bc9-bbbd-a193f7effe40.title: Distributed Database
153a4b6e-0e05-4bc9-bbbd-a193f7effe40.definition: Database systems in which data is stored on multiple interconnected computers, often located in different geographical locations.

e231cf8b-6013-4a02-aa17-e233d1dd2baf.title: Cloud Database
e231cf8b-6013-4a02-aa17-e233d1dd2baf.definition: Database systems are deployed and managed on cloud computing infrastructure, providing scalability, flexibility and cost efficiency.

2eff6598-f194-4c2e-ab3e-4cd329eb5238.title: Structured Data
2eff6598-f194-4c2e-ab3e-4cd329eb5238.definition: Data is organized in a fixed format, such as in relational database tables, with predefined fields and data types.

1cb00d5b-f20e-45c1-96b7-63b1837e0f68.title: Semi-structured Data
1cb00d5b-f20e-45c1-96b7-63b1837e0f68.definition: The data does not follow the fixed schema model of a relational database but contains tags or delimiters to separate semantic elements, e.g. XML, JSON.

55e77908-2f51-4b93-9341-96ecf6947dd2.title: Unstructured Data
55e77908-2f51-4b93-9341-96ecf6947dd2.definition: The data has no predefined structure or organizational pattern, e.g. text, images, video, audio.

5ec38075-ddb9-40b2-8fea-afdfeb845a2a.title: Declarative Query Language
5ec38075-ddb9-40b2-8fea-afdfeb845a2a.definition: Learn to use query languages ​​in which the user specifies the desired result without specifying how to achieve it, for example, SQL.

d2cbdece-b091-4709-818f-d631502eefa8.title: Structured/Streaming Data Systems
d2cbdece-b091-4709-818f-d631502eefa8.definition: Study database systems and technologies designed to manage and process both structured static data and continuously stream data.

2aebae04-96f9-4d02-87ef-3fb09f0bcc71.title: Data Modeling
2aebae04-96f9-4d02-87ef-3fb09f0bcc71.definition: The process of creating an abstract and consistent model of the data used in an information system.

615ff8f8-2dc1-4f5d-a565-764100922e25.title: Relational Data Model
615ff8f8-2dc1-4f5d-a565-764100922e25.definition: A data model organizes data into tables (relations) with rows and columns, based on mathematical predicate logic.

6253ba1c-48d8-47d0-902f-602af9e92d37.title: Conceptual Models
6253ba1c-48d8-47d0-902f-602af9e92d37.definition: High-level data models are used to describe the overall data structure and relationships between entities, independent of the specific DBMS.

ad8fdac1-1b60-4b98-9c40-c7070ce8549e.title: E-R Diagram
ad8fdac1-1b60-4b98-9c40-c7070ce8549e.definition: A graphical tool for representing entities, attributes, and relationships between them in a conceptual database model.

e7d46e84-9707-4991-99d3-e62978fc1228.title: UML Data Modeling
e7d46e84-9707-4991-99d3-e62978fc1228.definition: Use Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams, especially class diagrams, to describe data structures and relationships.

51ad39de-4332-4621-bfeb-b7c987912e92.title: Semi-structured Data Model
51ad39de-4332-4621-bfeb-b7c987912e92.definition: The data models used to represent data do not have a strict fixed structure as in relational databases, but have some organization through tags or tree structures, e.g. XML, JSON.

98f22544-acda-4666-8aa1-7debf404eb90.title: DTD
98f22544-acda-4666-8aa1-7debf404eb90.definition: A markup language used to define the valid structure of an XML or SGML document.

1c86eeea-8eab-461c-9e94-0b31a54a4fd5.title: XML
1c86eeea-8eab-461c-9e94-0b31a54a4fd5.definition: A markup language used to encode documents in a format that can be read by both humans and machines.

da440770-5234-4dc6-a7a7-d1ab343579b0.title: JSON Schema
da440770-5234-4dc6-a7a7-d1ab343579b0.definition: A JSON-based standard for describing the structure and format of JSON data.

59e2cad3-1fa9-4374-bc26-ceb162aaa4ab.title: Spreadsheet Model
59e2cad3-1fa9-4374-bc26-ceb162aaa4ab.definition: Use spreadsheets to organize, store, and analyze data, often for simple applications or personal data analysis.

5e595019-ca94-4649-b8ba-7a6277b9d630.title: Object-Oriented Model
5e595019-ca94-4649-b8ba-7a6277b9d630.definition: Data models are based on the concept of objects, inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism, often used in object databases or object-relational mappings.

f3f1ded4-48d4-4bc6-b79e-63b4ab8fb69a.title: GraphQL
f3f1ded4-48d4-4bc6-b79e-63b4ab8fb69a.definition: A server-side runtime and query language for executing queries using a data type system defined by the provider.

a62b93e4-6034-4035-b2e4-6e5a769f14ce.title: New SQL Features
a62b93e4-6034-4035-b2e4-6e5a769f14ce.definition: Explore new features and enhancements introduced in recent versions of the SQL language, which expand query and data management capabilities.

c83fff0c-5590-4f5a-85fb-98f879d11f5f.title: Time-Series Data
c83fff0c-5590-4f5a-85fb-98f879d11f5f.definition: Data collected or recorded in chronological order, often used to track changes in a metric over time.

560e487e-3340-4951-bf00-54b6c48fc746.title: Time-Series Data Aggregation
560e487e-3340-4951-bf00-54b6c48fc746.definition: Aggregation techniques (e.g., averaging, summing, counting) on ​​time series data to extract meaningful information from different time periods.

5c9ceb88-44a7-4822-ae77-5ffd6d1d231a.title: Time-Series Data Joining
5c9ceb88-44a7-4822-ae77-5ffd6d1d231a.definition: Methods for combining different time series data sets based on time points or related attributes.

0e1cf990-b73c-4a1d-bbe5-7d1911dbc58c.title: Graph Data
0e1cf990-b73c-4a1d-bbe5-7d1911dbc58c.definition: Data is represented as nodes (entities) and edges (relationships) between them, commonly used in social networks, recommendation systems.

a6c219ad-476d-49ba-8ae1-c1fbe962d395.title: Graph Traversal
a6c219ad-476d-49ba-8ae1-c1fbe962d395.definition: The process of moving through relationships (edges) in a graph data structure to discover related entities or find paths.

d10f8c61-02ed-4517-ab59-50378dfe7524.title: Efficient Data Access Techniques
d10f8c61-02ed-4517-ab59-50378dfe7524.definition: Methods to optimize query performance by avoiding direct access and reprocessing of raw data, often including the use of special data structures and aggregation tools.

4f6d9d35-b18b-4cbf-a3f6-bad56948fbb9.title: Materialized Views
4f6d9d35-b18b-4cbf-a3f6-bad56948fbb9.definition: Database views whose results are physically stored in the database, allowing faster queries for complex or frequent queries.

5efbe804-b689-4e6f-b502-3b3be746145e.title: Efficient Data Structures
5efbe804-b689-4e6f-b502-3b3be746145e.definition: Data structures are specifically designed to optimize data access and processing, especially in big data situations, to improve performance.

022f1537-d31e-498f-b754-1c963590ede7.title: HyperLogLog
022f1537-d31e-498f-b754-1c963590ede7.definition: An algorithm that estimates the number of unique elements in a large data set with little error and low memory consumption.

6ef8fe6f-6b28-4364-9a3e-27debab03746.title: Bitmap (Data Structure)
6ef8fe6f-6b28-4364-9a3e-27debab03746.definition: A data structure used to represent a set of values ​​using a string of bits, where each bit represents the presence or absence of an element.

1d940b67-b7f5-44b2-8375-679935e655be.title: Geospatial Data
1d940b67-b7f5-44b2-8375-679935e655be.definition: Data describing objects, events or phenomena located on Earth, including spatial and non-spatial attributes.

d6a42893-35ad-4381-998e-c98ca146d1f2.title: GIS Database
d6a42893-35ad-4381-998e-c98ca146d1f2.definition: Database systems are specifically designed to store, manage, analyze and display geospatial data.

73d8210f-6274-4a3e-85ca-7a28307dbbcc.title: Entity Integrity
73d8210f-6274-4a3e-85ca-7a28307dbbcc.definition: The rule ensures that each row (record) in a table has a unique primary key and is not empty.

14885422-7588-4803-aa4c-2a92900f9a73.title: Referential Integrity
14885422-7588-4803-aa4c-2a92900f9a73.definition: The rule ensures that foreign key values ​​in one table refer to existing primary key values ​​in another table or are null.

81377089-4368-441b-a554-f4d65e273d07.title: Candidate Key
81377089-4368-441b-a554-f4d65e273d07.definition: An attribute or set of attributes in a table that uniquely identifies each row and contains no child attributes that also uniquely identify the rows.

df827a0c-c68f-4aaa-b391-cd4b09246bc5.title: Superkey
df827a0c-c68f-4aaa-b391-cd4b09246bc5.definition: An attribute or set of attributes that uniquely identifies a row in a table. A candidate key is a minimal superkey.

9a09be52-f629-4446-b699-f02aa86d0210.title: Relational Database Design
9a09be52-f629-4446-b699-f02aa86d0210.definition: The process of creating an efficient and consistent relational database structure that adheres to the principles of normalization and data integrity.

040e7c63-dd8c-4c14-86d2-1be21fa32e2c.title: Conceptual to Relational Mapping
040e7c63-dd8c-4c14-86d2-1be21fa32e2c.definition: The process of converting a conceptual data model (for example, an E-R diagram) into a concrete relational data model, including creating tables, columns, and key definitions.

ebb7e177-3bc1-47fd-ae3d-05ff293d18d8.title: Physical Database Design
ebb7e177-3bc1-47fd-ae3d-05ff293d18d8.definition: The process of designing the actual data storage structures on disk, including the selection of file structures, indexing methods, and data organization to optimize performance.

023302db-027a-4b2e-a287-3368a655627f.title: File Structures & Storage
023302db-027a-4b2e-a287-3368a655627f.definition: The methods and techniques used to organize and store data on physical storage devices, including file formats, indexes, and how the data is organized.

e5909fae-c13f-4034-84cf-6fec80181e1d.title: Functional Dependencies Intro
e5909fae-c13f-4034-84cf-6fec80181e1d.definition: Basic concepts of functional dependencies in relational databases, describing binding relationships between attributes.

4e8362e4-94e7-4a7f-b166-256d04d2df68.title: Normalization Theory
4e8362e4-94e7-4a7f-b166-256d04d2df68.definition: Deep dive into relational database normalization principles and techniques to eliminate data redundancy and improve data integrity, based on functional dependencies.

47fc5fa5-b386-4f3e-93fd-8ea2694ea05b.title: Schema Decomposition
47fc5fa5-b386-4f3e-93fd-8ea2694ea05b.definition: The process of dividing a large relational schema into smaller schemas to achieve higher normal forms.

896c0fe7-ba04-42f2-8f62-c50b432f2317.title: Lossless Join Decomposition
896c0fe7-ba04-42f2-8f62-c50b432f2317.definition: A property of schema decomposition ensures that when child tables are reconnected, no information is lost or spurious information is created.

e3a67780-f355-4f5c-9d1e-7f03e6a246a4.title: Dependency Preserving Decomposition
e3a67780-f355-4f5c-9d1e-7f03e6a246a4.definition: A property of schema decomposition ensures that all original functional dependencies can be tested by testing only the functional dependencies in the decomposed child tables.

cc79691f-3b2e-438f-9b61-04d7e1083644.title: Database Normal Forms
cc79691f-3b2e-438f-9b61-04d7e1083644.definition: Rules for evaluating the degree of normalization of a relational table, with Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) being one of the higher normal forms, eliminating more data anomalies than previous normal forms.

dcd3b173-f7db-4834-8dc9-f004be492575.title: BCNF
dcd3b173-f7db-4834-8dc9-f004be492575.definition: A standard form in relational database design, stricter than 3NF, that eliminates functional dependencies where a non-key attribute depends on part of a candidate key.

e226ff7a-818b-42bb-87b6-c823ee994a8c.title: Denormalization (Performance)
e226ff7a-818b-42bb-87b6-c823ee994a8c.definition: The process of intentionally introducing data redundancy into a normalized database schema to improve query performance, often by reducing the number of joins required.

db77a138-2287-4eff-85fd-925bf633005e.title: Advanced Functional Dependencies
db77a138-2287-4eff-85fd-925bf633005e.definition: In-depth study of functional dependencies, including properties and how they are used in database normalization.

40ebad57-f7b6-4e3e-8450-7003e652e0d7.title: Attribute Closure
40ebad57-f7b6-4e3e-8450-7003e652e0d7.definition: The set of all attributes that can be determined from an initial set of attributes through the given functional dependencies.

b5397c2e-c604-429e-8d72-b43b622e9bd4.title: Canonical Cover
b5397c2e-c604-429e-8d72-b43b622e9bd4.definition: A minimal set of functional dependencies is equivalent to a given set of functional dependencies, no functional dependencies can be inferred from other functional dependencies in that set.

7a569d00-8ee9-40c2-be53-9c415038adce.title: Advanced Normalization Theory
7a569d00-8ee9-40c2-be53-9c415038adce.definition: In-depth study of normalization theory, including higher normal forms and more complex types of dependencies.

034496fc-4bac-4129-8162-c319a2d1b577.title: Multivalued Dependency (MVD)
034496fc-4bac-4129-8162-c319a2d1b577.definition: A type of dependency in a relational database that describes a constraint in which one set of attributes defines a different set of values ​​for another attribute, independent of the other attributes.

973ecf8a-57d7-41cd-b0d8-cace78cdb0bd.title: Fourth Normal Form (4NF)
973ecf8a-57d7-41cd-b0d8-cace78cdb0bd.definition: A higher standard form than BCNF, resolving anomalies caused by multivalued dependencies.

2c5031e7-c490-434d-8025-148fa257b1f1.title: Join Dependency (JD)
2c5031e7-c490-434d-8025-148fa257b1f1.definition: A constraint in a relational database ensures that a table can be decomposed into smaller tables and then rejoined without losing or adding information.

aa9b3ec0-1113-4b85-bf4f-5c92dedccd0d.title: Project-Join Normal Form (PJNF)
aa9b3ec0-1113-4b85-bf4f-5c92dedccd0d.definition: A higher normal form than 4NF, resolving anomalies caused by connection dependencies. (Equivalent to 5NF)

29a31bc3-57bb-452a-ab2e-d305e8e63c6c.title: Fifth Normal Form (5NF)
29a31bc3-57bb-452a-ab2e-d305e8e63c6c.definition: The highest standard in relational databases, resolving join dependencies to ensure that all dependencies are inferred from candidate keys. (Equivalent to PJNF)

6d440ad7-5d58-4f7b-9f7b-f49a77c2250e.title: Representation Theory (Database)
6d440ad7-5d58-4f7b-9f7b-f49a77c2250e.definition: Study of how information and knowledge are represented in various database models, including the theories underlying data and relational representation.

0e0a2495-c035-46d3-aea9-0a4baa40e5fb.title: Conceptual to Relational Schema Design
0e0a2495-c035-46d3-aea9-0a4baa40e5fb.definition: Ability to build a relational schema from a conceptual schema, including handling 1:1, 1:n, and n:m relationships.

cde4ed07-2911-411b-8232-82e9e30ecb17.title: File Structure to Relation Mapping
cde4ed07-2911-411b-8232-82e9e30ecb17.definition: Ability to map appropriate file structures to relations and indexes in the database management system.

5c1b9a93-7e35-4c30-a1fe-43debd243ffa.title: Functional Dependency Theory
5c1b9a93-7e35-4c30-a1fe-43debd243ffa.definition: Describe how functional dependency theory generalizes the concept of locking in databases.

acbe8d31-f2e8-4a51-9ddf-8a1d58f666f8.title: Lossless & Dependency Preserving Decomposition
acbe8d31-f2e8-4a51-9ddf-8a1d58f666f8.definition: The ability to define and protect a given decomposition as lossless and/or dependency-preserving.

764fc836-6a02-4c62-8f55-9fcc8accc89c.title: Decomposition Normal Form Identification
764fc836-6a02-4c62-8f55-9fcc8accc89c.definition: The ability to detect the normal form that a given decomposition achieves (e.g., 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF).

0bb903f3-aaf0-4e99-99f2-59437e3d8de2.title: Denormalization Reasons
0bb903f3-aaf0-4e99-99f2-59437e3d8de2.definition: Gives the rationale and context for denormalizing a relationship in the database, often to improve performance.

4b70048b-70dc-428b-9b4f-e79ea269e64d.title: SQL Query Formulation
4b70048b-70dc-428b-9b4f-e79ea269e64d.definition: understand and implement the steps to build an effective SQL query.

680b6b0c-1b40-42de-85ac-31a296ce480e.title: Interactive SQL Execution
680b6b0c-1b40-42de-85ac-31a296ce480e.definition: Ability to execute SQL queries interactively via command line interface or GUI tool.

cca9e3ff-2247-4385-aa72-8ca3817b777f.title: Programmatic SQL Execution
cca9e3ff-2247-4385-aa72-8ca3817b777f.definition: Ability to execute SQL queries through program code, for example using APIs or database drivers.

0bd8256a-a5c9-4a2e-8a98-b17024af94b2.title: Relational Algebra
0bd8256a-a5c9-4a2e-8a98-b17024af94b2.definition: understand and use relational algebra operators (selection, projection, connect, union, intersection, difference) as the theoretical foundation for SQL.

d5ca3e21-c0a4-438c-aa44-831f19da96e0.title: SQL Data Definition Language (DDL)
d5ca3e21-c0a4-438c-aa44-831f19da96e0.definition: Use SQL to define relational schemas, including table creation, integrity constraints, and other specifications.

29d447c7-69b2-4a15-a6e5-8d5469ed9f33.title: SQL Integrity Constraints
29d447c7-69b2-4a15-a6e5-8d5469ed9f33.definition: understand and define data integrity constraints (e.g. primary key, foreign key, NOT NULL, CHECK, UNIQUE) in SQL.

6814ec27-b9a6-42a1-a26e-3108203c477a.title: SQL Data Manipulation Language (DML)
6814ec27-b9a6-42a1-a26e-3108203c477a.definition: Use the SQL update language subsection (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) to add, modify, or delete data in the database.

a5ed2bd2-5aae-4b88-949f-a5e9fd48c737.title: Relational Algebra
a5ed2bd2-5aae-4b88-949f-a5e9fd48c737.definition: Learn about relational algebra, a non-procedural query language based on first-order predicate logic.

f42f8907-a9f6-4752-974f-1157582ba840.title: Query By Example (QBE)
f42f8907-a9f6-4752-974f-1157582ba840.definition: Introduction to QBE, a visual query language for relational databases.

ad42ec15-4a21-4e2d-8fb2-719202eb2b7f.title: 4th-Generation Environments
ad42ec15-4a21-4e2d-8fb2-719202eb2b7f.definition: Learn about fourth-generation programming environments and tools, often bundled with high-level query and productivity languages.

dd630a81-3a97-4144-8531-94148c1eda0c.title: Non-Procedural Query Invocation
dd630a81-3a97-4144-8531-94148c1eda0c.definition: Various methods for calling non-procedural queries (like SQL) from within common programming languages.

e803f068-237e-4bb2-a14a-4e67fe6f8a64.title: Other Query Languages (XPATH, SPARQL)
e803f068-237e-4bb2-a14a-4e67fe6f8a64.definition: An introduction to important query languages ​​other than SQL, such as XPATH (for XML documents) and SPARQL (for RDF data).

9adca3e3-c816-4aac-a0ea-adefb29e0d78.title: Stored Procedures
9adca3e3-c816-4aac-a0ea-adefb29e0d78.definition: Learn about stored procedures, SQL scripts stored in a database to perform repetitive or complex tasks.

6289f1c4-8d57-45b4-ad6a-e491513d0a1d.title: SQL SELECT Queries
6289f1c4-8d57-45b4-ad6a-e491513d0a1d.definition: Ability to build SQL queries using SELECT clauses to select data.

c75763b2-4b4d-491b-b1cf-89080fcdc0a9.title: SQL PROJECT Queries
c75763b2-4b4d-491b-b1cf-89080fcdc0a9.definition: Ability to build SQL queries to project (select specific columns) data.

77d7d694-08c0-40bb-98b2-7a6b69e1f696.title: SQL JOIN Queries
77d7d694-08c0-40bb-98b2-7a6b69e1f696.definition: Ability to build SQL queries using JOIN clauses to join data from multiple tables.

13184f03-d073-411d-ae8b-2be0fa4a1596.title: SQL UNION Queries
13184f03-d073-411d-ae8b-2be0fa4a1596.definition: Ability to build SQL queries that use the UNION operator to combine result sets.

89df4dff-2d4b-489b-b98b-424722299a32.title: SQL INTERSECT Queries
89df4dff-2d4b-489b-b98b-424722299a32.definition: Ability to build SQL queries that use the INTERSECTION operator to find common rows between result sets.

c41884b2-cd1e-41a7-a42d-41187dfcd8fe.title: SQL EXCEPT Queries
c41884b2-cd1e-41a7-a42d-41187dfcd8fe.definition: Ability to build SQL queries that use the SET DIFFERENCE (subtract) operator to find row differences between result sets.

b9d8fa30-c38b-4d80-b5e8-9fc8968549f6.title: SQL SET DIVISION Queries
b9d8fa30-c38b-4d80-b5e8-9fc8968549f6.definition: Ability to build SQL queries using the SET DIVISION operator to resolve 'all' or 'every' queries.

db4e2185-1db4-4fed-94ec-7bd6b753a430.title: Correlated vs. Uncorrelated Subqueries
db4e2185-1db4-4fed-94ec-7bd6b753a430.definition: Ability to differentiate and understand the difference between correlated and uncorrelated nested SQL queries.

92dfe1ea-29d5-47d2-8413-11a500082565.title: Programmatic SQL Data Iteration
92dfe1ea-29d5-47d2-8413-11a500082565.definition: Ability to process and iterate through data result sets programmatically retrieved from an SQL query.

bc754db0-ee40-496a-85a1-8b3647983b97.title: SQL Schema Definition with Constraints & Triggers
bc754db0-ee40-496a-85a1-8b3647983b97.definition: Ability to define entire relational schema in SQL, including all integrity constraints and delete/update triggers.

bba9e336-7820-404e-8acf-8d2275c4a178.title: Page Structures
bba9e336-7820-404e-8acf-8d2275c4a178.definition: understand the structure and organization of data pages in a database management system and how they are stored on disk.

557452b2-e1c5-4f31-9bd9-cfb5a6734df0.title: Index Structures
557452b2-e1c5-4f31-9bd9-cfb5a6734df0.definition: understand the different types of index structures and their importance in speeding up database queries.

9661d140-f313-4203-ba25-db049bff97c7.title: B+ Trees
9661d140-f313-4203-ba25-db049bff97c7.definition: Research on the structure and operation of B+ trees, a popular type of index in database management systems.

4475c672-d9f7-40f3-bd3d-e4ec561b4cd8.title: Static Hash Indexes
4475c672-d9f7-40f3-bd3d-e4ec561b4cd8.definition: Study static hash indexes and how they provide fast access to data based on fixed hash values.

8c479926-84df-4c4b-b36a-e42c2e571d3b.title: Dynamic Hash Indexes
8c479926-84df-4c4b-b36a-e42c2e571d3b.definition: Study dynamic hash indexes and how they self-adjust to handle growth or decrease in the size of data.

842f8578-f7e0-483f-b873-d191a701ea88.title: SQL Index Creation
842f8578-f7e0-483f-b873-d191a701ea88.definition: How to use SQL commands to create and manage different types of indexes on database tables.

8ee188b4-54a8-4605-9773-ab1172886589.title: File Structures
8ee188b4-54a8-4605-9773-ab1172886589.definition: Learn about the basic file structures used to store data on disk in a database management system.

6fd8a5b4-36cf-4beb-873e-5e9b2a13e55e.title: Heap Files
6fd8a5b4-36cf-4beb-873e-5e9b2a13e55e.definition: Learn about heap files, a way of storing data in no particular order where records are added wherever there is free space.

b0fb5d6a-a479-4d88-8250-d235afa5ab79.title: Hash Files
b0fb5d6a-a479-4d88-8250-d235afa5ab79.definition: Learn about hash files and how they use hash functions to organize and access data quickly based on hash keys.

bc5d69d1-eaba-4ea8-94c7-cacc82ccd607.title: Query Operator Algorithms
bc5d69d1-eaba-4ea8-94c7-cacc82ccd607.definition: Study the basic algorithms used to implement query operators such as select, projection, and join.

387fb97f-2311-40a8-84b9-eefab78ed2b3.title: External Sorting
387fb97f-2311-40a8-84b9-eefab78ed2b3.definition: Learn about the external sort algorithm, used when the data to be sorted is too large to fit in main memory.

b9df0d7c-25d9-4b6f-809f-a3a6ce46471b.title: Selection Algorithms
b9df0d7c-25d9-4b6f-809f-a3a6ce46471b.definition: Algorithms are used to perform selection (row filtering) operators during query processing.

9b55c8f2-99c3-4c69-b91f-0f3538acef59.title: Projection Algorithms
9b55c8f2-99c3-4c69-b91f-0f3538acef59.definition: Algorithms are used to perform projection (column selection) operations, including handling the removal of duplicate records.

378eb076-c2ad-49af-bf3c-ef1a079c3ada.title: Natural Join Algorithms
378eb076-c2ad-49af-bf3c-ef1a079c3ada.definition: Study the algorithms used to perform natural joins between tables.

8ae20d81-554d-44d3-bdb7-9c65c996f665.title: Nested Loop Join
8ae20d81-554d-44d3-bdb7-9c65c996f665.definition: Learn about the nested loop join algorithm, one of the basic connection algorithms, traversing each pair of records.

1a4fce3a-7f03-47ef-9c1f-eb08323a18e9.title: Sort-Merge Join
1a4fce3a-7f03-47ef-9c1f-eb08323a18e9.definition: Learn about the sort-merge join algorithm, which requires tables to be sorted before merging.

5a72f3ea-81b7-4fb6-a30a-d207302ef0ff.title: Hash Join
5a72f3ea-81b7-4fb6-a30a-d207302ef0ff.definition: Learn about the hash join algorithm, which uses hash functions to group and connect records.

8b2cc4bc-5bab-45c8-8668-4efa89cd91f4.title: Algorithm Efficiency Analysis
8b2cc4bc-5bab-45c8-8668-4efa89cd91f4.definition: analyze the efficiency and complexity of query processing algorithms, often measured by the number of I/O operations.

d84ec35f-c942-4b61-8aab-fa66ee9bc4cb.title: Query Transformations
d84ec35f-c942-4b61-8aab-fa66ee9bc4cb.definition: Techniques for converting a query from its original form to an equivalent form that can be executed more efficiently by the database management system.

01d66384-7db7-4c0e-9b31-0b33e2031899.title: Query Optimization
01d66384-7db7-4c0e-9b31-0b33e2031899.definition: understand the process and techniques that a database management system uses to select the optimal execution plan for a query.

31d94ef2-5f68-4c22-b559-62e162eb9ed0.title: Access Paths
31d94ef2-5f68-4c22-b559-62e162eb9ed0.definition: The different ways the query optimizer can access data (e.g., table scans, using indexes).

98cc013b-58db-404a-8f68-50c87b07d078.title: Query Plan Construction
98cc013b-58db-404a-8f68-50c87b07d078.definition: The process of building a detailed execution plan for a query, including the order of operations and access methods.

834ae376-8c94-4e53-b438-7fb101b11489.title: Selectivity Estimation
834ae376-8c94-4e53-b438-7fb101b11489.definition: Methods that estimate the number of records that will be returned by a query operator, important for optimization.

18b39406-9781-4652-91c7-4707201d7381.title: Index-Only Plans
18b39406-9781-4652-91c7-4707201d7381.definition: Query plans can be executed entirely using indexes without accessing the original data table.

33f18b2c-499d-4741-8417-d3da963fb861.title: Parallel Query Processing
33f18b2c-499d-4741-8417-d3da963fb861.definition: Learn about parallel query processing to speed up query execution by dividing work across multiple processors or nodes.

5cee0a5c-819c-4beb-82ca-1b34e188f193.title: Parallel Scan
5cee0a5c-819c-4beb-82ca-1b34e188f193.definition: Parallel data scanning technique across multiple devices or streams to speed up retrieval.

868193ce-0b56-4d94-b77c-f238f52c47f0.title: Parallel Join
868193ce-0b56-4d94-b77c-f238f52c47f0.definition: Technique for performing parallel connections between tables to speed up processing.

498eb38a-8afe-4ebd-b1fb-546dd599ab94.title: Parallel Aggregation
498eb38a-8afe-4ebd-b1fb-546dd599ab94.definition: Technique for performing aggregate operations (e.g., SUM, COUNT, AVG) in parallel on data partitions.

90f28f8f-5823-46b2-854a-16f2ec983af6.title: Database Tuning & Performance
90f28f8f-5823-46b2-854a-16f2ec983af6.definition: Methods and techniques to tune and improve overall database performance.

1220750c-8171-44ce-9c02-c0930db1a6d8.title: Index Selection
1220750c-8171-44ce-9c02-c0930db1a6d8.definition: The process of deciding which indexes should be created or modified to optimize the performance of executing a set of queries.

6e03f5b9-4d9a-45f0-bfec-3fa656300510.title: Index Performance Impact
6e03f5b9-4d9a-45f0-bfec-3fa656300510.definition: analyze the impact of using indexes on query speed, update costs, and storage capacity.

6ccd6faf-15f8-471b-a153-4027c290be38.title: Denormalization for Performance
6ccd6faf-15f8-471b-a153-4027c290be38.definition: apply denormalization as a tuning technique to improve query performance by reducing the number of joins, although it may increase data redundancy.

81645e39-b2ab-4fbd-a51c-3ff6f685c019.title: DB Buffer Management
81645e39-b2ab-4fbd-a51c-3ff6f685c019.definition: understand how database management systems manage caches in main memory to optimize data access from disk.

d6ed277b-1ae3-4b5d-bd6c-cd6feb0e1142.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
d6ed277b-1ae3-4b5d-bd6c-cd6feb0e1142.definition: Learn about different isolation levels for database transactions (e.g., Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable) and their impact on consistency and performance.

4cba323d-c75e-4a9c-afb5-64644378bda1.title: ACID Properties
4cba323d-c75e-4a9c-afb5-64644378bda1.definition: Master the four basic properties of transactions in database management systems: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

2a3e421c-7de6-4b31-8feb-25d2cf80373f.title: Serializability
2a3e421c-7de6-4b31-8feb-25d2cf80373f.definition: understand the principles and methods of ensuring that the result of the simultaneous execution of multiple transactions is equivalent to several sequential executions of the same transactions.

9c752169-dab9-4ac5-985a-09f382176017.title: Distributed Transactions
9c752169-dab9-4ac5-985a-09f382176017.definition: Learn how to manage transactions that span multiple databases or systems, including challenges and solutions for consistency and reliability (See also: PDC-Coordination).

564542e6-1a08-4b8c-82c2-21e56ec4c1c0.title: Concurrency Control: 2PL
564542e6-1a08-4b8c-82c2-21e56ec4c1c0.definition: Research 2-phase locking (2PL) mechanism to ensure serialization in concurrent environments (See also: OS-Concurrency).

5c7fd16e-fce7-422f-8c77-031558872b93.title: Deadlock Handling Strategies
5c7fd16e-fce7-422f-8c77-031558872b93.definition: Learn methods to detect, prevent, and resolve deadlocks in concurrent database systems.

85dc16dc-3205-44a5-9494-56780cc895d5.title: Quorum Consistency Models
85dc16dc-3205-44a5-9494-56780cc895d5.definition: Explore quorum-based data consistency models, used to ensure reliability and availability in distributed systems.

47b7e9c3-66cb-4584-8360-f6026ca0b943.title: Recovery & Buffer Manager
47b7e9c3-66cb-4584-8360-f6026ca0b943.definition: understand the relationship and interaction between the recovery manager and the cache manager in a database management system.

ceb16bf4-7e66-4768-9471-87a90d8cc1f1.title: Optimistic Concurrency Control
ceb16bf4-7e66-4768-9471-87a90d8cc1f1.definition: Study optimistic concurrency control methods where transactions are assumed to be conflict-free and conflict checking is performed at the commit stage.

4dfa50bd-43d3-4cc1-92b2-cff1f2c38ee2.title: Timestamp Concurrency Control
4dfa50bd-43d3-4cc1-92b2-cff1f2c38ee2.definition: Learn how to use timestamps to control the execution order of concurrent transactions and ensure serialization.

ba7b4a59-68d4-4297-888a-495da7449ea3.title: Write-Ahead Logging
ba7b4a59-68d4-4297-888a-495da7449ea3.definition: Learn Write-Ahead logging (WAL) techniques to ensure transaction persistence during database recovery.

5806d063-d7f8-491c-bafa-534d7933cd56.title: ARIES Recovery System
5806d063-d7f8-491c-bafa-534d7933cd56.definition: Study in detail the ARIES recovery system, including the analyze, REDO and UNDO phases, used to recover the database after a crash.

fa2a5692-c9e9-4fb3-869b-fa707e362565.title: Why NoSQL?
fa2a5692-c9e9-4fb3-869b-fa707e362565.definition: understand the reasons and use cases when NoSQL systems are preferred over traditional RDBMS (e.g. impedance mismatch between Application [CRUD] and RDBMS).

f4f77432-3b0d-4852-844a-99794ad7620c.title: Key-Value & Document Models
f4f77432-3b0d-4852-844a-99794ad7620c.definition: Research the characteristics and applications of Key-Value and Document data models in NoSQL systems.

7aaf7d7a-f3c1-4fd1-aeb2-5e1424f53592.title: NoSQL Storage Systems
7aaf7d7a-f3c1-4fd1-aeb2-5e1424f53592.definition: Explore the types of storage systems used in NoSQL environments, including Key-Value systems and Data Lakes.

9a90384a-543c-43c3-82f5-3878d727297e.title: Sharding & Replication
9a90384a-543c-43c3-82f5-3878d727297e.definition: Learn data distribution techniques such as Sharding and Replication in NoSQL systems to increase scalability and availability (See also: PDC-Communication).

81711f35-bc8f-4203-bda4-f7ef178cb329.title: Graph Databases
81711f35-bc8f-4203-bda4-f7ef178cb329.definition: Research graph databases, modeling and querying data as nodes and edges, suitable for data with complex relationships.

66a78c8d-37bd-481e-8321-520d250a3e0e.title: NoSQL Consistency Models
66a78c8d-37bd-481e-8321-520d250a3e0e.definition: understand the different consistency models in NoSQL, including update and read consistency, Quorum consistency, and the CAP (Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance) theorem (See also: PDC-Communication).

da8b0a07-f443-4ce9-af6b-89bd7466510d.title: Map-Reduce Models
da8b0a07-f443-4ce9-af6b-89bd7466510d.definition: Learn big data processing paradigms like Map-Reduce, Multi-stage Map-Reduce, and Incremental Map-Reduce in a NoSQL context (See also: PDC-Communication).

448929fa-880d-4f55-8e83-6458056b4864.title: NoSQL Case Studies
448929fa-880d-4f55-8e83-6458056b4864.definition: Study real-life cases of cloud storage systems (e.g., S3), graph databases, and analyze situations where NoSQL is not suitable (See also: SPD-Web).

4c776bc1-92b4-4084-9d9e-68ba06f99be1.title: Data Security vs. Privacy
4c776bc1-92b4-4084-9d9e-68ba06f99be1.definition: Clear distinction between data security (protecting data from unauthorized access) and data privacy (managing how personal data is collected, used and shared) (See also: SEC-Foundations).

6bed313f-9b5f-4e53-94cf-331a93dedd49.title: Database Attack Protection
6bed313f-9b5f-4e53-94cf-331a93dedd49.definition: Learn methods and techniques to protect data and database systems from threats and attacks, including injection attacks such as SQL injection (See also: SEC-Foundations).

e9e06558-aaf6-4f92-9f61-8b56d8ba3a76.title: PII Protection
e9e06558-aaf6-4f92-9f61-8b56d8ba3a76.definition: Master the concept of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and strategies to protect it from misuse or unauthorized disclosure (See also: SEC-Foundations, SEP-Security, SEP-Privacy).

541e70b1-0b1f-4f62-b4da-5346410f922b.title: Data Security & Privacy Ethics
541e70b1-0b1f-4f62-b4da-5346410f922b.definition: Discuss ethical issues related to data collection, storage, processing, and sharing, especially in the context of security and privacy (See also: SEC-SEP, SEP-Ethical-Analysis, SEP-Security, SEP-Privacy).

f98ac427-53ec-4f91-a639-2593a07a5f7e.title: Data Security States
f98ac427-53ec-4f91-a639-2593a07a5f7e.definition: understand the importance and different methods to protect data in different states: when data is inactive (at rest), while in transit (in transit) and while being processed (during processing) (See also: SEC-Foundations, SEC-Crypto).

25da9636-fda4-420a-a1f1-c191f1af6433.title: Database Auditing & Forensics
25da9636-fda4-420a-a1f1-c191f1af6433.definition: The study of database auditing, including activity logging techniques, and its important role in digital forensics to detect and analyze security breaches (See also: SEC-Forensics).

5df21ee4-d260-4ae8-9de7-508574240650.title: Data Inference Attacks
5df21ee4-d260-4ae8-9de7-508574240650.definition: Learn how to infer sensitive information from non-sensitive data and measures to prevent inference attacks, especially in the context of database systems (See also: SEC-Crypto).

40ad4452-e200-44d2-a522-eb5436e91cb9.title: Data Privacy Regulations
40ad4452-e200-44d2-a522-eb5436e91cb9.definition: Master key laws and regulations related to data security and privacy, such as GDPR, HIPAA, etc., and their impact on data system design and management (See also: SEP-Security, SEP-Privacy, SEC-Foundations, SEC-Governance).

6976910d-8a8b-4904-b2b0-cd1f38139381.title: Data Integrity Risks
6976910d-8a8b-4904-b2b0-cd1f38139381.definition: analyze common risk factors that can affect data integrity and preventative measures to maintain data accuracy and consistency (See also: SEC-Governance).

791080bc-3377-4fa3-922c-c5f66c87ac95.title: Ransomware
791080bc-3377-4fa3-922c-c5f66c87ac95.definition: Learn about ransomware attacks and effective strategies to prevent data loss, data destruction, and ensure recovery from such attacks (See also: SEC-Coding, SEC-Forensics).

548ecfb1-2b0a-4bc5-8adc-535d58061083.title: Data Exploration
548ecfb1-2b0a-4bc5-8adc-535d58061083.definition: Master data exploration techniques, including data dynamics, representations, descriptive statistics, and visualization methods to better understand data sets.

1b7d1b84-07a5-4592-b730-9de0964f7182.title: Data Science Life Cycle
1b7d1b84-07a5-4592-b730-9de0964f7182.definition: understand the stages in the data science lifecycle, from business understanding to deployment and user adoption, as a basis for data analytics and machine learning projects (See also: AI-ML).

33c8391d-45f7-4660-8c24-de2b231954fc.title: Data Mining Algorithms
33c8391d-45f7-4660-8c24-de2b231954fc.definition: Algorithms and techniques are used to discover patterns, trends, and insights from large data sets.

f28fe9d4-2489-4e61-a093-d6254fbbb92a.title: Machine Learning Algorithms
f28fe9d4-2489-4e61-a093-d6254fbbb92a.definition: Algorithms allow systems to learn from data, recognize patterns, and make decisions without being explicitly programmed.

70e92358-c84c-4433-bb0b-359ff84fe388.title: Classification Algorithms
70e92358-c84c-4433-bb0b-359ff84fe388.definition: Machine learning algorithms are used to classify data into predefined categories or classes based on their characteristics.

4d72cee6-9913-49fe-9af6-fddb77d18bc7.title: Clustering Algorithms
4d72cee6-9913-49fe-9af6-fddb77d18bc7.definition: Machine learning algorithms are used to group similar data points together into clusters, based on their similarity.

a1e9d7da-710c-48b7-b5a5-1eb9e865ece2.title: Association Algorithms
a1e9d7da-710c-48b7-b5a5-1eb9e865ece2.definition: Algorithms are used to discover relationships (association rules) between variables in large data sets.

0939f3b7-7658-4e21-a1d5-66d54d7bc600.title: Regression Algorithms
0939f3b7-7658-4e21-a1d5-66d54d7bc600.definition: Machine learning algorithms are used to predict a continuous variable (dependent variable) based on one or more independent variables.

674125dc-da46-4b70-bb82-6fd5fc604f14.title: Data Collection
674125dc-da46-4b70-bb82-6fd5fc604f14.definition: The process of collecting, filtering, and cleaning data from various sources to prepare it for processing and analysis.

aaf8db24-ea9a-48d2-a32d-7b20537def14.title: Data Governance
aaf8db24-ea9a-48d2-a32d-7b20537def14.definition: A set of policies, standards, roles, and processes to ensure the quality, availability, usability, integrity, and security of data within an organization.

ad575fd6-a3c6-49f0-b3d7-e243e55790d1.title: Data Fairness
ad575fd6-a3c6-49f0-b3d7-e243e55790d1.definition: Ensure that data collection, use and analysis do not result in discrimination or disadvantage to particular groups of individuals.

772b7977-960c-41df-b34c-396fc528397f.title: Data Bias
772b7977-960c-41df-b34c-396fc528397f.definition: Systematic errors in the data or in the way the data is collected, leading to unfair or inaccurate results or decisions.

e45b4a43-08db-4416-a82d-ca77a309edc3.title: Data Visualization Techniques
e45b4a43-08db-4416-a82d-ca77a309edc3.definition: Methods and tools for presenting data in graphic or visual form to help users more easily understand and analyze information.

76e5fbe1-caa7-49c3-bbf1-2035cf23dcc1.title: Data Visualization Applications
76e5fbe1-caa7-49c3-bbf1-2035cf23dcc1.definition: How data visualization techniques are used to explore, present, and communicate findings from data analysis.

1ab9772c-e828-487c-9dbf-aaaad1848830.title: Entity Resolution
1ab9772c-e828-487c-9dbf-aaaad1848830.definition: The process of identifying and linking records that represent the same entity in one or more data sets.

5b42f9ef-8868-4ee4-aab3-9bd64b1417f7.title: EDA Methods
5b42f9ef-8868-4ee4-aab3-9bd64b1417f7.definition: Initial techniques for analyzing data sets aim to summarize their main characteristics, often using visual methods.

d2ade8a2-5cb6-4c95-af7c-cc0138c0988c.title: Distributed DBMS
d2ade8a2-5cb6-4c95-af7c-cc0138c0988c.definition: Database management systems allow data to be stored and managed on many different physical computers, but still operate as a single logical database.

4327aecf-2b8c-4e16-b7f9-a11f960d1959.title: Distributed Data Storage
4327aecf-2b8c-4e16-b7f9-a11f960d1959.definition: A method of storing data on multiple networked nodes or servers, allowing for scalability, fault tolerance, and efficient data access.

7fbcbd44-781f-47a9-9d9b-9ffba97394a5.title: Distributed Query Processing
7fbcbd44-781f-47a9-9d9b-9ffba97394a5.definition: Technique for handling queries on data stored across multiple locations in a distributed database system.

4499d57a-db36-458c-b730-a82e8cef7e44.title: Distributed Transaction Model
4499d57a-db36-458c-b730-a82e8cef7e44.definition: The model manages transactions involving multiple data sources or resources on different nodes in a distributed system, ensuring consistency and integrity.

9bf9fafa-83fd-4fd9-a346-c67eef43175c.title: Homogeneous Distributed DB
9bf9fafa-83fd-4fd9-a346-c67eef43175c.definition: Distributed database solutions where all nodes use the same database software and data schema.

e09a39db-d9ee-424e-b4cb-0fcd5faa1236.title: Heterogeneous Distributed DB
e09a39db-d9ee-424e-b4cb-0fcd5faa1236.definition: Distributed database solutions where nodes can use different database management systems or data schemas.

a3a7abb9-45f2-4969-a0f2-4488873554b9.title: Client-Server Distributed DB
a3a7abb9-45f2-4969-a0f2-4488873554b9.definition: Distributed database architecture where clients send requests to servers that manage and store data.

0ffc538d-0e32-4f5e-b2e3-da6d65e76de6.title: Parallel DBMS
0ffc538d-0e32-4f5e-b2e3-da6d65e76de6.definition: A database management system uses multiple processors and/or disks at the same time to execute database operations to improve performance.

8c382314-22dc-4c9b-9750-f52a0b995080.title: Parallel DBMS Architecture
8c382314-22dc-4c9b-9750-f52a0b995080.definition: Different architectural models for parallel DBMSs, including shared memory, shared disk, and shared nothing.

2aa899ea-69a2-435a-b435-6670a2b553b8.title: Shared-Memory Architecture
2aa899ea-69a2-435a-b435-6670a2b553b8.definition: A Parallel DBMS architecture where all processors share a common memory address space.

6b383056-e70a-4a2c-8576-d0cbbb351309.title: Shared-Disk Architecture
6b383056-e70a-4a2c-8576-d0cbbb351309.definition: A Parallel DBMS architecture where all processors have access to the same set of disks.

e6b5f7c3-5672-4987-aa61-d0b141b0660f.title: Nothing-Shared Architecture
e6b5f7c3-5672-4987-aa61-d0b141b0660f.definition: A Parallel DBMS architecture where each processor has its own memory and disk, not shared directly with other processors.

3bd77c57-bda3-4fe0-b870-b06f3a6719aa.title: Speedup & Scale-up
3bd77c57-bda3-4fe0-b870-b06f3a6719aa.definition: Parallel system performance measurement concepts: speedup is reducing execution time with fixed data and more resources; Scaling is maintaining execution time as data and resources increase.

b100c441-c41f-46fd-a8c6-3b2fad9db914.title: MapReduce Model
b100c441-c41f-46fd-a8c6-3b2fad9db914.definition: A programming model and software framework for processing large data sets using distributed algorithms across a computer cluster.

e6b4d90c-d6c6-421d-8f08-a5c25d84222d.title: Data Replication
e6b4d90c-d6c6-421d-8f08-a5c25d84222d.definition: The process of creating and maintaining multiple copies of data at different locations to increase availability, fault tolerance, and performance.

0332d5ea-62a2-44cd-b1ad-1f6e750899ba.title: Weak Consistency Models
0332d5ea-62a2-44cd-b1ad-1f6e750899ba.definition: The models ensure that data will eventually be consistent across all replicas, but allow that different replicas may be temporarily out of sync.

72179615-136a-4a8c-9833-5083d3709cad.title: Unstructured Data Vectorization
72179615-136a-4a8c-9833-5083d3709cad.definition: The process of converting unstructured data (text, video, audio) into digital representations (vectors) that can be processed by computer algorithms.

81e9a583-85ef-4f68-ae21-f2d6695d820f.title: Vector Storage
81e9a583-85ef-4f68-ae21-f2d6695d820f.definition: Systems or techniques designed to store and retrieve vector representations of unstructured data efficiently.

f06ad91b-8be4-4cf7-a031-02005734b851.title: TF-IDF Ngram Vectorization
f06ad91b-8be4-4cf7-a031-02005734b851.definition: A technique that converts text into numeric vectors, using term-frequency index-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) and word groups (ngrams) to capture context.

b3c29511-fb13-4346-9316-eb844702f562.title: Word2Vec
b3c29511-fb13-4346-9316-eb844702f562.definition: A word embedding technique to create vector representations of words, where words with similar meanings have vector representations close to each other in the vector space.

fb644139-637f-4bde-8e55-156de6238c8b.title: Array Database
fb644139-637f-4bde-8e55-156de6238c8b.definition: A type of database designed to efficiently store and manage large multi-dimensional array structured data sets, such as satellite images or sensor data.

e64f68d8-4d6e-4707-9bbe-ef9232a6eb8f.title: Array Data Processing
e64f68d8-4d6e-4707-9bbe-ef9232a6eb8f.definition: Techniques and methods for storing, querying, and manipulating array data types in databases.

175c9e21-07db-4565-bfd4-c6b58596bf05.title: Semi-structured Database
175c9e21-07db-4565-bfd4-c6b58596bf05.definition: Databases store data that does not follow the fixed structural model of a relational database, but contains tags or delimiters to separate semantic elements. JSON is a common example.

7b980c6f-914e-45a0-a06f-7637d841c67a.title: Semi-structured DB Storage
7b980c6f-914e-45a0-a06f-7637d841c67a.definition: Methods and systems are used to store semi-structured data efficiently, balancing flexibility and performance.

b2433248-74e6-4785-926e-9ac52363f27b.title: Nested Data Encoding
b2433248-74e6-4785-926e-9ac52363f27b.definition: Techniques for representing hierarchical or nested data types (as in JSON) into a format that can be stored and processed efficiently.

a23df3da-4cef-48ef-89fa-5f72cc4c3556.title: Nested Data Compression
a23df3da-4cef-48ef-89fa-5f72cc4c3556.definition: Methods for reducing the storage size of nested data types in semi-structured databases.

9bdafe88-29e0-4914-aa71-34b78fea92bb.title: Semi-structured DB Indexing
9bdafe88-29e0-4914-aa71-34b78fea92bb.definition: Indexing techniques to speed up queries on semi-structured data, taking into account their flexible and nested structure.

4d876a91-835b-407a-b242-12bb2111ad0c.title: B-tree Index
4d876a91-835b-407a-b242-12bb2111ad0c.definition: The B-tree index data structure is used for efficient search, insertion, and deletion of data, applied in the context of semi-structured databases.

bc08c4b1-fbe4-417b-ac7e-b7e06bf82dd1.title: Skip Index
bc08c4b1-fbe4-417b-ac7e-b7e06bf82dd1.definition: A type of index that allows queries to 'jump' over parts of unrelated data, speeding up searches in semi-structured data structures.

517d8e44-fe0d-480a-b8e4-8009d406aad1.title: Bloom Filter
517d8e44-fe0d-480a-b8e4-8009d406aad1.definition: A space-saving probabilistic data structure used to check whether an element is a member of a set, which can be applied to speed up queries on semi-structured data.

cf403f6d-2671-4eba-9327-69a50e1a5041.title: Inverted Index
cf403f6d-2671-4eba-9327-69a50e1a5041.definition: An index structure maps content values ​​to their location in the database, commonly used for full-text search in semi-structured data.

c88703f4-e165-40e2-998a-00c3ae51c578.title: Bitmap Compression
c88703f4-e165-40e2-998a-00c3ae51c578.definition: Technique that compresses bitmap indexes to save storage space and improve query performance, especially useful for data with many repeating values.

91b8a00a-4b93-499b-876b-a1c437db0eb0.title: Space-filling Curve Indexing
91b8a00a-4b93-499b-876b-a1c437db0eb0.definition: The indexing technique uses space-filling curves to map multidimensional geographic data into a one-dimensional order, optimizing the storage and querying of semi-structured geographic data.

5f7c98ec-b99a-4dd9-879a-e88680e526f8.title: Semi-structured Query Processing
5f7c98ec-b99a-4dd9-879a-e88680e526f8.definition: Methods and strategies for executing queries in semi-structured databases, supporting both online transaction processing (OLTP) and online analytical processing (OLAP) use cases.

6b9925f2-4a1f-4afe-a291-9e36373c0956.title: Semi-structured CRUD Trade-offs
6b9925f2-4a1f-4afe-a291-9e36373c0956.definition: analyze the performance and complexity trade-offs when performing CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations on semi-structured databases, due to their flexible nature.

8b71b17e-db9b-4da7-a4b7-c106244a7990.title: Postgres JSON Case Study
8b71b17e-db9b-4da7-a4b7-c106244a7990.definition: Study how PostgreSQL supports and manages JSON data, including the functionality and performance when working with this semi-structured data type.

f4745e11-4e53-4b04-8937-aedfc07a48a5.title: MongoDB Case Study
f4745e11-4e53-4b04-8937-aedfc07a48a5.definition: Study how MongoDB, a document-based NoSQL database, stores and processes semi-structured data (especially BSON, similar to JSON).

50e85d7f-ad77-4a09-9e87-c10f2036944e.title: Snowflake JSON Case Study
50e85d7f-ad77-4a09-9e87-c10f2036944e.definition: Study how Snowflake, a cloud-based data warehouse, processes and analyzes JSON data, leveraging its special features for semi-structured data.

bf2ba369-d952-4a34-92c6-8364a85d470d.title: Data Scale Issues
bf2ba369-d952-4a34-92c6-8364a85d470d.definition: Ethical, social, and technical challenges and implications arise from collecting, storing, and processing extremely large data sets, including privacy and security.

eb708b71-8620-438b-9c72-bc9baddca275.title: Data Privacy
eb708b71-8620-438b-9c72-bc9baddca275.definition: Overview of concepts, principles and laws related to protecting personal information from unauthorized access, use or disclosure.

59c3317b-acae-4d65-ab88-93e320b3ac9c.title: Privacy by Design Compliance
59c3317b-acae-4d65-ab88-93e320b3ac9c.definition: An approach that integrates privacy protection requirements into the system, product or service design and development process from the beginning.

957eb67b-1a47-4c61-a831-e010953348df.title: Data Anonymization
957eb67b-1a47-4c61-a831-e010953348df.definition: Techniques and principles for removing or masking personally identifiable information from data, making individuals unidentifiable.

33871bd9-5a7b-40b8-ba4e-1b7a7afc7f7c.title: Data Ownership
33871bd9-5a7b-40b8-ba4e-1b7a7afc7f7c.definition: Legal rights and responsibilities regarding data, including rights to access, use, modify, and share data.

f7605fc8-ac69-4fe7-be55-51a00f5d7d8d.title: Data Custodian Role
f7605fc8-ac69-4fe7-be55-51a00f5d7d8d.definition: Responsibility for technical management and data maintenance, ensuring data is stored securely, accessible and in compliance with policies.

5de94999-539f-4c31-ab5b-079ff9adcdf7.title: Intended Data Use
5de94999-539f-4c31-ab5b-079ff9adcdf7.definition: The planned and authorized purposes for which the collected and stored data will be used.

a4841db5-81ea-4bf3-b355-55f1408619a3.title: Unintended Data Use
a4841db5-81ea-4bf3-b355-55f1408619a3.definition: Uses of data that were not originally intended or authorized may lead to ethical, legal, or social issues.

c91458bb-2f48-4f68-ac0f-dbdcf2b961c2.title: Data Reliability
c91458bb-2f48-4f68-ac0f-dbdcf2b961c2.definition: The degree to which data can be trusted to be accurate, complete, consistent, and available when needed.

7043a522-dfc8-4510-b195-c0e00f2daf7a.title: Data Provenance
7043a522-dfc8-4510-b195-c0e00f2daf7a.definition: A detailed record of the origin of the data and the sequence of operations that have been applied to it since its creation.

b39e311f-67b6-46bf-acc8-dd38cae99d5a.title: Data Lineage
b39e311f-67b6-46bf-acc8-dd38cae99d5a.definition: The complete history of the data, including where it originated, how it was transformed, moved and used over time.

0b397439-a95a-49ce-aaaa-4df852585fef.title: Metadata Management
0b397439-a95a-49ce-aaaa-4df852585fef.definition: The process of managing information about data (metadata) to help organize, access, and understand data more effectively.

8184f85b-5ab5-433a-90a9-2fa420a6320a.title: Data Security
8184f85b-5ab5-433a-90a9-2fa420a6320a.definition: Measures and tools to protect data from unauthorized access, modification, destruction or disclosure.

076f6983-1585-4206-b9eb-b119af62919b.title: Collaborative Data Management
076f6983-1585-4206-b9eb-b119af62919b.definition: Data stewards and data users must collaborate to ensure accurate data is accessed and used only appropriately.

02fb4c18-7698-491c-9639-04160b95d103.title: Responsive Data Management
02fb4c18-7698-491c-9639-04160b95d103.definition: The data stored and accessed must always meet the needs/requirements of the organization.

49977258-9a61-445d-b648-3bfcf5802970.title: Probability & Statistics
49977258-9a61-445d-b648-3bfcf5802970.definition: Probability and Statistics requirements for those specializing in DM-Analytics.

ca7e584a-e25d-4515-a07e-59752e8d9779.title: Hash Functions & Tables
ca7e584a-e25d-4515-a07e-59752e8d9779.definition: Hash functions, and hash tables, are desired data structures in data management.

8c308723-f1c0-4eaa-a64f-dd28b3803d45.title: Balanced Binary Trees
8c308723-f1c0-4eaa-a64f-dd28b3803d45.definition: Types of balanced binary trees, e.g. AVL, 2-3-4, Red-Black Trees.

8d630584-620d-4d59-a4bd-50c6f3d0eb9e.title: AVL Tree
8d630584-620d-4d59-a4bd-50c6f3d0eb9e.definition: AVL tree, a type of self-balancing binary search tree.

439e8e18-ed50-48bd-940c-54654c085972.title: Red-Black Tree
439e8e18-ed50-48bd-940c-54654c085972.definition: Red-Black Tree, a self-balancing binary search tree.

be3f157a-3961-4b16-bf20-6af2acf916b3.title: B-Trees & B+ Trees
be3f157a-3961-4b16-bf20-6af2acf916b3.definition: B and B+ tree data structures, commonly used in database systems.

faadd8c4-311c-496c-b4ac-67f62f1f83e8.title: Database Design & Modeling
faadd8c4-311c-496c-b4ac-67f62f1f83e8.definition: One of the four main perspectives to approach databases, focusing on data design and modeling.

a8857b59-77ef-482c-be31-6050117f90a4.title: Database Usage
a8857b59-77ef-482c-be31-6050117f90a4.definition: One of the four main perspectives to approach databases, focusing on database usage.

c33d8bcb-49ff-494e-be0a-5f399f433617.title: Database Administration
c33d8bcb-49ff-494e-be0a-5f399f433617.definition: One of the four main perspectives to approach databases, focusing on database system administration.

db2d5fe5-d665-444d-839f-4aa0214e8f81.title: Database Development
db2d5fe5-d665-444d-839f-4aa0214e8f81.definition: One of four main perspectives for approaching databases, including implementation algorithms.

9fcd6362-9c67-4524-a138-ae0a5cea0959.title: Database Implementation Algorithms
9fcd6362-9c67-4524-a138-ae0a5cea0959.definition: Algorithms are used to implement and operate database systems.

98b229f3-ad54-4147-8546-f23b4617421f.title: DM-SEP
98b229f3-ad54-4147-8546-f23b4617421f.definition: One topic in the Database Systems course (3 hours).

cf384407-a81d-4881-9b67-fd98b5cef975.title: DM-Data
cf384407-a81d-4881-9b67-fd98b5cef975.definition: A data-related topic in the Database Systems course (1 hour).

48947934-4694-4594-89d2-b093aca2cd4d.title: DM-Core
48947934-4694-4594-89d2-b093aca2cd4d.definition: Core Topics in Data Management (3 hours).

53f2db66-c076-4b29-beda-bc12f46a367d.title: DM-Internals
53f2db66-c076-4b29-beda-bc12f46a367d.definition: Topics on the structure and inner workings of database systems (5 hours).

b6f20ccf-a797-4ea5-a74f-377381dfb905.title: Distributed Data Management
b6f20ccf-a797-4ea5-a74f-377381dfb905.definition: Basic concepts and principles of distributed data management, allocated 2 class hours.

0e42af6f-6fa9-439a-bea7-d7c36917a6be.title: Core Database Concepts (CS Core)
0e42af6f-6fa9-439a-bea7-d7c36917a6be.definition: Basic database concepts are integrated into the CS Core curriculum, especially in the absence of specialized database courses.

110c8161-21a7-4d3f-bacf-b208e1afb6c1.title: Database Access
110c8161-21a7-4d3f-bacf-b208e1afb6c1.definition: Students use databases to retrieve data in introductory programming courses, instead of using file I/O or interactive data entry. This level usually includes being provided with an access code.

e5a726d4-1d00-44f7-be7b-1d35127231bf.title: File I/O
e5a726d4-1d00-44f7-be7b-1d35127231bf.definition: File import/export method, mentioned as an alternative to database access in introductory courses.

6f7acadd-af1f-46b7-8a08-21a860e5d7c0.title: Interactive Input
6f7acadd-af1f-46b7-8a08-21a860e5d7c0.definition: Direct data entry, via an interactive interface, is mentioned as an alternative to database access in introductory courses.

11b2ae7e-2be3-4d18-920c-f84912c72c32.title: Basic SQL Query
11b2ae7e-2be3-4d18-920c-f84912c72c32.definition: Students are provided with SQL query code to access the database in introductory courses.

12bb99c2-e300-4529-8436-9d4c8b3f8c8b.title: Intermediate SQL Query
12bb99c2-e300-4529-8436-9d4c8b3f8c8b.definition: Students write their own SQL queries at the intermediate level.

2d9c8ea3-3d55-42a3-b333-8367b6b9e410.title: Database Design
2d9c8ea3-3d55-42a3-b333-8367b6b9e410.definition: Practice database design in Software Engineering courses or capstone projects.

aa99eade-9188-472d-863c-af976f69e2d7.title: Databases Across Curriculum
aa99eade-9188-472d-863c-af976f69e2d7.definition: An approach that integrates database concepts across the curriculum, from introductory to advanced courses, to integrate database-related CS Core concepts.

6f6b7a31-40ce-4a02-99b3-f50db4fb056a.title: Database SEP Topics
6f6b7a31-40ce-4a02-99b3-f50db4fb056a.definition: Database-related Software Engineering Practice (SEP) topics are integrated into the curriculum using the 'Databases across the curriculum' approach.

fa7bc374-f387-4099-bb5e-30f16eb175b8.title: Data Security Role
fa7bc374-f387-4099-bb5e-30f16eb175b8.definition: Examining the role of data from a security perspective (Security - SEC), could be the content of an in-depth course.

63173a84-adbf-4a28-8091-1f9695e4bb26.title: Data Ethics (SEP)
63173a84-adbf-4a28-8091-1f9695e4bb26.definition: Examining the role of data from a social, ethical, and professional issues (SEP) perspective could be the content of an in-depth course.

1544a466-4a1d-434f-bf6a-d01f0f1b4bb1.title: Discrete Math (FPL)
1544a466-4a1d-434f-bf6a-d01f0f1b4bb1.definition: Discrete mathematical principles underpin the field of Programming Language Foundations.

f05db28f-9995-4db3-91c4-ec72071e3489.title: Logic (FPL)
f05db28f-9995-4db3-91c4-ec72071e3489.definition: Logical principles underpin the field of Programming Language Platforms.

06418e26-ba24-484a-bc55-8d136632cca3.title: Formal Languages (FPL)
06418e26-ba24-484a-bc55-8d136632cca3.definition: Formal language principles underpin the field of Programming Language Platforms.

46c1445f-f861-4b94-a1b4-9609a72f2e74.title: Abstract Computation Models
46c1445f-f861-4b94-a1b4-9609a72f2e74.definition: understand the basic abstract model of computation that programming languages ​​share.

d1106814-2f19-4bc5-98f4-683d89713cbd.title: Program Development Model
d1106814-2f19-4bc5-98f4-683d89713cbd.definition: understand the basic model of program development.

a9ee4a01-a3ab-4e7b-8019-e2110d925932.title: PL Abstractions
a9ee4a01-a3ab-4e7b-8019-e2110d925932.definition: Master common abstractions used in programming languages.

94b86523-ecc1-4065-a381-cd3a9990c93b.title: Programming Paradigms
94b86523-ecc1-4065-a381-cd3a9990c93b.definition: understand different programming paradigms (e.g., object-oriented, functional, imperative).

3a5fce4b-dbd8-4ce3-acfc-59fec9fb75fc.title: Programming Concepts
3a5fce4b-dbd8-4ce3-acfc-59fec9fb75fc.definition: Presents the basic concepts that make up programming languages.

c13b5e7f-3ad9-439e-b766-452d4ccf987d.title: PL Principles
c13b5e7f-3ad9-439e-b766-452d4ccf987d.definition: Presents the basic principles that govern programming languages.

f5c5b6e0-8f6a-41df-aaa8-89114e6b38a8.title: Formal PL Specification
f5c5b6e0-8f6a-41df-aaa8-89114e6b38a8.definition: Ability to specify programming languages ​​formally and concisely.

1c46b777-0395-4c00-86d5-c436470cd0de.title: Formal Program Behavior
1c46b777-0395-4c00-86d5-c436470cd0de.definition: Formal specification of the behavior of a program.

f98a7799-9e21-41f1-b83a-6e9fec454d12.title: Compare Programming Paradigms
f98a7799-9e21-41f1-b83a-6e9fec454d12.definition: Compare the strengths and weaknesses of different programming models.

408c1a40-afd1-4138-a775-756bc4c6f0e2.title: PL-OS Interface
408c1a40-afd1-4138-a775-756bc4c6f0e2.definition: Describe how programming languages ​​communicate with operating systems.

ba07178e-7d4c-4524-a6db-2a663b756078.title: PL-Hardware Interface
ba07178e-7d4c-4524-a6db-2a663b756078.definition: Describe how programming languages ​​communicate with hardware.

dfbea9ee-8d56-43b6-b8d7-689918480f8c.title: Choose PL & Paradigm
dfbea9ee-8d56-43b6-b8d7-689918480f8c.definition: Ability to choose the programming model and language best suited to the specific problem.

8045a9e2-4d56-41f7-ad68-1596299af1c2.title: Programming Paradigms
8045a9e2-4d56-41f7-ad68-1596299af1c2.definition: understand different programming paradigms to make informed design choices.

316366e6-d3d4-48b3-8206-bf178959fd66.title: PL Features
316366e6-d3d4-48b3-8206-bf178959fd66.definition: understand the features and structures of programming languages.

16c790f7-5d35-4ce8-b790-e9ea886b8c0f.title: PL Structures
16c790f7-5d35-4ce8-b790-e9ea886b8c0f.definition: understand the structures and features of programming languages.

7caa0e81-5bd0-4886-97a3-a9cacfac2892.title: Define PL Features
7caa0e81-5bd0-4886-97a3-a9cacfac2892.definition: understand how programming language features are defined.

f05edd3c-1fb0-46ce-b7fc-ab01891bf3b5.title: Compose PL Features
f05edd3c-1fb0-46ce-b7fc-ab01891bf3b5.definition: understand how programming language features are put together.

b3c7eac8-69c2-4ab2-a6de-5530f9d4db38.title: Software Execution Efficiency
b3c7eac8-69c2-4ab2-a6de-5530f9d4db38.definition: Knowledge of how to improve software execution efficiency through understanding language features and implementations.

21a6279f-bb0c-428b-8c5a-00ad35196f75.title: Long-term Software Maintenance
21a6279f-bb0c-428b-8c5a-00ad35196f75.definition: Knowledge of how to improve long-term software maintainability through understanding language features and implementations.

2e729844-5959-402e-b9ce-4d713fd5880e.title: Language Translation
2e729844-5959-402e-b9ce-4d713fd5880e.definition: Basic knowledge of the programming language translation process.

3cf5ef73-ce4a-4d41-88e9-8e44e0947841.title: Program Analysis
3cf5ef73-ce4a-4d41-88e9-8e44e0947841.definition: Basic knowledge of program analysis techniques.

51dd9c57-9168-4a73-8885-30f547323bef.title: Program Runtime Behavior
51dd9c57-9168-4a73-8885-30f547323bef.definition: Basic knowledge of program behavior during execution.

31c8db9f-be04-4094-a3c4-35b96360f44b.title: Memory Management (PL)
31c8db9f-be04-4094-a3c4-35b96360f44b.definition: Basic knowledge of memory management in a programming language environment.

59b9c7e4-1aa5-4dd3-be77-f51f89d59d3c.title: Concurrent Process Interaction
59b9c7e4-1aa5-4dd3-be77-f51f89d59d3c.definition: Knowledge of interactions between concurrent processes.

2cac54c9-9c8d-48c3-a698-2cdc4e2b70b9.title: Message Passing (Concurrency)
2cac54c9-9c8d-48c3-a698-2cdc4e2b70b9.definition: Knowledge of message passing mechanisms for communication between concurrent processes.

1aef4ce2-12c3-4f7a-b908-624147afd536.title: Shared Memory (Concurrency)
1aef4ce2-12c3-4f7a-b908-624147afd536.definition: Knowledge of shared memory mechanisms for communication between concurrent processes.

c9bd698a-9965-471f-bb54-22706c0e6e95.title: Synchronization (Concurrency)
c9bd698a-9965-471f-bb54-22706c0e6e95.definition: Knowledge of synchronization mechanisms to coordinate concurrent processes.

68073d7f-fe61-42ca-b4fa-d3fcda2172e9.title: Programming Language Design
68073d7f-fe61-42ca-b4fa-d3fcda2172e9.definition: Requires deeper familiarity with the fundamentals for designing new languages.

87c02b06-72b8-4528-b315-1a6a749db1fd.title: OOP
87c02b06-72b8-4528-b315-1a6a749db1fd.definition: A programming model based on the concept of 'objects' that can contain data and code. The number of core hours spent on this topic has decreased by 4 hours.

84448e43-b42e-4335-8a8c-92c4616b2a97.title: Functional Programming
84448e43-b42e-4335-8a8c-92c4616b2a97.definition: A programming model that constructs programs by applying and combining functions, avoiding changing states. The number of core hours spent on this topic has been reduced by 2 hours.

017e9980-8b46-444a-bfbb-7e82cbd4320c.title: Event-driven & Reactive PL
017e9980-8b46-444a-bfbb-7e82cbd4320c.definition: A programming model in which the flow of program execution is determined by events and continuously reacts to changes. The number of core hours spent on this topic has increased by 1 hour.

80ce3adc-0ad8-4ab6-8249-a2465f4c7f8f.title: Parallel & Distributed Computing
80ce3adc-0ad8-4ab6-8249-a2465f4c7f8f.definition: Research how to split and execute tasks simultaneously across multiple processors or computers to increase performance. This unit is renamed from 'Concurrency and Parallelism' and has core hours increased by 3 hours.

85427a92-0193-46a1-8f39-64c797976da5.title: Type Systems
85427a92-0193-46a1-8f39-64c797976da5.definition: A set of rules that assign a 'type' to programming language constructs to detect errors and increase reliability. The topics 'Basic Type Systems' and 'Type Systems' have been merged into this unit, with the core hours reduced by 1 hour.

671ffabc-bf70-4eb5-8655-7b2b3f3ab3da.title: Program Abstraction & Representation
671ffabc-bf70-4eb5-8655-7b2b3f3ab3da.definition: Methods of representing the structure and meaning of a computer program at different levels of abstraction. This unit is renamed from 'Program Representation' and has core hours reduced by 1 hour.

0eea4ff6-7904-44d8-869e-33c8b7731484.title: Program Analysis & Tools
0eea4ff6-7904-44d8-869e-33c8b7731484.definition: The study of automatically examining a program's source or object code to detect errors, optimize, or understand program behavior. This unit was renamed from 'Static Analysis'.

4fbc7b42-dea7-42a5-b664-0c619cf59c00.title: Runtime Behavior & Systems
4fbc7b42-dea7-42a5-b664-0c619cf59c00.definition: The study of how a program behaves during execution, including memory management, garbage collection, and services provided by the runtime environment. This unit was renamed from 'Runtime Systems'.

132153ca-00d0-45ed-9f8c-e536bedae7d6.title: Shell Scripting
132153ca-00d0-45ed-9f8c-e536bedae7d6.definition: Write scripts using a command line interface (shell) to automate system tasks or file management. This is a new unit added to the program with 2 core hours.

1596391c-11a7-4f19-b053-79c327ddd3b4.title: System Memory Model
1596391c-11a7-4f19-b053-79c327ddd3b4.definition: The study of how operating systems and hardware execute programs, manage and allocate memory, and how programs interact with memory. This is a new unit added to the program with 3 core hours.

e8cdb056-06db-4cc1-9d64-46430f14ed13.title: Formal Methods
e8cdb056-06db-4cc1-9d64-46430f14ed13.definition: Software development methods rely on rigorous mathematics to describe, design and verify systems, to ensure correctness and safety. This is a newly added unit of knowledge.

cd541baf-7f33-45fc-8bce-f829b8bfdfd3.title: Programming Language Design
cd541baf-7f33-45fc-8bce-f829b8bfdfd3.definition: Important principles and factors to consider when designing a new programming language, including syntax, semantics, data types, and execution model. This is a newly added unit of knowledge.

f9b3c32f-455a-49d0-a9f3-ce63ab2489b0.title: Programming Language Basics
f9b3c32f-455a-49d0-a9f3-ce63ab2489b0.definition: Basic concepts and principles that underlie understanding and analyzing various programming languages. This is a newly added unit of knowledge.

11775af9-b055-4c84-94a0-dd052f247172.title: Society, Ethics, Professionalism
11775af9-b055-4c84-94a0-dd052f247172.definition: Social, ethical, and professional aspects related to the field of computer science and software development. This is a newly added unit of knowledge.

084f9167-1542-43c1-8aff-754562c92116.title: Software Development Basics
084f9167-1542-43c1-8aff-754562c92116.definition: Core concepts and skills required for software development, often taught in introductory courses. This is another area of ​​knowledge that FPL can build on or overlap.

a87d4799-52c0-4007-a183-da25617b321b.title: Programming Paradigms
a87d4799-52c0-4007-a183-da25617b321b.definition: A basic programming style or approach that guides the organization and structure of a program. Modern languages ​​often integrate multiple paradigms.

47f58aac-a32d-4a76-8955-f863466dcc57.title: Imperative Programming
47f58aac-a32d-4a76-8955-f863466dcc57.definition: A programming model focuses on describing the steps (commands) that a program must perform to change its state. Often integrated with other paradigms such as object oriented.

fcdd89fd-95b1-4b78-8e9b-269ce70110ee.title: Logic Programming
fcdd89fd-95b1-4b78-8e9b-269ce70110ee.definition: A programming model based on formal logic, in which programs are represented as facts and rules, and computation is performed by inference. Often integrated with other paradigms such as object oriented.

49e1fadf-0f71-41ed-8ea2-53bb2d9cd0bc.title: Distributed, Concurrent, Parallel Integration
49e1fadf-0f71-41ed-8ea2-53bb2d9cd0bc.definition: understand and integrate the concepts of distributed, concurrency, and parallelism with various programming models as a core area in the context of multicore computing, cloud computing, and computer networks.

8cc6f24c-268b-4305-8a05-3535434e4e4a.title: Event-Driven Development
8cc6f24c-268b-4305-8a05-3535434e4e4a.definition: Master the software development aspects related to event-driven programming, especially important for real-time and pervasive computing applications.

dad91f78-f2f4-47f8-a103-6aaf6801e0cf.title: Reactive Programming Development
dad91f78-f2f4-47f8-a103-6aaf6801e0cf.definition: Master the software development aspects related to reactive programming, especially important for real-time and pervasive computing applications.

ae88b1b1-95e0-4ba2-be3b-70b5cda3cb13.title: Parallel Computing Development
ae88b1b1-95e0-4ba2-be3b-70b5cda3cb13.definition: Master the software development aspects related to parallel computing, especially important for real-time and pervasive computing applications.

ee111814-d118-465a-8019-69e005b190cc.title: Distributed Computing Development
ee111814-d118-465a-8019-69e005b190cc.definition: Master the software development aspects related to distributed computing, especially important for real-time and pervasive computing applications.

3b6012ac-a19c-4b47-b601-f3294aab8d33.title: Formal Program Correctness Proofs
3b6012ac-a19c-4b47-b601-f3294aab8d33.definition: Use formal methods to prove the correctness of a program, an optional advanced topic.

e6ca1c0c-4edc-4709-8915-c9958192bba5.title: Formal Program Properties Proofs
e6ca1c0c-4edc-4709-8915-c9958192bba5.definition: Use formal methods to demonstrate other properties of the program, an optional advanced topic.

6b9c2e86-b615-441e-9f7a-f7efac729ffc.title: OOP (CS Core)
6b9c2e86-b615-441e-9f7a-f7efac729ffc.definition: Overview of object-oriented programming, including core concepts required for all students.

02f3a306-5c32-41d9-819a-1b7d2b7aba21.title: OOP (KA Core)
02f3a306-5c32-41d9-819a-1b7d2b7aba21.definition: Additional aspects of object-oriented programming, recommended for specialized students.

554f61bc-8d46-4ade-8b04-b836cabb75c0.title: Functional Programming (CS Core)
554f61bc-8d46-4ade-8b04-b836cabb75c0.definition: Basic concepts of functional programming, required for all students.

1dbe6805-6ac3-4ce1-907d-a58b58ed5fcb.title: Functional Programming (KA Core)
1dbe6805-6ac3-4ce1-907d-a58b58ed5fcb.definition: Advanced topics in functional programming, recommended for majors.

936a2bd9-5807-4326-b82a-661cc9f668d0.title: Logic Programming (KA Core)
936a2bd9-5807-4326-b82a-661cc9f668d0.definition: Concepts and applications of logic programming, recommendations for specialized students.

00fd0e22-ce4f-4e1d-80f4-a98dec692b65.title: Shell Scripting (CS Core)
00fd0e22-ce4f-4e1d-80f4-a98dec692b65.definition: Basic knowledge of shell script programming, required for all students.

734fc9a4-aca7-4f3d-bcad-2b5d6ebf4657.title: Event-Reactive Programming (CS Core)
734fc9a4-aca7-4f3d-bcad-2b5d6ebf4657.definition: Basic concepts of event-driven and reactive programming, required for all students.

db0b8cf9-c65c-4f4b-aa19-f4bc1c33b3b1.title: Event-Reactive Programming (KA Core)
db0b8cf9-c65c-4f4b-aa19-f4bc1c33b3b1.definition: Advanced topics in event-driven and reactive programming, recommended for majors.

939b62ca-b72d-48ef-a7f9-82a063325faa.title: Parallel Distributed Computing (CS Core)
939b62ca-b72d-48ef-a7f9-82a063325faa.definition: Basic concepts of parallel and distributed computing, required for all students.

2caa0602-80a2-4771-983a-826ea3cda1d5.title: Parallel Distributed Computing (KA Core)
2caa0602-80a2-4771-983a-826ea3cda1d5.definition: Advanced topics in parallel and distributed computing, recommended for majors.

1cff0dfa-6482-4c77-bd90-7ea51fd7ac24.title: Aspect-Oriented Programming (KA Core)
1cff0dfa-6482-4c77-bd90-7ea51fd7ac24.definition: An introduction to aspect-oriented programming, recommended for majors.

d3ac7b53-808a-47bf-8f06-981b5aedb309.title: Type Systems (CS Core)
