d3ac7b53-808a-47bf-8f06-981b5aedb309.definition: Basic concepts of type systems in programming languages, required for all students.

7c1df2f8-ed41-488f-9769-120e4f3c9135.title: Type Systems (KA Core)
7c1df2f8-ed41-488f-9769-120e4f3c9135.definition: Advanced topics in type systems, recommended for majors.

18d64e1b-14e6-4526-be84-d29d41100afc.title: System Memory Model (KA Core)
18d64e1b-14e6-4526-be84-d29d41100afc.definition: Concepts of how systems execute programs and manage memory, recommended for specialized students.

bfd79460-67d2-463c-84e6-afdbbf9542f6.title: Language Translation Execution (CS Core)
bfd79460-67d2-463c-84e6-afdbbf9542f6.definition: Fundamentals of how programming languages ​​are translated and executed, required for all students.

a922b0fd-001c-4638-921c-5e09eb0a5725.title: Language Translation Execution (KA Core)
a922b0fd-001c-4638-921c-5e09eb0a5725.definition: Advanced topics in language translation and implementation, recommended for majors.

ba79fac3-1deb-4d5b-a383-8e6c2eb35f0e.title: Program Abstraction Representation (KA Core)
ba79fac3-1deb-4d5b-a383-8e6c2eb35f0e.definition: Program abstraction and representation methods, recommendations for specialized students.

64b49e62-8ad8-4725-9ecb-a501c57786e8.title: Syntax Analysis (KA Core)
64b49e62-8ad8-4725-9ecb-a501c57786e8.definition: Parsing techniques in compilers and interpreters.

c05459f2-d620-499e-ba67-681652ebe12a.title: Compiler Semantic Analysis (KA Core)
c05459f2-d620-499e-ba67-681652ebe12a.definition: Semantic analysis methods are used in compilers.

d1f9fb47-3a7f-4a0d-b72c-4e7aea0d8586.title: Program Analysis Tools (KA Core)
d1f9fb47-3a7f-4a0d-b72c-4e7aea0d8586.definition: Techniques and tools for analyzing programs to determine properties and behavior.

95697537-c40f-4845-93e9-4d932d0b206c.title: Code Generation (KA Core)
95697537-c40f-4845-93e9-4d932d0b206c.definition: Methods for generating machine code from high-level source code.

6ea83b48-253e-467e-afd6-d4a283298959.title: Runtime Behavior Systems (KA Core)
6ea83b48-253e-467e-afd6-d4a283298959.definition: understand program behavior during execution and runtime support systems.

fe8e70f0-d906-4c68-a8d3-759f30814453.title: Advanced Programming Constructs (KA Core)
fe8e70f0-d906-4c68-a8d3-759f30814453.definition: Study advanced programming structures and techniques.

e07747d2-dc0c-4506-be45-1fd6cc767372.title: Language Pragmatics (KA Core)
e07747d2-dc0c-4506-be45-1fd6cc767372.definition: The study of how programming languages ​​are used and influence their design and use.

b0a00e9c-7a2e-48b8-a6fe-e739aeefc9ee.title: Formal Semantics (KA Core)
b0a00e9c-7a2e-48b8-a6fe-e739aeefc9ee.definition: Methods for describing the semantics of programming languages ​​formally and accurately.

6f414618-447f-4d50-85a2-f661965a37c6.title: Formal Methods (KA Core)
6f414618-447f-4d50-85a2-f661965a37c6.definition: Math-based software development methods to increase reliability and correctness.

f9ffc7ea-7b96-4eb5-b90e-fa86fbafa065.title: Programming Language Design (KA Core)
f9ffc7ea-7b96-4eb5-b90e-fa86fbafa065.definition: Study the principles and philosophies behind the design of programming languages.

0a055cf6-84c3-4976-821c-39e7608cfbb7.title: Society, Ethics, Professionalism (SEP)
0a055cf6-84c3-4976-821c-39e7608cfbb7.definition: Social, ethical and professional issues related to the field of programming languages ​​are integrated into Social, Ethical and Professional Knowledge (SEP) classes.

5ff0f37c-987d-4345-bb6f-a4f9e3e49f2d.title: Imperative as OOP Subset
5ff0f37c-987d-4345-bb6f-a4f9e3e49f2d.definition: understand imperative programming not as a separate paradigm but as a subset of object-oriented programming.

53b37917-c453-43c8-b0bf-38b7b82e5d94.title: OOP Design: State & Behavior
53b37917-c453-43c8-b0bf-38b7b82e5d94.definition: Object-oriented design techniques, focusing on decomposing the system into objects with state (data) and behavior (methods).

176ef91e-732e-4df6-a8b9-923709fecb84.title: OOP Design: Class Hierarchy
176ef91e-732e-4df6-a8b9-923709fecb84.definition: Object-oriented design technique, focusing on building class hierarchies to model relationships and structures within a system.

ee80e411-8c95-4ac2-b629-734a2d59f39d.title: Class Definition: Fields
ee80e411-8c95-4ac2-b629-734a2d59f39d.definition: How to define fields (member variables) in a class to store the state of an object.

ddca806e-eb0d-450b-96da-8ae610cef6f2.title: Class Definition: Methods
ddca806e-eb0d-450b-96da-8ae610cef6f2.definition: How to define methods (member functions) in a class to define the object's behavior.

fee89dad-01fc-43a3-8a1b-aadb6e5136dd.title: Constructors
fee89dad-01fc-43a3-8a1b-aadb6e5136dd.definition: How to define constructors in a class to initialize objects when they are created.

47da46c8-abb7-4765-a636-b08d7ca19168.title: Subclass
47da46c8-abb7-4765-a636-b08d7ca19168.definition: Concept of subclass, a class that inherits from another class for extension or specialization.

a9595547-6cc8-471b-b342-71f30ec4fcfa.title: Inheritance
a9595547-6cc8-471b-b342-71f30ec4fcfa.definition: The concept of inheritance, allows subclasses to inherit properties and methods from the superclass, including cases of multiple inheritance.

fd0867a4-b3ed-4793-a0ec-3e72d3ee1a4a.title: Multiple Inheritance
fd0867a4-b3ed-4793-a0ec-3e72d3ee1a4a.definition: The concept of multiple inheritance, where a class can inherit from multiple parent classes, and related challenges.

4174010d-8af7-4446-9661-7530cbc0c2f2.title: Method Overriding
4174010d-8af7-4446-9661-7530cbc0c2f2.definition: The concept of method overriding, allows a child class to provide its own implementation of a method already defined in the parent class.

ebb14810-ae53-4c02-9b53-5c08f88221fe.title: Dynamic Dispatch
ebb14810-ae53-4c02-9b53-5c08f88221fe.definition: The concept of dynamic dispatching, the mechanism that determines which methods will be called at runtime based on the type of the object.

d6088fd6-ed75-499f-a266-38c8f9b6885e.title: Exception Handling
d6088fd6-ed75-499f-a266-38c8f9b6885e.definition: Exception handling techniques for robust program management of errors and unusual situations.

a942b7bd-c974-410e-b6b0-cc0851ea493a.title: Encapsulation: Privacy
a942b7bd-c974-410e-b6b0-cc0851ea493a.definition: apply privacy as an object-oriented idiom for encapsulation, controlling access to class members.

422e7c40-555a-4835-822e-9f4c96d422b8.title: Encapsulation: Data Hiding
422e7c40-555a-4835-822e-9f4c96d422b8.definition: apply data hiding as an object-oriented idiom for encapsulation, hiding the internal implementation details of an object.

79a883cd-18e6-4afd-81d3-38a84889497f.title: Encapsulation: Member Visibility
79a883cd-18e6-4afd-81d3-38a84889497f.definition: Controls the visibility of class members (public, private, protected) as part of encapsulation.

8c85c3b0-abed-44f8-9ea5-a121b6ef63ea.title: Encapsulation: Interfaces
8c85c3b0-abed-44f8-9ea5-a121b6ef63ea.definition: Use interfaces as an encapsulation idiom, revealing only the method signature without the implementation.

8c578ff5-36bb-4dbd-bec6-f809d02d98ed.title: Abstract Base Classes
8c578ff5-36bb-4dbd-bec6-f809d02d98ed.definition: Use abstract base classes to define common interfaces that subclasses must implement.

280848e8-67ba-49de-8081-ec5f4e53b9fe.title: Encapsulation: Traits
280848e8-67ba-49de-8081-ec5f4e53b9fe.definition: Use traits as an encapsulation mechanism, allowing reuse of behavior across classes without inheritance.

deaa5c8f-4b2a-4e80-a7d4-559ed5689d46.title: Encapsulation: Mixins
deaa5c8f-4b2a-4e80-a7d4-559ed5689d46.definition: Use mixins as an encapsulation mechanism, allowing classes to combine functionality from multiple sources.

d433fffd-e3c0-47ac-b084-adb00f898160.title: Dynamic vs Static Properties
d433fffd-e3c0-47ac-b084-adb00f898160.definition: Compare and differentiate dynamic and static properties in programming languages, including how they are defined and behave at compile time and run time.

02080cf4-d846-4a46-bf2d-8b400dce2a90.title: Composition vs Inheritance
02080cf4-d846-4a46-bf2d-8b400dce2a90.definition: Compare and contrast object-oriented design paradigms such as composition and inheritance, analyzing the pros and cons of each and when to use each.

14385c74-4fb5-41ae-8523-6e85226f74ba.title: Subtyping Polymorphism
14385c74-4fb5-41ae-8523-6e85226f74ba.definition: Study the basic concept of subtyping in programming languages.

e10043d0-e9a1-4d78-aa05-574a91165d5d.title: Subtyping & Implicit Upcasting
e10043d0-e9a1-4d78-aa05-574a91165d5d.definition: Learn about subtype polymorphism and automatic implicit upcasts in programming languages ​​with type checking.

c253f902-7924-4b70-9256-7b3943baa9b8.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
c253f902-7924-4b70-9256-7b3943baa9b8.definition: understand the principle of behavioral substitution, where a subtype can replace a parent type without changing the correctness of the program (Liskov principle).

73a2be70-5bc6-4ecf-9e1a-de597c26c98d.title: Subtyping & Inheritance Relation
73a2be70-5bc6-4ecf-9e1a-de597c26c98d.definition: analyze the complex relationship between the concept of subtyping and inheritance in object-oriented design.

0aec1c4f-ccd1-4691-8ce6-2f0087afabf8.title: Collections, Iterators & Libraries
0aec1c4f-ccd1-4691-8ce6-2f0087afabf8.definition: Learn about data collection classes (e.g., lists, sets, maps), iterators, and other standard library components in programming languages.

101f9a19-0ba8-4772-a432-53954a1ef741.title: Metaprogramming & Reflection
101f9a19-0ba8-4772-a432-53954a1ef741.definition: The study of metaprogramming, which allows a program to manipulate itself, and reflection, the ability to examine and modify a program's structure and behavior at runtime.

45fc5488-dd46-4309-a271-d34c30e18aee.title: Imperative vs OOP
45fc5488-dd46-4309-a271-d34c30e18aee.definition: List and explain the basic differences between the imperative programming model and the object-oriented programming model.

65735aae-73e7-4602-9344-ee32e018e733.title: Class Design, Implement, Test
65735aae-73e7-4602-9344-ee32e018e733.definition: The process of designing, implementing, and testing a class to meet specific behavioral requirements.

b60c7db1-b474-4e4d-96d9-d5f6ab0120bf.title: Class Hierarchy & Code Reuse
b60c7db1-b474-4e4d-96d9-d5f6ab0120bf.definition: Build a simple class hierarchy using the subclassing mechanism for efficient code reuse across different subclasses.

9d181c98-52f3-40ff-bffb-665ca86d0aa3.title: Dynamic Dispatch & Control Flow
9d181c98-52f3-40ff-bffb-665ca86d0aa3.definition: Predict and verify the flow of control in programs using dynamic dispatch.

b272060c-c26e-4635-9bdb-eddf85731bbf.title: Procedural vs Functional vs OOP
b272060c-c26e-4635-9bdb-eddf85731bbf.definition: Compare and contrast how computational solutions to a problem differ in procedural, functional, and object-oriented approaches.

b598e86c-a900-4a63-af53-9225368dc1be.title: Data Definition & Protection
b598e86c-a900-4a63-af53-9225368dc1be.definition: Compare and contrast mechanisms for defining and protecting data elements in procedural, functional, and object-oriented approaches.

cb388559-858d-44b8-9f46-1fa0ca3d062b.title: Inheritance vs Composition Costs
cb388559-858d-44b8-9f46-1fa0ca3d062b.definition: Compare and contrast the benefits and costs/impacts of using inheritance (subclassing) and composition (especially how to build components based on higher-order functions).

b428dff3-2199-4d46-9c27-2f35a8188a97.title: OOP Inheritance & Subtyping Relation
b428dff3-2199-4d46-9c27-2f35a8188a97.definition: Explain the relationship between object-oriented inheritance (code sharing and overriding) and subtype polymorphism (the idea of ​​a subtype being usable in a context that expects the parent type).

6620d193-dcb4-452b-a286-6d5f9b847c74.title: OOP Encapsulation Mechanisms
6620d193-dcb4-452b-a286-6d5f9b847c74.definition: Use object-oriented encapsulation mechanisms such as interfaces and private members.

bfd89e47-eb11-4bf3-ac7e-9a9d75f99669.title: Iterators & Collection Operations
bfd89e47-eb11-4bf3-ac7e-9a9d75f99669.definition: Define and use iterators and other operations on aggregates, including operations that take functions as arguments, in a variety of programming languages, choosing the most natural expressions for each language.

4d87bd33-3bd4-48b2-80d0-25cadb272d17.title: Efficient Collections & Iterators
4d87bd33-3bd4-48b2-80d0-25cadb272d17.definition: Effectively use collection classes and iterators to solve a problem.

a9345685-8866-4d8b-9348-6fba2af90114.title: Lambda Expressions & Evaluation
a9345685-8866-4d8b-9348-6fba2af90114.definition: understand lambda expressions (anonymous functions) and how they are evaluated in functional programming.

3401cf5b-c366-4111-afb3-55d531203096.title: Lambda Variable Binding & Scope
3401cf5b-c366-4111-afb3-55d531203096.definition: Master the variable binding and scope rules that apply to lambda expressions.

d3d8f4c0-45ce-4f41-95a7-8382179833b2.title: Lambda Parameter Passing
d3d8f4c0-45ce-4f41-95a7-8382179833b2.definition: understand the mechanics of passing parameters when using lambda expressions.

f42a5d11-d107-4432-93d4-23f72a7c5dc2.title: Nested Lambda & Reduction Order
f42a5d11-d107-4432-93d4-23f72a7c5dc2.definition: analyze nested lambda expressions and their reduction order.

6e2c9186-d896-4f5c-96b3-d21241bf9505.title: Side-Effect Free Programming
6e2c9186-d896-4f5c-96b3-d21241bf9505.definition: The concept of side-effect free programming, where functions depend only on their inputs and do not cause changes in external state.

c07a94a2-67bb-4b6c-804f-4226930f0962.title: Pure Functions & Compositional Reasoning
c07a94a2-67bb-4b6c-804f-4226930f0962.definition: Understanding that function calls have no side effects facilitates compositional reasoning.

efecd8ba-dca5-4e09-af3a-e55b677885f8.title: Immutable Variables & Data Copying
efecd8ba-dca5-4e09-af3a-e55b677885f8.definition: Study the concept of immutable variables and compare data copying and reduction in functional programming.

87cebd2e-29f0-4e91-95da-7091dbf56ba9.title: Recursion vs Loops vs Map/Reduce
87cebd2e-29f0-4e91-95da-7091dbf56ba9.definition: Compare and apply recursion, loops, and pipelining techniques such as map/reduce to solve problems.

4b7ca56f-cabd-4b49-9ee5-64795ecf5360.title: Structured Data Processing (FP)
4b7ca56f-cabd-4b49-9ee5-64795ecf5360.definition: Master how to handle complex data structures like trees by defining functions with appropriate cases for each variant or node of data, a fundamental technique in functional programming.

9d94e8c4-9f3d-4079-96c7-d481b203ef5a.title: Composite Data Functions
9d94e8c4-9f3d-4079-96c7-d481b203ef5a.definition: understand and apply function design principles to complex data, in which large functions are built upon applying smaller functions to each constituent element of the data.

c05e5f61-765b-4191-8f44-4cfe016cb555.title: Persistent Data Structures
c05e5f61-765b-4191-8f44-4cfe016cb555.definition: Learn about immutable data structures, where every modification creates a new version of the structure without changing the original version, ensuring persistence and easy state management.

45cca097-e2e3-47ca-964a-73d81bc9ddac.title: Higher-Order Functions
45cca097-e2e3-47ca-964a-73d81bc9ddac.definition: Master the concept and use of higher-order functions – functions that can take other functions as arguments, return a function, or store functions – to write flexible and abstract code.

0871e15b-3f0c-4a39-b3ff-d858098393e6.title: Metaprogramming
0871e15b-3f0c-4a39-b3ff-d858098393e6.definition: Learn about metaprogramming, a programming technique in which a program has the ability to manipulate (analyze, modify, create) other programs or itself during runtime or compilation.

0da0333d-6381-4ce7-81b2-ca4b1e8ed90a.title: Reflection
0da0333d-6381-4ce7-81b2-ca4b1e8ed90a.definition: Master the concept of reflection, the ability of a program to inspect, introspect, and modify its own structure and behavior at runtime.

d520010b-aa93-4ea7-b860-2959406c5668.title: Function Closures
d520010b-aa93-4ea7-b860-2959406c5668.definition: Understanding function closure, a function is 'encapsulated' along with its lexical reference environment, allowing the function to access variables from an external scope even when that scope is no longer active.

02571bfd-7f78-4c92-a23b-9ae54211b5ba.title: Closure Creation at Runtime
02571bfd-7f78-4c92-a23b-9ae54211b5ba.definition: understand how function closures are created at runtime by 'capturing' the environment from its declared scope.

2f260e69-544f-4e70-82af-efd457a93ab9.title: Closures: Callbacks
2f260e69-544f-4e70-82af-efd457a93ab9.definition: apply function closure in common use cases such as call-backs, where a function is passed as an argument to be executed later by another function.

02b243bc-cc33-43bc-bfe8-00974b95e594.title: Closure Idioms: Iterators
02b243bc-cc33-43bc-bfe8-00974b95e594.definition: Use function closures as arguments to iterators or collection traversals to customize the behavior of each element.

3cb07895-d2c4-4a0a-b9df-c763af06f108.title: Closure Idioms: Reusable Code
3cb07895-d2c4-4a0a-b9df-c763af06f108.definition: Develop reusable code patterns by passing functions (or closures) as arguments, allowing flexibility in behavior without modifying the main structure.

cb9b6661-b911-4b63-b290-6f91553b9f36.title: Closure Data Encapsulation
cb9b6661-b911-4b63-b290-6f91553b9f36.definition: apply function closure as a mechanism to encapsulate data, where the data is kept private within the closure's environment and can only be accessed and manipulated through that closure function.

4756422a-a1d7-4229-8e45-289cbe46864f.title: Lazy Evaluation
4756422a-a1d7-4229-8e45-289cbe46864f.definition: understand delayed evaluation, an evaluation strategy in which execution of an expression is postponed until its value is actually needed, which optimizes performance and allows processing of an infinite stream of data.

19302bc0-170a-4a04-9833-76c79ca9b684.title: Eager Evaluation
19302bc0-170a-4a04-9833-76c79ca9b684.definition: understand strict evaluation, an evaluation strategy in which expressions are evaluated immediately when they are assigned or passed as arguments.

0b9ba532-4813-4953-8ebb-da5fae94f05c.title: Graph Reduction Machine
0b9ba532-4813-4953-8ebb-da5fae94f05c.definition: Learn about graph reducers, an execution model for functional programming languages, especially those that use deferred evaluation, where expressions are represented as graphs and reduced as needed.

b764565b-6b87-4f82-bf24-aeff44a3735b.title: Call-by-Need
b764565b-6b87-4f82-bf24-aeff44a3735b.definition: Master the concept of call-by-need, an argument passing strategy that combines call-by-name and call-by-value, where the argument is evaluated no more than once as needed and the result is cached.

48457704-6ad7-4ecf-bdcc-9bb9d30b4a30.title: Lazy Evaluation Implementation
48457704-6ad7-4ecf-bdcc-9bb9d30b4a30.definition: Learn and implement techniques for implementing deferred evaluation mechanisms in systems or programming languages.

3939ca8a-e15d-4413-8452-e7b468b26cec.title: Logic Programming Integration
3939ca8a-e15d-4413-8452-e7b468b26cec.definition: Explore how functional programming concepts and techniques can be integrated or interacted with the logic programming model to create hybrid programming languages ​​and systems.

5943d0b6-849f-4c29-96b6-212581a267bb.title: Equational Logic
5943d0b6-849f-4c29-96b6-212581a267bb.definition: Master the concept of equational logic, a system of logic based on solving equations and the principle of substituting equals, commonly used in functional-logic programming and rewriting theory.

eccce77a-b9b7-4c85-a44c-47b19f240aff.title: Narrowing
eccce77a-b9b7-4c85-a44c-47b19f240aff.definition: Learn about narrowing, a powerful combination of evaluation and unification used in functional logic programming to find solutions.

77f0a794-e540-4fb4-8f50-0def2271c492.title: Residuation
77f0a794-e540-4fb4-8f50-0def2271c492.definition: understand the concept of residuation, a mechanism in functional-logic programming that allows calculations to be delayed until enough information is available to perform them without looking up.

34ab1fc2-46e9-473c-b471-0d7fe12c109a.title: Semantic Unification
34ab1fc2-46e9-473c-b471-0d7fe12c109a.definition: Understanding semantic unification, an extension of traditional unification, considers the meaning or semantics of expressions in addition to their syntactic structure.

cbed89a1-45c0-4f24-9d97-c488db2c2464.title: Imperative Integration
cbed89a1-45c0-4f24-9d97-c488db2c2464.definition: Study how functional programming concepts and techniques can be integrated or interacted with the traditional imperative programming paradigm, creating hybrid programming approaches.

3f5b4ec5-d91a-4173-9bf6-35e1e0275ebf.title: OOP Integration
3f5b4ec5-d91a-4173-9bf6-35e1e0275ebf.definition: Explore how functional programming concepts can be integrated or interacted with the object-oriented programming paradigm, for example in API design or software architecture.

4f6a752b-1215-4847-af47-9f26882d9bba.title: Immutable State Algorithms
4f6a752b-1215-4847-af47-9f26882d9bba.definition: Skills in designing and implementing basic algorithms that comply with the principle of immutability in functional programming, avoiding directly changing the state of variable variables to minimize errors and increase predictability.

b52ff924-ed94-4f12-be88-a84ce4a7e92a.title: Value Equality Algorithms
b52ff924-ed94-4f12-be88-a84ce4a7e92a.definition: Skills in designing and implementing algorithms that focus on value equality rather than reference equality are especially important in functional programming and with immutable data.

c65b280e-215d-4fdb-ada0-67fa2fb9facf.title: Higher-Order Functions
c65b280e-215d-4fdb-ada0-67fa2fb9facf.definition: Skill in writing high-order functions that take other functions as arguments or return other functions as results, taking advantage of the flexibility and code reuse in functional programming.

f6c2244b-ce10-49ef-aa96-20e1ae3d6dc2.title: Paradigm Problem Solving
f6c2244b-ce10-49ef-aa96-20e1ae3d6dc2.definition: analyze and compare how different programming paradigms (procedural, functional, object-oriented) approach, structure, and solve the same computational problem, including the advantages and disadvantages of each.

46976eba-ca5d-4cf7-adab-d0450c657423.title: Data Protection Paradigms
46976eba-ca5d-4cf7-adab-d0450c657423.definition: analyze and compare different methods for defining and protecting data (e.g., encapsulation, immutability, scope) in procedural, functional, and object-oriented programming paradigms.

c4e4c000-3ca6-459a-8a6d-c3458a733ba3.title: Lambda SECD Machine
c4e4c000-3ca6-459a-8a6d-c3458a733ba3.definition: Able to explain in detail how a simple lambda expression is deployed and executed on an abstract virtual machine such as a SECD machine, illustrating the process of storing and reclaiming the environment.

2d4033b3-8665-46e4-a53f-764497a8113b.title: SECD Machine
2d4033b3-8665-46e4-a53f-764497a8113b.definition: Learn about the architecture and operation of the SECD (Stack, Environment, Control, Dump) machine, a classic abstract virtual machine used to execute lambda expressions and functional programming languages.

a8ff0b57-3737-4e06-9d73-e36d17aec4f1.title: VM Environment Management
a8ff0b57-3737-4e06-9d73-e36d17aec4f1.definition: understand the technical mechanisms for storing and managing (including revoking) execution environments in the context of virtual machines, especially with regard to closures and lexical scoping.

464e2717-c25c-46a0-9805-b6e9f7aa4e89.title: Closure Scope & Variables
464e2717-c25c-46a0-9805-b6e9f7aa4e89.definition: Ability to properly analyze and understand how variables and lexical scope operate in programs that use function closures, including accessing variables from the outside environment.

f1f396e7-b936-4417-b405-768e6c313099.title: Functional Encapsulation
f1f396e7-b936-4417-b405-768e6c313099.definition: apply encapsulation mechanisms in functional programming, including closures to protect internal state and modular interfaces to organize and hide implementation details.

5067544b-d7d7-4918-8063-8f9085d8e0fd.title: Functional Modular Interface
5067544b-d7d7-4918-8063-8f9085d8e0fd.definition: Master how to design and use modular interfaces to organize and manage code components in a functional programming context, promoting modularity and reusability.

06c7456c-f4cf-4d27-ad61-cd24a4bb868f.title: Stateful vs Stateless Execution
06c7456c-f4cf-4d27-ad61-cd24a4bb868f.definition: Distinguish and compare the differences between stateful and stateless execution models, especially emphasizing the advantages and disadvantages of each model in functional programming and system architectures.

0757e621-7024-4f96-a6e9-ea5f095f458d.title: Stateful Execution
0757e621-7024-4f96-a6e9-ea5f095f458d.definition: understand the stateful execution model, where functions or components can maintain and modify internal state between calls, affecting output.

1607b205-714f-4acc-bd5e-99bd521c0a23.title: Stateless Execution
1607b205-714f-4acc-bd5e-99bd521c0a23.definition: Understanding the stateless execution model, where functions or components do not store any internal state and always return the same output for the same input, makes it easy to test and parallelize.

40a53ef9-6b0e-413c-874f-367c2ac8c5f9.title: Iterators Definition & Usage
40a53ef9-6b0e-413c-874f-367c2ac8c5f9.definition: Skill in defining and using iterators to efficiently and flexibly traverse data sets, often in a functional programming context.

24957eeb-6fe5-4d34-a6fa-c6f4849ce9d5.title: Aggregate Operations
24957eeb-6fe5-4d34-a6fa-c6f4849ce9d5.definition: Skills in defining and using common operations on data sets such as filter, map, reduce, and other operations.

2db1ddfa-e320-4816-afdb-72729b0bc123.title: Higher-Order Aggregate Operations
2db1ddfa-e320-4816-afdb-72729b0bc123.definition: apply operations on collections (e.g. map, filter, reduce) that themselves take other functions as arguments, allowing flexible customization of data processing behavior.

1a83f316-37e4-40d4-9693-94b5215ea934.title: Iterator & Aggregate Idioms
1a83f316-37e4-40d4-9693-94b5215ea934.definition: Select and use the most natural and effective idioms in different programming languages ​​for working with iterators and set operations, optimizing readability and performance.

0a8134c8-2165-4ee0-aac9-769da9c47adb.title: Common Subexpression Graph Reduction
0a8134c8-2165-4ee0-aac9-769da9c47adb.definition: Ability to illustrate in detail the graph reduction process when executing a lambda expression, especially when common subexpressions are present, to understand how to optimize execution in functional languages.

be60bb5e-c65b-41d4-bdab-1656e4ad5137.title: Lambda Common Subexpressions
be60bb5e-c65b-41d4-bdab-1656e4ad5137.definition: understand the concept and impact of common subexpressions in lambda expressions, and how they can be leveraged to improve performance through techniques such as graph reduction.

f4e2e5bb-65d9-4444-9911-e9e4cf74748c.title: Nested Lambda ABC Machine
f4e2e5bb-65d9-4444-9911-e9e4cf74748c.definition: Ability to illustrate the execution of a simple nested lambda expression on an abstract machine like the ABC machine, understanding how levels of nesting are handled.

c6d37c51-e274-4756-95ad-1636f0a7d065.title: ABC Machine
c6d37c51-e274-4756-95ad-1636f0a7d065.definition: Learn about the architecture and operation of the ABC machine, an abstract machine designed to execute functional programming languages, especially in the context of lazy evaluation and general data structures.

f42a3327-2098-4061-a8a9-08a21c4f7502.title: Narrowing, Residuation, Semantic Unification Examples
f42a3327-2098-4061-a8a9-08a21c4f7502.definition: Ability to give and explain simple examples to illustrate complex concepts such as narrowing, residuation, and semantic unification, clarifying how they work in functional-logic programming.

e35ed67b-d29d-433b-97dd-ba9389ebd887.title: Concurrency Structures Examples
e35ed67b-d29d-433b-97dd-ba9389ebd887.definition: Illustrate concurrency constructs with simple programming examples, such as reading and writing to a buffer simultaneously or sequentially.

30edc5ae-25ea-40bf-b6d1-64f0d7865bfb.title: Universal & Existential Quantifiers
30edc5ae-25ea-40bf-b6d1-64f0d7865bfb.definition: Compare and distinguish between universal quantifiers and existential quantifiers in predicate logic.

102eba68-58df-454b-a024-03333fcf1fd0.title: First & Higher-Order Logic
102eba68-58df-454b-a024-03333fcf1fd0.definition: Distinguish between First Order Predicate Logic, which only quantifies variables, and Higher Order Logic, which can quantify predicates or functions.

e171b789-065a-4d9c-adcd-2e07fe0c9b8e.title: Complex Relations with Logic Connectives
e171b789-065a-4d9c-adcd-2e07fe0c9b8e.definition: Skills in using logical connections (AND, OR, NOT, IF-THEN) to build complex relationships from basic relationships.

bf43adeb-f054-4dc2-a2c7-000458d72335.title: Horn Clauses, Facts, Goals
bf43adeb-f054-4dc2-a2c7-000458d72335.definition: understand the definitions and roles of Horn clauses, facts, goals and subgoals in logic programming.

a67b62f5-0a25-4471-a7d2-360d1dc3488c.title: Unification & Algorithm
a67b62f5-0a25-4471-a7d2-360d1dc3488c.definition: The concept of unification and its algorithm, along with the distinction between unification, assertion, and expression evaluation in the context of logic programming.

3bf6a890-0b89-4cdf-b828-4763147f063c.title: Relations & Functions Mixing
3bf6a890-0b89-4cdf-b828-4763147f063c.definition: How to use a combination of relations and functions in logic programming to represent more complex problems.

51899b09-dbae-40a7-a848-506df1c48dca.title: Cuts, Backtracking, Nondeterminism
51899b09-dbae-40a7-a848-506df1c48dca.definition: Concept of cuts to control the search process, backtracking mechanism and non-determinism in logic programs.

3b2539c2-8646-4130-a577-cb95302382d8.title: Closed & Open World Assumption
3b2539c2-8646-4130-a577-cb95302382d8.definition: Distinguish between closed-world assumptions (what is not known is false) and open-world assumptions (what is not known may be true or false).

93734542-5ad5-402f-adbc-77b37d9f8e2f.title: Loop Variable Copy Cost
93734542-5ad5-402f-adbc-77b37d9f8e2f.definition: analyze the memory overhead incurred by variable copying in iterative programs, especially in the context of logic programming.

f1d40310-0a69-4ab1-8d6a-d489538a865b.title: Partial Computation & Search Pruning
f1d40310-0a69-4ab1-8d6a-d489538a865b.definition: Programming techniques and structures allow storing intermediate computational results and pruning unnecessary branches in the search tree to optimize performance.

14c366dd-19ed-4a93-9128-73fa53a46e9c.title: Functional-Logic Integration
14c366dd-19ed-4a93-9128-73fa53a46e9c.definition: Explore how to integrate the functional and logic programming paradigms through in-depth concepts such as equational logic, narrowing, residuation, and semantic unification.

08730687-d346-4316-be8b-24acaea9a777.title: Advanced Logic Programming
08730687-d346-4316-be8b-24acaea9a777.definition: Introduces advanced areas of logic programming, including higher-order logic programming, constrained logic programming, and inductive logic programming.

6c894345-6ac2-4980-93a7-cd98408c2920.title: Logic Prog. Integration
6c894345-6ac2-4980-93a7-cd98408c2920.definition: Methods and challenges when integrating logic programming with other popular programming paradigms, such as object-oriented programming.

3aa5031c-2f48-4d0f-966d-4f8cd57c03a9.title: Advanced Logic Structures
3aa5031c-2f48-4d0f-966d-4f8cd57c03a9.definition: Learn advanced programming constructs in programming logic such as difference-lists, how to create custom data structures, and aggregation operators.

9813cd45-8e66-4453-8660-e9b87a4ceb0d.title: Error Handling
9813cd45-8e66-4453-8660-e9b87a4ceb0d.definition: Error and exception handling techniques and methods in shell scripts to ensure stable and reliable program operation.

eaa13bf2-a383-4663-b384-0c5636ea142d.title: Piping
eaa13bf2-a383-4663-b384-0c5636ea142d.definition: Concept and usage of pipes to connect the output of one command to the input of another command in the shell.

97a3537f-97d8-4079-9582-ae7644675840.title: System Commands
97a3537f-97d8-4079-9582-ae7644675840.definition: Knowledge of basic system commands and their use in shell scripts.

7efff7e1-ee27-4b15-81dd-5bfef8ada8ad.title: OS Interaction
7efff7e1-ee27-4b15-81dd-5bfef8ada8ad.definition: How shell scripts interact with and control operating system functions through commands and system calls.

0b131d53-5237-43f2-a3ab-d19c63276d11.title: Environment Variables
0b131d53-5237-43f2-a3ab-d19c63276d11.definition: Concepts, how to set, access and use environment variables in shell scripting.

71d048dc-6c17-4d86-a0ef-5764a4557083.title: File Abstraction & Ops
71d048dc-6c17-4d86-a0ef-5764a4557083.definition: How shell scripts handle and manipulate files is through file abstraction concepts and related operators (e.g. read, write, check for existence).

0ff77fe0-f595-4da2-8708-c70966a610d3.title: Shell Data Structures
0ff77fe0-f595-4da2-8708-c70966a610d3.definition: Use basic data structures such as arrays and lists in shell scripting to organize and manage data.

fd4817a8-95ca-410e-8831-3c4d7e60f4fe.title: Regular Expressions
fd4817a8-95ca-410e-8831-3c4d7e60f4fe.definition: understand and use regular expressions to search, match, and manipulate text in shell scripts.

40809e86-6cc8-4c5b-a371-8a9a9eeee067.title: Programs & Processes
40809e86-6cc8-4c5b-a371-8a9a9eeee067.definition: Concept of programs and processes in the operating system environment, and how shell scripts manage or interact with them.

c9068fd0-d66b-42ef-a6fc-0c9a126933ff.title: Workflow Automation
c9068fd0-d66b-42ef-a6fc-0c9a126933ff.definition: Design and automate task sequences or workflows using shell scripts.

c565cae2-8147-4fee-8f11-88eb63859772.title: Reactive Programming Advantages
c565cae2-8147-4fee-8f11-88eb63859772.definition: Compare procedural and reactive programming paradigms, emphasizing the advantages of reactive programming in handling and responding to events.

f5cc1f5e-c0c6-4240-a904-ccfaa79c52d6.title: Reactive Components
f5cc1f5e-c0c6-4240-a904-ccfaa79c52d6.definition: understand the components that make up a reactive programming system, including event sources, signals, listeners, dispatchers, event objects, adapters, and event handlers.

03aa3fb4-6fd8-4795-a087-5707a96dc122.title: Stateless vs. State-Transition
03aa3fb4-6fd8-4795-a087-5707a96dc122.definition: Distinguish between stateless and state-transition programming models.

b8439a8d-89b9-44b9-92dd-82dc7ffaad72.title: Reactive Use Cases
b8439a8d-89b9-44b9-92dd-82dc7ffaad72.definition: Identify common and typical applications of event-driven and reactive programming in areas such as graphical user interfaces (GUIs), mobile devices, robotics, and servers.

26d939ca-2efa-40c3-a266-9b7d0613a173.title: Event Handlers & Listeners
26d939ca-2efa-40c3-a266-9b7d0613a173.definition: Skills in defining and implementing event handlers or listeners in a reactive programming framework.

6e069490-ab37-4581-a6d8-8a96d2fd87f2.title: Event Parameterization
6e069490-ab37-4581-a6d8-8a96d2fd87f2.definition: How to parameterize event dispatchers and the arguments (data) associated with the event to pass information.

8e01d24e-cdbe-437f-8c67-593cc920b499.title: External vs. Internal Events
8e01d24e-cdbe-437f-8c67-593cc920b499.definition: Distinguish and handle events that arise from outside the system (e.g., user interactions) and events that are generated internally by the program.

e60fbceb-372b-43d9-8d6c-228fb2580269.title: MVC Separation
e60fbceb-372b-43d9-8d6c-228fb2580269.definition: understand and apply the principle of separation of Model, View, and Controller components in event-driven application design.

cefce932-b6be-4695-9422-9c40f040c2f6.title: Event-Driven State Machines
cefce932-b6be-4695-9422-9c40f040c2f6.definition: Conceptualize event-driven and reactive programs as state transition systems, where events trigger state changes.

b632471b-cf32-4747-b8f8-dcbbedd54434.title: MVC Architecture
b632471b-cf32-4747-b8f8-dcbbedd54434.definition: Ability to describe an interactive system using a Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture, clearly distinguishing data model (Model), user interface (View), and control logic (Controller) components.

2552cee9-b26c-4f9f-a73a-90201c89a67c.title: Safety & Liveness
2552cee9-b26c-4f9f-a73a-90201c89a67c.definition: Basic concepts of safety and liveness in parallel and distributed computing, ensuring programs execute correctly and can progress.

3d7e969d-47cf-493d-ac26-d85d2ae5e88f.title: Race Conditions
3d7e969d-47cf-493d-ac26-d85d2ae5e88f.definition: Definition and examples of race conditions in parallel programs, where multiple threads access and change shared data without proper synchronization.

7eba0520-7575-46e7-a0d5-a08271588a28.title: Dependencies & Preconditions
7eba0520-7575-46e7-a0d5-a08271588a28.definition: Understanding of data dependencies and preconditions in parallel tasks, necessary to ensure correctness and order of execution.

5571ceb3-c9dc-4f22-bdb7-282ed28498af.title: Fault Models
5571ceb3-c9dc-4f22-bdb7-282ed28498af.definition: Models to classify and analyze the types of errors that can occur in parallel and distributed systems, e.g. node failures, network failures.

0666deb3-c45f-437a-bf71-d89f201f1c3b.title: Parallel Termination
0666deb3-c45f-437a-bf71-d89f201f1c3b.definition: The concept of termination of parallel programs or tasks, ensuring that all components have completed their work and the system has reached its final state.

bf6998de-2d9b-44f5-b6db-cf582b597899.title: Parallel Programming Models
bf6998de-2d9b-44f5-b6db-cf582b597899.definition: Different methods and frameworks for designing and implementing parallel and distributed programs.

6a94f8d5-e2b9-4979-bb66-77060ce1ef31.title: Actor Model
6a94f8d5-e2b9-4979-bb66-77060ce1ef31.definition: The parallel programming model is based on Actors, independent computational units that communicate by exchanging messages.

59af4eac-3f89-4d5a-9545-86ddf880dd3e.title: Procedural vs. Reactive
59af4eac-3f89-4d5a-9545-86ddf880dd3e.definition: Compare and differentiate between traditional procedural programming paradigms and reactive programming paradigms in a parallel context.

a89f2f8d-f646-42f7-b1e6-a21d9200fa68.title: Synchronous vs. Asynchronous
a89f2f8d-f646-42f7-b1e6-a21d9200fa68.definition: understand the differences and applications of synchronous and asynchronous programming models in managing parallel tasks.

90b58ea4-c871-4879-a7fe-2d007162a75a.title: Data Parallelism
90b58ea4-c871-4879-a7fe-2d007162a75a.definition: Data parallelism technique, where the same operation is applied simultaneously to different elements of a large data set.

fc09a865-714b-43f9-a5e3-c03f7a764498.title: Concurrency Properties
fc09a865-714b-43f9-a5e3-c03f7a764498.definition: Important properties of parallel systems relate to the ordering and consistency of data.

0e444f04-ec01-4a4a-880b-909046de6ccc.title: Order-Based Properties
0e444f04-ec01-4a4a-880b-909046de6ccc.definition: Properties related to the execution order of operations in a parallel environment.

b3055b18-e54a-4147-99c4-ab0b4cdd15ad.title: Commutativity
b3055b18-e54a-4147-99c4-ab0b4cdd15ad.definition: The property of operations that their order of execution does not affect the final result.

91b1d1fb-761e-4da8-a102-41b8f6f3df40.title: Operation Independence
91b1d1fb-761e-4da8-a102-41b8f6f3df40.definition: The property of operations is not dependent on each other and can be performed in parallel without affecting each other.

8836e86b-cc5b-47f3-b8e1-feadb0741994.title: Consistency Properties
8836e86b-cc5b-47f3-b8e1-feadb0741994.definition: Attributes that ensure data consistency in a parallel or distributed system.

2a1093e6-624e-4a9e-9973-2eac4911eb18.title: Atomicity
2a1093e6-624e-4a9e-9973-2eac4911eb18.definition: The concept of atomicity, ensures that a set of operations is performed completely or not at all.

637735ce-0c63-4f08-857e-556d9351e7bf.title: Consensus
637735ce-0c63-4f08-857e-556d9351e7bf.definition: The concept of consensus in a distributed system, where processes must reach a common agreement on a value or state.

e2d12d9c-179a-4077-aaa3-5a60fb90f97b.title: Parallel Execution Control
e2d12d9c-179a-4077-aaa3-5a60fb90f97b.definition: Mechanisms and techniques to control the execution flow of parallel tasks.

3407ea68-4987-4045-b65d-6c1f5d9080d3.title: Async/Await
3407ea68-4987-4045-b65d-6c1f5d9080d3.definition: The asynchronous programming model uses the `async` and `await` keywords to manage non-blocking operations.

116679d6-9b6a-4123-84e4-5211c67bd4bf.title: Promises
116679d6-9b6a-4123-84e4-5211c67bd4bf.definition: Concept of Promises as an object that represents the final result of an asynchronous operation.

cca898ad-01cc-4444-ac2d-ac4e489f4869.title: Threads
cca898ad-01cc-4444-ac2d-ac4e489f4869.definition: Thread mechanism to execute different parts of the program simultaneously, serving the purpose of execution control.

3b72714c-f35a-4b87-be6d-6f6d1d5935c9.title: Parallel Communication
3b72714c-f35a-4b87-be6d-6f6d1d5935c9.definition: Methods and tools for parallel components to communicate and work together.

654bcae9-8585-4cc6-9a68-1c3e4b5462eb.title: Mutex
654bcae9-8585-4cc6-9a68-1c3e4b5462eb.definition: Mutual exclusion locking mechanism (mutex) to protect shared resources from concurrent access.

79aa0fbc-5e21-470a-bbe8-f9839e3c3e0a.title: Message Passing
79aa0fbc-5e21-470a-bbe8-f9839e3c3e0a.definition: Models communication between processes or threads through message exchange instead of memory sharing.

9a09271e-0d4f-4d69-93cb-4e4c6b2a8750.title: Shared Memory
9a09271e-0d4f-4d69-93cb-4e4c6b2a8750.definition: Communication model where processes or threads access and modify the same memory region.

93ba5330-9ad8-405d-82df-8f6dcef6c6e2.title: Cobegin-coend
93ba5330-9ad8-405d-82df-8f6dcef6c6e2.definition: Language construct for specifying a block of instructions that can be executed in parallel, starting with `cobegin` and ending with `coend`.

105b4451-545b-4979-91d8-c3eadbff27c0.title: Monitor
105b4451-545b-4979-91d8-c3eadbff27c0.definition: A high-level synchronization mechanism allows threads to securely access shared resources through protected methods.

6d4632fa-f624-4b6d-aab1-def255d60793.title: Channels
6d4632fa-f624-4b6d-aab1-def255d60793.definition: The communication mechanism allows threads or goroutines to send and receive data securely.

3aa28bc5-49fc-4ccd-8933-110814358463.title: Threads
3aa28bc5-49fc-4ccd-8933-110814358463.definition: Use a thread as a unit of execution for communication and coordination purposes in a parallel program.

24ae2584-4241-441c-9c8d-b4e3ddb252a2.title: Guards
24ae2584-4241-441c-9c8d-b4e3ddb252a2.definition: Guards are used to control the execution of sections of code based on the state of the system in a concurrent environment.

149d3b6c-7ca9-49f7-891e-53d208de0aa7.title: Futures
149d3b6c-7ca9-49f7-891e-53d208de0aa7.definition: The concept of Futures is an object that represents a value that will be available in the future, usually as a result of an asynchronous calculation.

b447b91b-56f8-4797-8d88-e2d45ff022d0.title: Data Parallelism Support
b447b91b-56f8-4797-8d88-e2d45ff022d0.definition: Language features and programming constructs that support data parallelism, including examples such as `forall`, loop unrolling techniques, and paradigms such as Map/Reduce.

3b52209e-b8c1-4ec1-99ce-be599f611cbf.title: Memory Consistency Effects
3b52209e-b8c1-4ec1-99ce-be599f611cbf.definition: Understanding of how memory-consistency models affect programming language semantics and correct code generation in multiprocessor systems.

c47b9903-4633-4ace-8e3d-f04f37ee6976.title: REST APIs
c47b9903-4633-4ace-8e3d-f04f37ee6976.definition: Architecture and principles of Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interfaces (REST APIs) for communication between distributed systems.

3408f582-a227-49b5-841d-ec5bbcf1404d.title: Parallel & Distributed Computing
3408f582-a227-49b5-841d-ec5bbcf1404d.definition: Overview of advanced technologies and approaches in parallel and distributed computing, including cloud computing, high performance computing (HPC), quantum computing, and ubiquitous computing.

5a82fce0-8216-46b5-bb3e-01d73aa9451f.title: Message Passing Overhead
5a82fce0-8216-46b5-bb3e-01d73aa9451f.definition: analyze the performance costs (such as latency, bandwidth) associated with message passing mechanisms in distributed systems.

21826e82-979e-4eb0-8312-89c8d0e4083f.title: Concurrency Granularity
21826e82-979e-4eb0-8312-89c8d0e4083f.definition: understand the importance of choosing the right granularity for concurrent tasks to optimize performance and exploit resources efficiently.

8551bd25-a47b-4472-8c75-bd240130d3ff.title: Concurrency & Other Paradigms
8551bd25-a47b-4472-8c75-bd240130d3ff.definition: The relationship and integration between concurrency and other programming paradigms, such as functional programming.

2de6abd1-6800-479d-9702-29e885186f42.title: Aspects
2de6abd1-6800-479d-9702-29e885186f42.definition: Definition of aspect in aspect-oriented programming (AOP), representing cross-cutting concerns.

c839f659-6693-4779-a0fb-60d360dfff8f.title: Join Points
c839f659-6693-4779-a0fb-60d360dfff8f.definition: Points in a program's execution flow where an aspect can be inserted (e.g., method invocation, field access).

63f685eb-bd02-4f4e-baaa-f53d3f45e09b.title: Advice
63f685eb-bd02-4f4e-baaa-f53d3f45e09b.definition: Code is executed at a certain junction by an aspect.

3630c235-909d-48b8-b1b0-f7763ee1f70b.title: Before Advice
3630c235-909d-48b8-b1b0-f7763ee1f70b.definition: The `advice` code is executed before a join point is made.

2b263f14-c04b-4f55-83dc-a7382c9cfd4c.title: After Advice
2b263f14-c04b-4f55-83dc-a7382c9cfd4c.definition: The `advice` code is executed after a join point completes, including returning, throwing, or finally.

7eeb4ceb-eeb0-4cab-b2fd-405b2193aa1f.title: Around Advice
7eeb4ceb-eeb0-4cab-b2fd-405b2193aa1f.definition: The `advice` code wraps and can control the execution of a junction.

5172ca3e-dc17-4252-a093-269cf09f90f4.title: Pointcuts
5172ca3e-dc17-4252-a093-269cf09f90f4.definition: Expression defining the set of junctions at which an `advice` will be applied.

de917d0e-5437-4461-87fb-6b2fb8b91263.title: Pointcut Designators
de917d0e-5437-4461-87fb-6b2fb8b91263.definition: Keywords or syntax are used in `pointcut` to specify different types of junction points (e.g. `call`, `execution`).

db947492-189a-4108-b170-12b8d8c2cef1.title: Weaving (Static & Dynamic)
db947492-189a-4108-b170-12b8d8c2cef1.definition: The process of integrating aspects into the code base, including static weaving (at compile or load time) and dynamic weaving (at run time).

356038ca-f48e-4eb7-acd8-f86bf3a0e912.title: AOP Alternatives
356038ca-f48e-4eb7-acd8-f86bf3a0e912.definition: Alternative or complementary methods to aspect-oriented programming to handle cross-references, such as using annotations or support tools from the IDE.

913c5b82-a205-4221-bd7f-85ccddd45d41.title: Data Type Definition
913c5b82-a205-4221-bd7f-85ccddd45d41.definition: The concept of a data type is a set of values ​​along with a set of operations that can be performed on those values.

3499ba75-5f4b-42c6-9654-10daf4b5b7d8.title: Primitive Data Types
3499ba75-5f4b-42c6-9654-10daf4b5b7d8.definition: Basic data types are built into programming languages, such as integers, floats, and booleans.

f1307865-0c18-47bd-8647-b5de2a30d743.title: Composite Data Types
f1307865-0c18-47bd-8647-b5de2a30d743.definition: Data types are built from other types using set operations, for example: records/structs, unions, arrays, lists, functions, references.

84d3de4b-3517-44e8-8a57-6892a21847e8.title: Data Type Binding
84d3de4b-3517-44e8-8a57-6892a21847e8.definition: How data types are associated with variables, function arguments, function returns, and fields in data structures.

96acf1e2-a052-4fed-9f5e-57f4b7d9f9b4.title: Type Safety
96acf1e2-a052-4fed-9f5e-57f4b7d9f9b4.definition: The concept of type safety as an important element of program correctness, prevents errors caused by using values ​​inconsistent with the intended type.

5cb09372-8d51-4639-bd96-99fe33c2fba5.title: Type Errors
5cb09372-8d51-4639-bd96-99fe33c2fba5.definition: Errors arise when values ​​are used inconsistently with the intended data type, and the role of type safety in preventing them.

0f509251-5778-4d9f-806f-3b65f0f6e90e.title: Static & Dynamic Typing Pros/Cons
0f509251-5778-4d9f-806f-3b65f0f6e90e.definition: Learn about the goals and limitations of both static and dynamic typing systems, especially in detecting and eliminating errors as early as possible in software development.

3383e439-681a-4d75-8507-dbdff2e5deeb.title: Polymorphism Definition & Benefits
3383e439-681a-4d75-8507-dbdff2e5deeb.definition: understand the definition and general advantages of polymorphism in programming languages.

21a9056b-d948-4ccd-91dc-4c7dea61f86e.title: Parametric Polymorphism
21a9056b-d948-4ccd-91dc-4c7dea61f86e.definition: Master the concept of parametric polymorphism, where a function or data type can be written generically to operate on different types without modification.

7cc637b5-a779-4ea0-bac3-c769e69140c1.title: Subtyping Polymorphism
7cc637b5-a779-4ea0-bac3-c769e69140c1.definition: understand subtype polymorphism, where an object can be considered to be of its own type or any of its parent types.

9e7d6fca-d77e-4a2d-b061-322118610403.title: Overloading
9e7d6fca-d77e-4a2d-b061-322118610403.definition: Master the concept of overloading, which allows multiple functions or operators to have the same name but differ in type or number of parameters.

c4e32253-c4e7-419a-b8d9-dee2321ed795.title: Type Coercion
c4e32253-c4e7-419a-b8d9-dee2321ed795.definition: understand forced conversion, the automatic or implicit process of converting values ​​from one data type to another.

9780d8fe-46ea-47c4-9702-37230fe117b7.title: Monomorphic vs. Polymorphic Types
9780d8fe-46ea-47c4-9702-37230fe117b7.definition: Distinguish and compare between monomorphic (works with only one specific type) and polymorphic (can work with many types).

ac087bca-558b-4692-87ae-0e54208db650.title: Polymorphism Comparison
ac087bca-558b-4692-87ae-0e54208db650.definition: analyze and compare the characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of parametric polymorphism, ad-hoc polymorphism (overloading) and subtype polymorphism.

83504ed0-101d-4099-8bc8-7368c47b76f8.title: Generic Parameters & Typing
83504ed0-101d-4099-8bc8-7368c47b76f8.definition: understand how global parameters work in styling and how they enable flexible and reusable code.

c6c57e5a-d5ac-427d-bd02-bb7fd6e698b2.title: Generic Libraries Usage
c6c57e5a-d5ac-427d-bd02-bb7fd6e698b2.definition: Know how to effectively use generic libraries, such as collection data structures (lists, sets, maps) in languages ​​that support generics.

dcd882d9-c8fc-4156-bd16-f06bca8e84e8.title: Prescriptive vs. Descriptive Polymorphism
dcd882d9-c8fc-4156-bd16-f06bca8e84e8.definition: understand the difference between prescriptive polymorphism (where types must conform to a specific interface or rule) and descriptive polymorphism (where behavior is inferred from structure).

a88a77b8-9e0d-4d52-a443-de3734f9d247.title: Polymorphism Implementation Models
a88a77b8-9e0d-4d52-a443-de3734f9d247.definition: understand different paradigms for implementing polymorphism in programming languages, such as monomorphization or erasure.

4df558d3-cd84-482a-95f7-466313956893.title: Subtyping
4df558d3-cd84-482a-95f7-466313956893.definition: understand the basic concept of subtyping, where one data type can safely be substituted for another.

1c87ba38-9a57-4a40-87c4-84cabd6280f6.title: Structural Type Equivalence
1c87ba38-9a57-4a40-87c4-84cabd6280f6.definition: understand structural equivalence, where two types are considered equivalent if they have the same underlying structure.

327e0921-2d5d-4bd8-9108-fdcd7c2eec54.title: Name Type Equivalence
327e0921-2d5d-4bd8-9108-fdcd7c2eec54.definition: understand name equivalence, where two types are considered equivalent if they are defined using the same type name.

d2727766-1d8d-47a9-890e-0ece5205495f.title: Static Typing: Early Error Detection
d2727766-1d8d-47a9-890e-0ece5205495f.definition: Explain the benefits of static typing in detecting program errors at the early compilation stage.

b61188f3-9026-4b43-a403-8888473027d9.title: Dynamic Typing: Late Error Detection
b61188f3-9026-4b43-a403-8888473027d9.definition: Explain the benefit of dynamic typing in allowing errors to occur at runtime or avoiding some errors until execution.

136fe521-645d-429a-8aca-f8d3cceb743b.title: Static Typing: Invariant Enforcement
136fe521-645d-429a-8aca-f8d3cceb743b.definition: Understanding how static typing helps enforce program invariants, improves reliability during code development and maintenance.

76862005-8ac9-44f6-a947-39b1fc2c5e91.title: Dynamic Typing: Deferred Type Decisions
76862005-8ac9-44f6-a947-39b1fc2c5e91.definition: Explain the benefit of dynamic styling in allowing style decisions to be deferred, facilitating rapid prototyping.

154e7763-021d-4e52-9e00-8270b61f5512.title: Dynamic Typing: Flexible Code Patterns
154e7763-021d-4e52-9e00-8270b61f5512.definition: understand how dynamic typing supports flexible models, allowing the convenient use of heterogeneous collections.

e832102b-6fec-4b4e-a1e4-78ea2cba9d6f.title: Function Type Rules
e832102b-6fec-4b4e-a1e4-78ea2cba9d6f.definition: understand the style rules that apply to functions and how they ensure the correctness of function calls.

a4f46b71-d0fb-4038-9344-1864c3eb2c1a.title: Product Type Rules
a4f46b71-d0fb-4038-9344-1864c3eb2c1a.definition: Master the styling rules that apply to product types (also called records or structures) and how they handle the components of product types.

0a0628ff-ff06-4950-a0b6-e21c25a46cd9.title: Sum Type Rules
0a0628ff-ff06-4950-a0b6-e21c25a46cd9.definition: Master the styling rules that apply to aggregate types (also called unions or variants) and how they handle different cases.

9e527402-fcf7-4e54-9f5a-78a2b41c1458.title: Static Typing: Code Misuse
9e527402-fcf7-4e54-9f5a-78a2b41c1458.definition: Understanding static typing helps prevent abuse or misuse of code, improving program safety.

74b9c3c8-2458-4a29-81f9-57518612b1aa.title: Dynamic Typing: Code Reusability
74b9c3c8-2458-4a29-81f9-57518612b1aa.definition: Explain how dynamic styling can promote more flexible code reuse, especially in scenarios where the type doesn't need to be known completely in advance.

604f2d8d-e088-4dc3-9f6d-b6ff5dc699bd.title: Static Typing: Incomplete Program Detection
604f2d8d-e088-4dc3-9f6d-b6ff5dc699bd.definition: Understanding static typing can help detect parts of programs that are incomplete or style-inconsistent.

4639943b-5c3d-4d82-b11c-da41e74c1f36.title: Dynamic Typing: Incomplete Program Execution
4639943b-5c3d-4d82-b11c-da41e74c1f36.definition: Explain how dynamic typing can allow incomplete or incomplete programs to run, useful for iterative development.

fa447689-6d98-4e5f-a7d9-244222b26f5d.title: Typing & Static Analysis
fa447689-6d98-4e5f-a7d9-244222b26f5d.definition: analyze the relationship between the type system and other static analysis techniques to ensure program correctness.

663e4193-7ef8-4376-a768-624c7c90878f.title: Type System Decidability
663e4193-7ef8-4376-a768-624c7c90878f.definition: Grasp the concept of determinism in relation to type systems, especially the ability to determine the type correctness of a program automatically.

b5a4be0f-4101-4ad8-82c8-e6760eda8f67.title: Compositional Type Constructors
b5a4be0f-4101-4ad8-82c8-e6760eda8f67.definition: Understanding the fundamentals of type constructors allows building complex types from simpler types.

36c5f3a8-9dd7-4dbd-8b8a-a18bc01da67e.title: Product Types
36c5f3a8-9dd7-4dbd-8b8a-a18bc01da67e.definition: Master the concept of product types, which represent collections of values ​​of different types (e.g. records, structures).

4321281b-9101-46e8-afdd-346b87a61cdc.title: Sum Types
4321281b-9101-46e8-afdd-346b87a61cdc.definition: Master the concept of aggregate types, which represent a value that can be of one of many different types (e.g. union, variant).

cd966bfb-90fd-435b-90c6-3214a761b746.title: Function Types
cd966bfb-90fd-435b-90c6-3214a761b746.definition: understand function types, describe the input and output types of a function.

8a3e438c-2357-4fe1-acb7-2ce326a616a1.title: Quantified Types
8a3e438c-2357-4fe1-acb7-2ce326a616a1.definition: Master the concept of quantified type, allowing type variables to be introduced and used within a specific scope (e.g. Forall in polymorphism).

2fd90dda-85ed-410d-bf1e-52ca02e85fcf.title: Recursive Types
2fd90dda-85ed-410d-bf1e-52ca02e85fcf.definition: understand recursive types, types defined by themselves, commonly used for data structures such as linked lists and trees.

53cbb6d9-ee46-437c-ac1b-91700bd6785f.title: Type Checking
53cbb6d9-ee46-437c-ac1b-91700bd6785f.definition: understand type checking, where a system checks the data types of expressions in a program to ensure consistency and safety.

4e2eb5a8-8d84-490a-9b56-1a2e06ceadf8.title: Subtype Polymorphism
4e2eb5a8-8d84-490a-9b56-1a2e06ceadf8.definition: Further understanding subtype polymorphism, a form of polymorphism that allows a function or method to operate on objects of different types as long as they are subtypes of a specified type.

52722bc6-8f41-43eb-993a-016bcc6df502.title: Implicit Upcasting
52722bc6-8f41-43eb-993a-016bcc6df502.definition: understand how implicit casting (safely converting a subtype to its parent type) works in typed languages.

564a14ed-9dee-4d32-8207-1d494bb138df.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
564a14ed-9dee-4d32-8207-1d494bb138df.definition: understand the behavioral substitution principle (e.g., the Liskov substitution principle), where a subtype object can replace a parent object without changing the correctness of the program.

ef209b11-33b6-4aa9-ba12-ecade5c3b30f.title: Subtyping & Inheritance
ef209b11-33b6-4aa9-ba12-ecade5c3b30f.definition: analyze the close but distinct relationship between subtyping and inheritance in object-oriented programming languages.

9e811f09-4a84-436e-9b81-3a577587b6e5.title: Type Safety (Preservation & Progress)
9e811f09-4a84-436e-9b81-3a577587b6e5.definition: Understanding the formal definition of type safety, including the concepts of preservation and progress, ensures that the program never encounters type errors.

06d25ecf-8263-485f-9635-6627b5bdfb3b.title: Type Inference
06d25ecf-8263-485f-9635-6627b5bdfb3b.definition: understand the concept of type inference, the ability of a compiler or interpreter to automatically determine the type of expressions without the need for an explicit type declaration.

901f9241-7ef1-419b-b451-a8761f6f9bc9.title: Static Overloading
901f9241-7ef1-419b-b451-a8761f6f9bc9.definition: understand static overloading, where the choice of function or method to be overloaded is determined at compile time based on parameter type.

0d56f5dc-94aa-4106-ba73-a675daeb4756.title: Propositions as Types
0d56f5dc-94aa-4106-ba73-a675daeb4756.definition: Explore the Curry-Howard relationship, where logical statements correspond to types in the type system, and proofs correspond to programs.

198cdfeb-94ee-4d98-8c9a-dbc79586b901.title: Implication as Function Type
198cdfeb-94ee-4d98-8c9a-dbc79586b901.definition: understand how in the Curry-Howard relationship, the logical implication (A => B) is mapped to the functional type (A -> B).

bb795afc-a23d-41da-ae75-582040355193.title: Conjunction as Product Type
bb795afc-a23d-41da-ae75-582040355193.definition: understand how in the Curry-Howard relationship the logical conjunctions (A and B) are mapped to the product type (A x B).

21f77abd-9af7-40ff-a120-eff05c1e15ac.title: Disjunction as Sum Type
21f77abd-9af7-40ff-a120-eff05c1e15ac.definition: understand how in the Curry-Howard relationship, the logical selection (A or B) is mapped to the total type (A + B).

a47f78f4-3b9e-4990-aacd-c79959752a44.title: Dependent Types
a47f78f4-3b9e-4990-aacd-c79959752a44.definition: Learn about dependent types, an advanced concept where data types can depend on data values.

8778477f-4608-4771-af7d-0b7e220e8f13.title: Universal Quant. as Dependent Function
8778477f-4608-4771-af7d-0b7e220e8f13.definition: understand the relationship between universal quantifiers and dependency functions in the context of dependency types.

3dedb221-caa3-4554-8e3f-e05db8eafb04.title: Existential Quant. as Dependent Product
3dedb221-caa3-4554-8e3f-e05db8eafb04.definition: understand the relationship between existential quantification and dependency products in the context of dependency types.

6c1aed2f-4cb9-45ee-a3e4-75d39f3ebaa3.title: Primitive Type Values
6c1aed2f-4cb9-45ee-a3e4-75d39f3ebaa3.definition: Describes a set of values ​​of a primitive type (e.g., integer, boolean, character) in a programming language.

84461731-66df-447d-82c8-562264890d08.title: Composite Type Values
84461731-66df-447d-82c8-562264890d08.definition: Describes a collection of values ​​of a complex type (e.g., array, record, class) in a programming language.

7707179a-e09c-4520-a38f-57ffb72a3477.title: Static Type Violations
7707179a-e09c-4520-a38f-57ffb72a3477.definition: Describes the types of operations that are prohibited by the static type system at compile time, such as passing an argument of the wrong type to a function.

ab5c675a-d808-4ea1-ba38-539e9dc58245.title: Type System Error Detection
ab5c675a-d808-4ea1-ba38-539e9dc58245.definition: Give specific examples of program errors that a type system is capable of detecting (e.g., trying to add a string to an integer).

5376d444-80f6-400d-88e7-7ec1671612cd.title: Static Checked Properties
5376d444-80f6-400d-88e7-7ec1671612cd.definition: Defines program properties that are checked at compile time (static checking) in various programming languages.

1be05006-c5e2-4f2d-a64a-dc12de589d2a.title: Dynamic Checked Properties
1be05006-c5e2-4f2d-a64a-dc12de589d2a.definition: Defines program properties that are checked at run time (dynamic testing) in a variety of programming languages.

fd6067a0-b71b-4465-9ad3-09b4f3a91178.title: Type Check False Positive
fd6067a0-b71b-4465-9ad3-09b4f3a91178.definition: Describe a program example that does not pass type checking in a particular language but will still run without errors (an example of a type system false positive).

1b536d89-6160-4273-9e8e-ed082c94d5e3.title: Type Errors: Debugging & Coding
1b536d89-6160-4273-9e8e-ed082c94d5e3.definition: apply knowledge of types and the ability to interpret type error messages to write code accurately and debug programs effectively.

557d1f2c-5a9f-4030-82fb-cc781c4a419f.title: Type Rules: Valid Operations
557d1f2c-5a9f-4030-82fb-cc781c4a419f.definition: Explain how style rules in a programming language define the set of valid operations that can be performed on a particular data type.

b4855e6c-6341-45fe-9aef-6f47c83ea97d.title: Complex Type Rules
b4855e6c-6341-45fe-9aef-6f47c83ea97d.definition: List and explain the specific type rules that govern how a given complex type (e.g., array, structure, class) is used.

064d5278-75b5-4413-ad44-d032819e9826.title: Undecidability & Conservative Approximation
064d5278-75b5-4413-ad44-d032819e9826.definition: Explain why nondeterminism in determining program properties requires type systems to conservatively approximate program behavior.

dd879144-2056-4a7a-aae1-3a096e13e306.title: Generic Types Definition & Use
dd879144-2056-4a7a-aae1-3a096e13e306.definition: Ability to define and use program elements (functions, classes, methods) that apply generic styles to achieve flexibility.

986f8b94-f53f-44a2-a3f3-6920587b678a.title: Generics for Collections
986f8b94-f53f-44a2-a3f3-6920587b678a.definition: Make effective use of generic types when working with collections (e.g. List<T>, Map<K, V>) to ensure type safety and reusability.

b053763c-da4b-4af7-b548-e122eb9c0bc8.title: Generics, Subtyping, Overloading Comparison
b053763c-da4b-4af7-b548-e122eb9c0bc8.definition: Discuss and clearly distinguish the differences between the concepts of generics (parametric polymorphism), subtyping (subtype polymorphism) and overloading (overloading).

acaa2bb9-c453-40d0-aeba-e6c88497358d.title: Static Typing Benefits
acaa2bb9-c453-40d0-aeba-e6c88497358d.definition: Explain the various benefits of static typing during the software development, maintenance, and debugging phases.

ca6e5515-3029-4d78-b0eb-fc58f8f3d6aa.title: Static Typing Limitations
ca6e5515-3029-4d78-b0eb-fc58f8f3d6aa.definition: Explain how the limitations of static typing, including potential rigidity and the need for explicit type declarations, affect writing, maintenance, and debugging.

5131e49c-3fcd-45a7-9476-fab700e8628d.title: Formal Type System Definition
5131e49c-3fcd-45a7-9476-fab700e8628d.definition: Be able to define a formal and compositional type system, including rules for each language construct.

a89da2ec-0201-42b6-952d-160a22e92531.title: Basic Type Constructors: Values
a89da2ec-0201-42b6-952d-160a22e92531.definition: For basic type constructors (e.g., product, sum, function), clearly identify the sets of values ​​they can describe.

f2c55328-da0c-46bd-b7ce-c14bc7864ee4.title: Basic Type Constructors: Invariants
f2c55328-da0c-46bd-b7ce-c14bc7864ee4.definition: For basic type constructors, specify the invariants they enforce to ensure program correctness.

83929360-dd81-4f8b-8584-31304bc5a0e5.title: Sound Type System Invariants
83929360-dd81-4f8b-8584-31304bc5a0e5.definition: Describes precisely the invariants that a sound type system ensures are preserved during program execution.

22afc119-0f71-4f79-8af7-47ebbc3d1ab1.title: Type Safety Proof (Preservation & Progress)
22afc119-0f71-4f79-8af7-47ebbc3d1ab1.definition: Be able to prove type safety for a simple language using preservation and progress theorems.

f226acf9-99b8-47d3-8a33-ab17d4a0414f.title: Unification-based Type Inference
f226acf9-99b8-47d3-8a33-ab17d4a0414f.definition: It is possible to implement a type inference algorithm based on unification for a simple programming language.

41ec395a-5898-40b6-9d64-ade68500998a.title: Static Overloading & Dynamic Behavior
41ec395a-5898-40b6-9d64-ade68500998a.definition: Explain how static overloading and related resolution algorithms affect a program's dynamic behavior at runtime.

0c0c7c05-aa39-46ab-8bb0-11efd28a9d2d.title: Function Call Translation
0c0c7c05-aa39-46ab-8bb0-11efd28a9d2d.definition: Explain how to translate function and procedure calls, including parameter passing mechanisms, so that they can be executed on an abstract machine.

c5bcf681-3a8f-4609-8842-dc11c5f42c5f.title: Function Return Translation
c5bcf681-3a8f-4609-8842-dc11c5f42c5f.definition: Learn how to interpret and handle returns from function or procedure calls, including restoring state and releasing resources.

bd333a31-6c21-4a70-8bec-dd24f03331cc.title: Parameter Passing Mechanisms
bd333a31-6c21-4a70-8bec-dd24f03331cc.definition: Study different parameter passing mechanisms (e.g., pass by value, pass by reference) and how they are implemented on an abstract machine during language translation.

5d27a825-1dff-463f-922d-05c8a8c48d06.title: High-Level Data Structures
5d27a825-1dff-463f-922d-05c8a8c48d06.definition: Learn low-level memory allocation and data access for high-level data structures such as basic data types, n-dimensional arrays, vectors, records, and objects.

724b05d8-8378-4c9d-ac73-581a003440af.title: Stack Memory Deallocation
724b05d8-8378-4c9d-ac73-581a003440af.definition: understand how memory for local variables on the stack is automatically released when a function or procedure terminates and returns.

ff516a23-b039-47c7-a9fe-d6af2e8aecec.title: Manual Heap Memory Management
ff516a23-b039-47c7-a9fe-d6af2e8aecec.definition: Study manual memory management techniques, including how to allocate, free, and reuse memory on the heap.

43ac3fbc-d0b3-4bf1-a9b1-1623d15d97a3.title: Garbage Collection Reachability
43ac3fbc-d0b3-4bf1-a9b1-1623d15d97a3.definition: Learn about garbage collection as an automatic memory management technique that focuses on the concept of reachability to identify objects that need to be freed.

b7e91aee-ef27-45db-b76e-3b89c3e5754e.title: Green Computing
b7e91aee-ef27-45db-b76e-3b89c3e5754e.definition: Introduction to green computing and the principles related to minimizing the environmental impact of information technology.

02dfc7df-c318-4957-924f-d96e1ea4e19e.title: Language Core Abstractions
02dfc7df-c318-4957-924f-d96e1ea4e19e.definition: Explain how core language constructs such as data abstraction and control abstraction are implemented in a system.

6d3e3324-121f-4615-83a7-5efaa14ed52d.title: Memory Organization
6d3e3324-121f-4615-83a7-5efaa14ed52d.definition: Explain how programming language implementations typically organize memory into global data, program code, heap, and stack sections.

c0b594d4-22c8-4c72-90c9-f8b32f8beb03.title: Recursion Memory Mapping
c0b594d4-22c8-4c72-90c9-f8b32f8beb03.definition: Describe how features such as recursion and memory management are mapped into the memory organization model of a programming language.

1fd933ed-776c-456a-9c09-f76d544ef29e.title: Memory Leak
1fd933ed-776c-456a-9c09-f76d544ef29e.definition: Explains the causes of memory leaks and the methods programmers can use to avoid or fix them.

6cfb8307-1a7b-4a15-84ee-f503a967aec9.title: Dangling Pointer
6cfb8307-1a7b-4a15-84ee-f503a967aec9.definition: Explains the causes of hanging pointer problems and the methods programmers can use to avoid or fix them.

c36179ae-e890-4ca0-80c0-efdfa4a66445.title: JIT Execution Model
c36179ae-e890-4ca0-80c0-efdfa4a66445.definition: Learn about the Just-In-Time (JIT) execution model and how it works in language translation and execution.

5cf71f18-9efe-4e5d-ab7d-3b6e523e1311.title: Compiler Execution Model
5cf71f18-9efe-4e5d-ab7d-3b6e523e1311.definition: Learn about the compiler's execution model, including the stages of compilation and machine code generation.

67dc24d1-97d3-4fa5-8bce-3efe00d270d7.title: Interpreter Execution Model
67dc24d1-97d3-4fa5-8bce-3efe00d270d7.definition: Learn about the interpreter's execution model, where source code is read and executed line by line.

40e4ca2c-7308-44ac-a04a-33513fde9ccb.title: Intermediate Code
40e4ca2c-7308-44ac-a04a-33513fde9ccb.definition: Research the role and usage of intermediate code in the language translation process to increase portability and optimization.

c457830f-d7c0-4a4b-9105-67eca943995c.title: Bytecode
c457830f-d7c0-4a4b-9105-67eca943995c.definition: Learn about bytecode as a common form of intermediate code, used by virtual machines like the JVM.

63ebb56e-e9bb-4703-87f8-97aaa661b99c.title: JIT Pros & Cons
63ebb56e-e9bb-4703-87f8-97aaa661b99c.definition: analyze the limitations and benefits of the Just-In-Time (JIT) execution model compared to compilers and interpreters.

60c97770-8066-40ec-814e-c513603d5f12.title: Compiler Pros & Cons
60c97770-8066-40ec-814e-c513603d5f12.definition: analyze the limitations and benefits of compilers in converting source code to machine code.

7386e4b1-20b1-4b59-878c-69c59a021692.title: Interpreter Pros & Cons
7386e4b1-20b1-4b59-878c-69c59a021692.definition: analyze the limitations and benefits of interpreters in executing source code.

a2c7f465-fdd3-4c19-ab38-e711917ac1b0.title: Cross Compiler
a2c7f465-fdd3-4c19-ab38-e711917ac1b0.definition: Learn about cross compilers, tools that translate source code for a target platform different from the one on which it is running.

45317f01-94e0-432c-bd93-81d276aa6336.title: Transpiler
45317f01-94e0-432c-bd93-81d276aa6336.definition: Learn about transpiler, a tool that translates source code from one programming language to another programming language of equivalent level of abstraction.

6bca7a95-ee5c-4c59-8ad9-d91e05a6bee1.title: BNF Grammar Representation
6bca7a95-ee5c-4c59-8ad9-d91e05a6bee1.definition: Learn how to use BNF to describe the syntax of context-free grammars, which are fundamental to language design and parsing.

067d04ae-ef85-4cc2-b0fb-97d70c65bb13.title: EBNF Grammar Representation
067d04ae-ef85-4cc2-b0fb-97d70c65bb13.definition: Learn how to use EBNF to describe the syntax of a context-free grammar, which provides a more extensible and readable syntax than BNF.

146b17af-069a-4cfd-bc30-e9f11478c1c5.title: Parse Tree Generation
146b17af-069a-4cfd-bc30-e9f11478c1c5.definition: Learn how to build a parse tree for simple statements such as arithmetic expressions or if-then-else statements to represent their syntactic structure.

2c5e0f73-d3ef-4175-930c-823a11afd08b.title: Native Code Execution
2c5e0f73-d3ef-4175-930c-823a11afd08b.definition: Learn about program execution as the processor's native machine code, delivering peak performance.

c520ed0b-4727-4d94-9dc9-0e5986819720.title: Virtual Machine Execution
c520ed0b-4727-4d94-9dc9-0e5986819720.definition: Learn about program execution in a virtual machine environment, which provides portability and a layer of abstraction from hardware.

c9900f13-d530-4292-93ac-7948ce799cdc.title: Language Translation Process
c9900f13-d530-4292-93ac-7948ce799cdc.definition: Study the entire language translation process, from parsing to execution, including the main stages.

5c0f02fe-ae09-48d8-ad6e-4c1b8c0f4290.title: Lexical Analysis
5c0f02fe-ae09-48d8-ad6e-4c1b8c0f4290.definition: Learn about the lexical analysis stage in the language translation process, turning character strings into tokens.

c0e4a70d-d67b-4f2b-b9e3-6b6df4ae4630.title: Parsing
c0e4a70d-d67b-4f2b-b9e3-6b6df4ae4630.definition: Learn about the grammar analysis stage to build a syntax tree structure (parse tree or abstract syntax tree) from tokens.

8fab8fd1-fca8-4caf-b7a7-e18d741d75e1.title: Optional Type Checking
8fab8fd1-fca8-4caf-b7a7-e18d741d75e1.definition: Learn about the type checking phase of the language translation process, which can be required or optional depending on the language, to detect type errors.

6bf33454-a269-4505-8bf7-f5f3b3b65ecd.title: Code Generation
6bf33454-a269-4505-8bf7-f5f3b3b65ecd.definition: Learn about the stage of translating source code to target code (machine code or intermediate code) in the compilation process.

26300eb6-f200-4457-8b39-bdf56820bb42.title: Code Optimization
26300eb6-f200-4457-8b39-bdf56820bb42.definition: Learn about code optimization techniques to improve the performance, size, or energy consumption of the generated program.

04aea4c1-ec53-43b1-9fe8-7cc3e572dcb1.title: Linking
04aea4c1-ec53-43b1-9fe8-7cc3e572dcb1.definition: Learn about the process of linking compiled code modules and libraries to create a complete executable program.

d7198879-dfd1-4ebb-aa4c-e2943f839af6.title: Loading
d7198879-dfd1-4ebb-aa4c-e2943f839af6.definition: Learn about the process of loading a linked program into memory to prepare it for execution.

10f9da03-6b2d-421a-b508-c7f5d63dff0a.title: Execution
10f9da03-6b2d-421a-b508-c7f5d63dff0a.definition: Learn about program execution after it has been translated, linked, and loaded into memory.

8e14bdba-955d-47cb-93a1-8e59ffc597d7.title: Object Runtime Representation
8e14bdba-955d-47cb-93a1-8e59ffc597d7.definition: Study how objects are represented at runtime, including the structure of method tables to manage polymorphism and dynamic method invocation.

87eaa1cd-696c-4e88-b6f6-e288e851c2cf.title: Closure Runtime Representation
87eaa1cd-696c-4e88-b6f6-e288e851c2cf.definition: Study how functions can be passed as parameters or returned from other functions, especially the concept of closure, and how they can be represented at runtime to preserve their definition environment.

a077169f-1b5c-42c3-9dd9-de7a4eef63f8.title: Secure Compiler Development
a077169f-1b5c-42c3-9dd9-de7a4eef63f8.definition: Learn the principles and techniques for developing secure compilers to prevent security vulnerabilities in the generated code and ensure the integrity of the compilation process.

dd202c91-42aa-4564-b8f0-9f7aa9ff91da.title: Syntax, Parsing, Semantics
dd202c91-42aa-4564-b8f0-9f7aa9ff91da.definition: The ability to clearly distinguish between aspects of syntax (the formal structure of the language) and parsing (the process of checking syntax) and semantics (the meaning of language structures) and evaluation (the process of executing a program).

cb1ec8c8-22b8-4da8-95cb-845fe41f49c1.title: BNF/EBNF Syntax Definition
cb1ec8c8-22b8-4da8-95cb-845fe41f49c1.definition: Use Backus-Naur Grammar (BNF) and Extended Backus-Naur Grammar (EBNF) to specify the syntax of simple programming constructs such as `if-then-else` conditional statements, data type declarations, and looping constructs in popular programming languages ​​such as C++ or Python.

92969975-7948-4680-b4f0-7fd5d091fec0.title: Parse Tree Illustration
92969975-7948-4680-b4f0-7fd5d091fec0.definition: Illustrates how to construct and interpret a parse tree for a simple arithmetic statement or expression.

2dddc60e-fb46-4587-8e09-47e85ae958c3.title: Syntax Diagram to BNF/EBNF
2dddc60e-fb46-4587-8e09-47e85ae958c3.definition: Illustrates the process of converting syntax diagrams into BNF or EBNF rules for simple constructs such as `if-then-else`, type declarations, and looping structures.

ae363f30-ce33-454f-b8f7-4bb1b2a3cccb.title: Parsing Ambiguity & Precedence
ae363f30-ce33-454f-b8f7-4bb1b2a3cccb.definition: Illustrate ambiguity in parsing using examples such as nested `if-then-else` statements or arithmetic expressions, and show how this ambiguity can be resolved by applying precedence order.

79b67c35-361c-40a4-af89-5883bf1c436d.title: Garbage Collection Pros & Cons
79b67c35-361c-40a4-af89-5883bf1c436d.definition: Discuss the benefits and limitations of garbage collection, including the concept of reachability of objects in memory.

dd2c89fd-026c-4309-8151-ee8f2ae73cee.title: BNF & Regular Expressions
dd2c89fd-026c-4309-8151-ee8f2ae73cee.definition: Concept of Backus-Naur Grammar (BNF) to describe language syntax and Regular Expressions to describe character patterns.

987249cd-0db2-455c-98b1-a12faf9479f5.title: Program Processing Programs
987249cd-0db2-455c-98b1-a12faf9479f5.definition: Types of programs that receive input from other programs, such as interpreters, compilers, type-checkers, and documentation generators.

1ed8d140-796a-479f-a143-bc1abe42e826.title: Language Components
1ed8d140-796a-479f-a143-bc1abe42e826.definition: Defines the basic components of a programming language, including alphabets, delimiters, sentences, syntax, and semantics.

e1f64505-5326-49fb-9457-c79265608b19.title: Syntax vs Semantics
e1f64505-5326-49fb-9457-c79265608b19.definition: Clearly distinguish between syntax – how to write code correctly – and semantics – the meaning of the code.

9e803cee-b21a-4c18-8dcc-c923d3916705.title: Program
9e803cee-b21a-4c18-8dcc-c923d3916705.definition: understand that a program is a set of meaningful, unambiguous statements, written according to the rules of a language.

556a53b2-f40d-4a3a-be0b-bed946344ab7.title: Declarations
