556a53b2-f40d-4a3a-be0b-bed946344ab7.definition: Concept of declaration in programming, including nested declarations.

c992bd01-d1e6-4514-961e-d10795fd4ad3.title: Assignment
c992bd01-d1e6-4514-961e-d10795fd4ad3.definition: Concept of value assignment to variables.

2fa3d55b-c32b-45f7-8cd0-3006780ef1ed.title: Selection Statements
2fa3d55b-c32b-45f7-8cd0-3006780ef1ed.definition: Concept of selection structure or conditional statement.

8edd9a79-ca10-48b5-a31f-a00da78cc8af.title: Definite Iteration
8edd9a79-ca10-48b5-a31f-a00da78cc8af.definition: The concept of a definite iteration structure, such as a `for` loop.

10abedd9-a83e-4052-9741-ceb33aadb005.title: Indefinite Iteration
10abedd9-a83e-4052-9741-ceb33aadb005.definition: The concept of an indefinite iteration structure, such as a `while` loop.

b5ebb8f5-e7fc-4ebf-b810-6b4a439d3e68.title: Iterators
b5ebb8f5-e7fc-4ebf-b810-6b4a439d3e68.definition: Concept of iterators to traverse data structures.

53dfe616-32a1-4baf-8088-dc5255a240bd.title: Procedures
53dfe616-32a1-4baf-8088-dc5255a240bd.definition: The concept of procedure in programming.

15f8d87e-b770-47f5-93ff-a0e6a4c48626.title: Modules
15f8d87e-b770-47f5-93ff-a0e6a4c48626.definition: Concept of modules to organize and reuse code.

f09763eb-78fd-40c6-bb7b-6a2748a8623a.title: Exception Handling
f09763eb-78fd-40c6-bb7b-6a2748a8623a.definition: Concept of exception handling mechanism in programming.

c0a3b123-3d38-4050-bdda-3b6f8eb86c5d.title: Mutable vs Immutable
c0a3b123-3d38-4050-bdda-3b6f8eb86c5d.definition: Compare mutable and immutable variables, discuss the advantages and disadvantages of reusing existing memory locations versus copying and keeping old values; storing intermediate calculations vs. recalculating.

1b1b9a0a-992c-4693-a6dc-97b79a4ed62b.title: Variable Scopes
1b1b9a0a-992c-4693-a6dc-97b79a4ed62b.definition: Types of variables in programming: static variables, local variables, non-local variables and global variables; needs and problems that arise when using non-local and global variables.

3bf3dc68-56be-4e5c-ab99-8c155d9cbfc9.title: Scope Rules
3bf3dc68-56be-4e5c-ab99-8c155d9cbfc9.definition: Scope rules of variables, including static scoping and dynamic scoping; visibility of variables and the concept of side-effects.

6a85969b-996f-4fe1-83aa-970c5922fb87.title: Side Effects
6a85969b-996f-4fe1-83aa-970c5922fb87.definition: Side-effects can occur due to the use of non-local variables, global variables and aliased variables.

45921102-8f6a-40d2-a269-043abb0e0477.title: L-values and R-values
45921102-8f6a-40d2-a269-043abb0e0477.definition: Concept of L-values ​​(representing assignable memory locations) and R-values ​​(representing the value of an expression); how to map mutable variable names to L-values ​​and immutable variable names to R-values.

eb54646e-0156-499b-b248-a8023786ad86.title: Environment vs Store
eb54646e-0156-499b-b248-a8023786ad86.definition: Distinguish between environment (environment - maps variable names to memory addresses or values) and memory (store - maps memory addresses to values), along with their properties.

80f6ffc4-7e49-485a-b57d-8d3df110565e.title: Data/Control Abstraction
80f6ffc4-7e49-485a-b57d-8d3df110565e.definition: Concepts of data abstraction and control abstraction in language design.

5ce9dda8-46c5-46f6-bf76-db266fabef16.title: Inter-Unit Communication
5ce9dda8-46c5-46f6-bf76-db266fabef16.definition: Mechanisms for exchanging information between program units such as procedures, functions and modules, including non-local variables, global variables, parameter-passing and import-export mechanisms between modules.

b115df5a-4091-42d3-85fc-0e0646dbc566.title: Source Code Representation
b115df5a-4091-42d3-85fc-0e0646dbc566.definition: Data structures are used to represent source code for execution, translation, or transport purposes.

8a446680-ffb2-4d58-a80f-9ac1cdbf1108.title: Low-Level Instructions
8a446680-ffb2-4d58-a80f-9ac1cdbf1108.definition: Low-level forms of command representation such as virtual machine commands, assembly language, and binary representation.

86ff6325-8ae7-4188-837e-3970d67fac50.title: Lambda Calculus
86ff6325-8ae7-4188-837e-3970d67fac50.definition: Concept of Lambda calculus, a formal system for studying functions and their applications.

269927fb-1f46-4840-89b0-b1c85cd43436.title: Variable Binding
269927fb-1f46-4840-89b0-b1c85cd43436.definition: The concept of variable binding in formal systems and programming languages.

1781d787-bba3-44f8-a0c9-06e7babd15cc.title: Variable Renaming
1781d787-bba3-44f8-a0c9-06e7babd15cc.definition: The concept of variable renaming, often used to avoid name conflicts.

d307d4fc-7bae-44f9-a0f1-7f6d27e33b18.title: PL Semantics
d307d4fc-7bae-44f9-a0f1-7f6d27e33b18.definition: Types of programming language semantics: operational semantics, axiomatic semantics, denotational semantics, and behavioral semantics.

bdd3d108-5a6b-42a9-8886-a436ec2ac8d1.title: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
bdd3d108-5a6b-42a9-8886-a436ec2ac8d1.definition: Definition and usage of abstract syntax trees (ASTs) to represent the grammatical structure of code.

18091e7f-b960-4301-a89b-9ae48569b436.title: Abstract vs Concrete Syntax
18091e7f-b960-4301-a89b-9ae48569b436.definition: Contrast abstract syntax – which focuses on the semantic structure – and concrete syntax – which focuses on the precise textual representation of the language.

1694953c-a9a4-4183-b834-f7a25ef30749.title: Regular vs Context-Free Grammars
1694953c-a9a4-4183-b834-f7a25ef30749.definition: Compare and distinguish between regular grammars and context-free grammars, two basic types of grammar in formal language theory.

ef56a808-1765-4127-a188-07625216ef77.title: Lexical Analysis & Parsing
ef56a808-1765-4127-a188-07625216ef77.definition: The concept of lexical analysis/scanning and parsing is based on given language specifications.

de103817-b81b-430d-bd3a-6344be18a0e0.title: Lexical Analysis with Regex
de103817-b81b-430d-bd3a-6344be18a0e0.definition: Lexical analysis or scanning uses regular expressions to identify tokens.

e1c3f128-f728-410d-ab6c-8b2773410349.title: Tokens
e1c3f128-f728-410d-ab6c-8b2773410349.definition: Concept of tokens (lexical symbols) and their role in the parsing process.

8ecfae13-8429-406a-915e-9f7dec7ecc6f.title: Parsing Strategies
8ecfae13-8429-406a-915e-9f7dec7ecc6f.definition: Parsing strategies include top-down (e.g., recursive descent, LL) and bottom-up (e.g., LR, GLR) methods.

d39ba826-e5dd-4c48-8a77-0e2e32f53a37.title: Lookahead Tables
d39ba826-e5dd-4c48-8a77-0e2e32f53a37.definition: The concept of lookahead tables and how they are applied in the parsing process.

411e2800-0ee9-4e44-b24b-ffbe26265279.title: Chomsky Hierarchy
411e2800-0ee9-4e44-b24b-ffbe26265279.definition: The Chomsky Hierarchy classifies formal languages ​​based on their representational capabilities.

891197f5-7864-4acd-959c-5334823c9122.title: Derivations & Ambiguity
891197f5-7864-4acd-959c-5334823c9122.definition: The concepts of left-most derivation and right-most derivation arise in grammar, and ambiguity may arise.

2de1ef28-ce6b-45f4-bbfe-ad6d665182f1.title: Grammar Transformation
2de1ef28-ce6b-45f4-bbfe-ad6d665182f1.definition: Grammar transformation techniques to remove ambiguity or make the grammar more suitable for specific parsing strategies.

22d3d113-d0dd-49a8-aeb3-88ace7ecf1df.title: Parser Error Recovery
22d3d113-d0dd-49a8-aeb3-88ace7ecf1df.definition: Error recovery mechanisms are used in the parser to handle syntax errors and continue analysis.

7dd2b182-1da4-49e0-b8bf-166eaef565b4.title: Scanner/Parser Generation
7dd2b182-1da4-49e0-b8bf-166eaef565b4.definition: Method for automatically generating scanners and parsers from the declarative specifications of the language.

e104456a-e604-4bd3-a5a4-d82736911de1.title: Operator Associativity
e104456a-e604-4bd3-a5a4-d82736911de1.definition: The concept of associativity of operators in syntax definitions, helps resolve ambiguities in expressions.

e99a076b-293f-4648-9907-a616fb92a534.title: High-Level IR Manipulation
e99a076b-293f-4648-9907-a616fb92a534.definition: How to define, traversing, and modifying high-level program representations, typically ASTs or other intermediate representations, during semantic analysis.

63070319-f4e8-4344-af18-aedf46b65b22.title: Scope & Binding Resolution
63070319-f4e8-4344-af18-aedf46b65b22.definition: Techniques for resolving the scope resolution of identifiers and binding resolution of names to corresponding objects in the program.

7438f38f-3b18-4ccc-b042-d97173b8c9e0.title: Static Semantics
7438f38f-3b18-4ccc-b042-d97173b8c9e0.definition: Concept of static semantics, the rules of the language can be checked at compile time.

6211497e-65bd-4c91-898c-d7f6f2c3c883.title: Type Checking
6211497e-65bd-4c91-898c-d7f6f2c3c883.definition: Type checking process to ensure consistency of data types in the program.

734a1eae-e7af-45d3-8ffb-b27ef331a4d7.title: Declare Before Use
734a1eae-e7af-45d3-8ffb-b27ef331a4d7.definition: The rule requires variables or functions to be defined or declared before being used in a program.

188d34df-5c52-4e40-ae19-310db20857a5.title: Extended Static Checking
188d34df-5c52-4e40-ae19-310db20857a5.definition: Frameworks and tools enable annotations to be added to source code to support extended static checks, beyond basic syntax and type checks, to enhance software reliability.

a069e2d9-96e2-4499-8459-5d90b2ae373d.title: L-values and R-values
a069e2d9-96e2-4499-8459-5d90b2ae373d.definition: The concept of L-values ​​is expressions that have a memory address (assignable) and R-values ​​are expressions that only have a value (non-assignable) in the context of a programming language.

260441b2-bbcd-4426-891b-820eec41e3c3.title: Call Semantics
260441b2-bbcd-4426-891b-820eec41e3c3.definition: The rules and manner by which a function (or procedure) is called, including how arguments are passed and return values ​​are processed, as well as how the state of the program changes during the function call.

d464c469-e9c5-4e0a-8341-737ff4ee4800.title: Parameter Passing
d464c469-e9c5-4e0a-8341-737ff4ee4800.definition: Different methods for passing arguments to functions, including pass by value (copy by value), pass by reference (pass address), pass by result-value (copy in and out), pass by name (text replacement), and pass by need (lazy evaluation), along with their variations and comparisons.

1a1e51af-2799-45ed-9007-a61de0a0cc20.title: Attribute Grammars
1a1e51af-2799-45ed-9007-a61de0a0cc20.definition: Declarative specification techniques such as attribute grammars, and their applications in limited context-based grammar processing, allow the definition of attributes associated with nodes in the syntax tree and their systematic computation.

17b2472f-f84d-4f00-999f-0d539bb2172d.title: AST
17b2472f-f84d-4f00-999f-0d539bb2172d.definition: The tree data structure represents the abstract syntactic structure of source code, used in compilers and program analyzers.

c57ae52c-a84d-4ad3-834c-2f911e647ea6.title: Context-Sensitive Analysis
c57ae52c-a84d-4ad3-834c-2f911e647ea6.definition: Source-level static analysis techniques that consider the code's execution context, such as type checking or identifier resolution, to determine their binding locations.

fed8f761-70e9-43ac-bd15-9f1973b57f12.title: Type Checker
fed8f761-70e9-43ac-bd15-9f1973b57f12.definition: The tool or component of the compiler is responsible for checking the correctness of using data types in the program according to the rules of the language.

db694d50-be28-4d2b-ac03-2dadec0b31b5.title: Identifier Resolution
db694d50-be28-4d2b-ac03-2dadec0b31b5.definition: The process of determining which variable or function is referenced by a particular identifier in the source code, and the locations in the program where an identifier is declared and associated with a value or object.

b77c4a83-9ca8-4225-8f78-a85db8650991.title: Semantic Analysis (AG)
b77c4a83-9ca8-4225-8f78-a85db8650991.definition: The way attribute grammar is used to describe and perform semantic analysis, checking the validity and meaning of a program goes beyond syntax.

343a27ac-c7f7-480a-b9c0-df45d2d9e76a.title: Basic Block
343a27ac-c7f7-480a-b9c0-df45d2d9e76a.definition: A basic block is a sequence of instructions in program code such that if one instruction is executed then all other instructions in the sequence will also be executed, used as the basic unit in many program analysis.

34753fc7-17e5-4989-907e-5505c1e09fc2.title: CFG
34753fc7-17e5-4989-907e-5505c1e09fc2.definition: A control flow graph (CFG) is a graph that represents all possible paths a program can traverse during execution, with nodes being the basic blocks and edges representing the transfer of control between them.

3ff5c600-f6f3-4922-b783-e74dd96e8cd9.title: Def-Use Chain
3ff5c600-f6f3-4922-b783-e74dd96e8cd9.definition: A definition-use chain is a data structure or analysis in which each definition of a variable is associated with all the places that variable can be used after that definition.

1899853f-2b22-455b-849f-dad84526e659.title: SSA
1899853f-2b22-455b-849f-dad84526e659.definition: Static single assignment (SSA) is an intermediate representation of program code in which each variable is assigned a value only once, simplifying data flow analysis.

27fde7cc-1bcd-45f9-8c3b-81a42dfac9f5.title: Undecidability in Analysis
27fde7cc-1bcd-45f9-8c3b-81a42dfac9f5.definition: Concept of problems that cannot be solved algorithmically (e.g., stopping problems) and the limitations they impose on the ability to perform accurate and complete program analyses.

094ba172-065b-4ddc-aa96-78caed22c688.title: Flow-Insensitive Analysis
094ba172-065b-4ddc-aa96-78caed22c688.definition: A type of program analysis that does not consider the order of execution of instructions, is often faster but less accurate, e.g. type checking.

a1aabc59-ba0d-438a-b324-a0c02dc8987a.title: Scalable Pointer Alias Analysis
a1aabc59-ba0d-438a-b324-a0c02dc8987a.definition: Techniques that analyze the relationship between pointers and determine when two different expressions may refer to the same memory location (alias), designed to work efficiently on large programs.

2bc366fc-fe1a-40de-808a-3d6c3bb3ee25.title: Flow-Sensitive Analysis
2bc366fc-fe1a-40de-808a-3d6c3bb3ee25.definition: A type of program analysis that considers the execution order of instructions and program state at different points in the control flow, for example, forward and backward data flow analysis.

ba095e49-62b9-47e1-ab33-931058e18a80.title: Forward Dataflow Analysis
ba095e49-62b9-47e1-ab33-931058e18a80.definition: A data flow analysis technique that gathers information about a program by going from the beginning to the end of the control flow.

61b5ae56-56cb-46ef-9a8b-2a51ca61f0d7.title: Backward Dataflow Analysis
61b5ae56-56cb-46ef-9a8b-2a51ca61f0d7.definition: A data flow analysis technique that gathers information about a program by going back from the end to the beginning of the control flow.

3dd7d7ff-bd87-45b6-bdff-ca30fa63470c.title: Path-Sensitive Analysis
3dd7d7ff-bd87-45b6-bdff-ca30fa63470c.definition: A type of program analysis that examines specific execution paths through code, allowing the detection of errors or properties that appear only on certain paths, e.g., software model checking and software verification.

c13cc902-d950-47a2-a433-fd303f1a3cbe.title: Software Model Checking
c13cc902-d950-47a2-a433-fd303f1a3cbe.definition: An automatic verification technique that explores all possible states of a program to verify specified properties.

05d8b2d0-2f4b-47ba-8a53-1ab516d1861f.title: Software Verification
05d8b2d0-2f4b-47ba-8a53-1ab516d1861f.definition: The process of ensuring that software meets given requirements or specifications, often through formal or semi-formal methods.

a026cac2-9860-4334-b3f1-a2c7324f18b9.title: Analysis Tools & Frameworks
a026cac2-9860-4334-b3f1-a2c7324f18b9.definition: Software and libraries that support the construction of program analysis tools, including lexer/parser generators, graph processing libraries, and analysis development environments.

821a9852-2578-4b8a-b9f2-1ca1c5ff0dc6.title: Static Analysis for Optimization
821a9852-2578-4b8a-b9f2-1ca1c5ff0dc6.definition: Static analysis is used to gather information about a program without executing it, which is then used to make more effective code optimization decisions.

e8b82704-a3ad-43e3-a47e-40894aea2ff9.title: Data Dependence Analysis
e8b82704-a3ad-43e3-a47e-40894aea2ff9.definition: analyze dependencies between read and write data operations to identify parts of the program that can be safely and efficiently executed in parallel.

5d34f48c-2072-42a6-942f-1f74a9d8958f.title: Analysis for Verification & Debugging
5d34f48c-2072-42a6-942f-1f74a9d8958f.definition: How program analysis techniques are used to partially test software for correctness or automatically detect potential errors.

0f4017d6-d90f-4cfa-9a8a-069fda66a8f0.title: Automatic Parallelization Analysis
0f4017d6-d90f-4cfa-9a8a-069fda66a8f0.definition: Source code analysis techniques to automatically identify and convert parts of a program into a parallel form that can run on multiple processors.

80032614-9222-4290-8eb0-2f3920a60149.title: Concurrency Bug Detection
80032614-9222-4290-8eb0-2f3920a60149.definition: Program analysis methods to identify errors related to concurrency, such as race conditions or deadlocks.

ee62177a-6057-4cb5-86fb-83d81c94fee4.title: Data Flow Graph
ee62177a-6057-4cb5-86fb-83d81c94fee4.definition: A diagram that describes how data moves and is transformed by mathematical operations in a program.

1cbc69a3-a57c-4ee6-85b0-aee77839fff7.title: Approximation in Analysis
1cbc69a3-a57c-4ee6-85b0-aee77839fff7.definition: The notion that for a non-trivial program analysis to be sound and stopable, it must usually accept a certain level of approximation, sometimes omitting some details for the sake of feasibility.

b9f052d2-301a-46c1-9689-e0936ee73e98.title: Soundness
b9f052d2-301a-46c1-9689-e0936ee73e98.definition: The property of a program analyzer that ensures that it never misses any errors or unexpected properties (e.g., if it says there are no errors, there really are no errors).

949a02a7-deca-4218-b712-d10af300d8d4.title: Termination
949a02a7-deca-4218-b712-d10af300d8d4.definition: The property of a program analysis that ensures that it will always finish in a finite amount of time, never run indefinitely.

af4971b5-9287-4e8d-bce5-33a8c00fd7de.title: Aliasing Impact on Analysis
af4971b5-9287-4e8d-bce5-33a8c00fd7de.definition: Situation where two or more different expressions in a program refer to the same memory location, causing difficulty and limiting the possibility of reliable program analysis.

82390267-6fd9-41e1-9a5d-ba2171d9c46f.title: Alias Analysis
82390267-6fd9-41e1-9a5d-ba2171d9c46f.definition: Program analysis technique to identify pairs of expressions that can be pseudonyms for each other, helping to improve the accuracy of other analyses.

21b341f7-cb0e-471f-847e-269be5ae62b1.title: Analysis for Optimization
21b341f7-cb0e-471f-847e-269be5ae62b1.definition: Using the results of program analysis to transform code, aiming to improve the performance or other characteristics of a program without changing its semantics.

c4d05c42-d108-4446-9bee-415c0ed789f2.title: Analysis for Partial Verification
c4d05c42-d108-4446-9bee-415c0ed789f2.definition: Using the results of program analysis to verify that a program satisfies certain properties or requirements, even if the entire program cannot be verified.

ef6890bd-d559-41e5-b4de-27ed6694410d.title: Instruction Set
ef6890bd-d559-41e5-b4de-27ed6694410d.definition: The set of all instructions that a processor can understand and execute, is the goal of code generation.

9db67b29-c213-4af0-95d2-fc9b0f3a4e57.title: Control Flow (Code Gen)
9db67b29-c213-4af0-95d2-fc9b0f3a4e57.definition: How control structures (e.g., if, loop) in source code are converted into jump and conditional statements in machine code or assembly language.

466bd961-9c83-4cd7-b50d-8c17cbb5d015.title: Memory Management (Code Gen)
466bd961-9c83-4cd7-b50d-8c17cbb5d015.definition: Techniques and strategies that compilers use to allocate and free memory for variables, data structures, and other program elements during code generation.

d168dc20-9285-4310-9080-e5508fc8b723.title: Procedure Call & Dispatch
d168dc20-9285-4310-9080-e5508fc8b723.definition: How procedure (or function) calls are compiled and how methods (in object-oriented programming) are dispatched to their correct implementation at run time.

bd8cb148-bc97-4a65-8b45-f75f3db66714.title: Separate Compilation
bd8cb148-bc97-4a65-8b45-f75f3db66714.definition: The technique of compiling different parts of a program independently, then linking them together to form the final program.

c701cf8b-e65f-4aa9-a4d2-a5d926f2d8cf.title: Linking
c701cf8b-e65f-4aa9-a4d2-a5d926f2d8cf.definition: The process of combining separate compilation-generated object files and necessary libraries into a single executable program.

c2c6cf86-dad6-4019-b099-2e68e199148b.title: Instruction Selection
c2c6cf86-dad6-4019-b099-2e68e199148b.definition: The stage in code generation where operations in the program's intermediate representation are mapped to specific instructions of the target instruction set.

3b42046a-47bb-4c8c-945f-68a39afdd787.title: Instruction Scheduling
3b42046a-47bb-4c8c-945f-68a39afdd787.definition: The stage in the code generation process where the execution order of instructions is optimized to improve performance, often by exploiting the processor's pipeline architecture.

2f1a70ee-86af-475e-ab0a-e78081ecbf4f.title: Register Allocation
2f1a70ee-86af-475e-ab0a-e78081ecbf4f.definition: The process of assigning program variables to processor registers to optimize data access and minimize main memory usage.

4f4233ee-2b13-4cab-8813-effa9e219810.title: Code Optimization as Analysis
4f4233ee-2b13-4cab-8813-effa9e219810.definition: Realize that code optimization techniques in compilers often rely on program analytics to gather information and make decisions that improve performance.

960568ce-1982-42d2-90ac-6d1874d6fe6c.title: AI Code Generation
960568ce-1982-42d2-90ac-6d1874d6fe6c.definition: The use of generative artificial intelligence models to automatically generate program code based on high-level descriptions or requirements.

d5160b9b-6349-4195-97c9-52eaa6fddf23.title: Compiler Phases
d5160b9b-6349-4195-97c9-52eaa6fddf23.definition: Overview of the stages required to automatically convert source code into assembly or other low-level languages, including lexical, syntactic, semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, optimization, and final code generation.

8fb78697-83c7-43d3-9eff-77ef71d4cdb5.title: Low-Level Function Call
8fb78697-83c7-43d3-9eff-77ef71d4cdb5.definition: Explains in detail the low-level code required to make function or method calls in modern languages, including setting up stack frames, passing parameters, saving state, and restoring state.

b9f837fa-0eaf-493f-89cd-8c13b108e2f8.title: Calling Convention
b9f837fa-0eaf-493f-89cd-8c13b108e2f8.definition: The reason why separate compilation requires standardized function calling conventions so that independently compiled modules can interact properly.

ab332458-79f0-469d-be1f-4a4554e54b78.title: Separate Compilation Limits Optimization
ab332458-79f0-469d-be1f-4a4554e54b78.definition: Discussion of separate compilation limits the compiler's ability to optimize because the full impact of function calls outside the current module cannot be known in advance.

e532671a-b62b-4de9-8aa2-26d5f2ed8520.title: Naive Code Optimization
e532671a-b62b-4de9-8aa2-26d5f2ed8520.definition: Optimization opportunities arise from direct or simple translation, and methods for achieving optimization after the initial translation is performed.

0115d22c-77c9-48a5-9f69-45edd413e6b2.title: Peephole Optimization
0115d22c-77c9-48a5-9f69-45edd413e6b2.definition: A technique that locally optimizes code by looking at a small 'window' of instructions and replacing inefficient sequences of instructions with more efficient sequences of instructions.

97f86a63-a05f-42bc-8aae-c1b686133501.title: Stack & Heap Allocation
97f86a63-a05f-42bc-8aae-c1b686133501.definition: How processes use stack and heap data structures to allocate and deallocate activation records and dynamic memory.

8ac1c877-c8d6-4c39-b5cb-92c9a686fab1.title: Activation Record
8ac1c877-c8d6-4c39-b5cb-92c9a686fab1.definition: A data structure created on the stack for each function call, containing information such as parameters, local variables, return addresses, and frame pointers.

0afb1b07-9f26-443d-8eef-b9bcf230d6a8.title: Frame Pointer & Return Address
0afb1b07-9f26-443d-8eef-b9bcf230d6a8.definition: Mechanism by which the runtime system uses the frame pointer and return address stored in the activation record to restore the execution state of the calling function after the called function completes.

5f690aba-a13b-4780-9541-171e3bba0afc.title: Method Dispatch (OOP)
5f690aba-a13b-4780-9541-171e3bba0afc.definition: The way methods in object-oriented programming languages ​​are looked up and dispatched to their correct implementation at run time, often using hash tables or similar data structures.

fe1461f7-e391-4f97-ad58-2dccfe9bc257.title: Object & AR Data Layout
fe1461f7-e391-4f97-ad58-2dccfe9bc257.definition: How the data of objects (data fields, vtable pointers) and activation records (local variables, parameters, return addresses) are arranged in memory.

c8f8569f-78c6-49c2-a3d6-90fadfc428da.title: Heap Object Allocation
c8f8569f-78c6-49c2-a3d6-90fadfc428da.definition: The process of allocating memory for objects on the heap at runtime, typically performed by the language's runtime environment or operating system.

6c0043b9-65b5-41c8-a6d5-d778529b24d6.title: Virtual Method Implementation
6c0043b9-65b5-41c8-a6d5-d778529b24d6.definition: Techniques for implementing virtual concepts in object-oriented programming, allowing polymorphism and dynamic binding, including how virtual methods are called.

dc06502f-80e7-4960-aba5-2b74fc8a3792.title: Vtable
dc06502f-80e7-4960-aba5-2b74fc8a3792.definition: Data structures are used in object-oriented programming to implement polymorphism through virtual methods, allowing the runtime system to find the right method to call based on the actual type of the object.

4acf75a0-91a3-470e-9345-6e39dcf55eed.title: OOP Runtime Behavior
4acf75a0-91a3-470e-9345-6e39dcf55eed.definition: How concepts like inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation affect how object-oriented programs operate and manage resources at runtime.

a05b38aa-ee2a-46f8-984f-88859a6fd0f8.title: Parameter Passing Memory
a05b38aa-ee2a-46f8-984f-88859a6fd0f8.definition: How memory is allocated and used when information is exchanged between functions or procedures through various parameter passing mechanisms.

4f379a3b-60a7-47fe-9c99-78d419ffba0f.title: Non-Local Variable Allocation
4f379a3b-60a7-47fe-9c99-78d419ffba0f.definition: Memory allocation and access methods for non-local variables (i.e. variables declared in enclosing scopes but not the current scope), typically use static binding to keep track of nested environments.

daa638f9-c43f-4821-8f44-eb70070a4e72.title: Dynamic Memory Management
daa638f9-c43f-4821-8f44-eb70070a4e72.definition: Techniques for allocating and freeing memory during program runtime.

333741b2-74d8-4508-88b9-3660a5f37e4f.title: Malloc/Free
333741b2-74d8-4508-88b9-3660a5f37e4f.definition: Standard library functions to allocate (malloc) and free (free) memory dynamically as required by the program.

83943f26-8068-4d05-bb82-957df7a3cd65.title: Mark-Sweep GC
83943f26-8068-4d05-bb82-957df7a3cd65.definition: A two-phase garbage collection algorithm: the mark phase identifies all accessible objects, and the sweep phase reclaims memory from unmarked objects.

802154ed-65af-48ad-8afe-7363b3142e57.title: Copying GC
802154ed-65af-48ad-8afe-7363b3142e57.definition: A garbage collection algorithm divides heap memory into two regions and moves live objects from the currently used region to the remaining region.

033e32f6-45a9-4ba3-988c-eda7959737d9.title: Reference Counting GC
033e32f6-45a9-4ba3-988c-eda7959737d9.definition: A garbage collection algorithm keeps track of the number of references to each object and releases memory when the reference count reaches zero.

1e067a71-8cd8-450d-b92f-1468d1b8a8d2.title: Memory Arenas
1e067a71-8cd8-450d-b92f-1468d1b8a8d2.definition: A memory management technique in which related objects are allocated from a single large memory region, increasing allocation efficiency and freeing the entire region at once.

0e37d7e0-052e-4b70-a40b-a5a187c7b370.title: JIT Compilation
0e37d7e0-052e-4b70-a40b-a5a187c7b370.definition: A method of compiling code during a program's runtime, often used in virtual machines to convert bytecode to native machine code to improve performance.

ee064804-9195-4c8e-917b-66d965ebaf25.title: Dynamic Recompilation
ee064804-9195-4c8e-917b-66d965ebaf25.definition: A technique of recompiling parts of a program at runtime, often to apply new optimizations based on the program's actual behavior or to adapt to a changing environment.

c1b4f7ac-a06d-44d6-b59d-f9b0bf814eba.title: OS Program Initialization
c1b4f7ac-a06d-44d6-b59d-f9b0bf814eba.definition: The interaction points between the program and the operating system during program initialization, including code loading, stack and heap setup, and initial transfer of control.

1162640d-43e4-4227-a04a-ca5a5b1a5f8d.title: Language Interoperability
1162640d-43e4-4227-a04a-ca5a5b1a5f8d.definition: Challenges and techniques that enable components written in different programming languages ​​to communicate and operate together, including mechanisms for parameter passing and data representation.

a797c55a-1bd3-4dfa-bfff-703352697905.title: Interop Parameter Passing
a797c55a-1bd3-4dfa-bfff-703352697905.definition: Methods for passing arguments between functions written in different programming languages, often involve standardized calling conventions and data formats.

8944b9ec-d3be-4342-b90e-72fd9c2dc083.title: Interop Data Representation
8944b9ec-d3be-4342-b90e-72fd9c2dc083.definition: How data types and data structures are represented in memory to allow different languages ​​to share and understand data.

e9f4c9f5-78ff-4bf9-96dd-5b3444dc04a9.title: Endianness
e9f4c9f5-78ff-4bf9-96dd-5b3444dc04a9.definition: Two different byte arrangements in memory for multi-byte values, affecting data compatibility between systems.

ea7eee9e-2a11-4628-8eea-d373b2d01939.title: Complex Data Type Layout
ea7eee9e-2a11-4628-8eea-d373b2d01939.definition: How complex data types such as arrays, structures, or objects are arranged and stored in memory.

fc9b5868-8d87-42bc-be81-7c0674a1d1d5.title: VM Class Loading
fc9b5868-8d87-42bc-be81-7c0674a1d1d5.definition: The process of loading classes or modules into a virtual machine's memory when they are required, often involving code verification and dynamic linking.

17e8aeca-0745-4817-9d45-c4e174ae69ae.title: VM Threads
17e8aeca-0745-4817-9d45-c4e174ae69ae.definition: How virtual machines manage and support the concurrent execution of multiple threads within a program.

ca6f3788-b5da-486e-85de-864fc7c95c65.title: VM Security Checks
ca6f3788-b5da-486e-85de-864fc7c95c65.definition: Security mechanisms are implemented in virtual machines to limit access and prevent malicious behavior, ensuring program and system safety.

e3061ecd-a88d-43b1-bce9-3e0286543dae.title: Sandboxing
e3061ecd-a88d-43b1-bce9-3e0286543dae.definition: A security technique in which a program or part of a program is run in a restricted environment, isolated from critical system resources to prevent potential negative effects.

2ad74096-c7fa-4545-a0b3-1156fa8e81b1.title: Automatic Memory Management
2ad74096-c7fa-4545-a0b3-1156fa8e81b1.definition: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of automatic memory management, including mechanisms such as garbage collection.

d79379eb-3741-471a-a42d-036eff22adc1.title: Runtime Metadata
d79379eb-3741-471a-a42d-036eff22adc1.definition: Explain the use of metadata in object representation and run-time activation records, such as class pointers, array lengths, return addresses, and frame pointers.

136202cb-7195-4a28-ad63-d149540ce59a.title: Static Memory Allocation
136202cb-7195-4a28-ad63-d149540ce59a.definition: Compare and contrast memory allocation methods for data elements: static allocation.

b94e0d9d-c69a-4b43-9d41-b573b6793042.title: Stack Memory Allocation
b94e0d9d-c69a-4b43-9d41-b573b6793042.definition: Compare and contrast memory allocation methods for data elements: stack-based allocation.

04dd8401-7a81-4859-b04f-43affa5a3095.title: Heap Memory Allocation
04dd8401-7a81-4859-b04f-43affa5a3095.definition: Compare and contrast memory allocation methods for data elements: heap-based allocation.

4e4144fb-3bc3-4d17-9141-c4410b0b44d1.title: Garbage Collection Necessity
4e4144fb-3bc3-4d17-9141-c4410b0b44d1.definition: Explain why some data elements cannot be automatically released at the end of a procedure/method call and require a garbage collection mechanism.

46cd4d39-fff6-46e0-b833-841e14dbeee7.title: JIT Pros/Cons
46cd4d39-fff6-46e0-b833-841e14dbeee7.definition: Discuss the advantages, disadvantages, and difficulties of Just-in-time (JIT) compilation and dynamic recompilation.

da2b0773-7e50-4265-96fe-03922f4ae113.title: Dynamic Recompilation Pros/Cons
da2b0773-7e50-4265-96fe-03922f4ae113.definition: Discuss the advantages, disadvantages, and difficulties of dynamic recompilation.

00db7f28-c333-4b40-b09c-785308b4c3ac.title: Mobile Code Sandboxing
00db7f28-c333-4b40-b09c-785308b4c3ac.definition: Discusses the use of sandboxing (isolated environments) in mobile code to enhance security.

75dd1a7b-fecf-4644-bbf2-af4db0071079.title: Runtime System Services
75dd1a7b-fecf-4644-bbf2-af4db0071079.definition: Identify the services provided by the runtime systems of modern programming languages.

d6caf4e1-9ced-4aa0-b811-982bf02e182f.title: Encapsulation Mechanisms
d6caf4e1-9ced-4aa0-b811-982bf02e182f.definition: understand and use encapsulation mechanisms in programming to manage access and protect data.

0cc84d22-49f6-4774-ab5e-e8ced87575b0.title: Lazy Evaluation
0cc84d22-49f6-4774-ab5e-e8ced87575b0.definition: understand the concept of deferred evaluation, where an expression is evaluated only when its value is actually needed.

932dbbb9-f12f-47ae-a3c7-c93fa41718b6.title: Infinite Streams
932dbbb9-f12f-47ae-a3c7-c93fa41718b6.definition: Working with infinite data streams, often combined with deferred evaluation.

702cae8b-7ffa-4d05-9e26-bd7bf5d61123.title: Lazy vs Eager Evaluation
702cae8b-7ffa-4d05-9e26-bd7bf5d61123.definition: Compare and contrast two expression evaluation strategies: lazy evaluation and eager evaluation.

c934c6e9-ac0e-4fbd-9f29-1318f1471793.title: Eager Evaluation
c934c6e9-ac0e-4fbd-9f29-1318f1471793.definition: understand the concept of immediate evaluation, where an expression is evaluated immediately.

21026cd1-1867-4052-b70b-45e9d9afc379.title: Unification
21026cd1-1867-4052-b70b-45e9d9afc379.definition: Compare expression merging, validation, and evaluation mechanisms, especially in logic programming languages.

8c9e788c-f6ca-4a1d-bf4e-720aebe93a34.title: Assertion Evaluation
8c9e788c-f6ca-4a1d-bf4e-720aebe93a34.definition: Compare assertion evaluation and expression evaluation mechanisms, especially in the context of programming languages.

4c4449a1-2b05-47c3-8356-f3921c607617.title: Expression Evaluation
4c4449a1-2b05-47c3-8356-f3921c607617.definition: understand expression evaluation methods and rules in different programming languages.

ab7376e8-ecaa-4f3d-8c3e-4a93e6cd2d1b.title: Exception Handling
ab7376e8-ecaa-4f3d-8c3e-4a93e6cd2d1b.definition: understand and use exception handling as a control abstraction mechanism to manage errors and unusual situations.

b5b593b5-ee61-485f-869e-7753c31322af.title: Continuations
b5b593b5-ee61-485f-869e-7753c31322af.definition: Learn about continuations as a powerful control abstraction mechanism that enables non-local control of the flow of execution.

cc4d763e-c72f-45b7-abb5-f3c9dbb749ae.title: Monads
cc4d763e-c72f-45b7-abb5-f3c9dbb749ae.definition: Learn about monads as a control abstraction and code organization mechanism, especially in functional programming.

aac84b1e-f104-4e3c-813a-6860fa9d4cfd.title: Multiple Inheritance
aac84b1e-f104-4e3c-813a-6860fa9d4cfd.definition: understand the concept of multiple inheritance in object-oriented programming, its advantages and disadvantages.

6bb51516-9c0d-4be2-add7-2df82ad79fa8.title: Mixins
6bb51516-9c0d-4be2-add7-2df82ad79fa8.definition: Learn about mixins as a way to reuse code and add functionality to classes without traditional multiple inheritance.

8dfb2d10-d430-4cda-b397-13275f2831f8.title: Traits
8dfb2d10-d430-4cda-b397-13275f2831f8.definition: Learn about traits as a mechanism for grouping methods that can be reused in multiple classes.

9beca2c0-801d-4f1e-8baa-5dee0c8b1098.title: Multimethods
9beca2c0-801d-4f1e-8baa-5dee0c8b1098.definition: Learn about multimethods (or generic functions) where the choice of method depends on the type of multiple arguments.

d6189b46-3d5b-4793-b423-f655c7975f85.title: Macros
d6189b46-3d5b-4793-b423-f655c7975f85.definition: Use macros as a form of metaprogramming to generate code automatically during compilation or runtime.

e6491a29-3147-484c-b3b0-4bccd7bff1af.title: Generative Programming
e6491a29-3147-484c-b3b0-4bccd7bff1af.definition: understand generative programming, a programming method that automatically generates source code, components, or software systems based on specific descriptions or requirements.

b8923e50-43c3-43eb-ade8-f3aa08104f3b.title: Model-Based Development
b8923e50-43c3-43eb-ade8-f3aa08104f3b.definition: Learn about model-based development (MBD), where models are used as the primary means to design, deploy, and test systems.

6bdde45a-a821-4f0b-8172-b656c2e190f8.title: Regex Pattern Matching
6bdde45a-a821-4f0b-8172-b656c2e190f8.definition: Perform string manipulation using pattern matching, specifically through regular expressions to search, replace, and parse text.

959419be-1ab1-46fc-87cf-9bd126882122.title: Regular Expressions
959419be-1ab1-46fc-87cf-9bd126882122.definition: Use regular expressions to describe and match patterns in strings.

9e8511ce-b2d6-4c6f-94f6-0efdbb8419fd.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation (`eval`)
9e8511ce-b2d6-4c6f-94f6-0efdbb8419fd.definition: understand and use the ability to dynamically evaluate code at runtime, typically via the 'eval' function, and its advantages and associated security risks.

823d8bc8-0ce4-4ec4-a5f3-dd2b25373eb2.title: Language Assertions
823d8bc8-0ce4-4ec4-a5f3-dd2b25373eb2.definition: Learn about how programming languages ​​support checking assertions to ensure program correctness.

d87f24de-8182-4eb9-bfcc-4744c3376cd5.title: Language Invariants
d87f24de-8182-4eb9-bfcc-4744c3376cd5.definition: Learn about how programming languages ​​support checking invariants of objects or data structures.

6cd775bd-16d7-4ff9-afd3-2cdad293eba0.title: Language Pre-conditions
6cd775bd-16d7-4ff9-afd3-2cdad293eba0.definition: Learn about how programming languages ​​support checking pre-conditions of functions or methods.

6df2dd5b-746f-40a1-8242-5159f1bbc1c4.title: Language Post-conditions
6df2dd5b-746f-40a1-8242-5159f1bbc1c4.definition: Learn about how programming languages ​​support checking post-conditions of functions or methods.

f58d6d3e-f72e-49bf-ab81-7a3c8074ed7b.title: Domain-Specific Language (DSL)
f58d6d3e-f72e-49bf-ab81-7a3c8074ed7b.definition: understand the concepts and applications of domain-specific languages, designed for a specific application domain.

9033edea-594c-44bb-af21-12b52adcb596.title: Database Languages (DSL)
9033edea-594c-44bb-af21-12b52adcb596.definition: Learn about database languages ​​like SQL, which are examples of domain-specific languages.

a8b74594-a786-4f67-bf1f-0cc3c80ef3e2.title: Data Science Languages (DSL)
a8b74594-a786-4f67-bf1f-0cc3c80ef3e2.definition: Learn about languages ​​used in data science (like Python with Pandas, R libraries) as examples of domain-specific languages.

7c9b8c18-3103-4408-920a-81ad265e44a1.title: Embedded Computing Languages (DSL)
7c9b8c18-3103-4408-920a-81ad265e44a1.definition: Learn about languages ​​used in embedded computing (like C, Rust) as examples of domain-specific languages.

ad313587-df0d-47c4-b8dc-2b3ba8d8132e.title: Synchronous Languages (DSL)
ad313587-df0d-47c4-b8dc-2b3ba8d8132e.definition: Learn about synchronous languages ​​(e.g. Esterel, Luster) used for programming real-time and reactive systems.

cc791708-a4f5-493a-ac21-17dbc25758db.title: Hardware Interface Languages (DSL)
cc791708-a4f5-493a-ac21-17dbc25758db.definition: Learn about languages ​​used to communicate with hardware (e.g. VHDL, Verilog) as examples of domain-specific languages.

ab324ed7-a067-4067-bf92-003489890e36.title: High-Performance Parallel Computing
ab324ed7-a067-4067-bf92-003489890e36.definition: Study the paradigms and languages ​​used for massively parallel high-performance computing, such as CUDA, OpenMP, MPI.

d5993856-e1b6-488c-aace-1ce4ca1a46f9.title: Technology Influence on PL Design
d5993856-e1b6-488c-aace-1ce4ca1a46f9.definition: Discuss how technological needs drive the development and evolution of programming languages.

dee46a2a-9a9a-498f-949e-83214d84bbd3.title: Software Requirements on PL Design
dee46a2a-9a9a-498f-949e-83214d84bbd3.definition: Discuss how software requirements shape the development and evolution of programming languages.

20344ceb-df56-4d75-ba9a-d117f6f8d3d6.title: Problem Domains & PL Models
20344ceb-df56-4d75-ba9a-d117f6f8d3d6.definition: understand the relationships between different problem domains and the appropriate programming models to solve them.

30209a5e-d6f6-4013-acc7-9cad13e4b369.title: Good PL Design Criteria
30209a5e-d6f6-4013-acc7-9cad13e4b369.definition: analyze the criteria for evaluating a good programming language design, including principles such as orthogonality.

64de1a5f-cc0c-4bd6-9bba-5733d3ce00e7.title: PL Design: Orthogonality
64de1a5f-cc0c-4bd6-9bba-5733d3ce00e7.definition: Learn about language design principles like orthogonality, where language features can be used independently and combined consistently.

7ca7f41d-d88d-4842-a14b-14bfcf3f83fc.title: PL Design: Good Defaults
7ca7f41d-d88d-4842-a14b-14bfcf3f83fc.definition: Discuss the role of well-chosen defaults in language design and how they affect the programmer's experience.

073ede0c-67d8-4ae7-84f1-d1824e42107b.title: Control Structure Definition
073ede0c-67d8-4ae7-84f1-d1824e42107b.definition: understand the principles and techniques for defining control structures in a programming language.

1240efc4-fb33-4e4b-bd71-e18dcc79c91e.title: Loop Structure Definition
1240efc4-fb33-4e4b-bd71-e18dcc79c91e.definition: understand the principles and techniques for defining repeating constructs in a programming language.

081375ea-50e3-4746-9016-996c43b56361.title: Large Software Modularity
081375ea-50e3-4746-9016-996c43b56361.definition: Discuss the importance and principles of massive software modularization to improve structure and maintainability.

78612722-c454-4cef-b428-c98ccb1c70ba.title: Order of Evaluation
78612722-c454-4cef-b428-c98ccb1c70ba.definition: understand the rules for the order of evaluation of expressions and arguments in various programming languages.

b7c45827-a841-4f2f-9dea-f8e963293347.title: Operator Precedence
b7c45827-a841-4f2f-9dea-f8e963293347.definition: understand the precedence of operators in expressions and how they affect the evaluation results.

e9ba4b9e-cab5-4872-8582-be55e9fecf16.title: Operator Associativity
e9ba4b9e-cab5-4872-8582-be55e9fecf16.definition: understand the associativity of operators (left to right or right to left) and how they determine the order of evaluation when there are multiple operators with the same precedence.

332ef4fa-42bf-428c-8292-9e3da0ecb6ea.title: External Calls
332ef4fa-42bf-428c-8292-9e3da0ecb6ea.definition: Discusses the need to allow external calls and system libraries, as well as the consequences for language implementations.

52fcf3dd-7205-4f27-97fb-5a838c94a3cd.title: System Libraries
52fcf3dd-7205-4f27-97fb-5a838c94a3cd.definition: Discuss the role and integration of system libraries into programming languages.

c04a36b5-3bb4-4c7e-aa42-2c597afaf7c7.title: User-Defined Control Abstractions
c04a36b5-3bb4-4c7e-aa42-2c597afaf7c7.definition: Illustrates the use of deferred evaluation to create user-defined control abstractions.

04dfd01a-22c8-472b-98fa-4b3c26fbde0d.title: Syntax vs. Semantics
04dfd01a-22c8-472b-98fa-4b3c26fbde0d.definition: Distinguish and compare syntax (form of the language) and semantics (meaning of the language) in the context of programming languages.

e56ce896-5e9e-43e2-9691-e75bc2b0012c.title: Language Syntax
e56ce896-5e9e-43e2-9691-e75bc2b0012c.definition: understand how a programming language is described and parsed.

ab6c9c5f-7503-4548-827f-45770703e84d.title: Language Semantics
ab6c9c5f-7503-4548-827f-45770703e84d.definition: understand the importance of semantic definitions to clarify the meaning of linguistic structures.

715d70b8-1a8f-4959-a339-361816083a99.title: Axiomatic Semantics
715d70b8-1a8f-4959-a339-361816083a99.definition: Learn about axiomatic semantics as a method for describing the meaning of a program through preconditions and postconditions.

8cf6ec3c-7a45-4d69-8641-e6a354f03a9a.title: Operational Semantics
8cf6ec3c-7a45-4d69-8641-e6a354f03a9a.definition: Learning about semantics works as a method to describe the meaning of a program by identifying its computational steps.

03512494-53fe-47b0-9b3a-7da27c4734ec.title: Denotational Semantics
03512494-53fe-47b0-9b3a-7da27c4734ec.definition: Learn about model semantics as a method for describing the meaning of a program by mapping it to abstract mathematical objects.

1e6ca9d6-ed6e-4561-8830-ccef36f73676.title: Type-Based Semantics
1e6ca9d6-ed6e-4561-8830-ccef36f73676.definition: Learn about type-based semantics as a method for analyzing and ensuring program correctness through the type system.

2c3390da-2e6f-4420-bbf0-07c934569ac7.title: Axiomatic Semantics: Assignment
2c3390da-2e6f-4420-bbf0-07c934569ac7.definition: apply axiomatic semantics to analyze abstract structures such as assignments using preconditions, postconditions, and invariants.

6f3c2b70-2694-4fcf-ac2c-5ffc96f5a56d.title: Axiomatic Semantics: Selection
6f3c2b70-2694-4fcf-ac2c-5ffc96f5a56d.definition: apply axiomatic semantics to analyze abstract structures such as options (if-then-else) using preconditions, postconditions, and invariants.

4c4f2255-8c20-4376-aa3b-a1f82b2118c4.title: Axiomatic Semantics: Iteration
4c4f2255-8c20-4376-aa3b-a1f82b2118c4.definition: apply axiomatic semantics to analyze abstract structures such as iterations (loops) using preconditions, postconditions, and loop invariants.

32575572-7a3c-4471-afc8-61725d7a10ec.title: Preconditions (Axiomatic Semantics)
32575572-7a3c-4471-afc8-61725d7a10ec.definition: Use preconditions to specify a state that must be true before a piece of code is executed in axiomatic semantics.

3a41cdb8-df28-499e-8013-ae5b5846c5d3.title: Postconditions (Axiomatic Semantics)
3a41cdb8-df28-499e-8013-ae5b5846c5d3.definition: Use postconditions to specify the state that must be true after a piece of code is executed in axiomatic semantics.

905c26a8-a5dd-4fd2-adb7-d2feced3d514.title: Loop Invariant
905c26a8-a5dd-4fd2-adb7-d2feced3d514.definition: Using loop invariants to prove the correctness of iterative constructs in axiomatic semantics.

72c782ed-826e-47ba-a527-ed8bd4a71813.title: Operational Semantics: Assignment
72c782ed-826e-47ba-a527-ed8bd4a71813.definition: analyze the operational semantics of abstract constructs such as assignment, environment usage, and memory.

1e1cb771-8405-409e-89d7-2010b6ccf398.title: Operational Semantics: Expressions
1e1cb771-8405-409e-89d7-2010b6ccf398.definition: Operational semantic analysis of expression evaluation, environment and memory usage.

8b6d9448-ac43-4b44-91aa-ca31aea16fbc.title: Operational Semantics: Selection
8b6d9448-ac43-4b44-91aa-ca31aea16fbc.definition: analyze the operational semantics of abstract constructs such as selection, environment usage, and memory.

9700cc49-9f6f-42e1-84f8-feba36e671fd.title: Operational Semantics: Iteration
9700cc49-9f6f-42e1-84f8-feba36e671fd.definition: analyze the operational semantics of abstract constructs such as iteration, environment and memory usage.

869b894a-1128-4d31-ad99-09072e962102.title: Operational Semantics: Environment
869b894a-1128-4d31-ad99-09072e962102.definition: understand the role of the environment in operational semantics for tracking variable bindings.

e7aef1ab-14b5-461f-88be-9fadb6a27579.title: Operational Semantics: Store
e7aef1ab-14b5-461f-88be-9fadb6a27579.definition: understand the role of memory (store) in operational semantics for monitoring memory status.

4f3d2dd5-faf2-4be3-94d6-1132082ad73c.title: Symbolic Execution
4f3d2dd5-faf2-4be3-94d6-1132082ad73c.definition: Learn about symbolic execution as a program analysis technique that allows program execution with symbolic rather than concrete input values.

51ccaf76-0d11-4626-afb9-178bd9d98019.title: Constraint Checkers
51ccaf76-0d11-4626-afb9-178bd9d98019.definition: Learn about constraint checking tools used to verify constraints imposed on variables or program state.

9a56fb1f-2e3f-4a21-8b28-912090dd7d22.title: Lambda Calculus
9a56fb1f-2e3f-4a21-8b28-912090dd7d22.definition: Study Lambda Calculus as a formal system for expressing computation based on functional abstraction and application.

633d15ab-f709-43db-9d42-b97d53cbf967.title: Language Semantics Induction Proof
633d15ab-f709-43db-9d42-b97d53cbf967.definition: Use induction to prove the properties of all programs in a language, based on the definition of its formal semantics.

4d98ffb3-5045-4c24-8a57-5efa890e94c2.title: Formal Type System Definition
4d98ffb3-5045-4c24-8a57-5efa890e94c2.definition: Research formal definitions and proofs for the type system, ensuring program safety.

57af84aa-b14c-4ed1-b1b5-96f452beb353.title: Type System Proofs
57af84aa-b14c-4ed1-b1b5-96f452beb353.definition: Build proofs of the correctness of the type system, such as type consistency.

2d620d8b-70c1-482d-91a6-759e4a71bf2e.title: Propositions as Types
2d620d8b-70c1-482d-91a6-759e4a71bf2e.definition: Learn about the relationship between logical statements and types in advanced type systems.

97315f2e-da54-4a8b-aa11-6236bb1e8e5b.title: Implication as Function Type
97315f2e-da54-4a8b-aa11-6236bb1e8e5b.definition: understand how logical reasoning can be represented as functions in the context of 'propositions as types'.

d2f9e6c3-32e4-410e-9fff-f439860145e2.title: Conjunction as Product Type
d2f9e6c3-32e4-410e-9fff-f439860145e2.definition: understand how logical conjunctions can be represented as product types in the context of 'propositions as types'.

e7c9e6d4-2771-4307-8eba-40d9101b810b.title: Disjunction as Sum Type
e7c9e6d4-2771-4307-8eba-40d9101b810b.definition: understand how logical selections can be represented as sum types in the context of 'clauses as types'.

553d0cf4-4d72-48ff-aca0-06e54e5000f5.title: Dependent Types
553d0cf4-4d72-48ff-aca0-06e54e5000f5.definition: Learn about dependent types, a type system in which types can depend on values.

43576dde-06c5-48a8-9f2d-e963efa5f620.title: Universal Quantifier as Dependent Function
43576dde-06c5-48a8-9f2d-e963efa5f620.definition: understand how universal quantifiers can be represented as dependent functions in a dependent type system.

ff6ad012-b53b-4bc8-9b5c-8317ef89fa27.title: Existential Quantifier as Dependent Product
ff6ad012-b53b-4bc8-9b5c-8317ef89fa27.definition: understand how existential quantifiers can be represented as dependent products in a dependent type system.

79c4d22c-efde-4062-95c7-4bea779ecc54.title: Parametricity
79c4d22c-efde-4062-95c7-4bea779ecc54.definition: Learn about parametricity as a property of the polymorphic type system, which implies behavioral properties of generic functions.

c3eb2fbd-14ac-402f-94da-f23c4b49d971.title: Inductive Proofs for Typed Languages
c3eb2fbd-14ac-402f-94da-f23c4b49d971.definition: The ability to use mathematical induction to prove the properties of all programs in a language that are precisely typed according to a formally defined type system.

5b85f576-7c30-4d6b-afa4-65487a11bfb1.title: Parametricity for Code Behavior
5b85f576-7c30-4d6b-afa4-65487a11bfb1.definition: The ability to use parametricity to infer or establish the behavior of code based solely on information about its type, independent of the specific implementation.

bd183512-226e-48ab-977c-ecd6cdffc166.title: Formal Specification Languages
bd183512-226e-48ab-977c-ecd6cdffc166.definition: The study of languages ​​and methods used to describe the behavior of software systems in a precise, unambiguous, and verifiable manner.

1ee05606-e706-4dc1-adf8-f4ae45422bba.title: Theorem Provers, Proof Assistants
1ee05606-e706-4dc1-adf8-f4ae45422bba.definition: Software tools (such as theorem provers, proof assistants) and formal logic platforms are used to support the construction and verification of mathematical and logical proofs.

9b234736-f569-4204-9d8d-383030f1c59b.title: Constraint Checkers
9b234736-f569-4204-9d8d-383030f1c59b.definition: Tools are used to automatically check whether a system complies with defined constraints or rules.

38a0df2a-f72e-4b25-a816-5a9e9d52ea93.title: Dependent Types
38a0df2a-f72e-4b25-a816-5a9e9d52ea93.definition: The concept of data types that depend on values ​​rather than just types, allows the representation of complex specifications (e.g., universal quantifiers as dependent functions, existential quantifiers as dependent products).

16d05c44-136d-4540-ba7d-6828d46b134d.title: Proof Discharge Verified Software
16d05c44-136d-4540-ba7d-6828d46b134d.definition: Engineering specifies software requirements and uses automated or semi-automated tools to complete proof discharges of the correctness of fully verified software systems, using preconditions/postconditions, refinement types, etc.

54775b29-0494-457f-a86f-a35b050ac74f.title: Formal Modeling and Refinement
54775b29-0494-457f-a86f-a35b050ac74f.definition: The process of creating formal (mathematical) models of software systems and then manually refining or implementing them to meet design requirements.

8a00e80b-87cb-48df-89d5-0cdb469655d2.title: Symbolic Testing, Fuzzing
8a00e80b-87cb-48df-89d5-0cdb469655d2.definition: Automated software testing techniques include symbolic testing to explore execution paths and fuzzing to find errors by providing invalid or unexpected input.

01cb106d-a683-4b1b-94ff-d65ea25cb892.title: Model Checking
01cb106d-a683-4b1b-94ff-d65ea25cb892.definition: A technique for verifying the correctness of a hardware or software system design by automatically checking whether an abstract model of the system satisfies certain specifications.

f1b65a56-a619-4060-9e59-ea60caa4adc0.title: Effective Formal Methods Application
f1b65a56-a619-4060-9e59-ea60caa4adc0.definition: The ability to recognize the situations and contexts in which formal methods can be applied most effectively, as well as how to structure the development process to maximize their value.

65a4e4f2-1ee1-4f61-9d93-77050528fdd9.title: Formal Modeling for Architecture
65a4e4f2-1ee1-4f61-9d93-77050528fdd9.definition: Skills in applying formal modeling techniques to design, analyze and verify the correctness of software system architectures.

cb12f68d-9166-4d78-b49f-bdfe9cbd27b9.title: Proof-Assisted Programming
cb12f68d-9166-4d78-b49f-bdfe9cbd27b9.definition: Skills in using programming languages ​​that integrate proof assistant tools to build software components that are completely formally specified and verified.

1dfb438e-9968-4376-b95f-5ee21ba01237.title: Verification in Programming Languages
1dfb438e-9968-4376-b95f-5ee21ba01237.definition: Skill in leveraging verifiers and specification support available in programming languages ​​to formally test and validate desired system properties.

49f4e256-ac5f-47bf-b47e-05baf26510a7.title: Symbolic Validation Integration
49f4e256-ac5f-47bf-b47e-05baf26510a7.definition: Skill in incorporating symbolic validation tools into daily software development processes to improve code quality and reliability.

21b0f5f7-c9c4-474f-8a8d-7113dcdd4c65.title: Formal Methods Effectiveness
21b0f5f7-c9c4-474f-8a8d-7113dcdd4c65.definition: Ability to analyze and discuss optimal cases and ways to apply formal methods in the software development process, evaluating their benefits and limitations.

b1bb13fc-2fdd-4bf4-a57a-bfed452b343f.title: Programming Language Design Principles
b1bb13fc-2fdd-4bf4-a57a-bfed452b343f.definition: Basic principles guide the design of programming languages ​​that are efficient, easy to use, and highly applicable.

f798d354-9111-4088-90f7-290a44043ea9.title: Language Design: Simplicity
f798d354-9111-4088-90f7-290a44043ea9.definition: Principle of designing a programming language so that its syntax, semantics, and features are easy to learn, use, and understand.

f2f3721f-986d-4d54-a138-7385d9b1a71e.title: Language Design: Security
f2f3721f-986d-4d54-a138-7385d9b1a71e.definition: Programming language design principles to minimize potential security vulnerabilities and prevent unsafe behavior.

34cb0e11-9948-49f9-9152-0996e937d011.title: Language Design: Fast Translation
34cb0e11-9948-49f9-9152-0996e937d011.definition: Principle of designing programming languages ​​to be compiled or interpreted quickly, optimizing development and response time.

665563ee-7469-4419-9e3c-d08d5925cea4.title: Language Design: Efficient Object Code
665563ee-7469-4419-9e3c-d08d5925cea4.definition: Programming language design principles to create object code that runs efficiently in terms of time and resources, optimizing application performance.

c082903c-7a1e-4817-8658-c0a6fea3a05b.title: Language Design: Orthogonality
c082903c-7a1e-4817-8658-c0a6fea3a05b.definition: Programming language design principle in which independent features can be freely combined without causing unwanted side effects, increasing flexibility and reducing complexity.

2e70a347-72fc-4cd0-81ad-9be1a15370c8.title: Language Design: Readability
2e70a347-72fc-4cd0-81ad-9be1a15370c8.definition: Principles of programming language design so that the source code is easy to understand, read, and maintain by humans.

5c443668-133d-44f6-8508-3768fdb92153.title: Language Design: Completeness
5c443668-133d-44f6-8508-3768fdb92153.definition: Programming language design principles that provide enough functionality and expressiveness to solve a wide range of problems or tasks.

6ec5f594-8f02-468e-918b-5c71627e88d8.title: Language Design: Implementation Strategy
6ec5f594-8f02-468e-918b-5c71627e88d8.definition: The methods and techniques considered when designing a language, influence how the compiler, interpreter, or runtime environment is built for that language.

7d1aca82-6ef7-4893-8167-ccddfa1f9001.title: Domain-Specific Language Design
7d1aca82-6ef7-4893-8167-ccddfa1f9001.definition: Ability to design a specific programming language (Domain-Specific Language - DSL) according to the requirements of a specific application area or type of problem.

2f01b0ff-a4c4-4b82-8be2-93ec7d08c5cc.title: Language Interoperability
2f01b0ff-a4c4-4b82-8be2-93ec7d08c5cc.definition: The ability of different programming languages ​​to work together, exchange data, and call each other's functions or methods.

2ee7f566-c96d-46de-8c41-f95db20eb225.title: Language Portability
2ee7f566-c96d-46de-8c41-f95db20eb225.definition: The ability of a programming language and programs written in that language to run on different hardware platforms and operating systems without significant modification.

996d64a2-0230-4d32-ac65-b77fc170f93d.title: Formal Language Description
996d64a2-0230-4d32-ac65-b77fc170f93d.definition: The use of precise mathematical methods to define the syntax and semantics of a programming language, often using tools such as formal grammar and domain theory.

1a7b0e6f-d31b-4584-8b57-bfeef380f5dd.title: Green Computing
1a7b0e6f-d31b-4584-8b57-bfeef380f5dd.definition: Principles for designing and using computer systems, software, and programming languages ​​in a way that saves energy and minimizes environmental impact.

49835fcd-e20b-416b-af42-2440ed31cbb6.title: PL Design Evaluation
49835fcd-e20b-416b-af42-2440ed31cbb6.definition: The ability to understand the elements that make up a good programming language design and apply that knowledge to analyze and evaluate the pros and cons of an actual programming language.

b4711ecc-46c9-447f-bab2-af09f6459de1.title: English-centric PL Impact
b4711ecc-46c9-447f-bab2-af09f6459de1.definition: Discusses the effects, both positive and negative, of predominantly English-based programming languages ​​on the global developer community and inclusivity.

46e9a9f7-02c5-4b52-9f75-7a8ca170f16f.title: Programming Accessibility
46e9a9f7-02c5-4b52-9f75-7a8ca170f16f.definition: Methods and considerations for making programming languages, tools, and development environments more accessible to people with disabilities, including assistive technology support.

1441e720-0e03-4407-ace9-c6022c8f871d.title: PL Human Factors
1441e720-0e03-4407-ace9-c6022c8f871d.definition: Study of how programming language features affect user experience, productivity, comfort, and programmer perception.

024c3e4b-371b-4589-bfba-6f6130fa45fa.title: Syntax Accessibility
024c3e4b-371b-4589-bfba-6f6130fa45fa.definition: The influence of the syntactic structure of a programming language on its ease of use and accessibility for different user groups, including those with special needs.

eb10d758-8b86-4762-be2b-f85e02a68e79.title: PL Culturalization
eb10d758-8b86-4762-be2b-f85e02a68e79.definition: How programming languages ​​and applications can support culturally different formats and conventions (e.g. currency, decimal numbers, dates), ensuring globalization.

20c32fdb-bfb8-4caa-9463-a607a5cf6f01.title: Neurodiversity in Programming
20c32fdb-bfb8-4caa-9463-a607a5cf6f01.definition: Discuss how programming languages ​​and development environments can be designed to accommodate people with neurological differences, encouraging inclusion in the industry.

1204a06c-b229-4b78-88f6-55d1e2e3b0e3.title: Offensive PL Terms
1204a06c-b229-4b78-88f6-55d1e2e3b0e3.definition: Study the origins and historical meanings of terms like “class,” “master,” and “slave” in the context of programming languages, and discuss their social and ethical implications.

ed776d0a-29a9-4f50-bef7-27b20253bdc7.title: Multilingual App Support (UTF)
ed776d0a-29a9-4f50-bef7-27b20253bdc7.definition: Methods to make applications more accessible to users globally through support for multiple languages, often using Unicode (UTF) character encoding.

8c4dfe68-9b13-4d38-9b55-3ae271adc129.title: Inclusive PL Design
8c4dfe68-9b13-4d38-9b55-3ae271adc129.definition: The ability to consciously design programming languages ​​so that they are friendly, accessible, and free of potentially offensive terms or constructs promotes an inclusive programming environment.

17ee9fef-b8ad-436a-a66a-a52c0fc166e0.title: PL Professionalism
17ee9fef-b8ad-436a-a66a-a52c0fc166e0.definition: Attitude and skills that demonstrate the highest standards when using programming languages ​​and formal methods to build systems that are secure and fit for purpose.

d41c8d78-6466-48ba-88a0-375616de2e25.title: Programming Rigour
d41c8d78-6466-48ba-88a0-375616de2e25.definition: Careful attention to detail is necessary when using programming languages ​​and applying formal methods to avoid errors and ensure correctness.

17a56e54-4ecb-46df-af3d-139b4a8e6c2a.title: PL Creativity & Responsibility
17a56e54-4ecb-46df-af3d-139b4a8e6c2a.definition: Ability to demonstrate innovative approaches in solving programming problems and constructing formal proofs, while taking responsibility for one's choices and results.

9c357632-ca3e-4a9e-9bd4-e4a80f264666.definition: A mathematical model of computation used to design sequential reaction systems, including states and state transitions.

16d0ff05-2079-4c21-a7d6-ad25d55f2006.definition: A logical system represents statements about objects, their properties, and the relationships between them, including universal and existential quantifiers.

4af48655-dc1f-4d32-804b-80b2363599ec.definition: Method of logical deduction from specific observations or cases to reach a general conclusion, often used in mathematics and computer science.

8828158f-5b7c-4d46-8580-4c3535b157a8.definition: The method of logical deduction from one or more general premises believed to be true to reach a specific logical conclusion, ensuring correctness.

6ec9489a-cf01-4980-973b-f1ed1e596256.definition: Techniques for checking the meaning and validity of a program after parsing, including type checking, symbol table management, and intermediate code generation.

89809a42-0986-4ec9-adef-a85a61200639.definition: Method of inference from general rules to specific conclusions.

87f46bcd-e07d-4954-aed9-f7d67d203f9c.definition: Dynamic arrays can change size during program execution.

f4643a2a-954b-4b02-9870-f585738d121d.definition: How to define a subclass that inherits from a superclass, in object-oriented programming.

3536e49f-3f11-4426-9575-b95375a32f07.title: Variable Types
3536e49f-3f11-4426-9575-b95375a32f07.definition: Classify variables based on the type of data they store.

2a852aa1-ac67-47e4-bad0-fc5081f1408e.definition: The rules define the area in which a variable can be accessed in the program.

4ce215ea-f360-43f9-9559-e7ee3c7c6f90.definition: Mechanism for calling and executing a function in a program.

297ef6ed-a381-483d-89a4-53466742676a.title: Methods (Programming)

9113de38-3ef3-4bbe-81f3-fb32618bc5ab.definition: A system of communication paths used to transmit data between computer components.

0c2667b9-7ce4-451c-a0a8-18db29b28aaf.title: Register
0c2667b9-7ce4-451c-a0a8-18db29b28aaf.definition: Small, high-speed memory cells inside the CPU are used to temporarily store data during processing.

bacb0609-d753-46da-87e1-48233261a306.title: Cache Memory
bacb0609-d753-46da-87e1-48233261a306.definition: Small, high-speed memory is used to store frequently accessed data to reduce main memory access time.

a2ce63db-052e-435d-8384-012658461e76.title: RAM
a2ce63db-052e-435d-8384-012658461e76.definition: Random access memory is the computer's main memory used to store running programs and data.

866ee336-94f3-4b85-be2a-2f558beccbd0.title: Secondary Memory
866ee336-94f3-4b85-be2a-2f558beccbd0.definition: Long-term and non-volatile data storage devices, such as hard drives, SSDs.

b352e3f3-42c2-4768-8763-93efe07a9069.title: CPU
b352e3f3-42c2-4768-8763-93efe07a9069.definition: The central processing unit, which is the 'brain' of the computer, performs most of the calculations and controls.

b637660a-0b59-47fc-8785-d2ab66f859c8.title: GPU
b637660a-0b59-47fc-8785-d2ab66f859c8.definition: Graphics processor, specialized for image and graphics processing, as well as parallel computing tasks.

8caed8d7-5afd-4a67-a97e-7120698a6803.title: Interrupt
8caed8d7-5afd-4a67-a97e-7120698a6803.definition: Signal sent to the CPU to pause the current job and handle an emergency event.

c374409f-866b-4b2e-a37c-5967d3134c8b.title: Threads
c374409f-866b-4b2e-a37c-5967d3134c8b.definition: The smallest unit of execution in a process, allowing a process to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.

d1bb56df-24f9-44a9-9304-d6dc441a6881.title: Interrupt-driven Programming
d1bb56df-24f9-44a9-9304-d6dc441a6881.definition: Programming method in which tasks are triggered and processed when an interrupt event occurs.

aa904e14-b0f3-483b-b7f4-a799396d0de0.title: Thread-based Programming
aa904e14-b0f3-483b-b7f4-a799396d0de0.definition: Programming method that uses multiple threads to execute different parts of a program simultaneously.

f3e540af-5117-40a3-8560-901806332214.title: OS Scheduling
f3e540af-5117-40a3-8560-901806332214.definition: The operating system function to manage and distribute CPU resources to processes or threads.

61ad45b0-1c00-4a5f-8d8d-76be1d346c80.title: Scheduling Priority
61ad45b0-1c00-4a5f-8d8d-76be1d346c80.definition: Technique of assigning priorities to processes or threads so that the operating system decides the order of execution.

1dc85400-4cba-42a9-b18d-e9059af567c3.title: Memory Fragmentation
1dc85400-4cba-42a9-b18d-e9059af567c3.definition: The state of memory being divided into many small, non-consecutive blocks, leading to wasted space even though the total capacity is free.

4304806f-c0d7-4f02-bc0d-291ffe6e9a1c.title: Latency
4304806f-c0d7-4f02-bc0d-291ffe6e9a1c.definition: The delay between the request for an activity and the start or completion of that activity.

801eee21-b2de-442b-a9b0-ff3dfb92a860.title: Networking Basics
801eee21-b2de-442b-a9b0-ff3dfb92a860.definition: Core unit of knowledge on the fundamentals of networking and communications, including the importance of networking, Internet architecture, switching techniques, layering, network components, and queuing concepts. This is a CS Core unit with 2.5 class hours.

cb1d342b-5457-4d88-bdab-6efb0d48c697.title: Network Importance
cb1d342b-5457-4d88-bdab-6efb0d48c697.definition: understand the central role networks play in modern computing systems and their contributions to everyday life, as well as the transformation they bring.

cada733a-fcf5-4bd2-937a-28c3e2daab0f.title: Networking Challenges
cada733a-fcf5-4bd2-937a-28c3e2daab0f.definition: understand current and future challenges in designing, deploying, managing, and securing large-scale and complex network systems.

1a63531d-5757-47ea-81f7-42af1faf1720.title: Internet Organization
1a63531d-5757-47ea-81f7-42af1faf1720.definition: Describes the overall structure and organization of the Internet, including its major components and their relationships.

640a5407-67b1-4434-b3b5-f5b14b827e65.title: Internet Users
640a5407-67b1-4434-b3b5-f5b14b827e65.definition: understand the role of end users in the Internet ecosystem and how they interact with network services and resources.

cbab72ea-2bd7-4130-b840-7b9142969513.title: ISP
cbab72ea-2bd7-4130-b840-7b9142969513.definition: Learn about the functions, roles and types of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) in providing network connectivity.

75122314-b323-4d60-b39b-43d3cdac9561.title: Autonomous System (AS)
75122314-b323-4d60-b39b-43d3cdac9561.definition: Concept and role of Autonomous Systems (AS) as independent administrative units participating in the global routing structure of the Internet.

8fa654e6-c6f0-416a-af65-b9f3a446d22e.title: Content Providers
8fa654e6-c6f0-416a-af65-b9f3a446d22e.definition: understand the role of content providers in creating, storing and distributing information and services on the Internet.

d6fc9e5f-05f9-4ab0-9b3e-472f08ed4a4e.title: CDN
d6fc9e5f-05f9-4ab0-9b3e-472f08ed4a4e.definition: Concepts, benefits, and basic operations of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) in increasing the speed and efficiency of web content delivery.

ebf0abe9-bcc6-470c-a49f-fdcc7970982a.title: Switching Techniques
ebf0abe9-bcc6-470c-a49f-fdcc7970982a.definition: Overview of the basic methods for transferring data over a network, including circuit switching and packet switching.

22325976-5d18-4a0f-9811-0d9db510b348.title: Circuit Switching
22325976-5d18-4a0f-9811-0d9db510b348.definition: Principle and application of circuit switching technique, where a dedicated path is permanently established for a communication session.

b0d71fbc-ede5-4770-ae06-74bebe8537b4.title: Packet Switching
b0d71fbc-ede5-4770-ae06-74bebe8537b4.definition: Principles and applications of packet switching technology, where data is divided into small packets and transmitted independently over the network.

87780ea3-df17-4fea-9b61-b8768f717dbd.title: Network Layers
87780ea3-df17-4fea-9b61-b8768f717dbd.definition: understand the network's layered architecture (for example, TCP/IP or OSI model) and the specific roles and functions of each layer.

a14f4c41-0262-463e-890b-c6fd0b3e2f22.title: Application Layer
a14f4c41-0262-463e-890b-c6fd0b3e2f22.definition: Functions and protocols of the application layer, where software applications interact directly with the network to provide services to users.

5fae9c25-49be-4eb2-b148-e51d068d9209.title: Transport Layer
5fae9c25-49be-4eb2-b148-e51d068d9209.definition: Transport layer functions and protocols, responsible for reliable or unreliable data transfer between processes on different hosts.

495c27f1-775b-46e9-af00-e34c4eb8f072.title: Network Layer
495c27f1-775b-46e9-af00-e34c4eb8f072.definition: Network layer functions and protocols, responsible for routing packets across the network from source to final destination.

ce6044a7-45dc-4330-ac1d-b835b4cb8611.title: Datalink Layer
ce6044a7-45dc-4330-ac1d-b835b4cb8611.definition: Functions and protocols of the data link layer, responsible for transmitting data frames between devices on the same local network (single-hop).

f54ef5be-f31f-4feb-95ed-1613d25f2e4c.title: Physical Layer
f54ef5be-f31f-4feb-95ed-1613d25f2e4c.definition: The function of the physical layer, responsible for transmitting raw data bits over a physical transmission medium (e.g., cable, radio waves).

3905e7d1-6ca0-459e-9b92-88cee7422786.title: Layering Principles
3905e7d1-6ca0-459e-9b92-88cee7422786.definition: understand the fundamental principles behind layered architecture in networks, including the benefits of abstraction and separation of functions.

68db7297-f9db-498e-b870-09513173c157.title: Network Encapsulation
68db7297-f9db-498e-b870-09513173c157.definition: Data encapsulation principle, where data from a higher layer is encapsulated with the current layer's header (and footer) when transmitted to lower layers.

11912078-af63-47be-a10a-ca0f3dbd1ef6.title: Internet Hourglass Model
11912078-af63-47be-a10a-ca0f3dbd1ef6.definition: Describes the hourglass model of the Internet protocol suite, highlighting the IP layer as the common core, supporting many technologies on the lower layer and many applications on the upper layer.

5605839b-4762-436e-bd2d-0575d3088d03.title: Network Components
5605839b-4762-436e-bd2d-0575d3088d03.definition: Identify and differentiate the basic types of devices and components that make up a computer network.

0cc8d1aa-2574-48a4-931b-246483ca48a2.title: Router
0cc8d1aa-2574-48a4-931b-246483ca48a2.definition: The function and operating principle of a router is to connect subnets and forward packets between them.

d198cf76-c9a4-43c6-b8b1-31c9438098c9.title: Switches
d198cf76-c9a4-43c6-b8b1-31c9438098c9.definition: The function and operating principle of a switch in connecting devices on the same local area network (LAN) effectively.

d67dddfb-07c9-47dc-afae-92dc8e4df049.title: Hubs
d67dddfb-07c9-47dc-afae-92dc8e4df049.definition: The function and limitations of a concentrator are as a basic networking device, operating at the physical layer.

af096ab7-245b-4d07-8bae-aa1dda24a719.title: Access Points (APs)
af096ab7-245b-4d07-8bae-aa1dda24a719.definition: The function of a wireless access point is to allow wireless devices to connect to a wired network.

d7054f79-18c1-4700-8ae5-b279f1dee62a.title: Hosts
d7054f79-18c1-4700-8ae5-b279f1dee62a.definition: The role of terminal devices such as computers, servers, smartphones, etc., in computer networks.

3b61f6b8-3e31-47d8-9e2f-f676edc4214f.title: Network Queueing
3b61f6b8-3e31-47d8-9e2f-f676edc4214f.definition: understand the basic concepts of queuing in networks and how they affect network performance.

23282ce7-fabe-4eb5-94d2-5d1e9a89f6a7.title: Queueing & Latency
23282ce7-fabe-4eb5-94d2-5d1e9a89f6a7.definition: analyze how wait times in the queues of network devices (e.g., routers) contribute to the overall latency of data transmission.

ad255f43-890f-4b85-827e-f5bee5ade8c9.title: Queueing & Congestion
ad255f43-890f-4b85-827e-f5bee5ade8c9.definition: understand how overqueuing and buffer overflow lead to network congestion and performance degradation.

123712c7-6997-4fed-835e-e2e9cb1abc1a.title: Queueing & QoS
123712c7-6997-4fed-835e-e2e9cb1abc1a.definition: Explore how priority and queue management policies can affect the level of service (QoS) provided to different types of network traffic.

7cc7f2d4-f110-489d-9849-60e5926a9548.title: Network Applications
7cc7f2d4-f110-489d-9849-60e5926a9548.definition: Core unit of knowledge about network applications, how they work, and the impact of network structures and protocols on the behavior of distributed applications. This is a CS Core unit with 3.5 hours of study.

162d3d82-6734-42ba-b1ff-e71f5030c956.title: Reliability Support
162d3d82-6734-42ba-b1ff-e71f5030c956.definition: Core unit of knowledge on the mechanisms and principles that ensure reliability in network communications, including error control, flow control, and congestion control. This is a KA Core unit with 5.75 hours of study.

30e0bce8-76fa-4428-a9c7-5a58e4407f0b.title: Routing & Forwarding
30e0bce8-76fa-4428-a9c7-5a58e4407f0b.definition: Core unit of knowledge on the principles and techniques of routing (determining paths) and forwarding (moving packets) in networks. This is a KA Core unit with 4 hours of study.

72b12eb1-51bc-4328-9515-184cef603bdc.title: Single-Hop Communication
72b12eb1-51bc-4328-9515-184cef603bdc.definition: Core unit of knowledge on the fundamentals of direct communication between two devices within a single network link. This is a KA Core unit with 3 class hours.

fd6ec2ea-e5dd-468d-adc6-871f02a6d01e.title: Mobility Support
fd6ec2ea-e5dd-468d-adc6-871f02a6d01e.definition: Core unit of knowledge on the concepts and technologies that support mobility in networks, including device-to-device communication and multi-hop wireless networks. This is a KA Core unit with 4 hours of study.

2097dae8-1fbe-4e94-8695-6f990c4e81a1.title: Network Security
2097dae8-1fbe-4e94-8695-6f990c4e81a1.definition: Core unit of knowledge on security aspects of computer networks, including threats, countermeasures and access control. This is a KA Core unit with 2.25 hours of study.

69783542-ae54-4e2c-bccc-3f87602c240b.title: Emerging Topics
69783542-ae54-4e2c-bccc-3f87602c240b.definition: Core units of knowledge on cutting-edge and evolving topics in networking and communications, such as network virtualization, quantum networks, and middleboxes. This is a KA Core unit with 4 hours of study.

6c448280-877c-4d77-b171-cf0c809bcc4d.title: Proprietary Networks
6c448280-877c-4d77-b171-cf0c809bcc4d.definition: The existence and role of large networks owned and operated by specific companies or organizations, often used for distributed computing, storage, and private content distribution.

6e6aed44-deca-412c-b49a-16694dbf6925.title: Distributed Computing
6e6aed44-deca-412c-b49a-16694dbf6925.definition: The concept of distributed computing, where tasks are broken down and performed across multiple computers in a network to achieve a common goal.

b9dcc2d5-a87a-46bd-b6aa-5dce6ad0854a.title: Network Storage
b9dcc2d5-a87a-46bd-b6aa-5dce6ad0854a.definition: Data storage solutions and technologies are accessed and managed over the network, allowing resources and data to be shared.

94960c75-467d-4116-a43b-46718bb73460.title: Content Delivery
