94960c75-467d-4116-a43b-46718bb73460.definition: The methods and systems used to deliver content (e.g., videos, web pages, data) to end users efficiently and quickly.

99b7685a-93d1-4ffc-b192-0cd39ba10b21.title: Satellite Networks
99b7685a-93d1-4ffc-b192-0cd39ba10b21.definition: The technology and applications of the network use satellites to provide connectivity, especially to areas that are remote or difficult to reach through traditional infrastructure.

ca85000d-af94-4104-8ac7-ee65902a0353.title: D2D Communication
ca85000d-af94-4104-8ac7-ee65902a0353.definition: Principles and applications of direct communication between devices without the need for an access point or central server, commonly found in IoT.

9f9c694c-0907-4c73-b1ea-dc6112b19abd.title: IoT
9f9c694c-0907-4c73-b1ea-dc6112b19abd.definition: The concept of a network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other objects embedded with sensors, software, and other technologies to connect and exchange data.

3f98922c-ce7c-40f3-aaa1-796d6d76fd5f.title: Network Naming
3f98922c-ce7c-40f3-aaa1-796d6d76fd5f.definition: Systems and methods used to name and identify resources or devices in a network, allowing them to be easily addressed and accessed.

203a1433-8b82-4e80-b99d-2356e5d3028d.title: Network Addressing
203a1433-8b82-4e80-b99d-2356e5d3028d.definition: Protocols and techniques used to assign and manage addresses (e.g., IP addresses, MAC addresses) to network devices, allowing routing and forwarding of data.

5ba4cd44-7e9d-4562-9a2b-8e72cb3fb78f.title: Network Reliability
5ba4cd44-7e9d-4562-9a2b-8e72cb3fb78f.definition: Principles and mechanisms that ensure that data is transmitted over a network accurately, completely, and in order, despite errors or interruptions.

96a52eac-a683-4918-bf9e-062bca1fb151.title: Error Control
96a52eac-a683-4918-bf9e-062bca1fb151.definition: Techniques are used to detect and correct errors that occur during data transmission over the network, ensuring data integrity.

5db77ed0-2839-4f71-ab0e-5bb0473f8d01.title: Flow Control
5db77ed0-2839-4f71-ab0e-5bb0473f8d01.definition: Mechanisms regulate the data transfer rate between sender and receiver to prevent the sender from overwhelming the receiver with too much data, avoiding packet loss.

1086c6d8-7c40-4970-b367-584ddf838f02.title: Congestion Control
1086c6d8-7c40-4970-b367-584ddf838f02.definition: Techniques to prevent and resolve network congestion, where data traffic exceeds the processing capacity of network links or nodes, to maintain stable performance.

dde20675-2100-4c4c-9ac4-7ff0c5419670.title: Domain Hierarchy
dde20675-2100-4c4c-9ac4-7ff0c5419670.definition: The hierarchical structure of the domain name system (Domain Name System - DNS) and how it organizes the management and resolution of domain names into IP addresses.

a8c1df7b-0741-4dcb-97f4-0fe8c9b2cb1a.title: Routing
a8c1df7b-0741-4dcb-97f4-0fe8c9b2cb1a.definition: The process of determining the best path for data packets from source to destination across a network linking different networks, using routing protocols.

7649cf2d-3f0d-4deb-8c8c-9c0fee039d4c.title: Packet Forwarding
7649cf2d-3f0d-4deb-8c8c-9c0fee039d4c.definition: The act of moving a data packet from an input port of a router or switch to an appropriate output port, based on routing information.

aef3fadf-769b-43d0-b6a6-a0e6a4bd0734.title: Modulation
aef3fadf-769b-43d0-b6a6-a0e6a4bd0734.definition: The process of transforming one or more properties of a carrier wave (for example, amplitude, frequency, phase) according to an information signal to transmit data over a transmission channel.

f8345641-5c07-4717-bf08-27158ae1704f.title: Network Encoding
f8345641-5c07-4717-bf08-27158ae1704f.definition: The process of converting data into a signal form suitable for transmission over a physical communication channel, including transmission encoding schemes.

89c14940-faa1-40ea-af4e-1c387663f30f.title: Network Framing
89c14940-faa1-40ea-af4e-1c387663f30f.definition: The process of packaging data bits into frames at the data link layer, including adding control and address bits for transmission over a specific physical link.

65244b2f-d141-48c2-a69c-b5bf3d2fd77c.title: Network Access Control
65244b2f-d141-48c2-a69c-b5bf3d2fd77c.definition: Mechanisms and policies to restrict access to network resources (e.g. servers, data, services) to authorized users or devices.

7e37e61d-2a92-4561-b83b-4552dfa8fa44.title: Network Security
7e37e61d-2a92-4561-b83b-4552dfa8fa44.definition: Overview of principles, technologies, and practices for protecting computer networks and data from threats, attacks, and unauthorized access.

1a712c16-13d0-4c92-a4e2-828888ffe760.title: Security Threats
1a712c16-13d0-4c92-a4e2-828888ffe760.definition: Identify and classify common types of threats to cybersecurity, e.g., denial of service (DoS) attacks, malware, intrusions, phishing.

54fca5a1-24cc-44ea-9088-5bb85521ff56.title: Security Countermeasures
54fca5a1-24cc-44ea-9088-5bb85521ff56.definition: Strategies, tools, and techniques used to minimize risk and protect networks from threats (e.g., firewalls, encryption, VPNs, intrusion detection/prevention systems).

0ad1cec8-7de7-4f55-aec7-d9b1d213e53a.title: Multi-hop Wireless
0ad1cec8-7de7-4f55-aec7-d9b1d213e53a.definition: The concept of a wireless network where data is transmitted through multiple intermediate nodes (multi-hop) before reaching the final destination, typically in ad-hoc or sensor networks.

e72f8a43-3ebd-404c-8f8e-4a551ee214b3.title: Network Virtualization
e72f8a43-3ebd-404c-8f8e-4a551ee214b3.definition: The principle and technology enable the creation of independent and isolated logical networks on the same physical network infrastructure, providing flexibility and efficiency.

bd1cf606-85f0-49c6-99f7-85f30c379508.title: Quantum Networking
bd1cf606-85f0-49c6-99f7-85f30c379508.definition: Basic concepts of quantum networks, using quantum mechanical principles for secure communication (e.g., quantum key distribution), and developing new applications in computing.

a2b00da8-5900-46ea-8647-046a1dbfbb7f.title: Middleboxes
a2b00da8-5900-46ea-8647-046a1dbfbb7f.definition: Devices or network functions that perform additional packet processing services beyond basic routing or forwarding, for example, firewalls, network address translators (NATs), load balancers.

eece7b23-7085-4a19-a010-fe399ad0952b.title: SDN
eece7b23-7085-4a19-a010-fe399ad0952b.definition: The concept of SDN, where the network control plane is decoupled from the data plane, enables flexible network configuration and management through centralized software.

565bc4da-c4a3-400b-abb9-ddbb3fac0409.title: Naming & Addressing Schemes
565bc4da-c4a3-400b-abb9-ddbb3fac0409.definition: Describes the principles and techniques used to name and address network resources, including systems such as DNS and Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs).

0f1b680e-0a70-4184-a2b5-7e51016bee23.title: DNS
0f1b680e-0a70-4184-a2b5-7e51016bee23.definition: understand the function, structure, and operation of the Domain Name System (DNS) in translating domain names into IP addresses.

9f42b8c3-5669-4408-b765-9b5ef148182b.title: URIs
9f42b8c3-5669-4408-b765-9b5ef148182b.definition: Learn about the concept, syntax, and purpose of Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in identifying resources on a network.

f90f8aaa-898d-4ea6-9aaa-bc070b25bc54.title: Distributed Application Models
f90f8aaa-898d-4ea6-9aaa-bc070b25bc54.definition: Describes the basic architectural models for distributed applications, including how they interact and distribute work across multiple systems.

336bbafa-ec09-4875-87e2-fbc5da72b1b8.title: Client-Server Model
336bbafa-ec09-4875-87e2-fbc5da72b1b8.definition: understand the client/server architecture, in which the client requests a service from the server and the server provides that service.

43d5a19d-0a5a-4954-b41d-7fefdb0ade24.title: P2P Model
43d5a19d-0a5a-4954-b41d-7fefdb0ade24.definition: Learn about the P2P model, where nodes in the network can act as both clients and servers.

28eba163-25d6-487e-9915-234d4685366a.title: Cloud Computing Model
28eba163-25d6-487e-9915-234d4685366a.definition: The concept of cloud computing, services and architecture related to the provision of computing resources over a network.

fbce21ef-5162-48aa-938e-869e579165aa.title: Edge Computing
fbce21ef-5162-48aa-938e-869e579165aa.definition: understand edge computing, where data is processed closer to its source rather than sent to a cloud data center.

db6368da-9f6d-4259-8a8f-d5e74dfa84ba.title: Fog Computing
db6368da-9f6d-4259-8a8f-d5e74dfa84ba.definition: The concept of fog computing, an intermediate layer between edge and cloud computing, extends cloud services closer to the edge of the network.

beb49799-a1ac-46a2-ba85-65c6532d8be1.title: Network App Requirements
beb49799-a1ac-46a2-ba85-65c6532d8be1.definition: analyze the various requirements that network applications place on the network, including quality of service (QoS) factors.

38bba485-c2f0-473e-9260-8be0716d5487.title: Latency
38bba485-c2f0-473e-9260-8be0716d5487.definition: Impact of network latency on performance and user experience of applications.

9b034364-678b-44c4-8713-39f4f137178a.title: Bandwidth
9b034364-678b-44c4-8713-39f4f137178a.definition: The importance of network bandwidth for the data transfer ability of applications.

3aaa133f-b09d-4607-b118-249d38b00ac1.title: Fault Tolerance
3aaa133f-b09d-4607-b118-249d38b00ac1.definition: The degree to which applications can operate acceptably in the presence of packet loss in the network.

26d79406-e69c-49f2-a36f-aa29ef1223d4.title: Application Layer Protocols
26d79406-e69c-49f2-a36f-aa29ef1223d4.definition: Overview of the roles and functions of protocols operating at the application layer in network architecture.

56f283ac-80c5-46aa-97da-8898b9d5f07f.title: HTTP
56f283ac-80c5-46aa-97da-8898b9d5f07f.definition: Details about the HTTP protocol, how it works in exchanging data on the World Wide Web.

d52d894d-66c0-480b-a452-436f3e445cc6.title: TCP, UDP, Socket API Interaction
d52d894d-66c0-480b-a452-436f3e445cc6.definition: understand how network applications use transport layer protocols (TCP, UDP) and application programming interfaces (Socket APIs) to send and receive data.

e90d7b31-d7a1-4c64-8da8-909839d9d5b1.title: TCP
e90d7b31-d7a1-4c64-8da8-909839d9d5b1.definition: TCP's role as a reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol.

52bef64b-16d3-4871-9fc1-2a594e4db969.title: UDP
52bef64b-16d3-4871-9fc1-2a594e4db969.definition: UDP's role as an unreliable, connection-oriented transport protocol.

fb762d7c-7cb3-468f-a6f7-8c27fda1d128.title: Socket API
fb762d7c-7cb3-468f-a6f7-8c27fda1d128.definition: How to use Socket APIs for network programming, creating applications that communicate over the network.

a6a37141-3600-4cdc-9e92-bd2511b23718.title: Unreliable Delivery
a6a37141-3600-4cdc-9e92-bd2511b23718.definition: The concept of transmitting data without mechanisms to ensure arrival, order, or non-duplication, is commonly found in protocols such as UDP.

e3190dab-1da1-4a11-8331-6ef31379f85d.title: Network Reliability Principles
e3190dab-1da1-4a11-8331-6ef31379f85d.definition: The fundamentals for achieving reliability in network communications, including ensuring data is not lost, is not duplicated, and arrives in the correct order.

96f8076f-fada-4a46-94de-f40db6d9f004.title: Error Control
96f8076f-fada-4a46-94de-f40db6d9f004.definition: Techniques used to detect and correct errors during data transmission over a network.

73681fba-dfdf-4a4a-9686-59365a3e9eef.title: Data Retransmission
73681fba-dfdf-4a4a-9686-59365a3e9eef.definition: Mechanism to retransmit lost or corrupted data packets to ensure reliability.

5acc53d6-70de-458a-aad6-807a27d4a666.title: Error Correction
5acc53d6-70de-458a-aad6-807a27d4a666.definition: Data encryption methods so that the original data can be restored even if errors occur during transmission.

44b07af4-088d-4915-9f4e-0ac3fb3f6754.title: Flow Control
44b07af4-088d-4915-9f4e-0ac3fb3f6754.definition: Techniques that regulate the rate at which data is sent between two devices to prevent the recipient from being overloaded.

bd5803f1-f91c-458a-87a6-e5b1939ecc3f.title: Stop and Wait Flow Control
bd5803f1-f91c-458a-87a6-e5b1939ecc3f.definition: A simple flow control method in which the sender waits for acknowledgment from the receiver after each data packet.

4c932fd4-8add-4c73-b3a5-17250d1b4563.title: Window-Based Flow Control
4c932fd4-8add-4c73-b3a5-17250d1b4563.definition: The flow control method allows multiple data packets to be sent at the same time before receiving an acknowledgment, using the sliding window concept.

fad2c73c-bacc-4a66-b886-0a70f8f89a1c.title: Congestion Control
fad2c73c-bacc-4a66-b886-0a70f8f89a1c.definition: Strategies are used to prevent and handle congestion in the network to maintain performance.

4903cba3-3e27-4a6e-b294-cba9f71a8d82.title: Implicit Congestion Notification
4903cba3-3e27-4a6e-b294-cba9f71a8d82.definition: Detect congestion through indirect signs such as packet loss or increased latency.

a49dde75-76bd-40d2-8231-dec2b2c76319.title: ECN
a49dde75-76bd-40d2-8231-dec2b2c76319.definition: The mechanism allows routers to directly notify the sender of congestion without dropping the packet.

46eb56e6-a894-4672-b09a-1fd039ff16b9.title: TCP Performance Issues
46eb56e6-a894-4672-b09a-1fd039ff16b9.definition: Study the challenges and ways to optimize TCP protocol performance in different network environments.

a731c54f-d96f-4c29-9899-e3dbe8f4ab8d.title: TCP Tahoe
a731c54f-d96f-4c29-9899-e3dbe8f4ab8d.definition: One of the first versions of the TCP congestion control algorithm, including slow start, congestion avoidance, and fast recovery phases.

bf00d8f8-b799-4153-8632-a9930b523048.title: TCP Reno
bf00d8f8-b799-4153-8632-a9930b523048.definition: Upgraded version of TCP Tahoe, improving fast recovery after small packet loss.

bc06dd25-a640-4783-9ea8-91dd77a40b93.title: TCP Vegas
bc06dd25-a640-4783-9ea8-91dd77a40b93.definition: The TCP congestion control algorithm uses queuing delay to detect congestion early, instead of waiting for packet loss.

cb4ea000-e1d0-4075-9a82-ed5b11c33187.title: TCP CUBIC
cb4ea000-e1d0-4075-9a82-ed5b11c33187.definition: Modern TCP congestion control algorithm, designed to operate efficiently on high bandwidth and high latency networks.

71de88f6-690b-4fdf-99be-5bed218abf7c.title: Routing Models & Hierarchy
71de88f6-690b-4fdf-99be-5bed218abf7c.definition: Overview of the methods and hierarchies used to route packets in computer networks.

98b9bd85-967d-4934-aa64-40e35ca54ca2.title: Intra-Domain Routing
98b9bd85-967d-4934-aa64-40e35ca54ca2.definition: Routing protocols and techniques are used within a single Autonomous System (AS) domain.

dd3d5990-c873-4052-b51f-3a9b98f98944.title: Inter-Domain Routing
dd3d5990-c873-4052-b51f-3a9b98f98944.definition: Routing protocols and techniques are used to exchange routing information between different autonomous domains.

1c5b5b32-ab53-4d6c-9d07-413fd547ff6a.title: Centralized Routing
1c5b5b32-ab53-4d6c-9d07-413fd547ff6a.definition: Routing method in which a single central entity is responsible for calculating and distributing routes.

088024ec-e745-43e2-aa7f-f4a74684a421.title: Decentralized Routing
088024ec-e745-43e2-aa7f-f4a74684a421.definition: Routing method in which each router calculates its own routes based on local information and information exchanged with neighboring routers.

29869a28-36e2-4aa3-90e0-f693bd246921.title: Source Routing
29869a28-36e2-4aa3-90e0-f693bd246921.definition: A routing technique in which the sender specifies all or part of the path that the packet will take.

47f028a2-eacd-48af-8575-a3c0d7d32196.title: Virtual Circuit
47f028a2-eacd-48af-8575-a3c0d7d32196.definition: The concept of a pre-established logical path through the network for a data flow, ensuring some level of quality of service.

27ade489-9b26-4fdb-a383-06b768840846.title: QoS Routing
27ade489-9b26-4fdb-a383-06b768840846.definition: Routing is based on quality of service requirements such as bandwidth, latency, and packet loss.

61fe210d-2145-4bfb-969c-be9897b822c3.title: Network Forwarding Methods
61fe210d-2145-4bfb-969c-be9897b822c3.definition: The techniques and mechanisms that routers use to forward packets from the input port to the appropriate output port.

1234648d-3dda-46d5-8f88-b67ef244f35c.title: Forwarding Table
1234648d-3dda-46d5-8f88-b67ef244f35c.definition: The data structure that the router uses to store destination and output port information for packets.

651eda35-c40a-46d1-9a57-b94fe360ad41.title: Forwarding Match Algorithms
651eda35-c40a-46d1-9a57-b94fe360ad41.definition: Algorithms are used to look up the packet's destination address in the forwarding table and determine the appropriate output port.

cadd9d04-339c-4ad0-b046-1347b60ca7a7.title: IP Scalability Issues
cadd9d04-339c-4ad0-b046-1347b60ca7a7.definition: Research into Internet Protocol (IP) and scalability challenges as the Internet evolves, along with applicable solutions.

015b145c-b11d-4679-8e9d-410abfcedfe6.title: NAT
015b145c-b11d-4679-8e9d-410abfcedfe6.definition: The mechanism allows multiple devices in a private network to share a single public IP address, helping to solve the problem of IPv4 address exhaustion.

058a7fbb-44e4-48f4-b403-16fc75dcf05f.title: CIDR
058a7fbb-44e4-48f4-b403-16fc75dcf05f.definition: A more flexible method of IP address allocation and route aggregation to improve routing efficiency and reduce routing table size.

5d776198-9932-4d26-9379-48c894f327a5.title: BGP
5d776198-9932-4d26-9379-48c894f327a5.definition: The primary inter-domain routing protocol used on the Internet to exchange routing information between autonomous domains.

bfb2edca-8ec5-476f-9aa0-6f1518cee92d.title: IP Versions
bfb2edca-8ec5-476f-9aa0-6f1518cee92d.definition: Compare and differentiate between versions of the Internet Protocol, mainly IPv4 and IPv6, in terms of addressing structure, features, and extensibility.

4a835f85-7655-4484-9a87-406d1f83fa35.title: IPv4
4a835f85-7655-4484-9a87-406d1f83fa35.definition: Details about the structure, packet format, and working mechanism of IPv4, the most popular version of IP.

e63da48c-6178-4456-b38f-d6b414061e4c.title: IPv6
e63da48c-6178-4456-b38f-d6b414061e4c.definition: Details of the structure, packet format and operating mechanism of IPv6, designed to replace IPv4 and solve the problem of address exhaustion.

74f637c1-88fe-40f1-adc8-e52d3eb1478e.title: Modulation Intro
74f637c1-88fe-40f1-adc8-e52d3eb1478e.definition: Basic concepts of modulation, the process of transforming information signals for transmission through physical media.

2bb748cc-04c7-4cdb-8cf3-9a7f5991467c.title: Media Bandwidth
2bb748cc-04c7-4cdb-8cf3-9a7f5991467c.definition: The concept of bandwidth is the maximum capacity of a channel to transmit data on a communication environment.

a1435bf1-d85d-4ae7-ac8d-1e058fd9264a.title: Transmission Media
a1435bf1-d85d-4ae7-ac8d-1e058fd9264a.definition: Different types of physical media are used to transmit network signals, for example copper cables, fiber optic cables, radio waves.

be90e593-4a94-497a-90be-3c6111874a3e.title: Data Encoding
be90e593-4a94-497a-90be-3c6111874a3e.definition: Methods of converting data into electrical or optical signals for transmission over a network.

173c55b7-2f97-41e9-8afb-b418a986525c.title: Framing
173c55b7-2f97-41e9-8afb-b418a986525c.definition: The process of dividing a data bit stream into separate frames for transmission over a physical channel, including adding a frame header and trailer.

c9c8c8bf-e6c4-4312-a194-04138e8ef6f0.title: MAC
c9c8c8bf-e6c4-4312-a194-04138e8ef6f0.definition: Protocols and rules govern how devices share the same communication medium to avoid conflicts.

9ff55892-b746-4b1b-a23d-ce36b34b8f7b.title: Random Access MAC
9ff55892-b746-4b1b-a23d-ce36b34b8f7b.definition: Media access methods allow devices to transfer data at any time, handling collisions if they occur (e.g. CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA).

d7668359-b5af-4181-b97f-a8d04a7c77fd.title: Scheduled Access MAC
d7668359-b5af-4181-b97f-a8d04a7c77fd.definition: Media access methods in which devices are authorized to transmit data according to a specific schedule, avoiding conflicts.

e4252588-96ee-4f30-8d07-d8376773bf2c.title: Ethernet
e4252588-96ee-4f30-8d07-d8376773bf2c.definition: Popular wired LAN standard, including different versions, frame structures, and operating mechanisms.

f3bc78bc-7621-4154-8cd9-91e7d3f42192.title: WiFi
f3bc78bc-7621-4154-8cd9-91e7d3f42192.definition: Wireless LAN standard (IEEE 802.11), including different operating modes, security, and versions.

d8359386-5227-411f-84b6-9f1bb4f7b915.title: Network Switching
d8359386-5227-411f-84b6-9f1bb4f7b915.definition: Operating mechanism of switching devices (switches) to forward data frames in the local network.

b2ecff81-f315-403f-9a65-c800cdd0e421.title: STP
b2ecff81-f315-403f-9a65-c800cdd0e421.definition: The protocol is used to prevent loops in an Ethernet switched network by creating a single spanning tree.

c70de50b-6c3e-469c-a5d6-e22933e84c1d.title: VLAN
c70de50b-6c3e-469c-a5d6-e22933e84c1d.definition: Concept of dividing a physical network into multiple logical networks (VLANs) to enhance security, performance, and management.

a102d659-5135-4c93-9d63-9b8dcd481503.title: LAN Topologies
a102d659-5135-4c93-9d63-9b8dcd481503.definition: Different physical and logical layouts of local area networks, affect performance and reliability.

f288cbc4-e373-45fb-918e-1f4665546b02.title: Data Center Network
f288cbc4-e373-45fb-918e-1f4665546b02.definition: The special architecture and requirements of the networks used in data centers to connect servers and storage devices.

6d1033dc-f84e-4523-8d27-70c6feeaf434.title: Campus Network
6d1033dc-f84e-4523-8d27-70c6feeaf434.definition: Network structure and management deployed over a limited geographic area such as a university campus or enterprise.

e6736408-0ace-4df0-888d-35475fec6597.title: Network Security
e6736408-0ace-4df0-888d-35475fec6597.definition: Basic concepts of cybersecurity, including types of threats, vulnerabilities, and common countermeasures.

bd7c6cff-44de-4f35-84ae-ff273a664c03.title: Network Threats & Attacks
bd7c6cff-44de-4f35-84ae-ff273a664c03.definition: analyze unique types of attacks and threats to network systems, how they operate, and their impact.

c46eb8e7-ca18-4c32-8c54-e30aeacb2f55.title: DoS Attack
c46eb8e7-ca18-4c32-8c54-e30aeacb2f55.definition: Attacks aim to overload systems or network services, making them unable to provide services to legitimate users.

d7693959-f7d2-4f75-8c1e-127b7a17df7c.title: Spoofing Attack
d7693959-f7d2-4f75-8c1e-127b7a17df7c.definition: Attacks in which an attacker impersonates a legitimate entity for fraud or unauthorized access.

c2ddad10-b3d0-4788-aaa8-8d8826733938.title: Sniffing Attack
c2ddad10-b3d0-4788-aaa8-8d8826733938.definition: Technique for gathering information by intercepting and analyzing network traffic passing through a point in the network.

d1f18076-b06f-405c-9313-0ee05383fb04.title: Traffic Redirection Attack
d1f18076-b06f-405c-9313-0ee05383fb04.definition: Attacks aim to redirect network traffic to an unwanted destination, often to intercept or modify data.

4b0e0366-4461-413b-aafd-6741dd522fff.title: MITM Attack
4b0e0366-4461-413b-aafd-6741dd522fff.definition: A type of attack in which an attacker intercepts and can modify communication between two parties without either party knowing.

c5267c58-aded-46dc-a66a-3222cc0d6c32.title: Message Integrity Attack
c5267c58-aded-46dc-a66a-3222cc0d6c32.definition: Attacks aim to modify or corrupt data during transmission to change the content or invalidate the message.

a9b07ef4-816d-4174-9cff-87f21e54ab7b.title: Routing Attack
a9b07ef4-816d-4174-9cff-87f21e54ab7b.definition: Attacks aim to manipulate routing information in the network to redirect traffic or cause congestion.

f74263b2-24e3-4052-bde9-0132c6c03eec.title: Ransomware
f74263b2-24e3-4052-bde9-0132c6c03eec.definition: The malware spreads through the network, encrypting data and demanding a ransom for decryption.

a091fed9-31dc-400f-a8f3-4c66cd987f04.title: Traffic Analysis Attack
a091fed9-31dc-400f-a8f3-4c66cd987f04.definition: Technique that monitors and analyzes network traffic patterns to deduce sensitive information without decrypting the content.

b55e7f74-0951-4e35-9348-f1202730ed84.title: Network Security Countermeasures
b55e7f74-0951-4e35-9348-f1202730ed84.definition: Collection of techniques, tools, and policies used to protect networks from threats and attacks.

73703338-ec5b-4143-bf84-e2b4e1a9d1ca.title: Network Cryptography
73703338-ec5b-4143-bf84-e2b4e1a9d1ca.definition: Application of cryptography to protect confidentiality, integrity and authentication in network communications.

b69acf30-df10-4841-b903-cc5cdc3483dd.title: SSL
b69acf30-df10-4841-b903-cc5cdc3483dd.definition: The security protocol was once used to establish secure communication channels over networks, a predecessor to TLS.

9c3735c5-717c-446f-8da3-6e5069cbcbb6.title: TLS
9c3735c5-717c-446f-8da3-6e5069cbcbb6.definition: Cryptographic protocols are used to provide communication security over computer networks, protecting the integrity and confidentiality of data.

1b75c0c7-bc8e-41a2-8b2b-02f5e32828c8.title: Symmetric Cryptography
1b75c0c7-bc8e-41a2-8b2b-02f5e32828c8.definition: Cryptographic algorithms use the same key for both encryption and decryption.

a94e2324-fa61-4699-aa3e-045fa6ba2d2b.title: Asymmetric Cryptography
a94e2324-fa61-4699-aa3e-045fa6ba2d2b.definition: Cryptographic algorithms use a pair of keys (public key and private key) for encryption and decryption.

2b3e8d94-7e79-49f4-aef3-ef0b681d22f3.title: Secure Network Architecture
2b3e8d94-7e79-49f4-aef3-ef0b681d22f3.definition: Architectural designs and models are used to build and deploy highly secure networks.

863e93b4-caa8-4ce1-93b8-6f69b5e0a046.title: Secure Channel
863e93b4-caa8-4ce1-93b8-6f69b5e0a046.definition: Communication channels are protected by encryption and other measures to ensure data security and integrity.

0afb40ed-64b0-4ffd-b306-b6c0ea12b27f.title: Secure Routing Protocol
0afb40ed-64b0-4ffd-b306-b6c0ea12b27f.definition: Routing protocols are designed with security mechanisms to protect against routing attacks.

fa88e487-148e-4cb6-98aa-520d3e3c8259.title: DNSSEC
fa88e487-148e-4cb6-98aa-520d3e3c8259.definition: Security measures are applied to DNS to protect the integrity and authenticity of DNS records.

8fa9080a-feb1-494b-baa5-b45a11bae012.title: VPN
8fa9080a-feb1-494b-baa5-b45a11bae012.definition: Technology that allows a secure connection to be made over a public network (such as the Internet) to access private network resources.

6c074d48-f38d-44a6-b3a8-6042b481a702.title: DMZ
6c074d48-f38d-44a6-b3a8-6042b481a702.definition: A physical or logical network segment that contains externally exposed services, designed to enhance the security of the internal network.

ecc6c3b4-bc2c-4f69-b896-47aa9edc5c34.title: ZTNA
ecc6c3b4-bc2c-4f69-b896-47aa9edc5c34.definition: A network security model based on the 'never trust, always verify' principle, requiring strict authentication and authorization for every access request.

880b91ea-084c-4f16-861a-83f13bb05ee0.title: Advanced Network Security
880b91ea-084c-4f16-861a-83f13bb05ee0.definition: Advanced cyber security concepts, often related to protection in highly distributed and complex environments.

1e2abd4e-4a8f-4572-965d-5e772ffbae32.title: Anonymous Communication Protocol
1e2abd4e-4a8f-4572-965d-5e772ffbae32.definition: Protocols are designed to protect the identities of users or parties participating in network communications.

86073a85-a07f-4eb6-abc7-5913d0eba904.title: Network Isolation
86073a85-a07f-4eb6-abc7-5913d0eba904.definition: Technique that separates parts of the network to limit the spread of attacks or unauthorized access.

0a5aa8ef-7810-459c-8a00-4c3fd7dba522.title: Network Monitoring
0a5aa8ef-7810-459c-8a00-4c3fd7dba522.definition: The process of monitoring and analyzing network traffic, performance, and events to detect unusual activity or threats.

1acb57e0-f534-45a9-81a3-8905d8cc382f.title: IDS
1acb57e0-f534-45a9-81a3-8905d8cc382f.definition: Systems monitor network and system activity to detect signs of attacks or policy violations.

8bb27d75-cc68-4c2e-ae80-1a697d18a353.title: Firewall
8bb27d75-cc68-4c2e-ae80-1a697d18a353.definition: Devices or software that control the flow of data into and out of a network based on defined security rules.

cd69fd3b-d027-4a69-bb1d-93685c3d6074.title: Anti-Spoofing Protection
cd69fd3b-d027-4a69-bb1d-93685c3d6074.definition: Techniques and measures to prevent attacks that spoof IP, MAC addresses, or other identifying information.

48f9c02c-6b3c-4cf0-ab9b-ee976d9ad366.title: DoS Protection
48f9c02c-6b3c-4cf0-ab9b-ee976d9ad366.definition: Measures and systems designed to detect, mitigate and prevent denial of service attacks.

9e8f3740-62b9-4fd0-bd7d-4a0bfb353969.title: Honeypots
9e8f3740-62b9-4fd0-bd7d-4a0bfb353969.definition: Systems or networks designed to attract and monitor attacker activity, gathering information about attack techniques.

d3978dda-4700-47ed-b8ec-401251a88097.title: Network Forensics
d3978dda-4700-47ed-b8ec-401251a88097.definition: Techniques and tools used to identify the origin of attacks or malicious traffic in a network.

743c3ebc-fd56-4be1-805d-93cc9d5119a0.title: BGPsec
743c3ebc-fd56-4be1-805d-93cc9d5119a0.definition: Security extensions to the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) to authenticate routing information and prevent routing attacks.

86574eea-6dae-4013-be64-e6b809a97aaf.title: RPKI
86574eea-6dae-4013-be64-e6b809a97aaf.definition: A public key-based system for authenticating ownership information of Internet resources (IP addresses and AS numbers), to enhance routing security.

b091d6be-082e-4da2-943e-a3dec80a9e29.title: Network Countermeasures
b091d6be-082e-4da2-943e-a3dec80a9e29.definition: Describes specific network-based countermeasures deployed to combat security threats.

e7045e6a-1960-4edc-8d3a-1c69fb8048e1.title: Network Security Case Studies
e7045e6a-1960-4edc-8d3a-1c69fb8048e1.definition: analyze different aspects of cyber security through real-life case studies.

4661271f-2408-4558-aa94-2e137b8b5f7a.title: Mobile Communication Principles
4661271f-2408-4558-aa94-2e137b8b5f7a.definition: The fundamentals of mobile communication, including technologies such as 4G and 5G.

e4717b1a-c84d-41d3-a3ad-1844a6632bd5.title: Mobile Communication Registration
e4717b1a-c84d-41d3-a3ad-1844a6632bd5.definition: Describe aspects of the registration process in mobile communication.

28effbf8-10f6-4cd8-9a35-6e8f0adcfd44.title: Wireless LAN Principles (802.11)
28effbf8-10f6-4cd8-9a35-6e8f0adcfd44.definition: The fundamentals of wireless local area networks, primarily focusing on the 802.11 (Wi-Fi) standard, including how to support mobile users.

76f1996e-8257-4cb1-8961-0352e3eb568f.title: Device-to-Device (D2D) Communication
76f1996e-8257-4cb1-8961-0352e3eb568f.definition: Principles of direct communication between devices, such as communication in IoT.

fde36cd2-c35a-4321-9522-b3345b6dc354.title: D2D Communication Applications
fde36cd2-c35a-4321-9522-b3345b6dc354.definition: Describe practical applications of direct communication between devices.

a94888ea-58dd-4790-bf7d-0eb78d7f54c7.title: Multi-hop Wireless Networks
a94888ea-58dd-4790-bf7d-0eb78d7f54c7.definition: The principles and architecture of wireless networks where data is transmitted over multiple hops, including ad hoc networks, opportunistic networks, and delay-tolerant networks.

80dbd447-acb6-466a-a46f-0768d4770eb6.title: Multi-hop Network Applications
80dbd447-acb6-466a-a46f-0768d4770eb6.definition: Describe practical applications of multihop wireless networks, such as ad hoc networks.

146d50f2-f70c-40db-9705-9b01e0a043b2.title: Middleboxes
146d50f2-f70c-40db-9705-9b01e0a043b2.definition: Intermediate network devices perform additional functions beyond basic routing, including advances in the use of AI, intent-based networking, filtering, deep packet inspection, load balancing, NAT, and CDN.

9df0983f-3e12-47b2-93ae-4d306dad403e.title: AI in Middleboxes
9df0983f-3e12-47b2-93ae-4d306dad403e.definition: Advances in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in intermediate network devices.

fe13e4de-e5bb-4e29-b231-9f71b4840414.title: Intent-Based Networking (IBN)
fe13e4de-e5bb-4e29-b231-9f71b4840414.definition: The concept and principles of intent-based networking enable network management through business objectives rather than specific device configurations.

4a4de4d5-0914-4365-bcb4-8ceb48bb6cf0.title: Packet Filtering
4a4de4d5-0914-4365-bcb4-8ceb48bb6cf0.definition: Packet filtering is performed by intermediate network devices for traffic control or security.

825095fe-9cda-43cf-ab21-d288b6a2934b.title: Deep Packet Inspection (DPI)
825095fe-9cda-43cf-ab21-d288b6a2934b.definition: Technique that examines the detailed content of network packets to perform security, traffic management, or analysis functions.

39488db5-22de-409e-b22d-a3ed9a618814.title: Load Balancing
39488db5-22de-409e-b22d-a3ed9a618814.definition: The function of distributing network traffic among multiple servers or resources to optimize usage and avoid overload, performed by intermediate network devices.

e926858c-87ad-4a9a-9e47-e1ae52e7fbd4.title: Network Address Translation (NAT)
e926858c-87ad-4a9a-9e47-e1ae52e7fbd4.definition: The technique of mapping private IP addresses to public IP addresses, and vice versa, is used to preserve IP addresses and provide a basic layer of security.

8f498277-5184-4af3-9e54-811056af11ae.title: Content Delivery Network (CDN)
8f498277-5184-4af3-9e54-811056af11ae.definition: The server system distributes web and multimedia content to end users based on geographical location, to increase access speed and reduce load on the origin server.

13907635-81e7-4b23-a44b-34eeeb842c94.title: Network Virtualization
13907635-81e7-4b23-a44b-34eeeb842c94.definition: Concepts and principles of network virtualization, including technologies such as SDN and data center networks.

a6cec37b-abe1-4321-b96b-7cdf6e10bb49.title: Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
a6cec37b-abe1-4321-b96b-7cdf6e10bb49.definition: The network architecture separates the control plane from the data plane, allowing flexible network management and configuration through software.

e6b9dfaf-779d-4e97-ae57-07a7dfdc7660.title: Data Center Networking
e6b9dfaf-779d-4e97-ae57-07a7dfdc7660.definition: Network architecture and technology specifically designed for data centers to support high traffic and virtualized applications.

412ff052-3842-42e3-bb6d-76882235ffa1.title: Quantum Networks
412ff052-3842-42e3-bb6d-76882235ffa1.definition: An introduction to the field of quantum networks, including concepts such as quantum teleportation, quantum security, and the quantum Internet.

d820f327-d7de-46ac-9e33-0f7582c10920.title: Quantum Teleportation
d820f327-d7de-46ac-9e33-0f7582c10920.definition: The concept of quantum teleportation in the context of quantum networks.

f5b3e923-373b-4686-ad27-7f71c9e9e71b.title: Quantum Network Security
f5b3e923-373b-4686-ad27-7f71c9e9e71b.definition: Security issues and solutions related to quantum networks.

ee8ab3c4-8f31-4405-81c5-dd03c5d7ceac.title: Quantum Internet
ee8ab3c4-8f31-4405-81c5-dd03c5d7ceac.definition: The concept and potential of an Internet based on quantum principles.

de9dc27f-88e6-439b-9c98-14a67f85d357.title: Satellite Communication
de9dc27f-88e6-439b-9c98-14a67f85d357.definition: Principles and applications of satellite communication.

40e31fcd-b33d-4e7c-ad5c-581891df1e03.title: Millimeter Wave (mmWave) Communication
40e31fcd-b33d-4e7c-ad5c-581891df1e03.definition: Wireless communication technology uses the millimeter wave band, often used in 5G.

97c67b8e-96de-4368-bb2e-5ea01e89dec4.title: Visible Light Communication (VLC)
97c67b8e-96de-4368-bb2e-5ea01e89dec4.definition: Communication technology that uses visible light to transmit data wirelessly.

2c739149-bc8e-4ffd-9f2c-c564a51dc38f.title: Probability (Networking Math)
2c739149-bc8e-4ffd-9f2c-c564a51dc38f.definition: Basic probability concepts and techniques essential for the field of Networking and Communications.

fa93c8e6-d3af-4182-8e33-5c3d2366cc83.title: Statistics (Networking Math)
fa93c8e6-d3af-4182-8e33-5c3d2366cc83.definition: Basic statistical concepts and techniques essential for the field of Networking and Communications.

6ad2487d-f518-4f4b-9d28-6a34b7ef8d32.title: Discrete Math (Networking Math)
6ad2487d-f518-4f4b-9d28-6a34b7ef8d32.definition: Basic discrete mathematics concepts and techniques essential for the field of Networking and Communications.

0bc1eac9-d6c2-4064-a6c5-eb41369d5df4.title: Linear Algebra (Networking Math)
0bc1eac9-d6c2-4064-a6c5-eb41369d5df4.definition: Basic linear algebra concepts and techniques essential for the field of Networking and Communications.

41bd9ac6-0d7e-493e-b046-c9e7c1e6fbfa.title: Queueing Theory Basics
41bd9ac6-0d7e-493e-b046-c9e7c1e6fbfa.definition: Basic concepts of queuing theory, used to analyze network performance.

aa9fae06-471b-4a9e-b127-1b5cb22f4cfc.title: Networking Basics (Introductory)
aa9fae06-471b-4a9e-b127-1b5cb22f4cfc.definition: Foundational concepts and fundamentals of computer networking for an introductory course.

b302fbeb-5b20-4935-96c3-c83c9ffd7e32.title: Network Applications (Introductory)
b302fbeb-5b20-4935-96c3-c83c9ffd7e32.definition: The types of applications that operate on networks and how they interact with network protocols for an introductory course.

54fe4d11-77ae-45a0-977e-480fdeb977fc.title: Network Reliability (Introductory)
54fe4d11-77ae-45a0-977e-480fdeb977fc.definition: Mechanisms and principles for ensuring reliability in network communications for an introductory course.

1770815a-386e-4832-b264-03c4ad25d0f0.title: Routing & Forwarding (Introductory)
1770815a-386e-4832-b264-03c4ad25d0f0.definition: Principles, algorithms, and protocols used to route and forward packets in networks for an introductory course.

69db68e1-18c1-4522-9601-1389a7fff64c.title: Single-hop Communication (Introductory)
69db68e1-18c1-4522-9601-1389a7fff64c.definition: Principles and mechanisms of direct, multi-hop device-to-device communication for an introductory course.

122e0e02-0c24-481c-a000-ca1923a0a8d3.title: Network Mobility (Introductory)
122e0e02-0c24-481c-a000-ca1923a0a8d3.definition: Issues and solutions related to supporting users and mobile devices in networks for introductory courses.

50d69a00-ef18-4645-9335-e408c8cfe865.title: Network Security (Introductory)
50d69a00-ef18-4645-9335-e408c8cfe865.definition: Principles, techniques, and mechanisms for protecting networks from threats and attacks for an introductory course.

2f085119-f8fb-483b-b503-a72dc3ad3107.title: Networking SEP Context
2f085119-f8fb-483b-b503-a72dc3ad3107.definition: Social, ethical and professional issues related to the field of Networking and Communications.

fb7b3b3e-ace2-45b7-b965-9a0b396a4974.title: Emerging Networking Topics (Introductory)
fb7b3b3e-ace2-45b7-b965-9a0b396a4974.definition: Emerging technologies and trends in the field of computer networking for an introductory course.

e2a40683-2913-44d2-ba9b-42339149864e.title: Networking Basics (Advanced)
e2a40683-2913-44d2-ba9b-42339149864e.definition: Foundational concepts and fundamentals of computer networks at an advanced level.

4f54ad92-1f1c-46f9-9de7-5e8d51c62c6c.title: Network Applications (Advanced)
4f54ad92-1f1c-46f9-9de7-5e8d51c62c6c.definition: The types of applications that operate on the network and how they interact with network protocols at an advanced level.

f4346b51-dd75-4890-9949-11680e54e271.title: Network Reliability (Advanced)
f4346b51-dd75-4890-9949-11680e54e271.definition: Mechanisms and principles to ensure reliability in network communications at an advanced level.

ba52c416-29f0-4076-a3e6-60d766f85c68.title: Routing & Forwarding (Advanced)
ba52c416-29f0-4076-a3e6-60d766f85c68.definition: The principles, algorithms, and protocols used to route and forward packets in networks at an advanced level.

5c88142d-5375-4e1f-a7e0-d9ec53bd062e.title: Single-hop Communication (Advanced)
5c88142d-5375-4e1f-a7e0-d9ec53bd062e.definition: The principles and mechanisms of direct communication between devices without requiring multiple hops at an advanced level.

935973a5-7b2c-478d-8cb6-f60979c5ee12.title: Network Mobility (Advanced)
935973a5-7b2c-478d-8cb6-f60979c5ee12.definition: Issues and solutions related to supporting users and mobile devices in the network at an advanced level.

c1b58411-49ec-4c13-bd85-5a6bb807a866.title: Network Security (Advanced)
c1b58411-49ec-4c13-bd85-5a6bb807a866.definition: Principles, techniques, and mechanisms to protect networks from advanced threats and attacks.

d5b4fd8b-134b-435a-b341-6449308e8be0.title: Privacy (SEP)
d5b4fd8b-134b-435a-b341-6449308e8be0.definition: Issues related to privacy in the context of technology and networks, from a social, ethical and professional perspective (as part of the total 2 hours of SEP topics in the advanced course).

00b007e9-2617-482d-9bbc-02a367f77087.title: Security (SEP)
00b007e9-2617-482d-9bbc-02a367f77087.definition: Security aspects from a social, ethical and professional perspective, in relation to technology and networks (as part of the total 2 hours of SEP topics in the advanced course).

7835333d-fc57-44a7-92d0-32d1916ea0ad.title: Sustainability (SEP)
7835333d-fc57-44a7-92d0-32d1916ea0ad.definition: Sustainability issues related to technology and networks, from a social, ethical and professional perspective (as part of the total 2 hours of SEP topics in the advanced course).

f7318504-ee35-4b5c-b6d3-d9fad937f4d8.title: Emerging Networking Topics (Advanced)
f7318504-ee35-4b5c-b6d3-d9fad937f4d8.definition: Emerging technologies and trends in the field of computer networking at an advanced level.

47bb36fd-c8d5-4e67-9bc1-cd5a19f9890f.title: Software & Systems Development
47bb36fd-c8d5-4e67-9bc1-cd5a19f9890f.definition: Foundational knowledge of how to develop software, computer systems (including operating systems) and applications, is the minimum requirement for all Computer Science graduates according to CS Core standards of CS2023.

14ec8aa4-6597-41cf-a1ff-6467c317ad0d.title: Beyond Professional Ethics
14ec8aa4-6597-41cf-a1ff-6467c317ad0d.definition: understand and act on broader responsibilities beyond those in the professional code of ethics, including global competencies, culture, and an awareness of the importance and impact of local values ​​and practices.

d3253f91-2fbe-41a1-b44c-ec1f6c936ff2.title: Global & Cultural Competence
d3253f91-2fbe-41a1-b44c-ec1f6c936ff2.definition: Ability to understand, interact and work effectively in multicultural and global environments, with an awareness of differences in values ​​and practices.

cf49f809-0f29-4c2e-8142-77f76b57aac1.title: Local Values Impact
cf49f809-0f29-4c2e-8142-77f76b57aac1.definition: understand the importance and impact of local values, priorities and practices around the world on work and professional responsibilities.

a0a1f816-5e83-4dd1-b430-299a54d3975e.title: Maximize Computing Benefits
a0a1f816-5e83-4dd1-b430-299a54d3975e.definition: Strive to ensure that computer technology provides maximum benefit to society at large.

d6e2e2be-a2f2-4bc9-aeb5-38ea36f4149d.title: Prevent Computing Harm
d6e2e2be-a2f2-4bc9-aeb5-38ea36f4149d.definition: Act to protect individuals from negative or harmful effects that may arise from the use or development of computer technology.

613a38a7-29bd-4e69-b448-b516ba55bf6a.title: Professional Dispositions
613a38a7-29bd-4e69-b448-b516ba55bf6a.definition: A set of essential attitudes, values ​​and personal characteristics that help a professional not only succeed at work but also thrive in the long term.

a641be5f-13fd-48e8-a1c2-2d01f3d2792f.title: CS Adaptability
a641be5f-13fd-48e8-a1c2-2d01f3d2792f.definition: Ability to continuously adjust and learn to adapt to the constant evolution of computer science.

6e346911-2d0d-41e5-b558-aa36680d5035.title: CS Collaboration
6e346911-2d0d-41e5-b558-aa36680d5035.definition: Skills to work effectively with others on group projects, as most real-world applications are team efforts.

093bfa40-9b93-47f7-837c-ec49235158f1.title: CS Creativity
093bfa40-9b93-47f7-837c-ec49235158f1.definition: Ability to think creatively to develop new solutions and apply existing solutions to new contexts.

ea5c6b0c-590f-4e44-8eaa-94f29b61e2a3.title: Solution Diligence
ea5c6b0c-590f-4e44-8eaa-94f29b61e2a3.definition: Care and attention to detail ensure the correctness and completeness of solutions.

dc94aa2e-d39d-4a88-8539-62d7ba91f34f.title: Computational Persistence
dc94aa2e-d39d-4a88-8539-62d7ba91f34f.definition: The ability to persevere through difficulties and challenges in solving computational problems, which is an iterative process.

4d497d0c-e810-4d91-a00e-511287ed01cf.title: Proactive Problem Solving
4d497d0c-e810-4d91-a00e-511287ed01cf.definition: Ability to proactively anticipate and resolve potential issues related to usability, security, ethics, etc., before they arise.

6934c431-87ab-4023-ba8d-1f89900c6510.title: Solution Lifecycle Responsibility
6934c431-87ab-4023-ba8d-1f89900c6510.definition: Demonstrate responsibility in all aspects of a technology solution, including the design, implementation and maintenance phases.

2e97a327-3ac8-45e7-855c-df99036fda5e.title: CS Lifelong Learning
2e97a327-3ac8-45e7-855c-df99036fda5e.definition: Ability to self-learn, self-direct self-development and commitment to lifelong learning to adapt to the rapid development of computer science.

bf850961-83a5-42f3-89af-4abbbd013bd6.title: CS Education Diversity
bf850961-83a5-42f3-89af-4abbbd013bd6.definition: Computer Science education has been facing a long-standing challenge of diversity in participation. The industry benefits from the active participation of all classes and all demographic groups, regardless of demographic identity. CS2023 recommends that programs strive to convey the message that Computer Science belongs to everyone and promote active participation by all populations. The CS2023 guidelines include a practice paper on accessibility in computer science education.

ea62c710-6e57-4109-86e7-604715f02b09.title: CS Professional Skills
ea62c710-6e57-4109-86e7-604715f02b09.definition: Employers are always looking for professional qualities (often called soft skills) such as perseverance, self-direction and adaptability in graduates. CS2023 emphasizes the need to clarify this, which has always been implicit, so that students are aware of the importance of these qualities for future career success and develop them during their studies. In CS2023, the most relevant professional qualities have been identified in each knowledge area.

cdaeef42-eca9-49c2-9337-6ca64bb5a3dd.title: CS Faculty Resource Pressure
cdaeef42-eca9-49c2-9337-6ca64bb5a3dd.definition: At many educational institutions, explosive growth in student numbers has put significant pressure on faculty resources, as reflected in class sizes and course loads. Managing faculty workloads is critical to ensuring the vitality of faculty, both in terms of the quality of their teaching and their professional development.

17b71386-6e2f-498a-aed3-0643e98fe826.title: CS Faculty Recruitment & Retention
17b71386-6e2f-498a-aed3-0643e98fe826.definition: Recruiting and retaining faculty is a significant challenge, especially given the high demand for graduates with advanced degrees in Computer Science. A prominent trend over the past decade is the formation of a team of lecturers dedicated to teaching. Educational institutions must find a balance between meeting teaching needs and supporting professional development for lecturers to ensure they keep their knowledge updated and maintain their enthusiasm.

4aa5e511-c60b-4d2e-b310-f296a9f7258b.title: CS Curriculum Evolution
4aa5e511-c60b-4d2e-b310-f296a9f7258b.definition: Computer Science is a rapidly evolving industry, bringing both new opportunities and associated challenges. Updating courses and curricula to keep up with the times requires significant resources from computer science educators and should be recognized and supported. CS2023 has highlighted emerging technologies and significantly expanded the rapidly growing sectors to meet this challenge.

ea6b052c-5361-422d-a309-cd39e77a975e.title: Quantum Computing
ea6b052c-5361-422d-a309-cd39e77a975e.definition: Quantum computing is highlighted by CS2023 as an emerging technology that Computer Science curricula need to consider. A hands-on article on quantum computing education has been included in the CS2023 guide.

7fcc79cc-85d0-4726-a418-fa796543ac9a.title: Machine Learning
7fcc79cc-85d0-4726-a418-fa796543ac9a.definition: Machine learning is a rapidly growing field in Computer Science and has been significantly expanded in the CS2023 curriculum guidelines, reflecting its growing importance in the industry.

84de3007-b801-4639-a25f-d2d1f4fd6e95.title: Generative AI in CS Education
84de3007-b801-4639-a25f-d2d1f4fd6e95.definition: Discusses the potential of generative AI to revolutionize computer science education, including impact on course content, pedagogy, and assessment techniques. This is a general principle that applies to the design and teaching of courses in all fields, including Operating Systems.

831c04c5-2a43-4234-b306-a77a2f9418b2.title: Generative AI Education Challenges
831c04c5-2a43-4234-b306-a77a2f9418b2.definition: Exploiting generative AI to serve the goals of formal education is one of the most important challenges facing the community over the next few years. This also applies to how AI is integrated and used in teaching and learning topics related to Operating Systems.

af470516-68c1-4135-8bd4-1b51569a6bbc.title: Generative AI Impact on CS KAs
af470516-68c1-4135-8bd4-1b51569a6bbc.definition: CS2023 includes a chapter that lists well-founded speculations about the implications of generative AI for various fields of knowledge. This includes predictions about how generative AI could influence the content and methods of teaching in the field of Operating Systems.

b63af26c-2c5f-4a3d-95bd-546125bc123b.title: Generative AI in Intro Programming
b63af26c-2c5f-4a3d-95bd-546125bc123b.definition: CS2023 includes a curriculum practice article on the implications of generative AI for introductory programming. Introductory programming is fundamental to many aspects of computer science, including understanding and developing Operating System components.

601a2a55-a378-447e-bfde-068df0f45d52.title: CS Math & Theory Foundation
601a2a55-a378-447e-bfde-068df0f45d52.definition: Emphasize that theoretical and mathematical foundations are core to what makes computer science a science and are essential for long-term career success. For Operating Systems, this includes understanding algorithms, data structures, and underlying theoretical models.

b0f68b43-b22c-47bc-ba40-0f4b2c169124.title: CS Theory vs. Tools Balance
b0f68b43-b22c-47bc-ba40-0f4b2c169124.definition: Discuss the challenge of finding the right balance between the goals of providing a solid theoretical/mathematical foundation and equipping students with tool/technology skills for immediate employability. This is a challenge common to all areas of knowledge, including Operating Systems, where both theory (e.g., process management) and practice (e.g., using debugging tools) are important.

742417f4-e415-4e77-9c3d-286452384c35.title: Growing CS Math Demand
742417f4-e415-4e77-9c3d-286452384c35.definition: Recognizes the growing need for mathematics in computer science (e.g., in machine learning) and the frequent inadequate mathematical preparation of students entering programs. This is an important consideration for curriculum design, including for Operating Systems courses that involve optimization or performance analysis.

7b946ee7-c9a7-4997-acb1-edd3829b050c.title: CS2023 KA Math Requirements
7b946ee7-c9a7-4997-acb1-edd3829b050c.definition: CS2023 has separately identified mathematics requirements for each knowledge area, including Operating Systems, to provide flexibility in the curriculum to accommodate varying levels of student preparation.

82e37a50-2358-4688-b69c-49bd2b268a0b.title: Flexible CS Math Requirements
82e37a50-2358-4688-b69c-49bd2b268a0b.definition: CS2023 provides flexibility so that students with limited mathematics proficiency can better navigate the curriculum. Instructors may require a prerequisite mathematics course or teach required mathematics as part of a computer science course, applicable to subjects with specific mathematics requirements such as Operating Systems.

f5f183be-3b3d-44aa-8e5f-98cdd115a456.title: Integrate Socio-Ethical Issues
f5f183be-3b3d-44aa-8e5f-98cdd115a456.definition: Emphasize that a computer solution is not just technical but must also incorporate social, ethical, and professional considerations. This is a fundamental principle that applies to the design and implementation of systems, including Operating Systems, where design decisions can have far-reaching impacts.

d228774e-5fc9-40bc-a960-81f7ff377a06.title: Integrating Ethics in Technical CS
d228774e-5fc9-40bc-a960-81f7ff377a06.definition: Identify the challenge of integrating social, ethical, and professional issues into the technical coverage of the curriculum so that they become inevitable. This is the responsibility of every educator, which applies to the teaching of technical subjects such as Operating Systems, where issues of privacy, security, and equity may arise.

bef2782a-c134-480b-88ff-54ab22c6c62d.title: Parallel & Distributed Computing
bef2782a-c134-480b-88ff-54ab22c6c62d.definition: One of the main knowledge areas in the CS2023 Computer Science curriculum standard.

0aa7981b-cd9b-49a0-b9b8-45e5c80ced25.title: Software Development Fundamentals
0aa7981b-cd9b-49a0-b9b8-45e5c80ced25.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

3222dedb-177d-424d-ae34-6b1e92769bae.title: Software Engineering
3222dedb-177d-424d-ae34-6b1e92769bae.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

2cb0dc63-2d7a-45e0-8d04-031d676d31f1.title: Security
2cb0dc63-2d7a-45e0-8d04-031d676d31f1.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

c69c4ff8-3feb-4008-86f7-9be10ce28793.title: Society, Ethics & Profession
c69c4ff8-3feb-4008-86f7-9be10ce28793.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

17645b7d-2376-43ae-a46d-b82bde1c1a57.title: Human-Computer Interaction
17645b7d-2376-43ae-a46d-b82bde1c1a57.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

cd3186bd-889c-450b-a0ef-f70251406be1.title: Math & Statistics Foundations
cd3186bd-889c-450b-a0ef-f70251406be1.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

e04b8ab9-9402-4bf6-88e7-81e5fdd5b7f9.title: Systems Fundamentals
e04b8ab9-9402-4bf6-88e7-81e5fdd5b7f9.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

fe3f480d-2e4c-4290-b291-5a0721402d85.title: Platform-Specific Development
fe3f480d-2e4c-4290-b291-5a0721402d85.definition: One of the knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum standard.

7359757e-9d4e-4c65-9f9e-93316559719f.title: Knowledge Area Definition
7359757e-9d4e-4c65-9f9e-93316559719f.definition: In CS2023, a knowledge area is defined as a collection of knowledge units and professional characteristics.

33411fbd-0e86-499b-b0b5-fc6ca056e206.title: Knowledge Unit
33411fbd-0e86-499b-b0b5-fc6ca056e206.definition: Components that make up a knowledge area in the CS2023 standard.

afc14944-2bd1-417f-97fd-5230db63bae7.title: Professional Characteristics
afc14944-2bd1-417f-97fd-5230db63bae7.definition: Values, beliefs, and attitudes are malleable, helping to demonstrate consistent desired workplace behaviors. Includes willingness and intention to apply skills to complete tasks.

d02b0965-16ca-4419-83dd-2a8ee06d286a.title: Professional Trait: Persistence
d02b0965-16ca-4419-83dd-2a8ee06d286a.definition: A career trait is considered essential at the introductory level of students.

0321e988-92b6-4316-ac0e-27b86ac26b14.title: Professional Trait: Self-Direction
0321e988-92b6-4316-ac0e-27b86ac26b14.definition: A career trait expected at advanced levels of student research.

1da2ed78-5298-4b12-b4cc-333274f96b92.title: Professional Trait: Communicative
1da2ed78-5298-4b12-b4cc-333274f96b92.definition: A professional trait that demonstrates the willingness and intention to apply communication skills to complete tasks.

27d3538e-f1c2-48ab-944a-999649aafca5.title: Professional Trait: Collaborative
27d3538e-f1c2-48ab-944a-999649aafca5.definition: An essential professional trait for team projects, demonstrating a willingness and intention to work together.

34fa31b1-5064-482b-b603-45c5e3be30c8.title: Professional Trait: Meticulous
34fa31b1-5064-482b-b603-45c5e3be30c8.definition: An essential career trait for mathematical foundations, requiring care and attention to detail.

446bbcc6-02f7-415d-a2a0-55f268cf0e97.title: CS Core
446bbcc6-02f7-415d-a2a0-55f268cf0e97.definition: Topics that every computer science graduate must know and that every computer science curriculum is expected to cover.

a733142d-2e75-4109-b882-e0e03393fcc5.title: KA Core
a733142d-2e75-4109-b882-e0e03393fcc5.definition: Topics are recommended for further study in a particular field of knowledge.

532ceeb2-f6d8-4404-a2ac-4909e152a76b.title: Non-core Topics
532ceeb2-f6d8-4404-a2ac-4909e152a76b.definition: Elective topics, renamed from 'Elective topics' in CS2023.

04fd1fe4-9d36-4752-94a7-64483001acad.title: SDF
04fd1fe4-9d36-4752-94a7-64483001acad.definition: One of the key knowledge areas identified in the CS2023 curriculum.

80f26d9d-66e4-42c4-94d9-34e08bf132cd.title: SE
80f26d9d-66e4-42c4-94d9-34e08bf132cd.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

a9cfce79-e240-4aa4-b043-31951e950cf4.title: SEC
a9cfce79-e240-4aa4-b043-31951e950cf4.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

9cb48170-a3fc-4eec-b4f3-5c2612c096a6.title: SEP
9cb48170-a3fc-4eec-b4f3-5c2612c096a6.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

eadd9685-19b1-4203-8bd4-d2db924ad8ff.title: HCI
eadd9685-19b1-4203-8bd4-d2db924ad8ff.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

f81e16dc-3342-4cc1-96cc-2ec1bbcdcfeb.title: MSF
f81e16dc-3342-4cc1-96cc-2ec1bbcdcfeb.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

218a0a19-1382-4dfa-97ff-b492f583ed24.title: SF
218a0a19-1382-4dfa-97ff-b492f583ed24.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

78826feb-b6a9-4eab-8835-2f12c15664f6.title: SPD
78826feb-b6a9-4eab-8835-2f12c15664f6.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum.

895a05d1-5a00-42b9-a105-76b79cc3a346.title: Knowledge Area
895a05d1-5a00-42b9-a105-76b79cc3a346.definition: In CS2023, a knowledge area is expanded to include knowledge units and career trends.

a88dd998-43a5-4c57-937a-49e73050490b.title: Knowledge Unit
a88dd998-43a5-4c57-937a-49e73050490b.definition: Specific content elements within a knowledge area.

705110c3-c72c-4114-a1ff-555952e3732a.title: Professional Propensity
705110c3-c72c-4114-a1ff-555952e3732a.definition: Values, beliefs and attitudes can change, allowing for consistent desirable workplace behaviors; When indistinguishable from skills, they refer to the willingness and intention to apply skills to complete tasks.

4fa9f6c3-8931-4d7f-803d-24b7799950dd.title: Persistence
4fa9f6c3-8931-4d7f-803d-24b7799950dd.definition: An important career orientation at the introductory level for students, encouraging persistence in study and work.

94df40be-1fa2-4b1d-81c2-e82dfacd9a48.title: Self-Direction
94df40be-1fa2-4b1d-81c2-e82dfacd9a48.definition: A career orientation is expected at advanced levels of study, demonstrating the ability to self-manage and lead oneself in study and work.

942d638c-d396-4dca-b02f-159bd463259c.title: Good Communication
942d638c-d396-4dca-b02f-159bd463259c.definition: A vocational disposition refers to the willingness and intention to apply communication skills to complete tasks effectively.

c8f814be-20e3-4f45-95d4-65574b59ea4d.title: Collaboration
c8f814be-20e3-4f45-95d4-65574b59ea4d.definition: A necessary professional disposition for team projects, demonstrating a willingness and intention to work together to achieve common goals.

4f459ef6-f814-4cdf-b427-4d705f1f70fb.title: Meticulousness
4f459ef6-f814-4cdf-b427-4d705f1f70fb.definition: A career trend that requires great care and precision, especially important for mathematical foundations.

95be2b43-e887-4e66-b22a-ba349e6050e2.title: CS Core
95be2b43-e887-4e66-b22a-ba349e6050e2.definition: Topics every computer science graduate is required to know, and every computer science curriculum is expected to cover them all.

c3392471-37f9-4e0d-b330-09050f931e8b.title: KA Core
c3392471-37f9-4e0d-b330-09050f931e8b.definition: Topics are recommended for more in-depth study in a specific area of ​​knowledge, with additional conceptual nuances.

0c7b77ff-d24b-4d35-b0ed-503a2a23276a.title: Non-core Topics
0c7b77ff-d24b-4d35-b0ed-503a2a23276a.definition: Elective topics have been renamed in CS2023, which are not mandatory but can be selected by students for more in-depth study according to their interests.

b224e565-b162-4620-b044-bb92ae376c2a.title: SEC
b224e565-b162-4620-b044-bb92ae376c2a.definition: One of the key knowledge areas in the CS2023 curriculum, focusing on concepts and practices related to information security and privacy.

716f19aa-78cd-4170-b413-07c17eedf6c6.title: SEP
716f19aa-78cd-4170-b413-07c17eedf6c6.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum, covering social issues, ethics and professional responsibilities in the field of computer science and information technology.

f2d5ec42-0267-413a-a594-d213212bc95c.title: HCI
f2d5ec42-0267-413a-a594-d213212bc95c.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 syllabus that focuses on the design, evaluation, and implementation of effective, easy-to-use computer systems and interfaces.

ff4c884c-8a92-4dd2-b423-fb2c5f6a7e24.title: MSF
ff4c884c-8a92-4dd2-b423-fb2c5f6a7e24.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 syllabus, covering the fundamental mathematical and statistical principles necessary for understanding and application in computer science.

db1ec968-c11e-486c-98ed-be916326a54e.title: SF
db1ec968-c11e-486c-98ed-be916326a54e.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 curriculum, focusing on the basic principles and architecture of computer systems, from hardware to software.

9e56e667-9ba9-4cef-ae65-b88d10405d42.title: SPD
9e56e667-9ba9-4cef-ae65-b88d10405d42.definition: An area of ​​knowledge in the CS2023 syllabus, related to the development of applications or systems on specialized technology platforms.

b977b0c4-b319-4a54-a84f-42a6befdac3f.title: Knowledge Area Structure
b977b0c4-b319-4a54-a84f-42a6befdac3f.definition: In CS2023, a Knowledge Area is defined as the combination of Knowledge Units and associated Professional Qualities.

3a75c29a-60a2-4602-8407-7922e9312e6e.title: Knowledge Unit
3a75c29a-60a2-4602-8407-7922e9312e6e.definition: Specific knowledge components constitute a Knowledge Area in the CS2023 curriculum.

18c642a5-c654-4258-b212-39e97e0358c6.title: Professional Propensities
18c642a5-c654-4258-b212-39e97e0358c6.definition: Values, beliefs, and attitudes can change, helping to shape desirable workplace behaviors (e.g., persistence, self-direction). They are essential factors for success at work and are sought after by employers.

47602a8f-2a16-483d-9646-7d61c34d560e.title: Persistence
47602a8f-2a16-483d-9646-7d61c34d560e.definition: A professional quality that demonstrates perseverance, not giving up in the face of difficulties, is considered essential at the introductory level of study.

47f1fab5-3a53-4456-9672-5db32859dc88.title: Self-Direction
47f1fab5-3a53-4456-9672-5db32859dc88.definition: A professional quality that demonstrates the ability to self-manage studies and work, and independently solve problems, is expected at advanced levels of study.

1578e0a5-34e5-41e4-99b4-3282f76fe72d.title: Good Communication
1578e0a5-34e5-41e4-99b4-3282f76fe72d.definition: A professional quality refers to the willingness and intention to apply communication skills to complete tasks.

01b183df-8dd8-4787-8faf-68b62ff22a5e.title: Collaboration
01b183df-8dd8-4787-8faf-68b62ff22a5e.definition: A professional quality that refers to the willingness and intention to apply collaborative skills to complete tasks, especially needed for group projects.

82ea3e06-4570-4165-a2d5-b084e03a48d9.title: Meticulousness
82ea3e06-4570-4165-a2d5-b084e03a48d9.definition: A professional quality that demonstrates care and attention to detail, required for fields requiring a mathematical background.

69d712f0-ed3e-44ac-ab8f-257c93787bcc.title: Curriculum Competency Model
69d712f0-ed3e-44ac-ab8f-257c93787bcc.definition: Curriculum patterns in which the knowledge, skills, and professional qualities needed to perform a task are grouped together.

a489a19c-7aa6-4c2f-b8a3-427b3199a224.title: CS Core
a489a19c-7aa6-4c2f-b8a3-427b3199a224.definition: Topics every computer science graduate is required to know. Every computer science curriculum is expected to cover all of these topics.

c3717388-1af9-4d10-9f65-da24206447e5.title: KA Core
c3717388-1af9-4d10-9f65-da24206447e5.definition: Topics are recommended for further study in a specific Knowledge Area, providing further specialization beyond CS Core topics.

e3558f94-c92b-4bc3-9c2d-de33f3267124.title: Non-core Topics
e3558f94-c92b-4bc3-9c2d-de33f3267124.definition: Topics are classified as electives, not in the CS Core or KA Core categories, allowing students to choose by interest or major.

113a8437-8cdf-407b-92e6-02106946aafa.title: GIT
113a8437-8cdf-407b-92e6-02106946aafa.definition: Knowledge area of ​​Graphics and Interactive Techniques (GIT) in the CS2023 program.

3bbfc50a-de09-4329-87ba-6b4bb05be5d5.title: IAS (CS2013)
3bbfc50a-de09-4329-87ba-6b4bb05be5d5.definition: The Information Assurance and Security (IAS) knowledge area in the CS2013 program, was renamed Security (SEC) in CS2023.

9c66f7ae-924c-4f45-bdfd-f7340ebb95cb.title: SEC (CS2023)
9c66f7ae-924c-4f45-bdfd-f7340ebb95cb.definition: The Security (SEC) knowledge area in the CS2023 program, is the new name of Information Assurance and Security (IAS) from CS2013.

09d50b2b-3b4b-47e3-9e52-8b7de8e2e6cb.title: IM (CS2013)
09d50b2b-3b4b-47e3-9e52-8b7de8e2e6cb.definition: The Information Management (IM) knowledge area in the CS2013 program, was renamed Data Management (DM) in CS2023.

c0edb787-c3e9-4e2d-9f5c-eb7c89c48bea.title: DM (CS2023)
c0edb787-c3e9-4e2d-9f5c-eb7c89c48bea.definition: The Data Management (DM) knowledge area in the CS2023 program is the new name of Information Management (IM) from CS2013.

69532cc1-9e0e-4647-96a7-bc93c3e00eac.title: IS (CS2013)
69532cc1-9e0e-4647-96a7-bc93c3e00eac.definition: The knowledge field of Intelligent Systems (IS) in the CS2013 program, was renamed Artificial Intelligence (AI) in CS2023.

259b1f3c-e948-456b-aaeb-2b8eca9f981a.title: AI (CS2023)
259b1f3c-e948-456b-aaeb-2b8eca9f981a.definition: The field of knowledge of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the CS2023 program, is the new name of Intelligent Systems (IS) from CS2013.

075d750f-1f86-4f6d-b18b-1631d900b005.title: PBD (CS2013)
075d750f-1f86-4f6d-b18b-1631d900b005.definition: The Platform Based Development (PBD) knowledge area in the CS2013 program, was renamed to Specialized Platform Development (SPD) in CS2023.

1db46229-2975-4c3c-8d4d-d5c0775839de.title: SPD (CS2023)
1db46229-2975-4c3c-8d4d-d5c0775839de.definition: The Specialized Platform Development (SPD) knowledge area in the CS2023 program, is the new name for Platform-based Development (PBD) from CS2013.

4bad8de4-aedc-4c92-9867-b623992112ab.title: PL (CS2013)
4bad8de4-aedc-4c92-9867-b623992112ab.definition: The Programming Languages ​​(PL) knowledge area in the CS2013 program, was renamed Programming Languages ​​Foundation (FPL) in CS2023.

cafd78f4-2a28-436c-8164-c3c1263c05f5.title: FPL (CS2023)
cafd78f4-2a28-436c-8164-c3c1263c05f5.definition: The knowledge area of ​​Foundations of Programming Languages ​​(FPL) in the CS2023 program is the new name of Programming Language (PL) from CS2013.

57f49416-0a40-4fe0-947c-233bca96eb6f.title: SP (CS2013)
57f49416-0a40-4fe0-947c-233bca96eb6f.definition: The knowledge area Social Issues and Professional Practice (SP) in the CS2013 program, was renamed Society, Ethics and Professional Practice (SEP) in CS2023.

8c7f7c85-0683-4f25-9c7f-e79708b8eae7.title: SEP (CS2023)
8c7f7c85-0683-4f25-9c7f-e79708b8eae7.definition: The knowledge area of ​​Society, Ethics, and the Profession (SEP) in the CS2023 program is the new name of Social Issues and Professional Practice (SP) from CS2013.

623bc220-0ccc-4909-b0a8-074fe48baa58.title: Computational Science (Deprecated)
623bc220-0ccc-4909-b0a8-074fe48baa58.definition: The Computational Science (CN) knowledge area from CS2013 has been removed from the CS2023 curriculum because there is very little computer science content that does not overlap with other knowledge areas. In CS2013, it is allocated 1 core hour for modeling and simulation.

baab1a8c-235e-4572-97c6-830f008cf878.title: Modeling & Simulation
baab1a8c-235e-4572-97c6-830f008cf878.definition: A core topic is allocated 1 hour of study in the Computational Science (CN) area of ​​CS2013.

37e0a58e-c59c-4e15-807a-270b5394f9ee.title: Modeling Application
37e0a58e-c59c-4e15-807a-270b5394f9ee.definition: Modeling applications are considered a cross-cutting topic in computer science.

c1870b08-febf-4234-8c51-bdd760fbeacd.title: Modeling Research
c1870b08-febf-4234-8c51-bdd760fbeacd.definition: Modeling research as it stands is seen as more relevant in the CS+X (Computer Science combined with other fields) space, rather than as a core area of ​​knowledge.

3e0b61a1-835f-428b-a1fd-8a4a720802e4.title: CS + X
3e0b61a1-835f-428b-a1fd-8a4a720802e4.definition: The concept of the CS+X space, where the principles of computer science are applied or studied in conjunction with other fields.

8b0c70e6-5cb5-439c-aae8-6382e021fe83.title: CS Math
8b0c70e6-5cb5-439c-aae8-6382e021fe83.definition: The role of the mathematical component in computer science has been expanded in CS2023, reflecting its increase in importance.

4d06e76c-b7e4-4306-9e0b-57299a7ac7d8.title: Discrete Structures (CS2013)
4d06e76c-b7e4-4306-9e0b-57299a7ac7d8.definition: One of the main mathematical components in the CS2013 curriculum, now part of the Mathematical and Statistical Foundations (MSF) in CS2023.

d1a99d04-8a59-4684-872e-529e7e8186c1.title: Probability (MSF)
d1a99d04-8a59-4684-872e-529e7e8186c1.definition: New mathematics component added to the Mathematical and Statistical Foundations (MSF) area in CS2023.

ba9b2c84-0465-4b45-a5dd-f7f8008c37b1.title: Statistics (MSF)
ba9b2c84-0465-4b45-a5dd-f7f8008c37b1.definition: New mathematics component added to the Mathematical and Statistical Foundations (MSF) area in CS2023.

f32719e2-adb2-44da-9104-1a3e871e0c92.title: Linear Algebra (MSF)
f32719e2-adb2-44da-9104-1a3e871e0c92.definition: New mathematics component added to the Mathematical and Statistical Foundations (MSF) area in CS2023.

57dbaf07-f312-4e53-bfc4-bfb496eda7e8.title: MSF (CS2023)
57dbaf07-f312-4e53-bfc4-bfb496eda7e8.definition: The Mathematical and Statistical Foundations (MSF) knowledge area in CS2023, expands from CS2013's Discrete Structures to include probability, statistics, and linear algebra.

64732cc2-258c-4b9c-8dce-1b2a9c5e7a4e.title: SEP
64732cc2-258c-4b9c-8dce-1b2a9c5e7a4e.definition: One of the key Knowledge Areas (KAs) in the CS2023 syllabus, focusing on ethical issues, social responsibility, and professional aspects of the computer science profession.

e5131f14-12f5-4bc5-abec-989e24cc5c37.title: HCI
e5131f14-12f5-4bc5-abec-989e24cc5c37.definition: One of the Knowledge Areas (KAs) listed in the CS2023 syllabus is the study of the design and use of computer systems that interact well with humans.

07a6db96-c974-4c34-9db7-5b2ed0ecc045.title: MSF
07a6db96-c974-4c34-9db7-5b2ed0ecc045.definition: One of the Knowledge Areas (KAs) listed in the CS2023 syllabus, covering the foundational and in-depth knowledge of mathematics and statistics required for other areas of computer science.

2fe8d1aa-21d4-428a-90d8-63618c414ce4.title: Systems Fundamentals (SF)
2fe8d1aa-21d4-428a-90d8-63618c414ce4.definition: One of the Knowledge Areas (KAs) listed in the CS2023 syllabus, focusing on the fundamental principles and concepts of how computer systems are structured and operate.

d89cd80e-49d4-4dc4-89c6-316024fc2f0a.title: Specialized Platform Development (SPD)
d89cd80e-49d4-4dc4-89c6-316024fc2f0a.definition: One of the Knowledge Areas (KAs) listed in the CS2023 syllabus, involves the development of applications and solutions on specialized technology platforms.

3fa225af-ef20-45c5-8922-3e49cf1141de.title: KA Definition (CS2023)
3fa225af-ef20-45c5-8922-3e49cf1141de.definition: In the CS2023 syllabus, a Knowledge Area is expanded to include Learning Units and Career Trends. Formula: Knowledge Area = {Knowledge Units} + {Career Trends}.

b593fc65-a9e7-4025-9291-48caa6f08945.title: Knowledge Unit
b593fc65-a9e7-4025-9291-48caa6f08945.definition: Specific knowledge blocks make up a Knowledge Area in the CS2023 curriculum.

a79d15f8-b18a-4b08-8918-0109f9ff3dce.title: Professional Trends
a79d15f8-b18a-4b08-8918-0109f9ff3dce.definition: These are values, beliefs and attitudes that can be changed, helping to form consistent and desirable behaviors in the work environment. They are sought after by employers and essential to career success.

0357396f-310c-49d2-a3ce-57136def5245.title: Persistence Trend
0357396f-310c-49d2-a3ce-57136def5245.definition: A desirable career trend, demonstrating perseverance and persistence in work. Especially considered an essential element at the introductory level for students.

f73b255e-04b9-4d22-a185-3ea081cf83b7.title: Self-Direction Trend
f73b255e-04b9-4d22-a185-3ea081cf83b7.definition: A desirable career trend, demonstrating the ability to self-manage and orient work independently. Expected at advanced levels of study and research.

17ffa81c-e570-47c3-9fc2-4f620a45e7d3.title: Communication Trend
17ffa81c-e570-47c3-9fc2-4f620a45e7d3.definition: A desirable career trend, which refers to the willingness and intention to apply effective communication skills to complete tasks.

e368f367-d29c-4638-b3a1-69235ceaa8d6.title: Collaboration Trend
e368f367-d29c-4638-b3a1-69235ceaa8d6.definition: A desirable career orientation, which refers to the willingness and intention to work together to complete tasks, especially important in group projects.

f6e8347a-e5a8-4540-a952-7372e0075be5.title: Competency Model
f6e8347a-e5a8-4540-a952-7372e0075be5.definition: Curriculum patterns in which the knowledge, skills, and career dispositions needed to perform a task are grouped together.

50be6bc3-0b34-47c3-bc2b-377940688fc2.title: Meticulousness Trend
50be6bc3-0b34-47c3-bc2b-377940688fc2.definition: A desirable career trend, demonstrating care and attention to detail, especially needed when working with mathematical foundations.

dd374133-307e-4da6-8b4f-5f0d6ea3ee0a.title: CS Core Topics
dd374133-307e-4da6-8b4f-5f0d6ea3ee0a.definition: Required topics that every computer science graduate must master. Every computer science curriculum is expected to cover all core CS topics.

e74bdf86-9199-4851-adfa-f74acace2685.title: KA Core Topics
e74bdf86-9199-4851-adfa-f74acace2685.definition: Recommended topics for more in-depth study in a specific Area of ​​Knowledge. They complement the core CS topics.

9e10a8d8-d384-4fdc-a6a9-15fbb28d823d.title: Non-Core Topics
9e10a8d8-d384-4fdc-a6a9-15fbb28d823d.definition: Optional or elective topics in the CS2023 curriculum, not in the CS Core or KA Core categories.

7b8feb52-99ed-464c-bebb-d4a0cf70ef62.title: MSF
7b8feb52-99ed-464c-bebb-d4a0cf70ef62.definition: The foundational knowledge area of ​​mathematics and statistics is the mainstay of modern computer science education. MSF inherits the 'Discrete Structures' area of ​​ACM CS2013 and covers mathematical and statistical topics essential to growing fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science and quantum computing.

c0eecf96-a4f4-41ab-8d81-5f8d52e7c5fb.title: Discrete Structures
c0eecf96-a4f4-41ab-8d81-5f8d52e7c5fb.definition: The mathematics literacy area, covered in the ACM CS2013 report, was the predecessor to the current MSF area. Although still an important part, the range of mathematics required for modern computer science has expanded beyond just discrete structures.

d8fac57f-1631-4f41-b748-0a92c0d5c6be.title: Continuous Math
d8fac57f-1631-4f41-b748-0a92c0d5c6be.definition: The field of mathematics underpins many recent burgeoning computer science fields such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and quantum computing. It is emphasized that it is necessary along with discrete structures.

fa3ae1f9-f58a-4ba0-89af-d403e71056a3.title: Probability
fa3ae1f9-f58a-4ba0-89af-d403e71056a3.definition: An important area of ​​mathematics, proposed to be concentrated in modern computer science programs. It is rated 98% for importance for careers in industry and graduate study, especially essential for AI, machine learning, robotics, data science and quantum computing.

7ee3ef4c-dec6-42cc-94c6-cf706828c239.title: Statistics
7ee3ef4c-dec6-42cc-94c6-cf706828c239.definition: An important field of statistics, it is proposed to be concentrated in modern computer science programs. It is rated 98% for importance for careers in industry and graduate study, especially essential for AI, machine learning, robotics, data science and quantum computing.
