f5d726a0-1f38-4922-b3cb-5d18fcb9e842.title: Common Discrete Distributions
f5d726a0-1f38-4922-b3cb-5d18fcb9e842.definition: Ability to recognize and differentiate common discrete distributions such as uniform, Bernoulli, binomial, and geometric.

191a384b-49df-42ee-92fa-5898fbbdb44a.title: Continuous Random Variable
191a384b-49df-42ee-92fa-5898fbbdb44a.definition: Define and understand continuous random variables.

ec2dc4f4-318e-414f-9e6d-8fbe8c15ca20.title: Continuous Uniform Distribution
ec2dc4f4-318e-414f-9e6d-8fbe8c15ca20.definition: understand and recognize uniform continuous distribution.

31a262b7-10f8-40f3-851c-f2895c77ec35.title: Normal Distribution
31a262b7-10f8-40f3-851c-f2895c77ec35.definition: understand and recognize normal distribution (Gaussian distribution).

2999f5d9-1d22-428b-b29b-93c519343b6d.title: Common Continuous Distributions
2999f5d9-1d22-428b-b29b-93c519343b6d.definition: Ability to identify and differentiate common continuous distributions such as uniform, normal, and exponential.

f6259a49-17de-402e-9b06-0a258bfb7b41.title: Cumulative Distribution Function
f6259a49-17de-402e-9b06-0a258bfb7b41.definition: Define and understand the cumulative density function (CDF) for a continuous random variable.

470f451b-4728-4af3-969c-168db55f9d1d.title: CDF Probability Calculation
470f451b-4728-4af3-969c-168db55f9d1d.definition: Skills in using the cumulative density function to calculate probabilities for continuous random variables.

68994c5a-24d7-40de-ba67-73e25fa27ca4.title: Expected Value
68994c5a-24d7-40de-ba67-73e25fa27ca4.definition: Defines the expectation (mean value) of a random variable.

c075554a-47c9-4585-a2b9-e994037ba1aa.title: Variance
c075554a-47c9-4585-a2b9-e994037ba1aa.definition: Define the variance of a random variable.

d2f1768d-fca5-4a1a-bcda-1951c347df4c.title: Expectation & Variance
d2f1768d-fca5-4a1a-bcda-1951c347df4c.definition: Ability to clearly define the concepts of expectation and variance of random variables.

bd82ed98-2839-4521-bf24-355aef8ed604.title: Calculate Exp. & Variance
bd82ed98-2839-4521-bf24-355aef8ed604.definition: Skill in calculating expected value and variance for common discrete and continuous random variables.

8026d151-6bc3-4946-8a7c-b0b4a4720975.title: Law of Large Numbers
8026d151-6bc3-4946-8a7c-b0b4a4720975.definition: understand the Law of Large Numbers, which describes the behavior of the sample mean as the number of samples increases.

a3fe7da8-8e36-4578-a00c-b5a812d9d022.title: Central Limit Theorem
a3fe7da8-8e36-4578-a00c-b5a812d9d022.definition: understand the Central Limit Theorem, which describes that the distribution of the sum (or mean) of independent and homogeneous random variables tends to be normally distributed as the number of variables increases.

d58f7724-bbdc-4472-8937-996eec71f4a0.title: LLN & CLT Relation
d58f7724-bbdc-4472-8937-996eec71f4a0.definition: Ability to explain the importance and application of the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem in probability calculations and statistical analysis.

8329e840-0ec0-49e8-a36d-39153360cc18.title: Joint Distribution
8329e840-0ec0-49e8-a36d-39153360cc18.definition: Define and understand the simultaneous distribution of multiple random variables.

d27ed7c8-1695-4992-a8d0-61d1d7d7175a.title: Marginal Distribution
d27ed7c8-1695-4992-a8d0-61d1d7d7175a.definition: Define and understand the marginal distribution, as derived from the concurrent distribution.

3ab885aa-094d-43e2-a9cc-6a3865feb941.title: Conditional Distribution
3ab885aa-094d-43e2-a9cc-6a3865feb941.definition: Define and understand the conditional distribution of a random variable given the value of another random variable.

e3abe224-d255-400e-9628-4de514164938.title: Distribution Types Comparison
e3abe224-d255-400e-9628-4de514164938.definition: Ability to distinguish and explain relationships between simultaneous, marginal, and conditional distributions.

5ca22d05-bc19-48cb-8173-5ee715a68c5d.title: Calculate Discrete Distributions
5ca22d05-bc19-48cb-8173-5ee715a68c5d.definition: Skill in calculating marginal and conditional distributions from a complete distribution for discrete random variables.

1a38e92f-c345-4f2d-9fe2-8cbe9a4847c7.title: Calculate Continuous Distributions
1a38e92f-c345-4f2d-9fe2-8cbe9a4847c7.definition: Skill in calculating marginal and conditional distributions from a complete distribution for continuous random variables.

1041f4a9-5ec4-465b-8cda-f8baa2b0d38f.title: Conditional Expectation
1041f4a9-5ec4-465b-8cda-f8baa2b0d38f.definition: Define and understand the conditional expectation of a random variable.

a3c66358-05fc-4187-a4e3-dbcf09ac8338.title: Calculate Discrete Cond. Exp.
a3c66358-05fc-4187-a4e3-dbcf09ac8338.definition: Skill in calculating conditional expectations for discrete random variables.

251ff784-41e5-4354-9ac9-9ce193b46057.title: Calculate Continuous Cond. Exp.
251ff784-41e5-4354-9ac9-9ce193b46057.definition: Skill in calculating conditional expectations for continuous random variables.

e793d6f6-7ea7-4f4f-8e53-f91a2f463466.title: Probability: Text Prediction
e793d6f6-7ea7-4f4f-8e53-f91a2f463466.definition: Ability to describe how to apply probabilistic models to real-life situations, such as in text prediction systems.

62a01f01-abe7-425d-b601-680d58e227f7.title: Probability: Hash Tables
62a01f01-abe7-425d-b601-680d58e227f7.definition: Ability to describe how to apply probabilistic models to real-life situations, such as in hash table performance analysis.

f186008d-eea6-4f5e-a547-c49a989a1a5f.title: Probability: Quantum Computing
f186008d-eea6-4f5e-a547-c49a989a1a5f.definition: Ability to describe how to apply probabilistic models to real-life situations, such as in quantum computing.

fb78f87b-cb27-4d4e-bc4b-b64d45f1bbe8.title: Probabilistic Algorithms
fb78f87b-cb27-4d4e-bc4b-b64d45f1bbe8.definition: Skills in applying probabilistic processes and models to design or analyze stochastic algorithms.

bdc3e024-490a-44cb-aa7f-83bc12680fd6.title: Probability: Security Apps
bdc3e024-490a-44cb-aa7f-83bc12680fd6.definition: Skills in applying probabilistic processes and models in security applications.

ac704307-a584-40f3-b423-6adb4f05c5f7.title: Probability vs. Statistics
ac704307-a584-40f3-b423-6adb4f05c5f7.definition: understand the fundamental differences in goals, methods, and approaches between probability theory and statistics.

e9423be7-981e-4ac6-bfee-ba92d1c1b312.title: Population (Statistics)
e9423be7-981e-4ac6-bfee-ba92d1c1b312.definition: Basic definition of the complete set of objects or events of interest in statistics.

60428062-0ab7-477c-acc6-12bdcec6c096.title: Sample (Statistics)
60428062-0ab7-477c-acc6-12bdcec6c096.definition: Basic definition of a subset of a population selected for statistical analysis.

52068444-ef0e-4634-9685-ec3c72bd6533.title: Measures of Central Tendency
52068444-ef0e-4634-9685-ec3c72bd6533.definition: The concept of values ​​representing the center of a data set. Includes the ability to recognize, describe and calculate averages, medians and quantiles to locate data.

96ed1765-e2cc-47b4-b8a9-e832a410506b.title: Variance & Interquartile Range
96ed1765-e2cc-47b4-b8a9-e832a410506b.definition: Concept of a measure of dispersion of a data set. Includes the ability to identify, describe and calculate variances and interquartile ranges to determine data dispersion.

d5d3c641-6da3-48f1-b4c9-f91bd364506d.title: Frequency Table
d5d3c641-6da3-48f1-b4c9-f91bd364506d.definition: Ability to create and interpret frequency tables to summarize the distribution of data.

f890d675-1095-4d92-9f21-92333b52336c.title: Data Visualization
f890d675-1095-4d92-9f21-92333b52336c.definition: Ability to display data graphically and interpret various types of graphs, especially histograms.

76649f5a-003c-4854-bc98-4135db629bc9.title: Univariate Data
76649f5a-003c-4854-bc98-4135db629bc9.definition: The concept of data having only one variable or one attribute.

4d665170-50b0-4b90-b09f-5f7766d4ad77.title: Point Estimation
4d665170-50b0-4b90-b09f-5f7766d4ad77.definition: The concept of using sample data to calculate a single value (point) to estimate a population parameter. Includes the ability to formulate maximum likelihood estimation in the linear-Gaussian setting as a least squares problem and calculate maximum likelihood estimates.

732d0688-0083-496d-afd0-68310161bf43.title: Confidence Interval
732d0688-0083-496d-afd0-68310161bf43.definition: The concept of an estimated range of values ​​for a population parameter, along with a degree of confidence that the interval contains the true parameter. Includes the ability to calculate confidence intervals as a measure of uncertainty.

f1684cfc-6ec1-42de-bb0c-1c7a6d925d5e.title: Maximum A Posteriori (MAP)
f1684cfc-6ec1-42de-bb0c-1c7a6d925d5e.definition: Ability to calculate maximum posterior estimates and establish relationships with the regularized least squares method.

8df0b859-be71-49b9-93a7-a2b1c83fcdc4.title: Sampling
8df0b859-be71-49b9-93a7-a2b1c83fcdc4.definition: Concepts and techniques of selecting a subset from a population for analysis.

e4fbeef2-70a1-4880-8121-d70f2918126d.title: Sampling Bias
e4fbeef2-70a1-4880-8121-d70f2918126d.definition: The concept of systematic bias in the sampling process, leading to inaccurate estimates.

1ca0a1e6-98a4-4a7c-8d21-8f2cfc431448.title: Sample Sufficiency
1ca0a1e6-98a4-4a7c-8d21-8f2cfc431448.definition: The concept of evaluating whether the size and quality of a sample is sufficient to draw reliable conclusions about a population.

c7e712da-6e7e-4605-98c3-9f87fb25b626.title: Bayesian vs. Frequentist
c7e712da-6e7e-4605-98c3-9f87fb25b626.definition: Differences and comparisons between two main approaches in inferential statistics: Bayesian statistics and frequentist statistics.

9bd3bf76-c774-45b3-9c25-79e9dab247c5.title: Multivariate Data
9bd3bf76-c774-45b3-9c25-79e9dab247c5.definition: The concept of data having multiple variables or attributes for each observation.

d664d90b-7a48-4313-b8f6-c745996f495c.title: Multivariate Estimation
d664d90b-7a48-4313-b8f6-c745996f495c.definition: Parameter estimation for multivariate data. Includes the ability to formulate the multivariate maximum likelihood estimation problem as a least squares problem and to interpret the geometric properties of maximum likelihood estimation.

8a3ffb9a-c6d6-4dfb-8bc3-b346183307cb.title: Multivariate Correlation
8a3ffb9a-c6d6-4dfb-8bc3-b346183307cb.definition: Concept of statistical relationships between multiple variables. Includes the ability to formalize and understand the concept of data correlation (e.g., in 2D).

fc7ccf66-3c9a-442c-8bef-1be573b00c4f.title: Multivariate Regression
fc7ccf66-3c9a-442c-8bef-1be573b00c4f.definition: Regression techniques for multivariate data. Includes the ability to infer and calculate the maximum likelihood solution for linear regression, infer and calculate the maximum posterior estimate for linear regression, and perform both types of estimation in the context of a polynomial regression problem.

b68c2660-964f-4f05-8518-39829676bbce.title: Data Transformation
b68c2660-964f-4f05-8518-39829676bbce.definition: Techniques that transform data to improve model performance or make data more consistent with assumptions.

b1660897-696f-47b3-8ea1-a3fedd883e58.title: Dimensionality Reduction
b1660897-696f-47b3-8ea1-a3fedd883e58.definition: Techniques for reducing the number of random variables are considered by obtaining a smaller set of key variables. Includes the ability to apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to data dimensionality reduction problems.

a2fb9bac-50e4-4fc4-ac07-38340a616026.title: Data Smoothing
a2fb9bac-50e4-4fc4-ac07-38340a616026.definition: Techniques that reduce noise or fluctuations in data to highlight trends and patterns.

55da6893-4f6b-4984-b929-08ac6388611e.title: Statistical Models & Algorithms
55da6893-4f6b-4984-b929-08ac6388611e.definition: Knowledge of statistical models and related algorithms for data analysis and prediction.

fcfe73a9-4bb1-42a4-bc44-95e92c23f4ee.title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
fcfe73a9-4bb1-42a4-bc44-95e92c23f4ee.definition: Data dimensionality reduction technique. Includes the ability to formulate and reason about PCA as a least squares problem, interpret PCA geometry, and describe when PCA works well (relating to correlated data).

8aa048b8-a40c-409f-9689-7b0a93052d08.title: Compression-Reconstruction Trade-off
8aa048b8-a40c-409f-9689-7b0a93052d08.definition: Concept of trade-off between data size reduction (compression) and the ability to recover the original data from the compressed version.

33d0c85f-b962-4877-ab91-c6fbfba57c5e.title: Linear Regression: Curve Fitting
33d0c85f-b962-4877-ab91-c6fbfba57c5e.definition: Ability to apply linear regression to fit curves to data. Includes geometric interpretation of linear regression solution (maximum likelihood).

210ebf45-2e78-4652-a6ae-95271005e283.title: Overfitting
210ebf45-2e78-4652-a6ae-95271005e283.definition: Concept of the phenomenon of models overlearning training data, leading to poor performance on new data.

bf26c0e7-ea16-4794-9347-1f98c00059ff.title: Cross-validation
bf26c0e7-ea16-4794-9347-1f98c00059ff.definition: Ability to discuss and apply cross-validation techniques in the context of overfitting and model selection (e.g., degrees of polynomials in a regression context).

3abb04f7-96df-4f99-a404-401b16de687a.title: Hypothesis Testing
3abb04f7-96df-4f99-a404-401b16de687a.definition: Concepts and methods for testing statistical hypotheses about populations based on sample data.

79e48270-8161-41c8-94f3-c3e1d6c02a97.title: Vector Definition & Representation
79e48270-8161-41c8-94f3-c3e1d6c02a97.definition: Describe the algebraic and geometric representations of vectors in Rn.

eb271a53-c8af-4c39-b92e-e2615efb59c2.title: Vector Operations
eb271a53-c8af-4c39-b92e-e2615efb59c2.definition: Vector operations include vector addition, vector multiplication by a scalar, and dot product.

8496f51b-de2d-4adc-91a4-bb58f29c88a4.title: Vector Geometric Interpretation
8496f51b-de2d-4adc-91a4-bb58f29c88a4.definition: understand the geometric meaning of vectors in Rn.

8b3da2fd-8108-4657-a662-0ba67ab9922a.title: Angle Between Vectors
8b3da2fd-8108-4657-a662-0ba67ab9922a.definition: Ability to calculate angle between two vectors in Rn.

2c69ef68-23d7-4274-9779-5b0b4e1af644.title: Vector Properties in Rn
2c69ef68-23d7-4274-9779-5b0b4e1af644.definition: List and understand the basic properties of vectors in n-dimensional space.

ac76e246-3a26-46cf-b4ab-044c5a61d8a0.title: Basic Matrix Operations
ac76e246-3a26-46cf-b4ab-044c5a61d8a0.definition: Basic matrix operations such as matrix addition, matrix multiplication with a scalar.

5867a4f3-f31d-4e7b-8e64-3f89563c86d5.title: Meaning of Ax=b
5867a4f3-f31d-4e7b-8e64-3f89563c86d5.definition: understand the matrix equation Ax=b as a system of linear equations and how it is represented.

4942f074-2e88-42e8-8ceb-e36e4fba0aaa.title: Advanced Matrix Operations
4942f074-2e88-42e8-8ceb-e36e4fba0aaa.definition: Ability to perform common matrix operations such as addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication, and matrix transposition. Includes recognizing when two matrices can be multiplied together.

6a0e601f-5644-4ab8-a677-9aea1b64d598.title: Matrix-Vector Equation
6a0e601f-5644-4ab8-a677-9aea1b64d598.definition: understand and work with equations involving matrices and vectors.

6d9099e4-8a13-4d38-afe6-6bb03ae3ebc2.title: Matrix Geometric Interpretation
6d9099e4-8a13-4d38-afe6-6bb03ae3ebc2.definition: Interpret matrices and their operations in geometric space.

291aed39-b738-4cdf-bae3-456f49f2a593.title: Geometric Transformations by Matrix
291aed39-b738-4cdf-bae3-456f49f2a593.definition: Relate various matrix transformations (e.g., rotation, scale, translation) to geometric illustrations.

ecf3ecf6-a8c6-4904-9114-95622cfdba13.title: Homogeneous Linear Systems
ecf3ecf6-a8c6-4904-9114-95622cfdba13.definition: Ability to relate a matrix to a system of homogeneous linear equations.

06d424d9-416f-4ffa-b7fc-567b9188ccdd.title: Linear Systems
06d424d9-416f-4ffa-b7fc-567b9188ccdd.definition: Ability to formulate, solve, apply and interpret properties of systems of linear equations. Includes solving systems of linear equations using matrix language and converting word problems into linear equations.

d3e63453-555d-4d53-abe0-719fd81afb1c.title: Elementary Row Operations
d3e63453-555d-4d53-abe0-719fd81afb1c.definition: Ability to perform basic row operations on matrices.

357827b1-1d47-40e3-ad15-d978a1929a04.title: Augmented Matrix
357827b1-1d47-40e3-ad15-d978a1929a04.definition: Ability to relate extended matrices to a system of linear equations.

58424cd6-6ccb-4c24-a4dc-c21157068161.title: Gaussian Elimination
58424cd6-6ccb-4c24-a4dc-c21157068161.definition: Ability to perform Gauss elimination to solve systems of linear equations.

ca174cad-2629-46ca-91d6-667d4ef2e45d.title: Linear Independence
ca174cad-2629-46ca-91d6-667d4ef2e45d.definition: The concept of vector sets cannot be represented as a linear combination of other vectors in the same set.

f6c47c33-8e21-4767-8b49-8c5e7e348e18.title: Span
f6c47c33-8e21-4767-8b49-8c5e7e348e18.definition: The concept of the set of all possible linear combinations of a set of vectors.

ef10ca1a-c6b2-4dab-9ad7-0e34b1fbfd45.title: Vector Space Basis
ef10ca1a-c6b2-4dab-9ad7-0e34b1fbfd45.definition: The concept of a set of linearly independent vectors forming a subspace.

8089da7b-1014-47dd-8022-6ea7a5f1c959.title: Vector Subspace
8089da7b-1014-47dd-8022-6ea7a5f1c959.definition: Define and understand the properties of a subspace in a vector space.

98c11fdb-254c-4990-a5e5-b9f839de5fbc.title: Orthogonality
98c11fdb-254c-4990-a5e5-b9f839de5fbc.definition: The concept of vectors or subspaces being perpendicular to each other.

c62c13d2-9ccc-4c3d-8dc6-cec38a698190.title: Projection (Linear Algebra)
c62c13d2-9ccc-4c3d-8dc6-cec38a698190.definition: Concept of projecting a vector onto a subspace or another vector.

9ecc5990-a4ec-4681-a1ce-5910366cb522.title: Least Squares (Linear Algebra)
9ecc5990-a4ec-4681-a1ce-5910366cb522.definition: Method to find approximate solutions for inconsistent linear equations by minimizing the sum of squares of the residuals.

b2ae95a9-3b4c-4796-acd9-8a5dad1f9ba6.title: Orthogonal Basis
b2ae95a9-3b4c-4796-acd9-8a5dad1f9ba6.definition: Concept of a basis whose vectors are all orthogonal to each other.

42883f04-d36b-49ea-96e3-c491be2eb83b.title: Polynomial Linear Combination
42883f04-d36b-49ea-96e3-c491be2eb83b.definition: Concept of creating a new polynomial by taking a weighted sum of other polynomials.

bfee2053-4917-45d3-a9f8-e63511851879.title: Bezier Curve
bfee2053-4917-45d3-a9f8-e63511851879.definition: The concept of parametric curves is widely used in computer graphics and computer-aided design.

53d084b2-1a8a-42e7-a673-a691ed19107e.title: Eigenvector
53d084b2-1a8a-42e7-a673-a691ed19107e.definition: The concept of vectors only scales (scales) by a constant when a linear transformation is applied.

100088ab-053c-406a-8e3d-85916937066a.title: Eigenvalue
100088ab-053c-406a-8e3d-85916937066a.definition: The concept of scalar values ​​represents the scaling factor to which the eigenvectors are scaled.

7043ce42-b945-4374-b6a5-dd87047af1aa.title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
7043ce42-b945-4374-b6a5-dd87047af1aa.definition: understand PCA as an important application of linear algebra to data dimensionality reduction.

30509dd1-f520-4c2f-9ade-1561097bbd6d.title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
30509dd1-f520-4c2f-9ade-1561097bbd6d.definition: The concept of a strong matrix decomposition has many applications in computer science.

392acb58-8f41-4073-908f-2127df494ef4.title: PageRank Algorithm
392acb58-8f41-4073-908f-2127df494ef4.definition: understand the PageRank algorithm and how it uses linear algebra to rank web pages.

0f712f75-3070-4e2e-b4d9-d6dd53deb38a.title: Linear Algebra in Computer Graphics
0f712f75-3070-4e2e-b4d9-d6dd53deb38a.definition: Explore applications of linear algebra in computer graphics, such as geometric transformations and projections.

93dd3696-3b06-46ce-97bd-0f5e7f926fff.title: Subspace Examples
93dd3696-3b06-46ce-97bd-0f5e7f926fff.definition: List examples of subspaces of a vector space.

a8a4ac6e-af3f-49be-a24f-c197afa756c2.title: Subspace & Vector Space Properties
a8a4ac6e-af3f-49be-a24f-c197afa756c2.definition: Recognize and use the basic properties of subspaces and vector spaces.

79152c18-a827-4b30-aa8b-5bd3c082fef5.title: Identifying Subspaces
79152c18-a827-4b30-aa8b-5bd3c082fef5.definition: Determines whether specific subsets of a vector space are subspaces or not.

cbf2f7d2-21eb-4038-aaad-6b9176102f3d.title: Basis Existence in Abstract Spaces
cbf2f7d2-21eb-4038-aaad-6b9176102f3d.definition: Discuss the existence of a basis for an abstract vector space.

e82453de-541d-4e12-b82b-8964bd8d175b.title: Vector Coordinates (Given Basis)
e82453de-541d-4e12-b82b-8964bd8d175b.definition: Describes the coordinates of a vector relative to a given basis.

4c7fbc56-073c-4d34-a51a-6afee3f5d2f7.title: Basis & Dimension (Finite Spaces)
4c7fbc56-073c-4d34-a51a-6afee3f5d2f7.definition: Determine the basis and dimensions of a finite dimensional space.

ac3c312f-8c21-42bc-8f52-f2d0d95a187a.title: Spanning Sets for Vectors in Rn
ac3c312f-8c21-42bc-8f52-f2d0d95a187a.definition: Discuss the generating systems (spanning sets) for vectors in Rn.

11ac466f-e0f1-4213-b3b0-911c21838d84.title: Linear Independence for Vectors in Rn
11ac466f-e0f1-4213-b3b0-911c21838d84.definition: Discuss linear independence for vectors in Rn.

42a659f2-2530-4c63-acdc-9603f54cb959.title: Vector Space Dimension Definition
42a659f2-2530-4c63-acdc-9603f54cb959.definition: Defines the number of dimensions of a vector space.

5578f699-20c3-4079-ab91-20b1a74fc92f.title: Orthogonal Projection Calculation
5578f699-20c3-4079-ab91-20b1a74fc92f.definition: Computes the orthogonal projection of a vector onto a subspace, with a basis for that subspace.

cd43dcf8-fc12-488c-b6cf-7f37cdf55ff9.title: Projection & Least Squares Relation
cd43dcf8-fc12-488c-b6cf-7f37cdf55ff9.definition: Explain the relationship between orthogonal projections and least square approximations.

aa6cb6f0-fe6b-414b-8aea-425d109decda.title: Polynomial Basis Linear Combination

23ccc135-ee82-4bda-bf88-5316c7753566.definition: Ability to calculate the area of ​​basic geometric shapes such as squares, rectangles, triangles, circles.

8de3f9da-4e44-4c5d-b230-73e9fcec4f2b.title: Functions
8de3f9da-4e44-4c5d-b230-73e9fcec4f2b.definition: Concept of functions, domain of determination, domain of values ​​and basic types of functions.

de93a303-43d4-427a-b0d2-9c069831683e.title: Function Notation
de93a303-43d4-427a-b0d2-9c069831683e.definition: understand and use the symbol f(x) to represent functions and their values.

7592bb49-e79e-41ba-a359-ec7113f058bb.title: Graphing Functions
7592bb49-e79e-41ba-a359-ec7113f058bb.definition: Skills in geometric representation of functions on the coordinate plane.

98aafa24-9ff2-45eb-b385-89eb9c4057ed.title: Function Graph Interpretation
98aafa24-9ff2-45eb-b385-89eb9c4057ed.definition: Ability to analyze information and draw conclusions from function graphs.

1a8954e7-3ce4-473a-9f40-ee2e0be62ddc.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Functions
1a8954e7-3ce4-473a-9f40-ee2e0be62ddc.definition: General understanding of exponential and logarithmic functions and their graphs.

8189f8b8-f0a9-44a1-85e7-1cb637f60243.title: Trigonometry
8189f8b8-f0a9-44a1-85e7-1cb637f60243.definition: Understanding of basic trigonometric functions and the unit circle.

ebd6b717-44de-4b83-b325-f41252755547.title: Computer Components
ebd6b717-44de-4b83-b325-f41252755547.definition: understand the basic building blocks and components of a computer system, including logic gates, flip-flops, registers, interconnections, datapaths, control units, and memory.

6ddc79fd-d7b6-42f4-8fd0-407cd7f1d174.title: Hardware as Computation Model
6ddc79fd-d7b6-42f4-8fd0-407cd7f1d174.definition: The concept of hardware as a fundamental model for computation, including basic logic building blocks, logic expressions, minimization, and sum of product forms.

54e5ce16-8482-45b3-bc9b-d26e7daebfe7.title: Basic Logic Gates
54e5ce16-8482-45b3-bc9b-d26e7daebfe7.definition: Learn about logic gates and other basic components used to build digital electronic circuits.

220ca8d3-6ca1-4fd0-af48-cc18c645fbf1.title: Boolean Expressions
220ca8d3-6ca1-4fd0-af48-cc18c645fbf1.definition: understand and work with boolean expressions that describe the operation of logic circuits.

b699d217-5337-4d77-9f98-71d1fcb615d7.title: Boolean Minimization
b699d217-5337-4d77-9f98-71d1fcb615d7.definition: Techniques for minimizing logic expressions to simplify circuit design and improve performance.

b9168e43-a53a-4420-97ae-802e60ebabc6.title: Sum of Products (SOP)
b9168e43-a53a-4420-97ae-802e60ebabc6.definition: understand the standard form of logic expressions, widely used in digital circuit design.

eae001ef-f097-41de-975a-d62719ba6f3a.title: Programming Abstraction
eae001ef-f097-41de-975a-d62719ba6f3a.definition: Learn about abstractions used in programming to manage system complexity, such as functions, classes, modules.

2f0b7ce0-3695-4e29-9af9-2cd915e1589d.title: API
2f0b7ce0-3695-4e29-9af9-2cd915e1589d.definition: The concept of interfaces allows software components to interact with each other, such as APIs.

6927e2e8-c492-4e41-bad5-244b742d9dc2.title: Library Usage
6927e2e8-c492-4e41-bad5-244b742d9dc2.definition: understand how to use software libraries to reuse code and build applications more efficiently.

241b59eb-4092-4c34-ba8d-325d8017160f.title: Application-OS Interaction
241b59eb-4092-4c34-ba8d-325d8017160f.definition: Master the differences and how applications interact with services provided by the operating system.

43b64179-62cb-40e2-b5b7-67d30f2f2e9d.title: Remote Procedure Call (RPC)
43b64179-62cb-40e2-b5b7-67d30f2f2e9d.definition: The concept of the RPC mechanism, allows a program to call a procedure (or function) in another address space (usually on another computer) as if it were a local procedure.

b53f65f5-36da-4036-9130-c78c815571ea.title: Pipeline Concept
b53f65f5-36da-4036-9130-c78c815571ea.definition: understand pipeline architecture, a technique for improving performance by processing multiple commands or tasks at the same time in overlapping stages.

2b656b2e-f589-495f-b873-8087802e2ed6.title: Overlapping Processing Stages
2b656b2e-f589-495f-b873-8087802e2ed6.definition: The concept of executing different stages of a task or multiple tasks in parallel, is often applied in pipeline architecture.

e1186179-65f6-407e-acff-e7d6f1bef05b.title: Scaling Concepts
e1186179-65f6-407e-acff-e7d6f1bef05b.definition: understand system scalability, which is the ability to handle increased workloads effectively.

60c3ff1b-04b6-40a1-af46-0d12cb493093.title: Performance vs. Problem Size
60c3ff1b-04b6-40a1-af46-0d12cb493093.definition: analyze the relationship between a system's performance and the size of the problem it is solving, especially in the context of scaling.

6b212077-563d-4db6-99c4-0723441086ad.title: System Fundamentals
6b212077-563d-4db6-99c4-0723441086ad.definition: The unit focuses on the fundamental concepts underlying computer systems. Includes concepts of states, state transitions, and finite state machines.

80c911d2-0ce2-4dd4-a537-3e4a5645ee31.title: Resource Management
80c911d2-0ce2-4dd4-a537-3e4a5645ee31.definition: The unit focuses on the principles and mechanisms of resource management in computer systems. Includes resource allocation and scheduling.

b6c02c1a-de3f-43ca-a437-e349a46b43e0.title: Resource Management (Core)
b6c02c1a-de3f-43ca-a437-e349a46b43e0.definition: More advanced unit of knowledge on the principles and mechanisms of resource management in computer systems, intended for advanced students.

1042b0c0-0073-480b-9e93-e3e7fad52dbb.title: System Performance
1042b0c0-0073-480b-9e93-e3e7fad52dbb.definition: The unit focuses on system performance aspects, including the topics of proximity, virtualization, and isolation.

96eec801-1f53-4924-a862-5cf6d89305d0.title: System Performance (Core)
96eec801-1f53-4924-a862-5cf6d89305d0.definition: More advanced units on system performance, including deeper topics on approximation, virtualization, and isolation, for advanced students.

f24f4abc-ccd5-4655-9fe6-803056858567.title: Performance Evaluation
f24f4abc-ccd5-4655-9fe6-803056858567.definition: The unit focuses on methods and techniques for evaluating system performance, covering topics from qualitative and quantitative evaluation.

53e77e9a-c628-4ce7-8b57-a9d210118a21.title: Performance Evaluation (Core)
53e77e9a-c628-4ce7-8b57-a9d210118a21.definition: More advanced units on system performance evaluation, including complex quantitative methods and models, for advanced students.

67206331-7da9-4c71-b1bb-a1ce941fbcbf.title: System Reliability
67206331-7da9-4c71-b1bb-a1ce941fbcbf.definition: The unit focuses on principles and techniques for ensuring computer system reliability, including the concept of redundancy.

03d9639c-7595-4217-8354-bcf1f28290d1.title: System Reliability (Core)
03d9639c-7595-4217-8354-bcf1f28290d1.definition: A more advanced unit on system reliability, including advanced techniques and models for designing fault-tolerant systems, for advanced students.

89d76b7d-c4a2-4dc9-be2b-666b49150221.title: System Security
89d76b7d-c4a2-4dc9-be2b-666b49150221.definition: The new unit focuses on fundamentals and security measures for computer systems.

cf8f539a-19ba-4aeb-bb0a-6012caf2ad59.title: System Security (Core)
cf8f539a-19ba-4aeb-bb0a-6012caf2ad59.definition: More advanced units on system security, including in-depth topics on vulnerabilities, attacks and defenses, for advanced students.

15c7bc60-91e4-44be-a503-f9f586ee311b.title: System Design
15c7bc60-91e4-44be-a503-f9f586ee311b.definition: The new unit focuses on the basic principles and methods of computer systems design.

a823b266-0ad3-4ef7-bd56-076082ba5816.title: System Design (Core)
a823b266-0ad3-4ef7-bd56-076082ba5816.definition: More advanced units on systems design, including methodologies, design patterns, and architectural considerations, for advanced students.

1386568d-a4df-42b6-a834-136e893a71bd.title: Social, Ethical, Professional
1386568d-a4df-42b6-a834-136e893a71bd.definition: New units have been added, covering topics on social responsibility, professional ethics, and issues related to practicing in the field of computer science. Class hours are included in total SEP hours.

55155e7d-2346-40ba-bcaf-79f32d18e76f.title: Computer Building Blocks
55155e7d-2346-40ba-bcaf-79f32d18e76f.definition: Describe the basic components that make up a computer (e.g. CPU, memory, I/O devices) and their functions.

e6655d37-7312-44bb-97e4-d7d901edd6fe.title: Computer Architecture History
e6655d37-7312-44bb-97e4-d7d901edd6fe.definition: Master the role and evolution of the basic building blocks of computers in the historical development of computer architecture.

a8ccd46a-b54e-4b39-9ae2-b7b541d3cb91.title: Logic Circuit Design
a8ccd46a-b54e-4b39-9ae2-b7b541d3cb91.definition: Ability to design simple logic circuits using basic logic gates to solve specific problems, such as adders.

de8d4058-a84d-4090-9c0e-9e7e7ae757cb.title: Layered System Architecture
de8d4058-a84d-4090-9c0e-9e7e7ae757cb.definition: understand how computer systems are built in a layered architecture, based on the principle of separation of concerns, with clearly defined interfaces that hide the details of lower layers from higher layers.

0f0aa963-da27-4b37-8230-9e7fd866dd29.title: Separation of Concerns (SoC)
0f0aa963-da27-4b37-8230-9e7fd866dd29.definition: Design principle in which a system is divided into parts with as little functional overlap as possible, each responsible for a separate concern.

1a5dc950-86a9-4744-8e39-f54b84c0814a.title: Well-defined Interfaces
1a5dc950-86a9-4744-8e39-f54b84c0814a.definition: The concept of clearly designed interfaces between components or classes of a system, helping them to communicate effectively without knowing internal implementation details.

eeb104ca-6366-4aa9-8af8-084effd66925.title: Information Hiding
eeb104ca-6366-4aa9-8af8-084effd66925.definition: The principle of abstraction, where complex details of lower layers are hidden from higher layers, simplifies system design and use.

4e99d0fd-eecd-45f8-b9aa-b4253760543b.title: Hardware Layer
4e99d0fd-eecd-45f8-b9aa-b4253760543b.definition: The physical layer of a computer system, including the CPU, memory, and peripherals, where the most basic operations are performed.

2c89c00b-4b97-474e-ad8d-a276a9640ee8.title: OS Layer
2c89c00b-4b97-474e-ad8d-a276a9640ee8.definition: The software layer provides the interface between hardware and applications, manages system resources, and provides basic services.

8c68a634-a729-470b-9e2b-6b2bde798e81.title: Virtual Machine (VM)
8c68a634-a729-470b-9e2b-6b2bde798e81.definition: The abstraction layer allows running multiple independent operating system environments on the same physical hardware, or an emulated environment.

b0442d4d-7eac-44d8-a515-faaf30a795cb.title: Application Layer
b0442d4d-7eac-44d8-a515-faaf30a795cb.definition: The highest layer in the system architecture, where the programs and services with which users directly interact are executed.

8fc3cfb9-8aa2-41a8-819b-39e2e58ce1f2.title: Error Detection
8fc3cfb9-8aa2-41a8-819b-39e2e58ce1f2.definition: Methods and techniques used to identify and detect errors occurring in system components or layers.

7547a42b-f1ad-459d-a313-67c91d1cb56b.title: Cross-Layer Error Signaling
7547a42b-f1ad-459d-a313-67c91d1cb56b.definition: How errors are reported and propagated from layer to layer in a layered system, allowing higher layers to recognize and react.

fe93b29b-1177-42de-a144-220caffda162.title: Layered System Error Handling
fe93b29b-1177-42de-a144-220caffda162.definition: Strategies and mechanisms to handle detected and signaled errors, ensuring system stability and resilience across layers.

9aa9047c-30fc-45c1-a108-be3e6500cf07.title: Layered Program Design
9aa9047c-30fc-45c1-a108-be3e6500cf07.definition: Ability to design and implement a simple program (e.g., TCP client/server application) by applying layering principles.

a2dc3d2f-6963-44b1-9da1-1550ba786849.title: TCP Client/Server Programming
a2dc3d2f-6963-44b1-9da1-1550ba786849.definition: Skills to develop basic network applications using TCP protocol, with client-server model.

906d33fd-9ce9-4c1a-b79e-d14d7d0465a7.title: Program Error Recovery
906d33fd-9ce9-4c1a-b79e-d14d7d0465a7.definition: Methods to handle and recover from program errors that occur during execution, to maintain stable operation.

999839d2-2a01-465a-8b72-143d50436dc7.title: Error State Reflection
999839d2-2a01-465a-8b72-143d50436dc7.definition: Technique for communicating error status from lower layers to higher layers in a layered application, allowing the upper layers to react appropriately.

379ddb07-b84a-4c1c-b595-29c6f1d104a8.title: Layered Program Debugging
379ddb07-b84a-4c1c-b595-29c6f1d104a8.definition: Ability to identify and correct errors in programs built on a layered architecture, using specialized debugging tools.

876aa0d9-fe55-4c7c-a4f2-b304d41d6225.title: Program Flow Monitoring
876aa0d9-fe55-4c7c-a4f2-b304d41d6225.definition: Technique of monitoring and recording the execution flow of a program to understand its behavior and determine the cause of errors.

8d8b8dda-27b3-45f6-96d3-8dd7cff2a5d6.title: Step-by-Step Debugging
8d8b8dda-27b3-45f6-96d3-8dd7cff2a5d6.definition: Debugging techniques allow the programmer to execute a program one instruction at a time, observing the state of variables and the flow of control.

d6e42721-67d4-49e7-a652-bfe89951a386.title: Debugging Tools
d6e42721-67d4-49e7-a652-bfe89951a386.definition: understand and use specialized software tools to detect, analyze and fix errors in program source code.

80bce3f6-e923-444d-a940-a9d03534ae19.title: Strong Scaling
80bce3f6-e923-444d-a940-a9d03534ae19.definition: The concept of strong scaling, describes how the time to solve a fixed-sized problem changes as the number of processing resources increases.

be7cfbd4-7aac-418f-9fec-6132418b28f9.title: Weak Scaling
be7cfbd4-7aac-418f-9fec-6132418b28f9.definition: The concept of weak scaling, describes how the time it takes to solve a problem when both the problem size and the number of processing resources increase proportionally.

febfa30d-0f42-4f7f-915a-74aa218d9826.title: Resource & Problem Scale Impact
febfa30d-0f42-4f7f-915a-74aa218d9826.definition: evaluate how the performance of a system or application changes based on the scale of the problem being solved and the scale of allocated resources.

c3574e41-ee3a-496a-b91f-f5bd3dafb635.title: Digital vs. Analog Systems
c3574e41-ee3a-496a-b91f-f5bd3dafb635.definition: Difference between digital system and analog system.

9248b0f9-6e0b-48dd-9d4a-2b86e86aee06.title: Discrete vs. Continuous Systems
9248b0f9-6e0b-48dd-9d4a-2b86e86aee06.definition: Difference between discrete and continuous systems.

7caa671d-0494-476b-a923-91eb26aeb99b.title: Basic Logic Gates
7caa671d-0494-476b-a923-91eb26aeb99b.definition: Describe basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, etc.) and their functions in electronic circuit design.

bbffb4f1-12e7-46bc-b2e2-c90969be0e7c.title: Logic Expressions
bbffb4f1-12e7-46bc-b2e2-c90969be0e7c.definition: understand and create logical expressions to describe the behavior of number systems, using Boolean operators.

c9da0167-19c0-4aed-9a6c-1fda4a72aeeb.title: Boolean Logic Minimization
c9da0167-19c0-4aed-9a6c-1fda4a72aeeb.definition: Techniques and methods for simplifying Boolean logic expressions to optimize electronic circuits and minimize resources.

48f6b425-123c-41ef-a6f0-7864576fe3ff.title: Digital System Clock
48f6b425-123c-41ef-a6f0-7864576fe3ff.definition: The role of clock in synchronizing and controlling operations in digital systems.

7e686e13-b390-4132-be04-e36264d285d6.title: Digital System State
7e686e13-b390-4132-be04-e36264d285d6.definition: The concept of state is a set of currently stored values ​​of a system, influencing its future behavior.

c45550dd-e023-4f45-a854-34d4fbbc7498.title: Digital System Sequencing
c45550dd-e023-4f45-a854-34d4fbbc7498.definition: How operations and state transitions are arranged in a particular sequence to perform a certain function in a digital system.

bbce286b-3677-4cff-8988-2f348cd28e9b.title: State & State Transitions
bbce286b-3677-4cff-8988-2f348cd28e9b.definition: The concept of the state of a system and how it transitions from one state to another, including the starting state, final state, and lifecycle of states.

53010b50-66d9-40b5-87d7-74e16c68f46c.title: Finite State Machine (FSM)
53010b50-66d9-40b5-87d7-74e16c68f46c.definition: Concepts and applications of finite state machines, including types such as non-deterministic finite state machines (NFA) and deterministic finite state machines (DFA).

9ce2f003-848a-4d62-a534-e58011e2cb97.title: Combinational Logic
9ce2f003-848a-4d62-a534-e58011e2cb97.definition: Logic circuits whose output depends only on the current input, with no memory or previous state.

eedc28e8-dad6-4323-a1ea-987e7c744207.title: Sequential Logic
eedc28e8-dad6-4323-a1ea-987e7c744207.definition: Logic circuits whose output depends on both the current input and the previous state (with a memory element).

98e08b60-8b91-4f3e-93a9-5f2705483125.title: Register
98e08b60-8b91-4f3e-93a9-5f2705483125.definition: Small, high-speed storage elements in a CPU or digital circuit, used to hold data or addresses temporarily.

4eb90dbb-1b34-41bb-be8e-2eafaadb6dd1.title: Digital System Memory
4eb90dbb-1b34-41bb-be8e-2eafaadb6dd1.definition: Devices or systems used to store data in computer and digital systems.

1facd0c0-0b97-4e40-9392-d9a151726291.title: Computer as State Machine
1facd0c0-0b97-4e40-9392-d9a151726291.definition: understand how a computer can be modeled as a state machine, with different states corresponding to current data and instructions.

a421d8dc-7f19-4b13-86ef-882dae98e5be.title: Network Protocol as State Machine
a421d8dc-7f19-4b13-86ef-882dae98e5be.definition: understand how network protocols can be modeled as a state machine, with states corresponding to different stages of the communication process.

a9220fc9-31f9-4b72-9806-a5b404fddc2a.title: Sequential Processing
a9220fc9-31f9-4b72-9806-a5b404fddc2a.definition: The concept of performing tasks or commands in a step-by-step sequence, each step completed before the next step begins.

1534e75a-b921-4723-9d03-90fee1cd8590.title: Parallel Processing
1534e75a-b921-4723-9d03-90fee1cd8590.definition: The concept of executing multiple tasks or instructions at the same time, often by using multiple processors or processing cores.

74adea72-8d13-411e-aabd-b8155fb35aa4.title: App-Level Single-Threaded Processing
74adea72-8d13-411e-aabd-b8155fb35aa4.definition: Execution of applications at the application level uses only a single thread, performing tasks sequentially.

4881c694-c2f0-4fd4-8597-bf4951c96b8a.title: App-Level Request Parallelism
4881c694-c2f0-4fd4-8597-bf4951c96b8a.definition: Parallel processing methods at the application level, focus on the simultaneous processing of multiple requests, for example in web services, client-server architectures or distributed systems.

d6ae5db0-ed21-4a7d-b16d-95f481a189d2.title: One Thread Per Server
d6ae5db0-ed21-4a7d-b16d-95f481a189d2.definition: Parallel processing model in which each server processes requests using a single thread.

07462e09-7042-42d1-9914-be92e5c63e63.title: Multi-Thread Multi-Server
07462e09-7042-42d1-9914-be92e5c63e63.definition: The parallel processing model is more complex, where multiple threads are used across multiple servers to enhance concurrency.

b819b6bf-b8a3-49be-a96f-328b4878d710.title: App-Level Pipelining
b819b6bf-b8a3-49be-a96f-328b4878d710.definition: Parallel processing technique in which different stages of a task are performed simultaneously on different elements of the system, similar to an assembly line.

79a27e46-eb4a-44b8-a551-19fc9551acad.title: Digital & Analog System Examples
79a27e46-eb4a-44b8-a551-19fc9551acad.definition: Ability to identify and provide real-life examples of digital and analog systems, clarifying the differences between them.

95d32c21-6ddb-4cf5-9551-44404325b9d7.title: Discrete & Continuous System Examples
95d32c21-6ddb-4cf5-9551-44404325b9d7.definition: Ability to identify and provide practical examples of discrete and continuous systems, clarifying the differences between them.

bdbd20f4-8d90-4f78-b94c-062cb06e4527.title: Computation as State Transition System
bdbd20f4-8d90-4f78-b94c-062cb06e4527.definition: Describes computational processes as a system characterized by a set of known configurations (states) and transitions from a single configuration (state) to another.

c7dfa59d-37ef-44c3-b27b-57886489a747.title: Stateless Systems
c7dfa59d-37ef-44c3-b27b-57886489a747.definition: Describes systems whose output depends only on the current input, without storing any information about previous transactions.

f4c95cfc-13cf-4c9f-93bb-4bd91fe945ec.title: Stateful Systems
f4c95cfc-13cf-4c9f-93bb-4bd91fe945ec.definition: Describes systems whose output depends on both the current input and a previous state (with memory/history), storing information about past transactions or events.

ba5066f7-747e-4ed1-9e7f-339c81ba8a6b.title: FSM Problem Description
ba5066f7-747e-4ed1-9e7f-339c81ba8a6b.definition: Ability to create state machine descriptions to solve simple problems, such as traffic light sequences or pattern recognizers.

9ac96cec-0728-4d00-9ce6-2609857a430a.title: Traffic Light FSM
9ac96cec-0728-4d00-9ce6-2609857a430a.definition: apply finite state machines to design and describe the operating sequence of traffic lights.

536f16e6-e7bc-4b8f-b321-59c2d6292c0d.title: Pattern Recognizer FSM
536f16e6-e7bc-4b8f-b321-59c2d6292c0d.definition: apply finite state machines to design and describe pattern recognition systems.

a9377f1c-0344-4b5f-a560-c34d1d774ade.title: Computer as Instruction FSM
a9377f1c-0344-4b5f-a560-c34d1d774ade.definition: Describes how a computer operates as a state machine, with the ability to interpret and execute machine instructions, switching between states based on these instructions.

5aeada3a-de86-48b9-ba05-46a968a6b965.title: Program/Network Protocol FSM
5aeada3a-de86-48b9-ba05-46a968a6b965.definition: Explain how a program or network protocol can be represented as a state machine and that alternative representations can exist for the same computation.

4a490d09-a0bb-4705-819f-14064931d1cf.title: FSM Time-Series Behavior
4a490d09-a0bb-4705-819f-14064931d1cf.definition: Infer the time series behavior of a state machine from its state machine representation (for example, a state machine that manages a TCP connection).

1095ca4c-8f2c-465c-a898-9d0f747aa94a.title: Sequential & Parallel Programs
1095ca4c-8f2c-465c-a898-9d0f747aa94a.definition: Write a simple sequential problem and a simple parallel version of the same program.

ce9a9f74-6e04-40b7-a261-2c0bfcbca9c0.title: Parallel Performance & Speedup
ce9a9f74-6e04-40b7-a261-2c0bfcbca9c0.definition: evaluate the performance of simple sequential and parallel versions of a program with different problem sizes and describe the speedup achieved.

3f712029-2e74-4c66-bea0-d5b55d97c02e.definition: Describe on the execution timeline how parallel events and activities can occur simultaneously. Explain how work can be done in less time if parallelism is possible.

d7f7a4e0-98ad-4a5a-b724-4a461ae52384.definition: understand different types of computer resources such as shared processor, memory, disk, and network bandwidth.

d16323d1-9460-43fb-971b-c398832c55d1.definition: understand popular resource allocation/scheduling algorithms such as FCFS (first-come-first-serve), priority-based scheduling, fair scheduling, and priority scheduling.

8c065a61-275c-41fd-8137-4eed66e94129.definition: analyze the advantages and disadvantages of popular scheduling algorithms.

c372fe93-5ece-4b54-bd39-da2890ebab8c.definition: Defines how finite computing resources (e.g., shared processor, memory, storage, and network bandwidth) are managed through careful allocation to existing entities.

bda91cbd-4bf9-46b6-add1-bd81b89f973d.title: Scheduling Algorithm Mechanics
bda91cbd-4bf9-46b6-add1-bd81b89f973d.definition: Describe how common resource allocation/scheduling algorithms work.

7df0cfdb-6b14-4734-a4ec-c02ddcadbb76.definition: Develop popular scheduling algorithms and evaluate their performance.

4d6a23c6-4182-4071-9a8a-e6be65776e19.definition: Describe the advantages and disadvantages of common scheduling algorithms.

b699e0f8-9163-40c0-ad17-7c12893aa84a.title: Computer System Latency
b699e0f8-9163-40c0-ad17-7c12893aa84a.definition: understand the concept of latency in general computer systems.

97e0ca21-1e16-4aff-bb68-a52138cf835d.definition: understand the relationship between the speed of light (one foot per nanosecond) and computer clock speed (one GHz).

673ac4c7-9ef4-4251-a41e-c5be2d6ddb23.definition: Compare latency between memory, disk, and network-accessed memory.

d0cccea4-9e0d-4ec0-a3b2-962a4e10e85f.definition: understand caches and how spatial locality and temporal locality affect performance in processors and systems.

a4778042-4a6d-4865-9c73-f3246e85fba6.definition: understand caches and cache coherency in databases, operating systems, distributed systems, and computer architecture.

b11b65b6-757e-4582-b5c5-d75ba5ad19d8.definition: Introduction to the processor memory hierarchy.

959611a3-f8f4-43ce-bc9c-9c5548beaf16.definition: Formula used to calculate the average time a system takes to access data from memory, taking into account the memory hierarchy (cache, RAM).

5a111902-aa27-4e2d-9760-bb7c831a3174.definition: Explain why virtualization and isolation mechanisms are important in computer systems, especially to ensure safety (protection) and stable, predictable performance between virtual environments.

58d393c8-1915-4d84-a07a-0751875269b4.definition: Describe the concept of levels of indirection in a computer system, with the specific example of virtual memory used to effectively manage physical memory resources.

f4649c36-39f0-4e29-8f71-6575f694cc4e.title: Virtualization Implementation Methods
f4649c36-39f0-4e29-8f71-6575f694cc4e.definition: Different techniques and methods are used to realize virtual memory and virtual machines in computer systems.

c96c5f2f-8ebd-4ba4-abf8-bc759f77fe51.definition: Ability to describe and analyze the components that cause overall latency in a computer system, including latency from memory access, disk storage, and network communications.

4a79ec12-38bc-42c9-bd89-7e52141ade75.title: Locality & Performance
4a79ec12-38bc-42c9-bd89-7e52141ade75.definition: Explain why the principle of locality (locality of reference - space and time) plays an important role in optimizing and determining the performance of a computer system, especially in cache usage.

07a36978-08ba-4dee-9197-4b6c00e117c3.title: AMAT Calculation
07a36978-08ba-4dee-9197-4b6c00e117c3.definition: Ability to calculate average memory access time based on parameters such as access time of each memory level and hit/miss ratio.

afabd0a6-95f4-44ee-a380-0832726eb767.definition: Describe the trade-off relationships between the capacity of memory levels, hit/miss rates, and access times to optimize the overall performance of the memory hierarchy.

b8ff3e1a-bca9-4be6-b991-0d1933dcd1fd.definition: Explain why it is necessary to isolate and protect the execution of individual programs and environments when they share the same underlying hardware or software resources.

92bef6f7-8d1e-4463-9008-70f96ec0367b.definition: Describe how the concept of indirection (e.g., through virtual memory, virtual machines) is used to create the illusion that each program or environment has a separate computer and resources, even when they are actually shared.

e917d1fd-c2c2-4289-9fe8-eee6b641711b.definition: Ability to evaluate the performance of applications running on separate virtual machines and determine the extent to which performance isolation mechanisms prevent interference with each other.

fbd7bbce-4e11-4023-beb4-a359787b4b80.title: Performance Metrics
fbd7bbce-4e11-4023-beb4-a359787b4b80.definition: Specific quantities or indices used to measure and evaluate the performance of a computer system.

1f59cb2a-d61d-4015-9b9e-192adcd09674.title: Workloads & Benchmarks
1f59cb2a-d61d-4015-9b9e-192adcd09674.definition: Concept of workloads and how to use representative benchmarks to test and evaluate system performance.

338aba95-877d-44a1-af6e-a54c5f4c77ff.title: Performance Data Analysis
338aba95-877d-44a1-af6e-a54c5f4c77ff.definition: Techniques and methods for collecting performance data and analyzing performance indicators of a system.

f1634c7d-83f8-4340-9821-3be3eda6839d.definition: The CPI (Cycles per Instruction) equation is used to analyze and understand the trade-offs in instruction set design, processing pipeline, and memory system organization.

2442f0d2-daff-4bdf-a572-64afe250aab2.title: Amdahl's Law
2442f0d2-daff-4bdf-a572-64afe250aab2.definition: Amdahl's Law describes the limit of a system's acceleration potential when only part of the system is improved, emphasizing that the part that cannot be accelerated limits the overall efficiency.

89e0a93b-1908-4b65-8430-75ae42892dbd.definition: Analyzing the complexity of an algorithm or system using Big O notation, allows estimation of performance behavior as input size increases.

249caf23-efe2-4eaf-b6e7-b901eaff295d.title: Fast/Slow Paths Analysis
249caf23-efe2-4eaf-b6e7-b901eaff295d.definition: Ability to identify and analyze components or processing flows in a system that cause slow paths or fast paths.

e773de9f-fee7-4681-b372-ed670d53ceb5.title: System Events & Performance
e773de9f-fee7-4681-b372-ed670d53ceb5.definition: Understanding of system events such as instruction stalls, cache misses, and page faults and how they negatively impact overall performance.

96474ac4-d58c-4a94-b77e-07c2ea21d3b6.definition: Analytical tools and techniques are used to perform performance assessments quantitatively, providing numerical data for decision making.

ad693635-e9d5-4476-ac4b-77fa12671f22.definition: Deep understanding of layered system architecture, different types of workloads and platforms, how they affect performance, and the challenges that arise when evaluating performance in these complex environments.

08f9d206-cc2e-4601-a9f5-feae1993b1f2.title: Microbenchmark Pitfalls
08f9d206-cc2e-4601-a9f5-feae1993b1f2.definition: Identify and understand the limitations and potential pitfalls of using microbenchmarks to measure performance, especially that they may not accurately reflect performance in real-world environments.

1e1a2930-c797-4aa4-a7c6-b945e8e7f0ae.definition: Ability to explain how different components of the system architecture (e.g., CPU, memory, I/O) interact and contribute to improving overall performance.

35006db5-3c1f-46e6-98df-3e6cef2abe44.definition: The ability to explain when and under what conditions a particular system performance metric (e.g., throughput, latency) becomes useful or appropriate for evaluation.

d3ffb038-fa5f-46b6-a1e4-20d3832f9f72.definition: Explains how to use benchmarks to measure system performance, and points out their limitations and shortcomings in reflecting actual performance.

423d65e9-e223-4307-a95a-5278ebcedbf3.title: Amdahl's Law Limitations
423d65e9-e223-4307-a95a-5278ebcedbf3.definition: Discuss the limitations and cases where Amdahl's Law may not apply or make inaccurate predictions about system speedup.

f0c53ba1-9956-41ed-9538-0ee9c9e59a24.definition: The ability to use frontier studies or simple calculations to provide order-of-magnitude estimates of a specific performance metric in a given context.

68add9b2-b9c7-45d0-9622-a48e92bfd513.definition: Ability to use specialized software tools to analyze program activity (profiling) and measure its performance indicators.

ae5a1f75-5e9b-47ea-9143-aa2ac3a4310b.definition: Ability to design and conduct performance-focused experiments for common systems such as operating systems or big data processing systems (e.g., Spark).

bc80c893-e667-40b2-bc9c-615132166ede.definition: Ability to design a performance experiment on a layered system to study and determine how a specific system parameter affects the overall performance of the system.

4eb94aff-a9be-4192-ac8e-c1f80feed5b8.definition: understand and clearly distinguish three concepts: bug (error in the source code), fault (error in the system that can lead to errors), and failure (system problem that does not work as expected).

7b8b2d74-215f-4d88-b6e9-4e78cad53e59.definition: Distinguish between reliability (the ability to function properly over a period of time) and availability (the proportion of time the system is available) of a system.

0981f5dc-8572-4dac-a4cd-fe64c5c9f252.definition: Concept of achieving system reliability using redundant components or information.

5e6ba618-a213-4d91-9526-29ec70b69ad4.definition: Encoding techniques add redundant information to data to detect and correct errors, including error correction codes, CRC, FEC, and RAID.

4bca3d3e-72c8-4ba9-a470-bc48448db9e4.title: Replication
4bca3d3e-72c8-4ba9-a470-bc48448db9e4.definition: Method of increasing reliability by creating copies (duplication, mirroring, replicas) of data or system components.

8086a497-c741-4db5-b4dc-415082e320a3.definition: Additional techniques and methods to enhance system reliability, beyond redundancy techniques, such as journaling in the file system.

1085b354-1ee6-4016-887c-ba1cc8a6a899.definition: Ability to distinguish different types of errors in computer systems, including program errors, system errors, hardware errors (e.g., corrupted memory), and exceptions (e.g., division by zero).

b4725061-bacb-468b-846d-c84bb25dc3ad.definition: Ability to distinguish between the stages of error management: detecting errors, handling errors when they occur, and recovering the system after errors, along with the technical methods to implement each stage.

0eb77ab8-b8ab-467b-bcde-5e27afcc5b3c.definition: evaluate and optimize the performance of computer systems.

9d82d868-e107-4a25-af88-32c9739b99c4.definition: understand key design principles for computer systems, including performance, reliability, and security.

b36d148f-ee16-485c-b1f6-075f982c2307.title: MySQL Deployment
b36d148f-ee16-485c-b1f6-075f982c2307.definition: Ability to deploy and evaluate typically complex systems such as MySQL based on documentation.
